- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessagePersister.swift:465-492 with TextProcessing/RichContentClassifier.swift:9-12 — prerun runs the same cleanup chain; the comment names the second cleanup as a known cost kept because the golden corpus pins preview derivation on the untrimmed string; skipped for own rows and newsletter-fallback text
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:90,119-123 and Sync/MessagePersister.swift:252-256,295-308 — batch of 50; concurrency min(cores,6) with a comment that it is deliberately near the core count; the whole prepared array is held through the sequential persist loop
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:444-450,744-755 with API/GmailAPIClient+Attachments.swift:8-17 — any non-attachment text part with an attachmentId is fetched whole with no size check; the 2 MiB limit at MessageProcessor.swift:9-12 caps only the per-message memo

**Trigger.** A catch-up sync of HTML-heavy mail (newsletters, marketing): up to 3 pages of 100 history records per app-refresh slice, 10 pages of 500 per foreground slice; or one multi-megabyte HTML body in a batch. Ordinary incremental syncs of a few messages do not show it. The cost is per ingested message and does not grow with S1-S3.

**Impact.** Ingest CPU per HTML message is five to seven DOM parses, plus re-serialization and about ten whole-document regex passes, where one or two parses would do. Not profiled, and no performance test covers preparation. Raw payloads and the prepared forms of a batch (two HTML strings per message, plus inline data) stay alive through the persist loop. An oversized body is fetched whole and run through all of it, with no cancellation check inside a parse, before anything in its batch is persisted. No failure was demonstrated.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited site; all are as described. Own rows and newsletter-fallback rows skip the prerun (four parses). Found no body-size cap by grep or in getAttachment. Repeat-on-expiry in app refresh is prior item bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored (docs/scalability-review.md:437). EmailPreviewClassifier's parsedEmail parameter saves at most one conditional parse (EmailPreviewClassifier.swift:33-36). Lowering concurrency contradicts Constants.swift:119-123 without a measured failure. SwiftSoup is 2.13.5; per-parse time unmeasured.

**October review.** None in docs/scalability-review.md. Nearest: list-search-contains-uncapped-snippet (lines 845-864, createCleanSnippet Int.max). The prerun's second cleanup is recorded only in code, at MessagePersister.swift:474-476.

**Invariant risks**

- RichContentVerdictResolver is the only verdict definition (RichContentVerdictResolver.swift:16-26). Two things would stamp verdicts the bubble load contradicts, so a row swaps from text to card after mount: a prerun computed on any string other than storedHTML, or a size shortcut placed outside RichContentClassifier without a richContentVerdictEpoch bump (CacheVersioning.swift:19-36).
- ChatPreviewRepair re-derives through MessageProcessor.deriveHTMLChatPreview over the stored file (ChatPreviewRepair.swift:436-442). An ingest-only rule for oversized bodies, or merging the snippet and preview pipelines, breaks agreement with the repair and with the cross-platform golden corpus (README_GOLDEN_CORPUS.md: 'remain separate'). Any change to the output needs a chatPreviewDerivationVersion bump, which re-reads every received body.
- Body-materialization contract: a size ceiling must never cap or skip fetching or saving the HTML body, and must never throw for a deterministic size. Cancellation must rethrow and never become a verdict (MessagePersister.swift:447-451). Any sub-batching keeps each ID in exactly one bucket and keeps chronological order.
- .unknown is never a stand-in. Stamping it on oversized rows moves the full classifier to the bubble load, behind the Loading pill. The epoch backfill walks only the rows already stored and will not revisit new ones (RichContentVerdictBackfill.swift:4-12).

**Fix.** Do not build one shared DOM. The snippet and preview pipelines are separate by contract (the golden corpus, web parity), the cleanup modes mutate the tree, and any change to the output forces epoch and derivation-version bumps that re-read every stored body. Take output-identical steps instead. Derive ingest's chat preview from storedHTML, the string ChatPreviewRepair already derives from. Run cleanedHTMLForProcessing once and feed it to two places: a deriveHTMLChatPreview overload (keeping one definition) and a prerun set in MessageProcessor. The persister computes the prerun only when it is nil and keeps its exact-string guard. Pass the extracted text to the newsletter classifier. Check for cancellation between steps. Admit one oversized HTML part at a time, sized by the payload's body.size. No ceiling, no unknown stamp, no fetch cap.

**First step.** Add a test that wraps every golden-corpus HTML input in MIME-like surrounding whitespace. It asserts deriveHTMLChatPreview(raw) == deriveHTMLChatPreview(trimmed) exactly, not through normalize, and decides whether sharing the cleanup needs a version bump.

**Pinning test.** An exact-string test of deriveHTMLChatPreview, raw versus trimmed, over the corpus. In MessageProcessorTests, processGmailMessage returns a richContentPrerun keyed to storedHTML (Revert-check: the processor's assignment). A stub-processor test: at most one oversized preparation runs at a time, and order is kept.

**Payoff.** Drops the prerun's repeated cleanup (one or two parses, more when a mode is rejected) and the classifier's second extraction. Bounds memory for oversized bodies, with no change to stored output and no re-derivation.

### `content-pipeline-cpu#4` · low · performance · effort S · known-open

**ParsedEmailProvider does all DOM work inside one actor, re-parses to upgrade, and still has no byte cap or memory-warning hook**

Area: HTML sanitization, DOM cleaning, text processing and preview builders. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

parsedEmail runs ParsedEmail.parse inside the actor with no suspension, so concurrent requests serialize. Production has two callers: preview cards (includePreviewImages adds a full sanitize plus two more SwiftSoup parses in the same turn) and bubble analysis, only for rows with attachments, calendar invites or an unresolved HTML hint. A row hitting both re-parses to add images. The cache is 256 entries by count, FIFO, no memory-warning clear. The reader's render-quality branch has no production caller, so the claimed mutual eviction and second HTML copy never occur.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/EmailDOM/ParsedEmail.swift:298-344 — actor method: cache lookup, ParsedEmail.parse, store, with no await between; :300-322 a cached entry lacking a requested fact is rebuilt by a full parse; :265-266 and :417-428 countLimit 256 with first-in eviction, no MemoryWarningHandler conformance
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSourceLoader.swift:462-465 — extractImages runs sanitizer.sanitize then EmailPreviewDOMQuery(html:); called from ParsedEmail.swift:120-122 inside the turn. EmailDOMHTMLSanitizer.swift:94-109 (SwiftSoup parse plus outerHtml) and EmailPreviewDOMQuery.swift:11-13 (SwiftSoup.parse) make it three DOM parses per preview request
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentLoader+SourcePreparation.swift:152-163 — the only includeRenderQuality: true call, gated on displayPurpose == .original && originalHTMLPreference == .automatic. HTMLContentLoader.swift:548-549,561-562 and OriginalEmailSourceLoader.swift:683-684 pass .original with .preferHTML; HTMLContentLoader.swift:480-481 and EmailPreviewPipeline.swift:373-383 are .preview. No production caller reaches the branch
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader+HTMLAnalysis.swift:139-155 — bubble analysis loads canonical HTML (and so reaches the provider at :106) only for rows with attachments, a calendar invite, or an unresolved HTML hint; other rows never parse
- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/RenderedMessageCache.swift:630-632 — producers run in separate Tasks, so the provider actor is the serialization point; :137-138 and :571-577 — preview source and analysis are memoized above it (500 entries / 20 MB, cleared on memory warning), so a message reaches the provider once per memo lifetime
- esc-chatmailTests/EmailDOM/ParsedEmailProviderTests.swift:83-84 and :126-149 — the image upgrade's second parse and one-entry-per-message pruning are pinned as intended; docs/scalability-review.md:1386-1407 — cache limits known-open, 'The refute verifier rated this hygiene', 15-40 MB typical and 80-130 MB heavy (estimated)

**Trigger.** First display in a session of several preview cards at once (opening a chat of newsletters or other rich emails), or one multi-hundred-KB body among them; a long session that views many distinct rich messages.

**Impact.** The parse step of preview cards runs one at a time: the last of K cards waits for the sum of the others' turns, each holding three DOM parses and the regex sanitizer over the whole body. Not measured; it happens behind a placeholder and once per message while RenderedMessageCache keeps the result. The cache retains up to 256 bodies (one HTML buffer each; prior estimate 15-40 MB typical, 80-130 MB heavy) through memory warnings. The reader is not affected.

**Verifier.** Checked every caller of loadContent, loadContentWithTimeout, preparePreviewHTML and prepareOriginalHTMLForCaching: none passes .original with .automatic, so the reader half of the finding is dead in production. "Every bubble analysis" is wrong: plain text rows never parse. "Hundreds of MB" is unsupported. Serialization, the triple parse and the count-only FIFO cache without a memory-warning hook stand. Severity lowered: latency unmeasured, bounded by visible cards, memoized above; the cache part was already rated hygiene.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1386-1407 `parsed-email-cache-no-byte-cap` (not in Suggested order's built steps; falls under step 15, line 1628). Actor serialization and images re-parse are new.

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: closeAccountWorkAndClear drains for free only because ParsedEmail.parse never suspends inside the actor (ParsedEmail.swift:298-344, 364-368). An off-actor parse must cancel and await its tasks before clearing. It must re-check a generation captured at entry, because nil-generation callers (SourcePreparation.swift:153) pass accepts(nil) across a close-reopen. It needs a per-message invalidation snapshot, or a late store undoes invalidate(messageId:).
- A memory-warning clear must not bump accountGeneration (CLAUDE.md's AttachmentCacheActor asymmetry, review line 1398 'Keep intact'). The observer goes on `.shared` only: tests build their own providers, and MessagePersisterUpdateTests:427,490 assert on `.shared`.
- Images must keep the sanitizer. extractImages (EmailPreviewSourceLoader.swift:462-465) drops 1x1 pixels by attribute and CSS, rewrites AVIF and modern-format URLs, replaces javascript:/data: srcs, and removes noscript/form/svg (EmailDOMHTMLSanitizer.swift:11-23). isTrackingLikeImageURL checks URLs only. The provider-less builders (NewsletterPreviewBuilder.swift:31-41) and ParsedEmailProviderTests:81 pin equality, so a switch would split production from the corpus and the builder tests.
- Keep canonicalHTML on ParsedEmail: seven `parsedEmail?.canonicalHTML ==` checks (EmailPreviewSourceLoader:294/322/393/417, EmailPreviewClassifier:38, MessageBubbleHTMLAnalysisBuilder:159, EmailRenderQualityEvaluator:60) prove the facts belong to that HTML. The actor is also today's one-DOM-at-a-time limit, so unbounded parallel SwiftSoup parses would raise peak memory.

**Fix.** Two steps, with parsing kept inside the actor. (1) The known-open memory item: a byte budget over summed utf8 counts (canonicalHTML, texts, image strings) beside the 256 count, an access stamp on each hit for LRU, and MemoryWarningHandler on `.shared` only, clearing entries without bumping accountGeneration. (2) An images-only upgrade runs the same extractImages and copies the cached facts through a new private copy-with, skipping EmailDocument.parse. Keep sanitize-then-query for images, and leave reader keys alone (no caller). Off-actor parsing is a measured follow-up. First, make capture/isCurrent lock-backed nonisolated reads: every bubble load hops here (MessageBubbleLoader.swift:162,182). Then add in-flight tasks with a two-lane cap, a drain on close and a generation captured at entry.

**First step.** In ParsedEmail.swift, give ParsedEmailProvider an init flag `startsMemoryWarningObserver` that is true only for `.shared`, as RenderedMessageCache.swift:136-150 does. Add a MemoryWarningHandler clear that empties the cache and its order but leaves accountGeneration and acceptsAccountWork alone.

**Pinning test.** ParsedEmailProviderTests: with a byte limit below two bodies, the last-hit entry survives and the other is evicted. After handleMemoryWarning nothing is cached, yet a pre-warning generation parses and stores. An images upgrade keeps debugParseAttemptCount at 1 (:84). Revert-check each.

**Payoff.** Parsed-email memory is bounded and released under memory pressure (the prior review's unmeasured estimate: 15-40 MB typical, 80-130 MB heavy). A row whose preview follows its analysis skips one full DOM parse.

### `startup-lifecycle#6` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**No launch-health record: a deterministic crash in a launch step or pass repeats on every launch, and launch telemetry goes to a no-op client**

Area: App startup, launch passes and scene lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The app keeps no launch-outcome state, and its one telemetry event goes to a no-op client. The two body-parsing passes (preview re-derivation, verdict backfill) are flag-gated one-shots that each derivation-version or epoch bump re-arms. They start from the list's onAppear, after the UI is up, wait for sync, and write their cursor only after a batch saves. A stored body that trapped the new derivation would be re-hit at the same cursor on each launch. No such body was found, and the same code runs unguarded at sync ingest.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:128,219-223,396-397,446-450 — both body-parsing passes return early once their migration flag is set; the flag keys embed chatPreviewDerivationVersion and richContentVerdictEpoch, so they run only until complete after a bump, not on every launch
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:346-351,512-528 — the checkpoint and the cursor are written only after the batch save succeeded, so a batch that dies is redone from the same cursor
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/RichContentVerdictBackfill.swift:74-92 — each unstamped row runs RichContentVerdictResolver.verdict in-process inside context.perform; lastMessageID advances only in the returned batch
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessagePersister.swift:481-491 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:959-964 — the same classifier and preview derivation run at ingest for every received message ("Shared by ingest and the versioned repair")
- esc-chatmail/Services/Observability/TelemetryClient.swift:31-40 and esc-chatmail/Services/Dependencies/Dependencies.swift:393 — NoopTelemetryClient is the default and record() is intentionally empty; git grep finds no MetricKit and no launch-outcome or crash-count state in esc-chatmail/
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:811-823,493-501 — signOut persists a durable cleanup marker before its first await, and the next launch's restore resumes it before any account is published: an exit other than deleting the app

**Trigger.** A chatPreviewDerivationVersion or richContentVerdictEpoch bump (the former last changed 2026-11-17, CacheVersioning.swift:17) re-arms a mailbox-wide pass, and the new derivation code traps on a stored HTML body that an older build ingested. No such body or trapping line was identified.

**Impact.** Hypothetical: the app would quit shortly after the conversation list appears on each launch (once the first sync ends and the pass reaches the row), until an update ships or the user signs out through the iOS Settings switch. The developer would learn of it only from platform crash reports. A launch-pass breaker alone would not cover the same trap at sync ingest or bubble load.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited location; the code facts hold. Corrections: body-parsing passes are one-shots per version, not every-launch; they start after the UI is published, so this is no watchdog loop; sign-out is a second exit; "owner sees nothing" ignores platform crash reports. RichContentClassifier read whole, no input-dependent trap found; the rest of the cleanup chain was not audited. Restore and send-reconcile crash claims have no support. Not covered by the prior review or CLAUDE.md. Downgraded: an unexercised missing safeguard.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1049 `version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation` covers only what these passes cost per bump, not crash safety. There is no launch-health item.

**Invariant risks**

- The preview pass's Checkpoint is saved inside the cleanup-sensitive hold, with no suspension after the batch save (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:322-351). Split and merge read its deferredConversations list through DeferredRetryAnchors.load over chatPreviewRepairCheckpointKeys (DataCleanupService.swift:438-446). If a breaker rewrites or steps that checkpoint at startup, or anywhere outside the hold, it can drop anchors and move rows that a retry still has to find.
- A stored verdict is never guessed as .unknown, and an epoch bump is never skipped (scalability-review.md:1061). So a row that was skipped must stay .unknown and keep its old preview. Latching a pass's migration flag to stop it would amount to skipping the bump.
- The Mac test host runs App.init against the real container's UserDefaults.standard, which the TestFlight MushMail also uses. A launch counter written in App.init, or straight to UserDefaults.standard instead of the injected storage.migrationFlags, would write or trip state in the user's real app. It must be skipped under RuntimeEnvironment.isRunningUnitTests.
- Reset Mailbox only works after a latched store-load failure, and it loses pending actions, drafts and unsent replies (AppLoadingModel.resetMailbox, AppLoadingPolicy.swift:48-52). Offering it after crashes would not fix a trap that sync hits again at ingest. A quarantine at ingest would need a MessagePersistDisposition bucket: .unprocessable silently loses the message, and .failed freezes the cursor.

**Fix.** No app-wide launch-stage breaker. A background cold launch, a force quit, or a jetsam kill while suspended in the middle of a pass that runs for minutes all look like a crash. Such a breaker also cannot cover ingest or bubble loads. Instead, add per-pass poison-row protection in ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator, through storage.migrationFlags:
- Before each batch, write a marker {pass, start cursor, deaths}, in its own key and not in chatPreviewRepairCheckpointKeys.
- Clear it in the same synchronous section that writes the checkpoint.
- After two deaths at one cursor, run that range one row at a time, with the row ID in the marker.
- On a third death, add that row to a quarantine set that both per-row loops skip. The row stays .unknown, and the cursor advances through the normal Checkpoint.advanced inside the hold.
- Separately, subscribe to MetricKit (MXMetricManager) outside the unit-test host, and log through the redacted Log pipeline.

**First step.** Add the per-pass marker key only. Write it through storage.migrationFlags before prepareBatch and prepareNextBatch, and clear it beside the cursor write and persistChatPreviewCheckpoint. For now a launch that finds it set only logs a Log.warning with the cursor hashed; behavior does not change.

**Pinning test.** In ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinatorTests and RichContentVerdictBackfillTests, with InMemoryMigrationFlagStore: preset a marker showing three deaths at row R. Assert that R is skipped and stays .unknown, the other rows are stamped, deferredConversations is preserved, and the pass completes. Revert-check: the quarantine guard.

**Payoff.** Insurance only: no trapping body was found. After a derivation or epoch bump, a crash on every launch in either pass would shrink to one skipped row. MetricKit would also make launch crashes, hangs and watchdog kills visible.

## Launch, offline and credentials (7)

### `account-boundary-auth#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Cold launch needs Google's token endpoint before it shows local mail; offline it lands on Sign In and never retries**

Area: Account boundary, auth session and credential lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

`initializeApp` awaits the launch restore before showing any UI. On a cold launch the SDK reads the keychain token, and it makes a network refresh unless more than 600 s are left. The keychain is written only by sign-in or restore; foreground refreshes stay in memory. A network error is not credential-invalidating, so the outcome is `.retryableFailure`: credentials are kept and no session is published. The bootstrap still returns true, and `ContentView` shows the first-run `SignInView`. No foreground path, scene change, Mac event or connectivity change runs the restore again.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:227 — `await AppStartupBootstrap.shared.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded()` gates `isInitialized = true` (line 273); scene and Mac system events (341-346, 365-369) act only when `canAccessMailbox` is true and never restore
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:561-580 — waits on the SDK callback; a nil user with a non-invalidating error gets `.retryableFailure` and no staged user. Lines 1503-1507: only GIDSignIn -4 and oauth_token -10 count as invalidating, so AppAuth's network error (general domain, -5) is retryable
- …/GoogleSignIn-iOS/GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDSignIn.m:866-899 — on a cold launch `authenticateWithOptions` calls `maybeFetchToken`, which skips the network only above `kMinimumRestoredAccessTokenTimeToExpire` (600 s, line 146). Lines 1040-1042 call the completion with (nil, error). The keychain is written only via `saveAuthState` (961/1173); GIDGoogleUser.m:151-156 refreshes in memory only
- esc-chatmail/App/AppStartupBootstrap.swift:225-249 — returns true whatever the outcome and sets `isAuthenticationRestored = outcome.isComplete` (false for retryable), so only a later caller re-runs it
- esc-chatmail/App/ContentView.swift:21-25 — `canAccessMailbox` false shows `SignInView()`. SignInView.swift:22-26 and 46-56 show 'A chat-style Gmail client' and 'Continue with Google', with no retry of the restore
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:42-44 — `prepareForBackgroundSync` is the only other caller. Lines 110-113 skip arming when `canAccessMailbox` is false, so only BG requests left pending by an earlier session can retry (iOS only)

**Trigger.** A cold launch while offline, behind a captive portal or on a stalled link. It applies when the last launch restore that refreshed (foreground or BGTask) was more than about 50 minutes earlier, which is nearly every cold launch of a daily-used app on iOS or the Mac. On a stalled link the loading view stays until the token request times out (default URLSession timeout).

**Impact.** A signed-in user who opens the app offline sees the first-run sign-in screen instead of their stored mailbox. Nothing is lost: credentials and the store are kept, and a same-account sign-in keeps the store. The screen stays until the user relaunches online or signs in through Google. On iOS, a background request left pending by an earlier session can also heal it, but only while the app is in the background. The Mac has no such path. Online, every cold launch waits for a token round trip before any local mail appears.

**Verifier.** Checked every caller of the restore: AppStartupBootstrap only, reached from initializeApp and BackgroundSyncManager. No NWPathMonitor or scene-phase retry exists, and the app does not override AppAuth's session. The test suite pins the narrow error classification on purpose, so credentials are kept. The resulting Sign In screen is acknowledged in mac-app-plan.md:444/463/468/482 ('an account held while signed out'), but nothing records it as a decision. One correction: the title's 'never retries' overstates the iOS case, where a previously pending BGTask can retry.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:482 and :468 name the held-account state (offline launch, expired token) and say only a re-run restore (an iOS BG task) brings it back. It is not an item in docs/scalability-review.md and not recorded as a decision.

**Invariant risks**

- Restore order and identity. AuthSession.swift:549-553 closes admission, quiesces and drains before the SDK call, and HTML content stays closed at cold launch until the reopen. Showing the mailbox first means reopening account work on the app-keychain email alone (AuthSession.swift:1266-1268 says app credentials do not restore by themselves). The restore after it then quiesces again over the live UI, and if the SDK names a different account, a restore would have to tear down a published session. No such path exists.
- A missing token is not an account-scoped abort. With currentUser nil, GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:24-27 throws TokenManagerError.noValidToken, which is not an APIError. PendingActionProcessor.swift:307-317 retries unknown errors, burning each action's retry budget until it is abandoned. MessageFetcher.swift:113-117 recognizes only APIError aborts, so message IDs would land in failure buckets. PendingActionsManager.swift:163-168 schedules work on connectivity changes with no auth guard.
- isAuthenticated, canAccessMailbox and userEmail are load-bearing. They gate sync start and BG arming, isDurablySignedOut() (AuthSession.swift:1306) and the Settings sign-out policy, and pendingActionAuthenticationDidRecover must fire only when a token-capable session is published. Moving launch invalid_grant to requiresReauthentication would change clearFailedGoogleSession's documented semantics (SettingsAppSignOutPolicy.swift:33-37), and requireReauthentication only works when isAuthenticated is already true (AuthSession.swift:1415).
- The auth gate has no reentrancy detection and its waits cannot be cancelled. A retry must start from outside any transition and join the single-flight bootstrap, never call restorePreviousSignIn directly. It relies on the isAuthenticated early return (AuthSession.swift:514, pinned by AuthSessionTests:799) after an interactive sign-in. A send in a local-only state would have to be refused before optimistic creation.

**Fix.** Keep the restore's order and its SDK-first identity, and show no mailbox before it. 1) Retry the existing restore in the foreground. A @MainActor coordinator, started at the end of initializeApp, calls AppStartupBootstrap.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded(): it is single-flight, serialized by the gate, and already re-runnable after .retryableFailure. It retries only when the app is initialized, !canAccessMailbox and !isDurablySignedOut(). Triggers: iOS .active, Mac activation and wake, the path monitor becoming satisfied, and a Try Again button. It backs off and keeps one attempt in flight. 2) Publish a separate heldAccountEmail, never userEmail or isAuthenticated. SignInView then says the mail is still on this device, offers Try Again, and prefills the login hint with that address. Reading mail locally before the token is a separate design.

**First step.** Add a pure LaunchRestoreRetryPolicy enum and an AppStartupBootstrap method that returns the restore outcome. Call it from the iOS .active handler and from handleSystemEvent's activation and wake cases in esc_chatmailApp.swift when the policy allows.

**Pinning test.** AuthSessionTests: the restore stub fails with URLError(.notConnectedToInternet) and the session stays signed out. The retry trigger then re-runs it against a succeeding stub, which publishes the session and calls pendingActionAuthenticationDidRecover once. Revert-check: the retry call. Policy tests: no retry when durably signed out.

**Payoff.** A user who opens the app offline gets the account back when connectivity returns, on iOS and the Mac, with no relaunch. The prefilled hint also guards against a wrong-account sign-in that resets the store.

### `concurrency-model#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Launch and the mailbox are gated on an un-deadlined Google restore held under the account boundary; an offline cold launch ends on the sign-in screen**

Area: Concurrency model and Swift 6 readiness. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

restorePreviousSignIn closes outbound admission, takes sync quiescence, then awaits the Google SDK restore through a continuation with no app-side deadline. SDK 9.0.0 does a token POST unless the keychain-saved access token has over 600 s left; it saves that state only at sign-in/restore, so most cold launches need the network. A network error (AppAuth general, -5) is not credential-invalidating: outcome .retryableFailure, nothing published, initializeApp still sets isInitialized, and ContentView shows SignInView over an intact store. No foreground path retries the restore.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:549-562 — closeAdmission, beginQuiescence, cancelAndAwaitAll, cache and download drains, then withCheckedContinuation around restorePreviousGoogleSignIn; no timeout in app code
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:571-579 and 1503-1507 — nil user with a non-invalidating error sets .retryableFailure and publishes nothing; only GID code -4 and org.openid.appauth.oauth_token -10 count as invalidating
- esc-chatmail/App/AppStartupBootstrap.swift:225-232,245-249 and esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:227-273 — restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded returns true for any outcome, latches only outcome.isComplete; isInitialized is set after it returns
- esc-chatmail/App/ContentView.swift:21-25 and esc-chatmail/Views/Main/SignInView.swift:82-105 — canAccessMailbox false shows SignInView, whose only action is interactive signIn; esc-chatmail/App/SettingsAppSignOutPolicy.swift:18-24 describes this exact state (offline, expired token, store and files remain)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:1,43,428-429 and esc-chatmail/App/AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:73,104-105 — the only other restore caller is the iOS-only BGTask readiness check; the scene-background arm needs an authenticated session; .active and didBecomeActive do nothing without canAccessMailbox
- DerivedData .../GoogleSignIn-iOS/GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDSignIn.m:146,892-899,961 — token fetch unless more than 600 s remain; the only saveAuthState call is in the sign-in/restore flow; .../AppAuth-iOS/Sources/AppAuthCore/OIDAuthorizationService.m:441-455 and OIDURLSessionProvider.m:29 — NSURLSession.sharedSession, error wrapped as OIDErrorCodeNetworkError

**Trigger.** A cold launch (iOS or Mac) with no usable network, more than about 50 minutes after the last interactive sign-in or the last launch restore that fetched a token. In-session refreshes are not written back to the SDK keychain state, so this is nearly every cold launch after an hour away. A stalled network gives the same result after the SDK request times out.

**Impact.** A signed-in user with a full local mailbox gets the loading view (briefly offline; up to roughly the URLSession default request timeout, about 60 s, on a stalled network) and then the sign-in screen. Stored mail cannot be read offline. Nothing is deleted. Recovery needs the network: relaunch, an interactive Google sign-in for the same account (store kept), or on iOS a BGTask request left pending from an earlier session. The Mac has no in-process retry.

**Verifier.** Nothing was run. Opened the restore path, bootstrap, ContentView, SignInView, lifecycle policy, BG manager, and SDK/AppAuth sources (Package.resolved pins 9.0.0). No foreground, reachability or wake retry exists. Tightened: the wait has no app deadline but is bounded by URLSession's default timeout (platform default, not measured); a failed launch arms no new BG requests; interactive sign-in also recovers. Docs mention the "held account" state (mac-app-plan.md:444,463,482) as a fact, not a decision; not in scalability-review.md.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:444 and :482 (an account held behind SignInView after a retryable launch restore is acknowledged there and in SettingsAppSignOutPolicy.swift:18-24, but never recorded as a decision); not in docs/scalability-review.md

**Invariant risks**

- The auth-transition gate is what keeps Google SDK calls one at a time (AuthSession.swift:2049-2052), and GIDSignIn holds a single _currentOptions slot (GIDSignIn.m:596, 1036-1039). A deadline, or a background restore that releases the gate while the SDK call is still running, lets an interactive signIn overwrite that slot. The restore's completion then consumes signIn's completion, performSignIn's continuation never resumes, and the gate, whose waits cannot be cancelled, is stuck. So the wait of about 60 s on a stalled network remains.
- The held state must not set isAuthenticated or canAccessMailbox. With no currentUser, GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:24-27 throws TokenManagerError.noValidToken. That is not an APIError, so MessageFetcher.swift:105,113-117 buckets it as a permanent per-message failure and PendingActionProcessor.swift:307-317 retries the action until it is abandoned. isAuthenticated would also end the retry early at AuthSession.swift:514. Never start a restore from a token refresh: a lease holder waiting on a transition deadlocks.
- Account boundary: the retryable path leaves participant caches, downloads and outbound admission closed (AuthSession.swift:549-553; they are reopened only when a user is returned, 627-647). Publishing the held state must go through reopenAccountWork(after:), all-or-none, before endQuiescence, and must honor .latchedRefusal and .supersededByAccountRemoval. The store check must be read-only: never prepareLocalStoreForAuthenticatedAccount, whose mismatch branch resets the store (1227-1242).
- The held flag must be cleared wherever isAuthenticated is cleared (signOut, signOutAndDisconnect, clearAuthState/clearFailedGoogleSession, both resume paths). Otherwise the mailbox stays on screen over a wiped store and no SignInView is reachable. Send in the held state must be refused before the optimistic message is created (the no-resend rule). pendingActionAuthenticationDidRecover runs only on a real publish, and SettingsAppSignOutSubject must still treat the held state as not signed in.

**Fix.** Keep the SDK restore inside restorePreviousSignIn's gate and quiescence, and change only what a retryable failure ends in. First, map TokenManagerError.noValidToken to APIError.authenticationError. Then, on a non-invalidating SDK error, check before endQuiescence, without writing anything, that the keychain email is readable, that no cleanup or signed-out marker exists, and that inspectLocalMailboxStore returns exactly one Account row with that email. If so, run reopenAccountWork(after:) and, on .reopened, publish a separate heldOfflineEmail. isAuthenticated and canAccessMailbox stay false, so sync, BG arms and pending-action recovery stay off. ContentView shows the mailbox, with Send disabled, when either flag is set. Clear the held flag everywhere clearAuthState runs. Retry through AppStartupBootstrap.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded on activation, on wake and when the network path is usable again, with backoff.

**First step.** In GmailAPIClient.authenticatedRequest, map TokenManagerError.noValidToken, which GoogleTokenRefresher throws when there is no currentUser, to APIError.authenticationError. Sync and PendingActionProcessor then treat a missing SDK session as account-scoped and stop bucketing message IDs or using up retryCount. This step is safe by itself.

**Pinning test.** AuthSessionTests: a restore stubbed to fail with appauth.general -5, over a store whose only Account row matches the keychain email, returns .retryableFailure. The held flag is set, canAccessMailbox is false, reopen runs once and the recovery hook is not called. With a second Account row: not held, no reset. signOut clears the held flag.

**Payoff.** A signed-in user who launches offline or on a stalled network can read and sort stored mail instead of landing on the sign-in screen, and the Mac gets a restore retry without relaunching.

### `startup-lifecycle#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Cold launch gates the local mailbox on a network token refresh; a failed refresh shows the sign-in screen and nothing in the foreground retries**

Area: App startup, launch passes and scene lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

initializeApp awaits AuthSession.restorePreviousSignIn before any UI. When the SDK-stored access token has under 600 s left, GIDSignIn's silent restore makes a token-refresh request (AppAuth on NSURLSession.shared) with no app timeout, under the auth gate and sync quiescence. A network error gives .retryableFailure; the bootstrap still returns true, canAccessMailbox stays false and ContentView shows SignInView over an intact store. Only a BGTask delivery re-runs the restore: scene activation, connectivity change and Mac wake do nothing, and the iOS scene-background arm is itself gated on canAccessMailbox.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:148-167,227,273 — AppLoadingView until initializeApp finishes; it awaits restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded() at :227 and sets isInitialized = true only at :273
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:549-562,571-579,659 — closeAdmission, beginQuiescence, then an un-timed withCheckedContinuation around restorePreviousGoogleSignIn; nil user with a non-invalidating error sets .retryableFailure; the session is published only at :659 from a GIDGoogleUser (:1503-1507 treats only GID -4 and oauth_token -10 as invalidating)
- DerivedData .../SourcePackages/checkouts/GoogleSignIn-iOS (rev 3996d908 = pinned 9.0.0) GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDSignIn.m:146,885,892-899,932,961 — silent restore calls maybeFetchToken, which skips the network only with more than 600 s left, else performTokenRequest; saveAuthState is called only in this flow. AppAuth OIDURLSessionProvider.m:29 uses [NSURLSession sharedSession]; OIDAuthorizationService.m:446-455 wraps a transport error as OIDErrorCodeNetworkError
- esc-chatmail/App/AppStartupBootstrap.swift:231-232,245-248 — restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded returns true for any outcome; isAuthenticationRestored = outcome.isComplete, so only a later caller re-runs it
- esc-chatmail/App/AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:73,90,104-105 and esc-chatmail/App/ContentView.swift:21-25 — activation, init completion and Mac wake/activate return .none without canAccessMailbox; ContentView shows SignInView (Views/Main/SignInView.swift has no restore retry and no offline message)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:43,111,428-430 — the only other restore caller is BGTask readiness (iOS only, file is #if os(iOS)); armBackgroundTasksForSceneBackground returns early unless canAccessMailbox, so a failed-restore session arms no new request

**Trigger.** A cold launch offline or on a stalled network while the SDK-persisted access token has under 10 minutes left. The SDK writes its keychain state only in the sign-in/restore flow (GIDSignIn.m:961); the app's in-session refreshes go through GIDGoogleUser.refreshTokensIfNeeded (GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:30), which does not save it. So this is any cold launch about 50 minutes or more after the last sign-in or refreshing restore, which is broader than "after the last token refresh".

**Impact.** A signed-in user with the mailbox on disk sees the loading view, then an unexplained sign-in screen, and cannot read stored mail offline. On a stalled link the loading view lasts until URLSession's request timeout (inferred: 60 s default, not set by AppAuth). No data is lost: credentials, store and body files are kept (pinned by AuthSessionTests.swift:464-476). Recovery is a relaunch online, an interactive Google sign-in (same account keeps the store), or on iOS a BGTask request left pending from an earlier session. The Mac has no automatic retry at all. Separately, most cold launches pay one token-refresh round trip before first content.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited line: all as described. Read the SDK at the pinned revision. Found no guard or retry: the restore's only callers are initializeApp and BGTask readiness. Comments and docs/mac-app-plan.md:444,482 acknowledge the held-account state but record no decision to withhold the mailbox offline. Tightened: broader trigger, interactive sign-in also recovers, iOS retry needs an already-pending request. Publishing offline needs a GIDGoogleUser (GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:24-27), so that half of the fix exceeds M; retry-on-path/active/wake is small.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:444 and :482 acknowledge the held-account state (a launch restore that failed retryably leaves the account behind SignInView) for Sign Out…, but no retry or offline UI is tracked; docs/scalability-review.md has no matching item

**Invariant risks**

- Wrapping the withCheckedContinuation at AuthSession.swift:561 in withSoftTimeout releases the auth gate while the callback can still fire. GIDSignIn still saves auth state and sets currentUser (GIDSignIn.m:951-975). The app's callback would then run clearFailedGoogleSession or the ungated persistSessionForBackgroundAccess outside quiescence, after a queued sign-out or another account's sign-in.
- Publishing from app-owned credentials is a new publish path beside the existing six (mac-app-plan.md:439, 'Don't add a seventh AuthSession path'). It leaves currentUser nil, so GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:24-27 throws noValidToken on every refresh. GmailAPIClient.swift:460-463 maps that to authenticationError, never to reauthentication.
- A lazy SDK restore started from TokenManager would run inside a sync run. restorePreviousSignIn's beginQuiescence drains that run (SyncRunCoordinator.swift:286-296), so it deadlocks under the lease-holder rule. Any late SDK completion must also check that the SDK user's email matches the published session, or another account's tokens get refreshed into this store.
- A retried restore that finishes while the iOS app is in the background arms no background tasks. The scene-background arm was skipped because canAccessMailbox was false, and handleAuthStateChange starts nothing when the scene is not active (esc_chatmailApp.swift:237-243, 409-421).

**Fix.** Keep the GIDGoogleUser restore as the only publisher and fix what surrounds it.
1. Bound the restore at its transport. In configureGoogleSignIn, install an AppAuth session (OIDURLSessionProvider.setSession) with about 15 s request and 30 s resource timeouts. The SDK callback then returns a non-invalidating network error inside the gate. Never soft-time AuthSession.swift:561.
2. Add AppLifecyclePolicy.retryAuthenticationRestore, throttled. It runs on scene active, on Mac activate and wake, and when OutboundNetworkPathMonitor reports a satisfied path, if the app is initialized and !isAuthenticated. It calls AppStartupBootstrap.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded.
3. Arm BG tasks when authentication lands while the app is in the background.
4. In SignInView, show a held-account banner with Retry and the email prefilled.
An offline publish is a separate redesign that needs Kevin's decision.

**First step.** Add a `.retryAuthenticationRestore` SyncAction to AppLifecyclePolicy for scene `.active` and for Mac activate and wake when `isInitialized && !isAuthenticated`. Pin it in AppLifecyclePolicyTests, and have performSyncAction call `AppStartupBootstrap.shared.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded()`.

**Pinning test.** AuthSessionTests: the restore stub fails with URLError(.notConnectedToInternet), then succeeds; two bootstrap.restoreAuthenticationIfNeeded() calls publish once and call pendingActionAuthenticationDidRecover once. AppLifecyclePolicyTests: active or wake with !isAuthenticated returns the retry action. Revert-check names that case.

**Payoff.** A signed-in user who launches offline or on a stalled link gets past the loading view within about 15 s. The account then comes back by itself when connectivity or focus returns, on iOS and the Mac.

### `account-boundary-auth#4` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**A launch restore rejects the Google session on any local fault, and rewrites a credential transaction every launch for a copy nothing reads**

Area: Account boundary, auth session and credential lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The restore callback has one catch for every error from account preparation and credential persistence. That catch calls `clearFailedGoogleSession()`, which signs the SDK out, deletes the tokens and persists the signed-out verdict, so the next restore ends terminal. Failed reads of the reset marker or the store change nothing and still get this treatment, while reopen failures keep the credentials. Each restore also writes a marker-bracketed transaction of about 9 keychain calls, and a kill inside it signs the user out. Correction: of the items that transaction writes, only the refresh-token copy is unread.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:609-615 — catch-all in the restore callback: `_ = self.clearFailedGoogleSession()`, then `.retryableFailure`
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1192-1208 — a marker read error or a failed `inspectLocalMailboxStore()` throws `localAccountIsolationFailed` before anything is changed; the comment at 1195-1197 says to refuse publication "until a later attempt" can tell whether the marker is missing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1459-1479 — clearFailedGoogleSession persists durableSignedOut, calls signOutGoogleSession() (GIDSignIn.signOut, line 338-340) and clearTokens(); lines 1707-1726 then return `.terminalNoSession` on the next restore
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthRestoreReopenPolicy.swift:28-34 — a transient reopen failure keeps the credentials: clearing them "would turn a recoverable hiccup into a forced re-authentication"
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1364-1379 — every restore runs: marker add, token saves, email save, durable-verdict delete, marker delete (KeychainService.swift:109-124: a save is an add, then an update on a duplicate); lines 1803-1859 sign out when the marker survives a kill
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager.swift:352-355,394 — the refresh-token item is written and deleted, and is read only by a presence probe (AuthSession.swift:1269-1283); GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:24-30 refreshes through `currentUser`; the access-token item IS read by getCurrentToken on a cold cache (TokenManager.swift:237)

**Trigger.** A launch restore, foreground or BGTask cold launch, in which the SDK restore succeeds and then one of these happens: the reset-marker keychain read fails, the Account fetch fails on the loaded store, a keychain write in persistSessionForBackgroundAccess fails, or the process is killed between the marker write and its delete.

**Impact.** The user is forced to sign in again. The store and body files are kept, but clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults drops the sync timestamps. Only the read failures are avoidable: once a write fails partway, the marker already signs the user out at the next launch by design. The keychain calls run synchronously on the main actor at every launch. How often any trigger happens is unmeasured, and it is likely rare.

**Verifier.** The mechanism holds. Nothing documents clearing on local faults as deliberate: SettingsAppSignOutPolicy.swift:33-35 names invalid_grant and a missing scope as the reasons to clear, and no test pins the catch. Narrowing: line 497→1738 has already read the same marker key successfully in this transition, and AppStartupBootstrap.swift:193-196 restores only after the store has loaded, so both read faults have to be transient. The title's "copy nothing reads" is wrong for the access-token and email items. isAuthenticated() has no production caller.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md history-recovery-window-install-fallback covers only the downstream cost (now mitigated by SyncTimeCalculator.historyRecoveryInstallBranchStartTime); CLAUDE.md Account-generation boundary, prepareLocalStoreForAuthenticatedAccount bullet

**Invariant risks**

- Supersession is wrapped the same way. When a sign-out is queued, performDurableLocalCleanup throws CancellationError (AuthSession.swift:1670-1672) and prepare wraps it at line 1241. The catch must check isAccountRemovalRequested first and clear nothing, because the queued sign-out owns the teardown (AuthRestoreReopenPolicy.swift:43-47). It must never call the crash-resume pair, and must never re-enter restorePreviousSignIn: the gate wait cannot be cancelled.
- Once a marker is persisted, the outcome must stay a rejection. Prepare persists localStoreResetRequired at line 1238 and persistSession persists credentialCleanupRequired at line 1367; after either, the next launch signs out by design (lines 1735-1862). Rejection must also stay for missingAccountEmail. Interactive signIn stays all-or-none (lines 699-701), and authenticated UI is never published before prepare returns.
- TokenManager epoch invariant. A replacement for the ungated saveTokens must still bump _cacheEpoch inside cacheLock (TokenManager.swift:343-348). The refresh populate must stay epoch-gated, with the MainActor re-check that the epoch matches and the cached token is the same one (lines 371-376). Otherwise a retired refresh publishes into a replacement session.
- The durable signed-out verdict must still be consumed after an interactive sign-in, and after a restore whose preparation reset the store: performDurableLocalCleanup persists the verdict at line 1679. The email is written before the verdict is deleted (lines 1373-1378). Legacy token items must be deleted under cacheLock, and they must stay in the hasPersistedBackgroundCredentialMaterial probe (lines 1269-1283).

**Fix.** Ship as two changes. First: keep AuthError.localAccountIsolationFailed, but have it carry a nominal stage: markerUnreadable and storeUninspectable (nothing was changed) versus resetRequiredOrFailed. Add a pure AuthRestorePreparationPolicy that returns the existing RestoreDisposition. In the restore catch: if isAccountRemovalRequested, return .retryableFailure without clearing. Nothing-changed stages map to .retryKeepingCredentials. Reset stages, a missing email and credential-persist failures call clearFailedGoogleSession, as they do now. Leave signIn all-or-none. Second, separately: stop writing the token items. Seed the cache through an ungated, epoch-bumping in-memory adopt. Delete the legacy items once, under cacheLock. On restore, write the email only if it changed, and always delete the verdict. Update CLAUDE.md's TokenManager bullet.

**First step.** Add a nominal LocalAccountIsolationStage carried by AuthError.localAccountIsolationFailed and set it at AuthSession.swift:1198, 1207 and 1241. Add AuthRestorePreparationPolicy (stage → RestoreDisposition) with a table test covering every stage.

**Pinning test.** In AuthSessionTests, a failing marker read and a failing store inspection each throw a nothing-changed stage with no keychain write. Add a policy table test, and a repositorySource pin that the restore catch asks isAccountRemovalRequested, then the policy. Revert-check each hunk.

**Payoff.** A transient keychain or store read fault at launch no longer forces a Google re-sign-in and a sync-default reset. Part two drops about 9 main-actor keychain calls per launch.

### `gap-wall-clock-time#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Setting the clock back blocks Gmail authentication: the 401 refresh cannot force a new token**

Area: The device's wall clock is the only clock: clock changes, skew and time zones. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The 401 path is as described: GmailAPIClient makes one refresh, through GIDGoogleUser.refreshTokensIfNeeded, and then throws authenticationError. But that GoogleSignIn check also looks at the ID token's expiry, which is the JWT `exp` claim in server time. When a fast clock is put right, that check fires at the real expiry and the refresh goes to Google. So the outage needs the clock to read behind true time by more than about 60 s, and to have moved back since the held token was issued. It lasts about the smaller of those two amounts minus 60 s. It happens once per backward jump, because the next token is stamped on the skewed clock.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:441-465 — the 401 case refreshes once via tokenManager.refreshToken(), reads getCurrentToken(), retries, then throws APIError.authenticationError
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:29-37 — the refresh is user.refreshTokensIfNeeded, never a forced refresh; it returns tokens.accessToken.expirationDate
- GoogleSignIn-iOS checkout at the pinned 3996d908 (9.0.0), GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDGoogleUser.m:120-127 — completes with self and no network call unless the access token OR the idToken expires within 60 s of the device's now
- AppAuth-iOS checkout at the pinned 145104f5 (2.0.0), Sources/AppAuthCore/OIDIDToken.m:87-95 — the idToken's expiresAt is the JWT `exp` via dateWithTimeIntervalSince1970 (server time); OIDFieldMapping.m:112-118 — the access token's expires_in becomes dateWithTimeIntervalSinceNow (device clock)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager.swift:152-153, 226-227 — the cached token is served while its device-clock expiry is more than 300 s away; the refresh saves the same token and expiry back (TokenManager+Refresh.swift:25-42)
- GoogleSignIn-iOS GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDSignIn.m:892-899 — the restore at launch fetches a token only when the access token's device-clock expiry is within 600 s, so relaunching does not end the window

**Trigger.** The device clock is set to read behind true time by more than about a minute while a token is held. Examples: a traveller who turns off automatic time and sets the wall clock back instead of changing the time zone, or a date set back to extend a trial or for a game. Correcting a fast clock to true time (switching back to automatic, a fast Mac being put right, undoing a forward time-travel) does not trigger it: GoogleSignIn's ID-token check catches those after one 401.

**Impact.** The window starts at the held token's real expiry. It lasts about the smaller of how far the clock moved back and how far behind it reads, minus 60 s. During it every Gmail call 401s twice and fails as authenticationError: sync shows 'Authentication failed', pending actions sit in authentication backoff, and replies fail as authenticationFailed. A 401 is a definite rejection, so no duplicate is sent. There is no reauthentication prompt and no data loss. It ends by itself and does not recur under the same skew.

**Verifier.** Checked that the DerivedData checkouts are at the revisions Package.resolved pins. The auditor missed the idToken term in GIDGoogleUser.m:121-122. The app does get an ID token: GoogleSignIn adds the email and profile scopes, and Constants.swift lists openid. This correction assumes Google's refresh response carries a new id_token, which cannot be read from code. If it does not, AppAuth's updateWithTokenResponse leaves idToken nil after the first refresh, and the auditor's fast-clock-corrected triggers would hold too. No clock-skew handling or documented decision was found. Severity was lowered for the narrow trigger, the bounded window, the one-time occurrence and the self-healing.

**Invariant risks**

- TokenManager epoch discipline (TokenManager.swift:162-176, 338-362): evicting the stale token with clearTokens() or saving it with an ungated saveTokens bumps the epoch, cancels in-flight refreshes and nil-publishes authSession.accessToken. clearTokens also deletes the keychain refresh token. The forced token may be saved only through saveTokens(ifCacheEpochMatches:) inside performTokenRefresh.
- TokenRefreshCoordinator single-flight per epoch (TokenManager.swift:10-53): if each caller forces its own refresh, a sync burst of about 10 concurrent 401s sends about 10 token requests. A forced caller that joins a plain in-flight task gets the stale token back.
- Non-idempotent send: a 401 is the only status on which messages.send is sent again (GmailAPIClient.swift:441-465, pinned by GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests:553-560). Keep the once-only hasAttemptedTokenRefresh / allowedAttempts += 1 bound. Never add a second refresh-and-resend round.
- Revocation verdicts: an invalid_grant from the forced refresh must reach TokenManagerError.invalidCredentials through performTokenRefresh, then the epoch-gated publishCredentialRevocation, then APIError.credentialsRevoked. A bypass, such as a direct POST to the token endpoint, would map it wrongly or publish it into a replacement session. It would also leave GIDGoogleUser holding the stale token.

**Fix.** Pass the rejected bearer down one path. In GmailAPIClient's 401 case, read the Authorization header that was sent and call a new TokenManager.refreshToken(rejecting:). If the cache holds a fresh token that differs from the rejected one, TokenManager returns it. Otherwise it joins a single-flight entry keyed on epoch plus rejected token and saves only through the gated save. GoogleTokenRefresher, on the MainActor, calls refreshTokensIfNeeded. If that returns the rejected token, it sets needsTokenRefresh on the user's OIDAuthState (reached through fetcherAuthorizer's GTMAppAuth AuthSession; add those package products in Xcode). It then runs a fresh-token action and reads user.accessToken. Keep the once-only 401 resend. If the token is still unchanged, throw authenticationError without sending again.

**First step.** Write the failing StubURLProtocol test first: a real TokenManager with MockKeychainService, and a MockTokenRefresher that returns the token which drew the 401. Then add refreshToken(rejecting:) to TokenManagerProtocol and pass in the bearer from the 401 case.

**Pinning test.** In GmailAPIClientRetryAccountingTests, script [401, 200]. A plain refresh returns the rejected token and a forced refresh returns a new one. Assert two requests, the second with the new bearer, and one forced refresh. Add a Revert-check on TokenManager's rejected-token comparison. Add concurrent-401 and sign-out-mid-refresh cases.

**Payoff.** Ends a silent Gmail auth outage after the clock is set back, at the cost of one extra token request. It also recovers from any 401 on a token the device still thinks is valid.

### `networking#3` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**Token failures on the ordinary path are not APIErrors, so revoked credentials bypass every account-scoped abort and park**

Area: Networking and Gmail API client. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

authenticatedRequest rethrows getCurrentToken's error unmapped. When the cached token is expiring, the proactive refresh throws TokenManagerError (invalidCredentials after publishing reauthentication, or refreshFailed/noValidToken). Only the 401 branch maps to APIError. Pending-action processing stops and parks only on an APIError, so it retries the oldest row five times with 2/4/8/16 s backoff and marks it abandoned, then moves to the next row. MessageFetcher classifies the same error as a permanent per-message failure, which stages deferred rows and one failure strike.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:202 — `let token = try await tokenManager.getCurrentToken()` with no catch; :457-463 is the only mapping to APIError.credentialsRevoked / .authenticationError, inside the 401 case
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager+Refresh.swift:71-82 — non-retryable refresh failure throws TokenManagerError.invalidCredentials (or the raw error) after publishCredentialRevocation; TokenManager.swift:270 getCurrentToken falls through to refreshToken() when the token is expiring
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionProcessor.swift:226-235 — stopRun requires `error as? APIError`; :307-317 any other error returns shouldRetry true; :339-347 retryCount+1 and `abandoned` at maxRetries (5); :253-254 backoff 2*2^retryCount capped at 30 s
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManager.swift:884-903 — loop re-fetches the oldest pending/failed row after .continueRun; :228-233 and :789-792 set isWaitingForCredentialRecovery only for outcome .credentialsRevoked
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:113-117 — accountScopedAbortError requires APIError; :77-107 a TokenManagerError is not retriable; :205-208 it lands in permanentlyFailedIds; Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:61-72 stages those IDs via recordFailure
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1414-1417 — requireReauthentication only sets a flag; esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:424-426 the flag stops foreground sync only, nothing parks or cancels the pending-action run

**Trigger.** Refresh token revoked (password change, access removed) and discovered by the proactive refresh, i.e. the cached access token is within 5 minutes of expiry or expired (app resumed after an hour idle, or a Mac app left open), while pending/failed PendingAction rows exist or an action is enqueued at that moment. For sync: the token crosses the 5-minute threshold between a run's history listing and its message fetches.

**Impact.** Each queued archive, spam or read-state action is marked abandoned about 30 s after the verdict, the next about 60 s later, until the user signs in again (the sign-in transition cancels the run; rows still under 5 retries survive). Abandoned rows are not deleted: the conversation-list banner offers Retry All after sign-in, but the queue's intended park-until-reauthentication is skipped. Sync: at most one run commits deferred rows and one of three escape-hatch strikes, because later syncs are gated on canAccessMailbox.

**Verifier.** Read both token paths, the whole pending-action manager and processor, MessageFetcher, MessageFetchPhase, the reauthentication handlers. No guard found: requireReauthentication only flips a flag and stops foreground sync. Not documented as deliberate; CLAUDE.md states the opposite invariant. No test covers a getCurrentToken failure outside sendMessage. Tightened: abandonment takes about 30 s, is recoverable from the banner, and the sync effect is one bounded run. The SDK's invalid_grant shape was not verified, but either branch throws a TokenManagerError.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1637 "Already sound": "quota and auth errors abort with no verdicts". That holds only on the 401 path (GmailAPIClient.swift:441-465). The review never looked at the token preflight in authenticatedRequest. Related invariant: CLAUDE.md, Sync cursor and staging invariants, the account-scoped aborts bullet.

**Invariant risks**

- Send outcome matrix (CLAUDE.md, Outbound send): the mapping must stay before the barrier, inside sendMessage's transmissionNotStarted wrap (GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:67-82). If a non-cancellation token failure becomes CancellationError, a chat reply that fails before the barrier is rolled back instead of staying Not sent (ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:491-533). Do not put a mapper that passes cancellation through into the 401 branch either: a CancellationError there reaches isAmbiguousSendFailure (GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:112), and a send Gmail rejected with 401 would show as Delivery unknown.
- Only authenticationDidRecover releases the parked pending-action queue (PendingActionsManager.swift:80-86, 377-407). If noValidToken or a transient refresh failure maps to credentialsRevoked, the queue parks without requireReauthentication ever being set. Nothing then prompts the user, and the queue stays parked until the next restore or process restart.
- isAccountScopedSyncAbort covers auth, revoked credentials and quota only (APIErrorRecovery.swift:17-24; the review's Keep intact). Map into existing APIError cases. Do not widen that set or add TokenManagerError checks at call sites. A token failure while fetching a large body or attachment moves from .bodyFetchFailed (MessagePersister.swift:443-455) to a run abort. That is the bucket the docs already prescribe, but it must be pinned by a test.
- TokenManager's epoch contract: a retired generation throws CancellationError (TokenManager+Refresh.swift:10-49), and AuthSession.withFreshToken, WebKitPrewarmer, ChatViewModel and TokenManagerTests all consume TokenManagerError directly. So map at the client boundary, never inside getCurrentToken or refreshToken.

**Fix.** Map only in GmailAPIClient.authenticatedRequest: wrap getCurrentToken() in a do/catch that goes through a pure static mapper beside classify403. A CancellationError (retired epoch) is rethrown unchanged. TokenManagerError.invalidCredentials becomes APIError.credentialsRevoked; TokenManager has already published requireReauthentication. Every other failure (noValidToken, tokenExpired, refreshFailed, networkUnavailable, unknown) becomes APIError.authenticationError, which is already an account-scoped abort: sync records no verdicts, pending actions are requeued behind the bounded 30 s to 5 min authentication retry, and sends still fail before the barrier inside transmissionNotStarted. Do not map to networkError: MessageFetcher would rerun the refresh on each of its three retry passes and still stage per-message failures. Leave the 401 branch and TokenManager unchanged. Update the expected underlying error in the send preflight test.

**First step.** Add a static apiError(forTokenAcquisitionFailure:) next to classify403 in GmailAPIClient.swift, with a table test covering each TokenManagerError case, CancellationError and a raw NSError. Then call it from a new catch around getCurrentToken() in authenticatedRequest.

**Pinning test.** Real GmailAPIClient with StubURLProtocol and a token preflight that throws invalidCredentials. getMessage throws APIError.credentialsRevoked and sends zero requests. A PendingActionsManager run leaves the row pending at retryCount 0 and parks. MessageFetcher.fetchBatch throws with empty fetchFailedIds. Revert-check: the mapper.

**Payoff.** A revocation found by the proactive refresh parks queued archive, spam and read actions until re-sign-in instead of abandoning them. Sync stops staging false per-message failures and escape-hatch strikes.

### `networking#4` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**Token acquisition sits in front of every request and is neither cancellable nor time-bounded**

Area: Networking and Gmail API client. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Each request awaits getCurrentToken. When a real refresh is needed, waiters plainly await the value of an unstructured task nothing cancels, so caller cancellation is not observed. That task wraps the SDK callback with no deadline and makes up to three attempts with uncancelled backoff; the epoch is checked only between attempts, and a failed cycle leaves no cooldown. Each attempt is bounded only by the SDK's URLSession.shared request. The 401 path calls the same refreshTokensIfNeeded, which returns the same token while 60 s or more remain.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:202 — authenticatedRequest awaits tokenManager.getCurrentToken() before any URLSession call and maps no error; :448-456 the 401 branch calls refreshToken() then getCurrentToken() and resends once; GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:69-78 shows sendMessage takes the token the same way, before its transmission barrier
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager.swift:277-307 — the coordinator's factory builds an unstructured Task; the waiter does `try await handle.task.value` with no cancellation handler; on failure clearTask (:48-52) only empties the entry, so the next caller builds a new task. `git grep` finds no cancel of the handle and no reader of lastRefreshError
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/GoogleTokenRefresher.swift:29-44 — withCheckedThrowingContinuation around user.refreshTokensIfNeeded; no deadline and no cancellation handler
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager+Refresh.swift:9-25 — loop of maxRetryAttempts (3, TokenManager.swift:143) with Task.sleep backoff (ExponentialBackoff.swift:18-23: base 1 s, factor 2); the epoch is checked at :10, :19, :45, :91, never during the SDK call; :113-120 refreshFailed is retryable unless invalid_grant
- ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/esc-chatmail-abfnxsrhwkxdmcctrhgryheknlhm/SourcePackages/checkouts/GoogleSignIn-iOS/GoogleSignIn/Sources/GIDGoogleUser.m:54 and :120-127 — kMinimalTimeToExpire = 60.0; with 60 s or more left the completion gets the same user on the main queue and no request is made; otherwise :151 OIDAuthorizationService.performTokenRequest, which AppAuth runs on [NSURLSession sharedSession] (AppAuth-iOS/Sources/AppAuthCore/OIDURLSessionProvider.m:29) with a plain NSURLRequest (OIDTokenRequest.m:344). Pinned versions 9.0.0 / 2.0.0 match Package.resolved
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:845-846 — signOut awaits beginQuiescence() and outboundTaskRegistry.cancelAndAwaitAll() before clearTokens() at :1689 bumps the epoch (reached from :879); SyncRunCoordinator.swift:286-296 cancels the run and waits for it with no bound; BackgroundSyncManager.swift:260-263 completes the BGTask only after the worker returns, and SyncEngine.swift:289-293 awaits the cancelled run

**Trigger.** The access token is expired or has under 60 s left (routine: a foreground resume or a warm background wake about an hour after the last refresh; AppStartupBootstrap.swift:197-199 skips the restore on a warm wake), on a network that reports a usable path while Google's token endpoint stalls, and during that wait a BGTask expires, the user signs out, or a sync or send is cancelled. Between 300 s and 60 s before expiry the SDK makes no request, so nothing can stall there. With no route the SDK attempt fails at once, and a sync run does not start without a path (SyncEngine.swift:512-516).

**Impact.** The cancelled run or send cannot unwind until the whole refresh cycle ends: up to three SDK attempts plus about 3 s of backoff. With Foundation's default 60 s request timeout (a platform default, not set in any file read) that is roughly 3 minutes at worst, not unbounded. For that time setTaskCompleted is not called after a BGTask expires, sign-out sits in beginQuiescence / cancelAndAwaitAll with the auth-transition gate held, and cancelSync does nothing. No data is lost, since nothing is mid-commit. Whether iOS terminates the app for the late completion is platform behavior that the repository cannot confirm. On a 401 with an unexpired token the client sends one more doomed request and throws authenticationError; no invalid_grant verdict is reached until the token nears expiry, so syncs keep failing without a reauthentication prompt for up to the token's remaining life.

**Verifier.** Read TokenManager and its refresh extension, the refresher, the client, AuthSession sign-out, SyncRunCoordinator, BackgroundSyncManager, and the pinned GoogleSignIn/AppAuth sources in DerivedData. Changed: bounded by the SDK's URLSession, not unbounded; the stall window is 60 s, not five minutes; offline fails fast. No guard, CLAUDE.md decision or scalability-review item covers it; awaitValueUnlessCancelled (AsyncTimeout.swift:113) exists but is unused here. Adjacent, downstream not traced: MessageFetcher.swift:105-106 and :205-208 bucket a raw TokenManagerError as permanently failed.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md, Account-generation boundary: the TokenManager paragraph (epoch, setCachedToken(_:ifEpochMatches:), TokenRefreshCoordinator single-flight). Not in docs/scalability-review.md.

**Invariant risks**

- TokenManager epoch fence and single-flight. A waiter that is cancelled or times out must not clear or replace the coordinator entry: TokenManager.swift:298-306 clears it from the waiter today, and a second refresh in the same generation would break single-flight. Nothing may clear a finished entry either (:35-37 returns it to the next caller), so a later caller could receive an old token or an old error. The shared task must still save only through saveTokens(ifCacheEpochMatches:).
- Timeout helper. The existing withTimeout (APIError.swift:126-143) is a task group, and a task group waits for its uncancellable child before it returns, so around the SDK continuation it bounds nothing. Its APIError.timeout counts as ambiguous in isAmbiguousSendFailure and mapSendError. Use the single-fire-gate pattern (AsyncTimeout.swift withDeadline / awaitValueUnlessCancelled) and an existing error class.
- Non-idempotent send. Today the 401 branch's catch-all (GmailAPIClient.swift:460-462) turns a refresh that is cancelled or times out into authenticationError, which correctly marks a 401-rejected send definitely unsent. Letting a bare CancellationError out of that branch makes isAmbiguousSendFailure report "Delivery unknown". The branch must mirror sleepBeforeRetry: RetryCancelledBeforeRetransmission when allowsRetransmission is false. Token waits must stay before checkCancellation/beforeTransmission.
- Account-scoped sync abort. A deadline turns stalls into failures, and authenticatedRequest passes TokenManagerError through raw. MessageFetcher then puts every ID into permanentlyFailedIds (MessageFetcher.swift:180-208), the abandoned drain spends retryCount, and PendingActionProcessor spends retry budget. Map token failures to authenticationError or credentialsRevoked, as the 401 branch does, but keep CancellationError raw.

**Fix.** Three changes, in this order. (1) TokenRefreshCoordinator: the shared task clears its own entry when it ends, through a completion watcher that calls clearTask. Waiters can then leave early without leaving a finished entry behind for their generation. (2) refreshToken(): await the handle through one single-fire gate (the awaitValueUnlessCancelled / withDeadline pattern, never withTimeout). The gate resolves on the task's result, on caller cancellation (CancellationError), or on an injectable deadline of about 15 s (refreshFailed(URLError(.timedOut))). The shared refresh and its epoch-gated save keep running. (3) authenticatedRequest: map invalidCredentials to credentialsRevoked and other token errors to authenticationError, and pass CancellationError through raw. Leave out the cooldown, which would fail a send made just after connectivity returns, and the 401 same-token shortcut.

**First step.** Write the failing TokenManagerTests case with a refresher blocked in an uncancellable continuation. Then move clearTask out of refreshToken's waiter into a watcher that runs when the shared task ends, and make the waiter cancellation-aware.

**Pinning test.** TokenManagerTests, with a refresher blocked in an uncancellable continuation: a cancelled waiter throws CancellationError promptly, a second waiter still receives the token, and callCount stays 1. A 0.1 s deadline throws refreshFailed(timedOut). Add a Revert-check naming the waiter's cancellation gate.

**Payoff.** Behind a stalled token endpoint, sign-out, BGTask expiry and cancelSync unwind in seconds instead of up to about 3 minutes, and sends fail at 15 s. Token stalls no longer leave per-message sync verdicts or spend retry budgets.

## Store lifecycle and data-loss paths (12)

### `coredata-stack#2` · high · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**Any migration-class load error is an automatic, unconfirmed mailbox wipe, and its backup does not survive the launch**

Area: Core Data stack, store lifecycle and migrations. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Ten 1341xx codes, including 134100 and 134130 (what a store from a newer model raises), go to automatic migration recovery on the first failure, unless out-of-space or I/O is found in the error chain. The store is backed up, removed and reloaded empty. The same launch's restore then sees an empty store beside body files and runs `performDurableLocalCleanup`. That deletes bodies, attachments and every backup, and moves the mailbox start to now, so only about 5 minutes of mail comes back. The corrupt branch and the confirmed Reset Mailbox end in the same cascade.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataErrorClassifier.swift:49-59 — ten migration codes incl. NSMigrationMissingSourceModelError and NSPersistentStoreIncompatibleVersionHashError; :126-129 the unavailable/out-of-space check runs first, then migration maps to .migrationRecovery
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:278-279, :367-368 — migration recovery on the first error, then reload; CoreDataRecoveryHandler.swift:52/:64 backup then removeStore; CoreDataStack.swift:199-203 the code's own note that an older model would delete a newer store
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:598 — restore calls prepareLocalStoreForAuthenticatedAccount; :202-208 an Account-less store with HTML/attachment files counts as mailbox data; :1217-1219 sets resetRequired; :1237-1239 runs performDurableLocalCleanup
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1632 — resetCoreDataStore → CoreDataStack.swift:513 destroyAllData → :483-484 removeAllBackups; CoreDataBackupManager.swift:5-6 says nothing reads a backup back
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1657 — restartMailboxStartTime in the same cleanup; SyncTimeCalculator.swift:126-131 the initial sync starts at the start minus the buffer, which contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'ladder moves nothing and re-lists up to initialSyncMaxWindow'
- esc-chatmail/App/AppLoadingPolicy.swift:46, :50, :125-130 — the kept-store reset needs 5 counted failures and a confirmation promising 'download your mail again from Gmail', yet it reaches the same cascade

**Trigger.** The first launch, foreground or cold BGTask, after either of these: a migration that fails on a user's data (for example a constraint violation when a future v7 model adds a uniqueness constraint), or a build whose model is older than the store (a TestFlight build with a reverted model, a tester installing a previous build, a dev build over a daily-use install). Corruption and a confirmed Reset Mailbox also qualify, today and with any model.

**Impact.** The user opens to an empty mailbox that refills only from now on, with no notice. Queued PendingActions, reply drafts, unsent sends and local_ originals are gone. Gmail keeps the mail, but the app never loads anything older. The backup that the log message names is deleted in the same launch.

**Verifier.** All cited code was read; the cascade is traced through code, not run. Corrections:
- The out-of-space and I/O guard runs before the migration check, so a migration that fails for lack of space keeps the store.
- Losing the backup costs only a forensic copy: nothing restores one (scalability-review.md:1579 lists this as left).
- The cascade also follows corruption and the confirmed Reset Mailbox, so the five-failure path differs in being confirmed, not in outcome.
- The restore re-saves credentials (AuthSession.swift:1378), so the user stays signed in.
- No v7 exists yet.
