**Pinning test.** A suite on a SQLite `TestCoreDataStack` beside `SyncEngineStoreMaintenanceTests`. `runStoreMaintenanceIfDue(in:)` purges transactions older than the retention and keeps newer ones. A second call within 24 h purges nothing. A cancelled run leaves the key unmarked. Revert-check: the hygiene call.

**Payoff.** Persistent history stays bounded on devices where BGProcessing rarely runs, with no main-thread cost. A maintenance job that has stopped running shows up in the log; today nothing records it.

### `observability-errors#6` · low · reliability · effort M · new

**Core Data read failures are folded into 'absent' by try? outside the sync-cursor path**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The count is right: 40 `try? fetch/count` sites. But none of the named sites does real harm. A duplicate Person is a state the app already makes routinely and merges on every maintenance run. A failed Account read in setAccountHistoryId leaves the cursor frozen, which only costs a replay of history and never skips mail. Its log wrongly says "No account found". The cleanup `try?` sites are fallbacks that run only after a batch failure that was already logged. The list-conversation nil is handled fail-closed by its caller.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:63-69,83-89,101-108 — fetchPerson is `try? context.fetch(request).first`; findOrCreate inserts a new Person when it returns nil
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:394-404 — documents that duplicate Persons are already created routinely by the creation serializer; mergeDuplicatePersons collapses them, run as a maintenance pass at DataCleanupService.swift:346
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AccountPersister.swift:129-139 — `if let account = try? context.fetch(request).first` else logs "No account found to set history ID"; IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:443-446 calls it after stageClear, so on error the cursor stays at the older durable position
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:440-442 — nil on fetch error; caller at 165-172, 185-191, 216-217 treats nil as hasUnresolvedExistingAnchor and retains the send record for a later sync (fail-closed)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:75-78,104,159-161,172 — the silent `try?` returns are in fallbacks reached only after the batch path logged an error
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:41-47,117-124 — a failed Account read caches empty AccountAliases, which getAliases reuses without re-reading until a sync's refreshSendAsAliases calls setAliases (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1033-1053)

**Trigger.** A Core Data fetch error on an already-open SQLite store. The app sets no file protection of its own, so a locked device is not a cause. That leaves genuine I/O faults or corruption mid-session, which are very rare.

**Impact.** Mostly the diagnostics: logs that blame a missing row ("No account found") or say nothing. The other effects are re-work or self-healing: the history window is replayed, a duplicate Person lasts until the next maintenance merge, and a cleanup pass waits for the next run. The worst site the auditor did not name is AliasManager. A cold-cache read failure leaves an empty alias set in place until the next sync. A send made in that window can hash without excluding the user and fork the chat.

**Verifier.** I opened every cited site and the callers that decide what happens next. `fetchPerson` duplicates are already routine and repaired. The cursor failure goes in the safe direction (frozen, never advanced). One cited contrast is wrong: the helper at line 440 is fail-closed through its caller. `finalizeSync` has no callers. The convention really is per-site, and the misleading logs are real, so the issue stands but at low severity, as hygiene. AliasManager's stickiness is the only path I found that is user-visible, and the next sync clears it.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md, "Sync cursor and staging invariants": "A failed Core Data read is never 'absent'/'empty'" (stated for the cursor path only). docs/scalability-review.md root cause 8 (line 73); step 1 (line 1534) fixed only the attachment orphan sweep. No review item covers these sites.

**Invariant risks**

- PersonFactory: letting fetchPerson's error propagate looks safe, but saveParticipant catches the throw, logs it and moves on (MessagePersister+Participants.swift:58-67). The message would then be saved without that MessageParticipant row, and an update never recreates the rows (lines 70-72). That breaks the rule that a message must not be persisted as-is, and replies and re-homing read those rows. Today's outcome is a duplicate Person, which mergeDuplicatePersons collapses (DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:394-404).
- setAccountHistoryId must stay a stager into the caller's context, with no save of its own (CLAUDE.md lists it). It must throw before the orchestrator's own save so the existing catch blocks roll back the ModificationTracker and drop the advance plan (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:434-446 and 587-592, InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:262-264). A Core Data error must not be treated as an account-scoped abort or put IDs into a failure bucket.
- AliasManager.getAliases(from:) must stay non-throwing and keep its Core Data fallback. The optimistic send hashes with it inside the gate and the conversation turns (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:103-106). Do not make it throw, turn it into a cache-only read, or refuse a send when it returns empty.
- Flag-gated one-time passes must set their flag only after a successful read and save. Today a failed fetch latches them as done: the archive-model V1 migration sets its flag after the fetch fails (Migration.swift:23-26, 54), and the RFC 2047 repair's `?? []` loops then save no changes, which counts as success (Migration.swift:454-494, 513; NSManagedObjectContext+Perform.swift:12).

**Fix.** Fix site by site; do not bulk-convert. (1) Make setAccountHistoryId `async throws`: throw AccountPersisterError.fetchFailed on a fetch error, keep the no-row warning, and add `try` at its three stagers so the existing catch rolls back. Delete finalizeSync, which nothing calls. (2) The flag-gated passes (archive-model V1, RFC 2047 repair) set their flag only when every read succeeded. (3) AliasManager.loadFromCoreData returns nil on an error, logs it and caches nothing, so the next call reads again. (4) PersonFactory and the cleanup fallbacks keep their defaults and log with Log.error(error:). (5) Add a per-file ratchet on `try? …fetch/count`, built on a shared repository-source enumerator.

**First step.** Make setAccountHistoryId throw on an Account fetch error (keep the no-row warning), add `try` in IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:445,856 and InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:334, delete the uncalled finalizeSync, and pin it in AccountPersisterTests with EntityFetchFailingContext.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: a terminal-slice run whose sync context is EntityFetchFailingContext("Account") throws, leaves the durable historyId and continuation unchanged, and writes no lastSuccessfulSyncTime (Revert-check: setAccountHistoryId's `try`). AliasManagerTests: after a failed load, the next call reads again.

**Payoff.** The only live cursor-adjacent silent read and two migrations that latch on a failed read become explicit, logged failures. A sticky empty alias cache that can fork chats goes away, and new silent sites are caught.

## Silent mailbox correctness (16)

### `contacts-person#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Self-identity is taken from any Contacts card that lists the user's address: over-broad, fail-open and volatile, yet it decides routing, isFromMe and reply recipients**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

ContactsSelfAliasProvider adds to the self set every address on every card that lists the account or send-as address, with no rule for cards that belong to someone else. That set decides isFromMe, is removed before the participant hash, and is filtered out of reply recipients. The 6-hour maintenance repair re-hashes active chats with the current set. That heals forks, and it also merges a wrongly included person's chats permanently. isFromMe is never repaired. The fail-open half is real but rarely reached.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:92-104,119-137 — every address of every matched card is unioned (any intersecting card in the Gmail enumeration); a throwing query is skipped via try?/continue, and a failed enumeration is logged and returns a partial set
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:100-114,138-139 — the result joins the self set with no 'unreadable' case and no single-flight; the fingerprint (113) is stamped after the await (101); IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1035,1053 call setAliases every run, which reads Contacts again
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:366 — isFromMe = myAliases.contains(sender); esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationIdentity.swift:75-88 — aliases are removed before hashing, and an empty remainder becomes the note-to-self identity keyed on myAliases.sorted().first
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ReplyMetadataBuilder.swift:107-118 — userAliases join userAddresses, which usableRecipients filters out of conversation and target recipients
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:87-92,226-262 — maintenance re-hashes with the current AliasManager set and merges active chats that share a hash; isFromMe is rewritten only on refetch (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:261)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactLinkedAddresses.swift:101-110 — the link code expects a card that lists a user address beside its owner's and refuses to treat either as the other; esc-chatmailTests/Sync/ContactsSelfAliasProviderTests.swift:7,30 — the only two tests, and neither uses a foreign card

**Trigger.** A Contacts card that lists one of the user's account or send-as addresses beside someone else's address: a household card for a shared Gmail account, or a company card that lists colleagues next to the user's work send-as address. Less often: a read that throws while access is authorized, or Contacts access still undecided during the first sync.

**Impact.** The other person's mail is stored as isFromMe (drawn as the user's own bubbles). Their one-to-one mail goes to note-to-self, and their group mail goes to a chat without them. Replies leave them out without any notice, because the reply row computes "differs" after the same filter. Maintenance then merges their existing active chats into note-to-self or other chats for good. When Contacts are unreadable, forwarded-alias mail forks into a separate chat until the 6-hour repair, and its isFromMe stays wrong.

**Verifier.** I confirmed every cited line. Corrections: a repair does exist (6-hour maintenance re-hashes active chats with the current set), but it makes the over-broad case permanent by merging chats. Denied access returning an empty set matches how the link store drops its map, so that part is not a defect. The fail-open path needs a throwing read while authorized, which nobody has observed. The feature is deliberate (commit 1bc11d9e), but its admission rule is written down nowhere and contradicts the documented rule in ContactLinkedAddresses. Trigger frequency is inferred, not observed.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1310-1335 `self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist` (only the cost side; still open: AliasManager.swift:71-77 still recomputes on every call) and Suggested order step 13 (line 1626, not built). The correctness defect itself is not covered there. CLAUDE.md "One chat per contact" and ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:15-33 describe the adopt-persist-repair path that the fix should reuse.

**Invariant risks**

- Hash parity. The self set is removed before every participant hash and is the key of note-to-self (`myAliases.sorted().first`, ConversationIdentity.swift:75-88). Narrowing it with no scoped repair forks chats, and that repair must hash with the same set routing uses (DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:87-92, DataCleanupService.swift:136-139).
- Single adoption point and cold-launch parity. ContactLinkedAddressStore adopts only inside the cleanup-sensitive hold and keeps the map in defaults (ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:15-21). A Contacts self set that is read live or kept only in memory gets re-adopted mid-run and is lost on a cold launch. Optimistic hashing must keep `getAliases(from: viewContext)` and its Core Data fallback. AliasManagerTests.swift:68-114 pin the live recompute and must be rewritten on purpose.
- Account boundary. AliasManager holds account-scoped state outside the participant contract. AuthSession invalidates it before the durable cleanup (AuthSession.swift:873,1787), yet the awaits at AliasManager.swift:45 and :101 then re-cache the old account's Account-row aliases. Any value the fix persists must be device-level card data, combined with the current Account row when read.
- Repairing isFromMe changes an input of RichContentVerdictResolver, the own-row preview and verdict paths, and the rollups. It has to be a background-context write inside ConversationRollupMutationSerializer that re-stamps the verdict. Merges already made stay merged, which is Kevin's recorded design call, so the fix must not try to un-merge.

**Fix.** Stop AliasManager reading Contacts. In ContactLinkedAddressStore's single refreshIfNeeded read, also adopt a self-candidate record: multi-address cards none of whose addresses appears on any other card (single-address cards counted), plus the Mac Me card. It is persisted; an unreadable read keeps it and withdrawn access drops it. AliasManager then unions the Account email and send-as with the candidate card containing one of them, synchronously, keyed on the store's adoption revision. It gains an invalidation generation around loadFromCoreData, and setAliases becomes a no-op when nothing changed. unifyConversationsByContactIfNeeded adds changed self addresses to its scoped repair, and a one-time active-scope repair covers the switch. ContactLinkedAddresses' link rules stay as they are; repairing isFromMe is a separate, later step.

**First step.** Write the self-candidate rule as a pure function over card address lists, next to ContactLinkedAddresses, with unit tests for a household card, a company card listing colleagues beside the send-as, the user's own card, and Gmail dot variants. Do not wire it yet.

**Pinning test.** Give a ContactLinkedAddressStore stub cards {me, spouse} and {spouse, spouse@work}. AliasManager.getAliases must exclude spouse, read no Contacts, and keep its set after the loader returns nil. Its Revert-check names the exclusive-card rule.

**Payoff.** Another person's mail stops turning into the user's own bubbles or note-to-self, replies stop silently dropping them, and the Contacts re-query on every persist, an open scalability item, goes away.

### `gap-message-shape-extremes#3` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Three MIME classifiers disagree: sync keeps only the first HTML part, recovery keeps a different one, and body parts become attachment rows**

Area: Message structure the sender controls, beyond HTML: recipients, MIME tree, part and attachment counts. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Sync's content walk keeps the first non-empty text/html and text/plain part it finds. Later text parts in a multipart/mixed are still decoded, or fetched, and then thrown away, so a body split around an inline attachment keeps only its first segment. Both the stored HTML and the bubble come from that segment. Recovery picks the single highest-scored HTML part, which can be a different segment. extractAttachments turns every non-multipart part with an attachmentId into a queued Attachment row, body parts included, although the comment above the call says they are excluded.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:424-431, 486-493 — mergeMissing keeps the first non-nil html/plainText; the loop goes on calling extract (decode or fetch) on later siblings until both are set, then drops their results
- esc-chatmailTests/Sync/MessageProcessorTests.swift:1271-1333 — Apple Mail fixture: multipart/mixed [text/plain, inline image0.jpeg, text/plain] shows the split shape occurs; only an empty trailing part is pinned
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleContentSource.swift:20-31 with MessageBubbleLoader+CompatibilityContent.swift:267 — the bubble uses stored HTML whenever it yields text; bodyText (full plain alternative) is consulted only when HTML yields none
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:346-358, 741-750 — recovery collects every HTML part and keeps one, the best-scored; it runs as Method 4 (HTMLContentLoader.swift:287-288) only when no stored HTML is usable
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:101-103, 1083-1096 — comment claims body parts are excluded; traverse makes any non-multipart part with an attachmentId an AttachmentInfo (filename falls back to attachment.<ext>)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:320 — new rows are stateRaw "queued", which the post-sync sweep downloads (AttachmentDownloader.swift:576-577)

**Trigger.** An Apple Mail or iOS Mail message with authored text after an inline attachment: plain [text/plain, image, text/plain], or HTML split [text/html, attachment, text/html] inside multipart/mixed. Phantom attachment: any body text part that Gmail returns with an attachmentId.

**Impact.** Text after the first inline attachment is missing from the stored body, the bubble, chatPreviewText and the reader. Nothing shows that text was lost, and nothing in the app re-derives it. A body restored by recovery can be a different segment than the synced one. A body part served by attachmentId becomes an 'attachment.html' or '.txt' card, and the post-sync sweep downloads it again.

**Verifier.** I read every cited line and found no guard. git show 2f095fc8 shows the line-101 comment was added with no code to exclude body parts. Narrowing: when the first HTML segment yields no text, the bubble falls back to bodyText. Recovery runs only when no stored HTML is usable, and it schedules a verdict refresh. The phantom half depends on Gmail serving body parts by attachmentId, which I did not verify. If the 25KB premise held, newsletters would routinely show such cards and no fix for that is in the history, so it is probably rare. The golden corpus has 0 of 82 inputs with two text/html parts.

**Invariant risks**

- Body-materialization contract (CLAUDE.md, MessageProcessor bullet; MessageProcessor.swift:28-38, 744-772): a planned continuation segment's fetch must still throw on a transient error and drop only on 404 or an undecodable response. If concatenation swallows a failed segment, a truncated body is stored and the cursor still advances. Recovery stays best-effort (HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:622-635).
- Pinned choices a 'concatenate every text sibling' rule breaks. MessageProcessorTests.swift:211-255 keeps a trailing multipart/mixed text/plain part (TRAILING_GENERATED_TOKEN) out of the body, so list footers and disclaimers stay out. HTMLContentRecoveryServiceTests.swift:298-341 and 392-431 pin skipping empty or hidden-only HTML alternatives. Which trailing parts count as body is Kevin's call.
- The attachment rule 'non-text type = attachment' would drop filename-less text/calendar parts, which drive the invite and reservation cards (Attachment+Extensions.swift:65-77, AttachmentDisplayFiltering.swift:84-91). hasAttachments, which counts any attachmentId, is also the bubble's trigger to recover HTML for a body-less row (MessageBubbleLoader+CompatibilityContent.swift:201-205). Do not recompute it from the new classifier.
- Bumping richContentVerdictEpoch is wrong here. It is for a resolver that answers differently on the same stored state (CacheVersioning.swift:19-36), and new rows are stamped at persist time (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:164-173). A bump marks every verdict unknown and re-runs the S2 backfill. The golden corpus has no MIME-tree category and is web's contract, so MIME fixtures belong in XCTest.

**Fix.** Do it in two steps. First, in extractAttachments.traverse, skip non-multipart text/plain and text/html parts that isAttachmentContentPart rejects. Keep text/calendar and every part with a filename or an attachment disposition. Leave checkForAttachments and hasAttachments as they are, and do not repair existing rows. Second, write one pure, nonisolated MIME body planner that does no I/O and serves both MessageProcessor.extractContent and HTMLContentRecoveryService. Rules: alternative picks one child (keeping recovery's meaningful-candidate rule), related takes its root, and mixed appends a text sibling only after an inline-disposition attachment. Each caller fetches the planned segments under its own error contract. HTML segments are spliced into the first segment's body before canonicalContent, with a cap on segment count and bytes. Bump nothing.

**First step.** In MessageProcessorLargeBodyFetchTests, add three tests: a filename-less text/plain body served by attachmentId yields no AttachmentInfo, hasAttachments stays true, and a filename-less text/calendar part stays an attachment. Then add the skip clause in extractAttachments.traverse.

**Pinning test.** MessageProcessorTests: alternative[text/plain, mixed[html SEG_A, inline PDF, html SEG_B]] stores both tokens in storedHTML. The same payload in HTMLContentRecoveryServiceTests recovers both. Large filename-less body: no AttachmentInfo. Revert-check: the planner, the traverse skip.

**Payoff.** Apple and iOS Mail messages with text after an attachment show in full. Synced and recovered bodies agree. No more phantom attachment.html or .txt cards or second downloads, and no discarded sibling fetches blocking the cursor.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#2` · high · security · effort M · new

**Address extraction takes the first <address> anywhere, including inside a quoted display name**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

EmailNormalizer.extractEmail tries the angle-bracket regex first and returns its leftmost match. Nothing skips a quoted display-name phrase, so for `"Boss <boss@corp.example>" <x@attacker.example>` it returns boss@corp.example. The raw From value goes through this function for isFromMe, senderEmail, the From MessageParticipant row and the participant hash, so the message lands in Boss's existing chat as Boss's bubble. Putting the user's own address inside the quotes makes isFromMe true. The domain-trust checks for preview cards read the same wrong address, and web uses the identical regex.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/EmailNormalizer.swift:39-41,52-57 — the bracket regex `<((?:"…"|[^<>"])+@[^<>]+)>` runs first and `firstMatch` (leftmost) wins. A quoted string is consumed only inside the brackets, never skipped in the phrase before them.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:363-367 — `processedHeaders.from = header.value` (raw), then `isFromMe = myAliases.contains(normalizedEmail(extractEmail(from: header.value)))`. From is not split with the quote-aware EmailAddressListParser that To/Cc use (line 407).
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Creation.swift:108,125-128 — `message.isFromMe` is copied from the header result, and `senderEmail` is set from `extractEmail(from: from)`.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:271-274 — the From MessageParticipant row and its Person are keyed on `extractEmail(from: headerValue)`, with the name from `extractDisplayName` ("Boss").
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationManager.swift:267-269 with ConversationIdentity.swift:177-178 — the raw From value is passed to makeConversationIdentity, which hashes `extractEmail(from: headerValue)`.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/Shared/PreviewTextUtilities.swift:31,45-48 — the domain-trust check, whose comment says it rejects display-name forgeries, runs extractEmail and so trusts the quoted address's domain.

**Trigger.** A received message whose From display name is a quoted string containing `<addr>`, for example `"Boss <boss@corp.example>" <x@attacker.example>`. This is legal RFC 5322, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC align on attacker.example. The app parses the raw header value it receives from Gmail. Whether Gmail's spam filter catches such a message, or rewrites the header, was not checked.

**Impact.** The message is routed into the impersonated contact's existing chat (the participant hash is the contact's), shown under that contact's name and avatar, and its From row names the contact. With the user's own address inside the quotes, the bubble is drawn as sent by the user, in note-to-self or in any chat the Cc set names. Preview cards keyed on the sender's domain (transactional, App Store, GitHub/Netlify) treat the forged domain as trusted. By default a reply goes to the impersonated address. Every scale is affected, on iOS, Mac and web.

**Verifier.** The code is as described. I ran the identical JS regex (web normalizeEmail.ts:97) with node: it returned boss@corp.example and me@gmail.com for the two shapes. I found no guard: CLAUDE.md and the docs record no decision about this, EmailNormalizerTests has no case with an address inside the quoted name, and MessageFormatBuilder.swift:191-193 protects only its own forward-formatting path by requiring exactly one '<'. Separately, To and Cc tokens re-serialized as `\"name <email>\"` (ConversationManager.swift:272, MessagePersister+Participants.swift:27) reopen the same injection through an RFC 2047-decoded name.

**Invariant risks**

- The participant hash is canonical, and the golden corpus pins it on iOS and web, so the Swift and TS parsers must change in one PR. No existing corpus case puts a bracketed address inside a quoted name, so every existing hash must stay byte-identical. A real sender writing `"Name <a> via X" <b>` gets new mail keyed on b, which splits its chat once. Do not add a hash re-key pass or bump the conversation-name refresh key.
- isEmailAddressShapedDisplayName, which PersonDisplayNameResolver uses, depends on extractEmail finding an address anywhere in free text (EmailNormalizer.swift:367-369). DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:551 requires a key bump whenever that predicate changes. Route it through the new quote- and comment-aware parser and names like `Acme (support@acme.com)` stop being hidden. Keep the old anywhere-in-text regex for that predicate.
- The sites at MessagePersister+Participants.swift:27,35,43 and ConversationManager.swift:272,277 rebuild `name <email>` from names that sanitizeDisplayName has already RFC 2047-decoded and stripped of quotes. A fix that skips quoted strings but keeps the first match therefore still lets an encoded `=3Cboss@…=3E` in a To/Cc name replace the real recipient, both in the participant rows and in the hash. Pass email and name as separate values there.
- Whole-header callers expect the first mailbox: MessageProcessor.swift:365 (From → isFromMe) and :289-290 (Reply-To mismatch, a newsletter-score signal), plus the persister's sender. A rule of 'last angle-addr in the whole string' would switch multi-mailbox values to the last one. Messages already stored are not healed: no raw From is kept. The update path (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:261,339) rewrites senderEmail and isFromMe but not the From row or the conversation, so a refetched forgery ends up with its fields disagreeing.

**Fix.** In one PR, add one pure scanner to EmailNormalizer.swift and to web normalizeEmail.ts. For each token it skips quoted strings and comments in the name part (backslash escapes allowed), restarts at a nested '<' as today, and takes the last complete angle-addr. If a quote or comment never closes, take the last angle-addr seen before it opened, otherwise the last bracketed match, never the first. extractEmail returns the first address-yielding token from EmailAddressListParser. extractDisplayName ends at that same '<', so an embedded address stays in the name and is hidden. Leave isEmailAddressShapedDisplayName on the old regex. Make makeConversationIdentity split with addressTokens, and stop rebuilding To/Cc strings: pass email and name as separate values.

**First step.** Add failing conversationIdentityCases to golden_message_corpus.json: the quoted-Boss From, the same From with the user's alias inside the quotes, an unclosed-quote form and a comment form. Confirm that ConversationIdentityTests and participantSet.test.ts fail before changing either parser.

**Pinning test.** Corpus cases that expect participants [x@attacker.example] on both platforms. Swift persister test: a forged From quoting the user's alias gives isFromMe false and attacker in both senderEmail and the From row. A To name holding encoded `<boss@…>` keeps the real recipient.

**Payoff.** New mail can no longer land in an impersonated contact's chat, show a forged "from me" bubble, or pass sender-domain trust checks with a forged domain on iOS, Mac and web. It also makes iOS production routing match the corpus.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#3` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**Quoted-printable is decoded by guesswork in five copies, and again on stored text at display time**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

The Swift code has five transfer-decoding copies: ingest, recovery, raw source, and two display-time normalizers. The raw-source copy decodes only when a header names the encoding. The other four can decode by guessing. Both display normalizers run on the stored bodyText every time a message is shown. They QP-decode it with no header whenever the text contains "=\n", "=3d", "=3c" or "=3e", in any case. Once that fires, the decoder turns every "=" plus two hex digits into a raw byte and removes every "=" at the end of a line, joining it to the next. Ingest already decoded any part labelled QP, and left parts labelled 7bit, 8bit or base64 as they were. So the display pass either decodes a second time or decodes text that was never encoded.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentLoader+PlainTextHTML.swift:23-30,65-72 — normalizedPlainTextFallback QP-decodes bodyText when looksQuotedPrintable matches (=\r\n, =\n, =3d, =3c, =3e), with no header input
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/CanonicalEmailContentLoader.swift:94,410-417,447-454 — every canonical load normalizes bodyText through the same header-less guess; its result becomes CanonicalEmailContent.plainText
- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/QuotedPrintableDecoder.swift:8,19-45 — removes every =\n, decodes every =XX hex pair to a raw byte, then String(decoding:as: UTF8) (invalid bytes become U+FFFD)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:861-870 — ingest decodes only when the header says QP or no header exists; a part labelled 7bit/8bit/base64 is stored as is, and the display pass decodes it anyway
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/OriginalEmailSourceLoader.swift:498-525 — the reader's native plain-text presentation is canonicalContent.plainText; esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageContentView.swift:353-361 — any row with non-empty bodyText opens the reader when its bubble is tapped
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader+CompatibilityContent.swift:267-268 — the bubble uses bodyTextFallback, which has no QP pass, so bubble and reader show different text

**Trigger.** A received plain-text-only message whose decoded text has a line ending in "=". That includes Markdown or RST "=====" heading underlines, "=====" separator lines, a URL token with base64 "=" padding at the end of a line, inline-PGP armor, and "x =". It also fires on any "=3c", "=3d" or "=3e" in the text. The user then taps the bubble to open the reader.

**Impact.** The reader shows wrong text while the bubble beside it is correct. In links, "?id=12345" becomes "?id" plus U+0012 plus "345", and "?token=Ab…" gets U+FFFD, so reset and verification links break. Underline and separator lines are joined to the line that follows. The rows themselves are not changed. The preview pipeline also reads the normalized text (EmailPreviewSourceLoader.swift:204-213), so the plain-text alternatives of HTML mail are affected too. If Gmail also removes QP from format=full bodies, ingest double-decodes every part labelled QP. Nothing in the repo shows which way Gmail behaves, so that case is not counted.

**Verifier.** I read every cited site and the decoder, then followed the path to the screen: a bubble tap opens the reader whenever bodyText exists, and the plain-text path uses the normalized text. I found no guard, no header input, no comment, no test and no CLAUDE.md or docs entry that makes the display-time guess a deliberate choice. It came in with 194b49ba, after ingest decoding (6c9cb028). One correction: RawEmailSourceSanitizer.swift:264-276 decodes only when a header says so, so four copies guess, not five. The trigger is broader than claimed, because ordinary "=====" lines set it off.

**Invariant risks**

- Do not 'align' the reader by adding a QP pass to the bubble path (MessageBubbleContentSource/ChatBubbleTextProcessor, which RichContentVerdictResolver reads): it changes verdict inputs, forcing a richContentVerdictEpoch bump, and breaks ChatPreviewRepair.backfilledPreview parity with the loader.
- processGmailMessage's throw contract: malformed or refused QP must stay a pure, non-throwing outcome. A thrown error becomes a blocking per-message failure that freezes the history cursor until the message is abandoned.
- The golden corpus is shared with web/: corpus.golden.test.ts replays rawSourceHTMLRecoveryCases, and web/src/mime/decode.ts:129-156 mirrors MessageProcessor's sniff. Fixture edits trigger web CI and drift unless decode.ts changes in the same PR, so pin this in Swift unit tests.
- Legacy rows: ingest decoded no QP before 6c9cb028 (2026-02-01). If Gmail returns QP undecoded, a retained pre-February row loses its decoding in the reader (the bubble already shows such rows raw). Accept that, or heal those rows once with a strict-form check, never with the loose sniff.

**Fix.** Make one shared TransferEncodingDecoder and route MessageProcessor, HTMLContentRecoveryService and RawEmailSourceSanitizer through it. It decodes QP only when the part's header names it: an absent header means 7bit per RFC 2045, and raw-source blobs decode by their own part headers. Until a capture settles Gmail's format=full contract, skip decoding when the text proves it is already decoded (an '=' followed by neither two hex digits nor a line break) and log a Log.diagnostic. If Gmail decodes, drop the header branch. Fold both display normalizers into one shared function without the QP pass, keeping the entity and whitespace steps. Leave the bubble path, RichContentVerdictResolver and the CacheVersioning epochs untouched.

**First step.** Write the failing pins first. normalizedMeaningfulPlainText must keep '?id=12345' and a '=====' underline. A header-less text/plain part embedding QP raw source must keep '?v=1712345678'. Then capture one format=full response for QP mail sent from Gmail web.

**Pinning test.** A pure PlainTextBodyNormalizer test: a reset link '?id=12345&token=Ab', a '=====' underline and an own-sent 'x =' line survive. In MessageProcessorTests: embedded QP raw source keeps '?v=1712345678'; QP-labelled data containing '="' stays verbatim. Revert-check: looksQuotedPrintable.

**Payoff.** The reader, previews and quality fallback show the bubble's text. '=XX' query values stop breaking reset links. Embedded raw source stops being decoded twice at ingest.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#4` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Multi-part HTML bodies keep one fragment, chosen by different rules in sync and recovery**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Sync's MIME walk keeps the first text/html and the first text/plain it finds (mergeMissing). Later siblings in a multipart/mixed are dropped, and HTML always beats the text/plain alternative. So when a client splits the body around an inline attachment, the text after it is missing from the body file, chatPreviewText, the snippet and the reader. In plain-only mail it is missing from bodyText too. Recovery instead keeps the HTML part with the most visible text. After a lost body file, the reader can show a different fragment than the stored bubble preview.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:424-431 — mergeMissing sets html/plainText only while nil, so the first fragment wins
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:486-493 — the multipart loop merges children in order; a later text/html sibling is never appended
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:72-85,520-528 — htmlBody, cleanedSnippet, chatPreviewText and the canonical HTML all come from that first fragment, and any HTML beats the full text/plain
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:346-358,725-760 — recovery collects every HTML part and keeps the top score, which visible-text length dominates
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader.swift:84-132 — the bubble shows the stored chatPreviewText; OriginalEmailSourceLoader.swift:364-369 and CanonicalEmailContentLoader.swift:96-111,233-239 have the reader read the HTML file or recover it when missing
- esc-chatmailTests/Sync/MessageProcessorTests.swift:1177-1269,1271-1345 — Mac Apple Mail images come as multipart/related with a cid and one HTML part (not split); an iPhone-shaped multipart/mixed {text/plain, image0.jpeg inline, text/plain} exists but is pinned only for an empty trailing fragment

**Trigger.** The body is split into sibling text parts around an inline attachment, with words after it. Typical cases: an iPhone Mail message with a photo placed mid-body, or an Apple Mail non-image attachment placed inline. The fragment divergence needs a missing body file: a restore, since Messages is excluded from backups, or another loss, followed by opening the reader.

**Impact.** Words after the attachment never appear in the bubble, the list preview or the reader. bodyText keeps them only when a text/plain alternative exists; in plain-only fragmented mail they never reach the store. After recovery, the reader can show the longer fragment, for example a trailing 'Sent from my iPhone' instead of a short message. Meanwhile the bubble keeps the first fragment's stored preview, and the rich-content verdict is re-stamped against the recovered fragment.

**Verifier.** I read both extractors, their callers and the bubble/reader routing in full. No guard, repair or documented decision covers split bodies. I found no concatenation anywhere, and the docs do not mention it. Corrections: Mac Apple Mail photos are not split (the repo's own multipart/related test shows a single HTML part with a cid). The same first-wins rule also drops later text/plain fragments, which the finding left out. The reader shows the first fragment in normal operation too. How often this happens in real mail was not measured.

**Invariant risks**

- Body-materialization throw contract (CLAUDE.md, MessageProcessor.swift:28-38, 744-772): sharing recovery's fetch policy, which turns every error into nil (HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:628-635), would let sync persist a partial body behind an advancing cursor. Each joined fragment must still throw on a transient failure, and only a 404 or an undecodable response may drop that one fragment.
- Rich-content verdict and preview inputs: a placeholder for the attachment (an <img> or text) in the stored HTML would change what RichContentVerdictResolver and chatPreviewText read, so ordinary iPhone photo mail would flip from a bubble to a card. storedHTML has to stay the one string that is saved, pre-classified (richContentPrerun) and previewed. Bumping chatPreviewDerivationVersion or richContentVerdictEpoch (CacheVersioning.swift:17,36) would run a pass over every row at S2 and heal nothing, because the local HTML is still the first fragment.
- Recovery's pinned candidate rules (HTMLContentRecoveryServiceTests:298-431): it skips empty and hidden-only parts and HTML file attachments, prefers MIME HTML over embedded raw source, and fetches no non-text attachment. Swapping its scoring for sync's first-wins rule, or for an unconditional 'last alternative' (which can pick text/x-amp-html or text/watch-html), breaks these. Any new fetch must also sit inside recovery's isCurrent re-checks.
- Joining too much: concatenating multipart/related siblings (they are resources, per RFC 2387), a Mailman text/plain footer after an alternative, or an inline message/rfc822 changes previews for list mail. Separately, web/src/mime/parse.ts:339-349 mirrors the first-wins merge, so a MIME case in the golden corpus triggers web CI, which allows zero warnings, and needs a matching web change.

**Fix.** Extract a pure shared MIME body extractor holding the duplicated helpers, with fetch injected and the failure policy chosen by the caller: sync throws on transient failures, recovery swallows them. Add one rule. When a multipart/mixed has two or more leaf parts of the same text type as direct children, separated by attachment parts, join them in order. Plain text joins with a blank line. HTML joins by appending each later fragment's <body> children to the first fragment's body. Insert no placeholders, and skip fragments that are empty or have nothing visible. Keep every other shape, and the choice within multipart/alternative, as today. Sync uses this in extract(from:). Recovery tries it first and keeps its scored fallback. The change is forward-only: bump no version, and rows heal when the update path refetches them.

**First step.** Capture scrubbed Gmail format=full payloads for both shapes: an iPhone photo placed mid-body, and a Mac Apple Mail PDF placed inline mid-body. Learn whether the HTML fragments are whole documents, then add them to MessageProcessorTests as failing fixtures.

**Pinning test.** MessageProcessorTests: {plain A, inline jpeg, plain B} keeps A then B in plainTextBody and chatPreviewText. alternative{plain, mixed{html A, pdf, html B}} stores A then B once, with no placeholder. Recovering that payload equals storedHTML. A transient failure fetching B throws.

**Payoff.** Words written after an inline photo or attachment reach the bubble, the list preview, the reader and bodyText. A recovered body then matches what sync stored, so the reader stops showing a different fragment.

### `gap-wall-clock-time#1` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**A fast device clock lets history recovery skip mail for good and turns off the missed-message check**

Area: The device's wall clock is the only clock: clock changes, skew and time zones. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The mechanism is real. lastSuccessfulSyncTime is stamped from the device's Date(). History recovery lists `after:` that stamp minus 10 min, and recovery's config has no maxWindow, so nothing clamps the floor to now. If the clock was F fast at the last sync, recovery skips mail from the last real sync to F−10 min after it. A clean listing then moves the cursor to the pre-scan profile historyId and stamps a fresh time, so nothing lists the gap again. Reconciliation's floor (stamp − 5 min) loses the first F−5 min after each sync.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncTimeCalculator.swift:58-64,104-121 — historyRecovery has maxWindow nil; the last-sync branch returns lastSuccessfulSync − primaryBuffer, raised only by the install floor and never clamped to now
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:317-321 — recordResolvedProgress writes Date().timeIntervalSince1970 to lastSuccessfulSyncTimeKey
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:927-947 — the recovery window comes from that stamp and is frozen; :851-856 clears the window and sets the cursor to profile.historyId; :893 commit(advancePlan) re-stamps the time
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:126-141,492-506 — the missed-message query is `after:` calculateStartDate(.reconciliation), which is stamp − 300 s; a negative timeSinceStart only falls back to the 100-message minimum
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncTimeCalculator.swift:182 and IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:955-959 — only the no-stamp install branch clamps to now
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor.swift:50-79 — fetch IDs come only from messagesAdded, so a later label change on a gap message never fetches it; the only listings are initial sync, recovery and reconciliation

**Trigger.** The device clock is more than 10 min fast at the last successful sync. iOS and macOS set the time automatically by default, so this takes a clock set by hand, for example set ahead on purpose or moved for a game. A Gmail history expiry must follow (usually a week or more with no sync). The narrowed reconciliation applies to every sync while the clock is more than 5 min fast, and finds nothing when syncs are closer together than F−5 min.

**Impact.** Mail whose server time falls in the first F−10 min after the last sync before the absence never appears in the app (Gmail still has it). For the common habit of setting a clock 10–15 min ahead, that window is 0–5 min. Only a clock that is hours or days off loses a large span. The weaker missed-message check matters only if Gmail's history drops a record. Both are uncommon conditions, so this is medium, not high.

**Verifier.** Every cited line is as described. I found no clock-change observer, no use of server time, and no other listing that would cover the gap. A history label change on a gap message does not trigger a fetch. Neither CLAUDE.md nor the docs record skew as an accepted cost. I lowered the severity because the trigger needs a hand-set clock plus a week-long absence, and with the typical small skew the loss window is minutes. Clamping to device now would not help while the clock is still fast; server time would.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:228 (history-recovery-window-install-fallback review correction: .historyRecovery stays uncapped and frozen); clock skew itself is not covered anywhere

**Invariant risks**

- performRetryingRequest also carries messages.send (allowsRetransmission false). A Date-header hook that throws or changes how a send's outcome is classified there is a duplicate-send hazard. Record only on non-send 2xx responses, and never throw.
- History recovery is deliberately uncapped and frozen at its first attempt (scalability-review.md:228; IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:919-947). Add no maxWindow or now-based floor, and never re-derive the window on resume. The fix may only lower `after:` floors (min of device and server time), never raise them.
- lastSuccessfulSyncTime is written only in SyncFailureTracker.commit after the final save, to the injected defaults the orchestrator and reconciliation share. Do not persist the offset in UserDefaults.standard (real in the Mac test host). Do not reroute SyncClock.now(), which paces the drain and FakeSyncClock tests.
- The mailbox start moves only at AuthSession's two sites, never over a retained store: clamp it on read. A per-sync newest-received fetch in reconciliation would be a new hot Message fetch that needs a ScaleQueryPlanTests plan.

**Fix.** Add an in-memory ServerClockEstimate (lock-guarded, anchored on ContinuousClock): GmailAPIClient.performRetryingRequest records a 2xx response's HTTP Date only when behavior.allowsRetransmission, never throwing. Expose conservativeNow() = min(Date(), estimate ?? Date()). Use it, injected with a .shared default, in three places: the lastSuccessfulSyncTime stamp in SyncFailureTracker.recordResolvedProgress; the `now` SyncTimeCalculator caps with, also clamping stamp and install to it on read (the reconciliation path too); and newestReceivedInternalDate's `<= now` filter. Rule: every `after:` floor may only move earlier than today; never replace device time outright or cap recovery. A read-time clamp alone fixes nothing: a week later the fast stamp is already past.

**First step.** Add a ServerTimeSource protocol with a fake for tests and inject it into SyncFailureTracker. Then write the failing IncrementalSyncCursorTests case (server 2 h behind the device: a clean run, then a history expiry) before touching GmailAPIClient.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: fake server clock 2 h behind the device; a clean run then a history expiry must list `after:` ≤ server-time last sync − 600 (Revert-check: recordResolvedProgress's conservativeNow). StubURLProtocol test: a send's malformed Date header changes nothing.

**Payoff.** Closes the path where a hand-set fast clock permanently hides mail after a history expiry, and restores the missed-message window, while no `after:` floor can ever move later.

### `sync-engine#1` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**History-expiry recovery only adds mail: deletions and label changes from the gap are never reconciled, and the new cursor skips them for good**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The mechanism holds. When history.list returns 404, performSync's catch runs performHistoryRecoverySync, which lists `after:<lastSuccessfulSyncTime - 600 s> -label:spam -label:drafts -label:trash`, upserts what is listed and stamps the pre-scan profile historyId. Rows stored before that window are never visited, so label changes and deletions made elsewhere during the gap are lost for them. Mail that arrived during the gap is fetched with its current labels. The only non-history label repair covers at most 100 messages dated within 24 hours. No doc records this as a decision.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:543-583 — the catch for APIError.historyIdExpired calls performHistoryRecoverySync and returns; the reconciliation phase (384-404) sits in the do block the 404 aborted
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:746-788, 851-856 — recovery is one MessageListPaginator.fetchAndProcess whose handler only calls saveMessages, then setAccountHistoryId(profile.historyId); the comment at 716-721 says a skipped span is one of 'never repairing their deletions/labels'
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncTimeCalculator.swift:58-64, 205-207 — the recovery window starts at last sync minus 600 s, uncapped; the query is `after:<start> -label:spam -label:drafts -label:trash`
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:576-583, 675 — label reconciliation lists `after:<now - 86400>` with maxResults 100 and discards the next page token; line 675 is the only caller of getMessageMetadata in the app
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor+MessageDeletions.swift:5-8, 33 — remotely deleted mail is removed locally only from history records; the comment calls a cursor advanced past unapplied deletions 'permanent ghosts'
- docs/scalability-review.md:1652 — the prior review checked only recovery's cost ('does not normally re-list the mailbox'); nothing in it or CLAUDE.md accepts unreconciled labels or deletions

**Trigger.** A device that does not sync for longer than Gmail keeps history for its cursor (Google documents about a week or more; not measured), then syncs. That is the Mac app after a week or more closed or asleep, since it syncs only while running, or an iPhone where neither the app nor background refresh ran for that long. It matters only where mail already stored on that device was archived, read, un-archived, trashed, marked spam or deleted elsewhere during the gap.

**Impact.** Those pre-gap rows keep their old state with no error. Conversations archived elsewhere stay in the list, unread badges stay, and trashed, spam or permanently deleted mail stays in its chat. Nothing repairs this later. Read state heals when the chat is opened and inbox state when the conversation is archived again on this device; a grep found no action that writes TRASH, so deleted mail has no local remedy. The stale set is the mail changed elsewhere during the gap, so it does not grow from S1 to S3.

**Verifier.** Read the orchestrator, SyncReconciliation, SyncTimeCalculator and the paginator whole; listMessages and getMessageMetadata have no other callers. Mechanism holds. Changed: scope narrowed to rows stored before the gap (gap arrivals are fetched with current labels); the lastSuccessfulSyncTime point dropped, since it concerns missed arrivals, not this; severity lowered because the stale set is small, no server data is lost and it partly self-heals. Gmail's retention was not measured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1652 (recovery was checked for cost only). Related item still open: history-recovery-no-checkpoint (lines 360-376); step 8 at line 1603 has no Built note.

**Invariant risks**

- Optimistic and ledger rows. A diff of local rows against remote rows also picks up optimistic rows, which carry local UUID ids (OutboundSendDeliveryState.localOptimisticMessageID), and retained Not-sent replies. A metadata GET on one of those returns 404, and deleting on 404 would delete the user's unsent mail. Deferred and abandoned ledger IDs already have owners (the re-scan and the drain), so this pass must leave them alone.
- Account-scoped aborts and cancellation. SyncReconciliation.fetchGmailMetadataInParallel (SyncReconciliation.swift:687-692) treats auth and quota errors as transient and keeps sending requests. reconcileLabelStatesWithDiagnostics (627) swallows CancellationError. Reused as they are inside a phase that commits, both break the rule 'rethrow so nothing commits'. Also, format=metadata messages must never go to saveMessages (the body-materialization contract).
- Commit-or-die and the cursor rules. Running the repair inside recovery's advancing save leaves two bad outcomes. Either a transient metadata failure holds the cursor, and recovery has no page checkpoint (known-open), or the cursor advances past a gap that was never repaired. Deletions must also stay out of intermediate saves (allowsIntermediateContextSaves).
- Local intent against server state. After a week offline, a queued archive's localModifiedAt is stale (maxLocalModificationAge is 1800 s). A diff against server state then resurrects the chat unless messages with non-terminal PendingActions are skipped. A plan applied outside the conversation's rollup turn is also written over a concurrent MessageActions archive by the object-trump merge policy.

**Fix.** Keep recovery's upsert as is. In its advancing branch (beside setAccountHistoryId), stage a new SyncCheckpoint kind owing a repair: account, watermark time, descending date-bucket bound down to mailboxStart. Later incremental runs that allow expensive work drain it after label processing: per bucket, ID-only list base, in:inbox and is:unread queries, diff against local rows (skipping optimistic rows, ledger IDs, fresh localModifiedAt, non-terminal PendingActions), metadata-GET only differing IDs, then, inside the final rollup-serializer block, delete on 404/TRASH/SPAM or set INBOX/UNREAD. Stage bucket progress into that save; rethrow auth/quota/cancellation; clear when done. Plan-test the bucket fetch.

**First step.** Add `HistoryRecoveryRepairCheckpointStore` (new `SyncCheckpoint` kind, account-validated, staging only) and stage it next to `setAccountHistoryId(profile.historyId)` at IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:851-856; pin with an IncrementalSyncCursorTests case that the advancing save commits the marker and a held one does not.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests with a query-keyed list stub: a pre-window INBOX/unread row archived and read remotely, one row 404, one optimistic row; after recovery plus one drain run, first archived/read, second deleted, optimistic kept, marker cleared. Revert-check: the stage call.

**Payoff.** After any history expiry, archived, read, trashed and deleted mail converge with Gmail instead of staying stale forever; the cursor can no longer advance past an unrepaired gap.

### `attachments-storage-disk#4` · low · reliability · effort S · known-open

**A body file that is gone is read as a body the message never had, so a restore, and any future eviction, turns cards into text and rewrites their stored verdicts**

Area: Attachments, body files and disk lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

With a body file missing and plain bodyText, the resolver's classifier term answers not rich, the stored-preview load publishes that, and the mismatch refresher persists it. But the row first mounts as a card from its stored verdict, and that card's pipeline starts an uncancelled Gmail recovery; on success the file is saved, the verdict re-stamped rich and the bubble reloads. Newsletter-flagged rows, invites and trusted senders are carded regardless. The durable flip needs that first fetch to fail; then nothing retries until the reader is opened.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/RichContentVerdictResolver.swift:114 — a bodyStorageURI whose file does not exist is skipped; :123-127 falls to bodyText and returns .none unless it holds HTML. Only an existing unreadable file gives .undetermined (:109, :118). Pinned as intended at esc-chatmailTests/Chat/RichContentVerdictResolverTests.swift:444
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader.swift:119 — a stored-preview load that differs from the stored verdict schedules the refresher (:122); esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/RichContentVerdictRefresher.swift:140 recomputes from disk and :171 writes it. This branch (:84-100) never attempts recovery
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageDisplayPolicy.swift:109 — before the load publishes, the stored verdict routes the row, so a rich-stamped row mounts the card; :35, :64 and :68 card trusted senders, newsletter-flagged rows and invites whatever the verdict
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewPipeline.swift:87 — the card loads with allowRecovery true; esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/CanonicalEmailContentLoader.swift:233 then calls recovery, with no Task.isCancelled check on the path
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:161 — the fetch runs in an unstructured task the card's unmount cannot cancel; :415 saves the file and :438 schedules a re-stamp from the recovered HTML
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageBubble.swift:635 — the load signature includes the file signature, which saveHTML refreshes (esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:277), so the bubble reloads once the file is back; docs/scalability-review.md:1088 already records the eviction consequence and :1592 says the state after a restore was not looked at

**Trigger.** A backup restored onto the same device (the store returns, Messages does not; a new device is wiped by FreshInstallHandler), followed by a chat first opened while Gmail cannot be reached or while the per-row recovery fetch fails or passes its 30 s limit. Body eviction, the other trigger named, is not built.

**Impact.** With Gmail reachable: each row carded only by its rich verdict (receipts and similar mail not flagged newsletter) flips card to text to card once and costs one messages.get(format=full); the stored verdict ends rich. If that fetch fails: the row is stamped not rich and stays a text bubble showing its stored preview until the reader recovers the body. Tap still opens the original. No data is lost.

**Verifier.** Read the resolver, loader, refresher, routing policy, card pipeline, recovery service, backfill and FreshInstallHandler. Changed from the claim: only verdict-routed rows are affected, the online case heals itself, and the durable flip needs a failed fetch. The fall-through for a missing file is test-pinned, and the compat gate cited applies only to blank-preview rows. No restore was made: the ordering and the reload after the re-stamp are read from code, not observed.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1088, html-bodies-no-retention "Review correction": the bodyEvicted marker that opens the recovery gate and stops the refresher, not built (steps 10 and 12). :1592 says the state after a restore was "not looked at".

**Invariant risks**

- There is one verdict definition, read from stored state only (CLAUDE.md, RichContentVerdictResolver). The rule for an expected body that is missing belongs in classifierCandidate, so the persister, the backfill, the refresher and the loader all agree. A guard in the loader alone would leave RichContentVerdictRefresher.swift:140 and the backfill still writing notRich. A newsletter or network input to the rule would break the stored-state rule.
- Do not bump richContentVerdictEpoch for this fix. A bump turns every stored verdict unknown, and on a store whose bodies are gone RichContentVerdictBackfill.swift:83 cannot work them out again. Every card in a restored mailbox would then become text.
- Return .undetermined only when bodyStorageURI != nil, and only at the two .none exits. Keyed on a missing file alone, every plain-text row would stay unknown for good and show the loading pill on every mount: such a row has a nil URI and no file, because storedHTML is nil and nothing is saved (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:48-55). Returning before the bodyText candidates would break the candidate order the tests pin (testClassifierCandidate_bodyTextWithHTMLTags_isClassifiedAsIs, and the raw-source rows).
- Do not add a recovery to the stored-preview branch (MessageBubbleLoader.swift:84-100). It would be a Gmail fetch on every mount of a body-less row, held for up to the 30 s deadline. It would also have to use the scoped accountContext.recovery token, because the unscoped overload skips the caller's generation. Body access goes through HTMLContentHandler only: reuse the existence checks already made and add no new raw FileManager calls.

**Fix.** Fix it in the resolver alone. In RichContentVerdictResolver.classifierCandidate, keep the candidate order. Return .undetermined instead of .none only when inputs.bodyStorageURI != nil: sync and the reader set that URI only after writing an HTML body, and both file checks have just failed. The persister's read-through, the backfill and the refresher then write nothing or unknown. The loader publishes the stored verdict and schedules no refresh, so stored-rich rows stay cards, and the card's pipeline retries recovery on each mount. Add no stored-preview recovery, no bodyEvicted attribute and no epoch bump. Rows already rewritten to notRich stay that way until the reader recovers the body. Any future eviction must keep bodyStorageURI set.

**First step.** In classifierCandidate, replace the two .none returns (RichContentVerdictResolver.swift:123 and :127) with `inputs.bodyStorageURI == nil ? .none : .undetermined`. Change testVerdict_blankBodyTextWithFallbackSnippetAndStorageURI_isNotRich to expect .unknown; its Revert-check still holds.

**Pinning test.** In MessageBubbleLoaderTests, a test shaped like testLoadContent_unreadableOwnHTMLFile_keepsStoredVerdictAndSchedulesNoRefresh: bodyStorageURI names a removed file and bodyText is plain. Stored rich, unknown and notRich publish true, false, false, with no refresh. Add a refresher test that keeps .rich. Revert-check: the new .undetermined exit.

**Payoff.** Restored stores keep their cards and stored verdicts. So do stores kept across a reopen rollback, which removes the Messages folder (AuthSession.swift:1523, :1571; renamed away and deleted later). It takes one resolver change and no model version.

### `data-model#6` · low · reliability · effort M · new

**participantHash is a stored key over three mutable inputs, and only one of them has change tracking**

Area: Data model and schema design. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The alias set (Account send-as list plus Contacts self-card addresses, the latter never persisted) is re-derived at each sync's setup and routes that run; nothing records the set stored hashes were made with. Contacts grant, withdrawal and own-card edits are nonetheless re-keyed, archived included, because the user's multi-address card is itself a link group. Untracked: Gmail send-as changes, Contacts aliases forming no link group, and a failed self-alias read. Those are repaired only by the cadence pass over active conversations, whose cost is a prior, known item.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:222-223 — refreshSendAsAliases, then myAliases = AliasManager.shared.getAliases(from:) at run setup; that set routes the run, before any cleanup step.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:100-114 — cacheAliases re-reads Contacts and, when the set differs, only calls rollupDependencyTracker.invalidateAll(); nothing is persisted and no re-key is requested. AccountPersister.swift:118 stores send-as addresses only.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:68-70 and :94-99 — unreadable Contacts return []; a throwing lookup is skipped with try?. Contrast ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:176-183, where a failed or undecided read keeps the adopted map.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:277-281 and ContactLinkedAddresses.swift:142-151 — every card with more than one address is a group, the user's own included, and addressesLinkedDifferently does not exclude own addresses; the scoped re-key (DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:388-415) hashes with the current aliases (:91) and gives archived rows the hash (:224-228).
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:385-386 and DataCleanupService.swift:340 — the maintenance pass is the default .activeConversations scope (archivedAt == nil); archived conversations are not read.
- docs/scalability-review.md:926-932 and :1618 — the unbatched full active-conversation fetch is item six-hour-maintenance-inside-sync-run; its batching is listed 'Not built'; all passes measured about 0.55 s at S3 on a Mac.

**Trigger.** A send-as alias is added in Gmail after mail to that address was already stored with it as a participant row; or a Contacts self-address that forms no link group appears (an address shared with another card, a one-address Mac "me" card); or one sync's self-alias Contacts lookup throws. Contacts grant, withdrawal and ordinary own-card edits are not triggers: the link pass re-keys them.

**Impact.** Archived chats whose rows name the newly own address keep the old hash, so new mail from that person never reactivates them, and the list shows no archived chats. Active ones stay split until the 6-hour pass merges them. A failed read forks only that run's mail to a Contacts-only alias, healed by the same pass while the fork is active. Rare, one-time per alias change, no data loss.

**Verifier.** Read whole: ConversationIdentity, AliasManager, ContactsSelfAliasProvider, ContactLinkedAddressStore, ContactLinkedAddresses, ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker, DataCleanupService, the unification pass, the repair pass, ConversationCreationSerializer, ConversationRoutingPolicy. The asymmetry is real and undocumented as a decision. Corrected: the trigger list overstated (the link diff covers Contacts-derived changes), the cost half is not new (prior item, measured small), severity lowered to low. Frequency of Contacts read failures is not established; nothing was run.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:922-932 six-hour-maintenance-inside-sync-run (batching 'Not built', :1618); related known-open self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist :1310-1326. Alias-change tracking itself is in neither.

**Invariant risks**

- Moving alias adoption into cleanup, as links do, would mis-stamp stored isFromMe for the run where an alias changes. MessageProcessor.swift:366 sets isFromMe from the run's set, no pass re-derives it, and it feeds RichContentVerdictResolver. Reply-recipient exclusion reads the same set. So keep routing on the current set and track only which set the stored hashes were made with.
- A merge cannot be undone: ConversationMerger moves the messages and the winner keeps its rows. Tracking would turn any back-and-forth of the alias set into permanent wrong merges, archived chats included. Two sources exist today: the try? at ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:94-99 returns a narrower set on a failed lookup, and IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1054 records the send-as refresh time while the Account update is still only staged in the sync context, so a failed run loses it for 24 h. Fix both first.
- A note-to-self chat is hashed with myAliases.sorted().first (ConversationIdentity.swift:81). Its only row is the old first alias (CoreDataFactories.swift:227), so .conversationsNaming(changed) misses it when a new alias sorts first. Add the old and new first alias to the scope.
- The applied set holds the account's addresses, so it must be cleared in clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults. Its shared store must write nothing under unit tests, because the Mac test host uses the real defaults. Do not narrow the 6-hour .activeConversations pass: it also repairs hashes stored wrong while nothing changed.

**Fix.** Three changes, in this order. (1) SelfAliasProviding returns nil when a lookup throws or Contacts access is undecided. AliasManager then keeps its last good Contacts part, and drops it only when access is denied or restricted, as ContactLinkedAddressStore does. (2) Record the send-as refresh time only inside the run's commit closure. (3) Leave routing as it is and add an injectable applied-alias record. In unifyConversationsByContactIfNeeded, take the link-changed addresses, add the difference between the applied and current alias sets and the old and new first alias, and run one .conversationsNaming pass. Mark links and aliases applied only on .completed. A removed alias moves nothing, as with unlinking.

**First step.** Make SelfAliasProviding.aliases return Set<String>?, nil when a Contacts call throws or access is undecided. AliasManager.cacheAliases keeps its previous Contacts part on nil. Pin it in AliasManagerTests with a throwing stub.

**Pinning test.** Seed an archived {X, alias} conversation and active {X, alias} and {X} ones, applied {me}, provider {me, alias}. runIncrementalCleanup gives the archived one hash [X], merges the active pair and records applied; a second run reads nothing. Revert-check it.

**Payoff.** Archived chats get the new hash in the same run the alias appears, so new mail reactivates them. A failed Contacts read no longer splits chats or causes repeated wrong merges.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#1` · low · reliability · effort M · new

**Body parts are decoded as UTF-8 whatever charset they declare**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The code does read every body as UTF-8 and never checks the part's charset. On the main path that is correct. With format=full, Gmail returns inline text-part body.data already converted to UTF-8 and leaves the charset label as it was. Outside tests measured this across 16 legacy charsets, among them windows-1252, Shift_JIS, ISO-2022-JP, GBK, Big5, EUC-KR and KOI8-R. What remains: bodies fetched by attachmentId (attachments.get returns the sender's original bytes) and inner parts of salvaged raw-source blobs. Both are read as UTF-8 whatever their charset, so their non-ASCII bytes become U+FFFD.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:774-779 — decodeBody base64-decodes inline body.data, reads it with String(decoding:as: UTF8.self) and never looks at the charset. That is right for inline data, which Gmail serves as UTF-8.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:731-755 — an attachment-backed body's bytes are read as UTF-8 (:754). The comment at :732 claims Gmail moves bodies over ~25KB to an attachmentId; no code measures that.
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Attachments.swift:13 — attachments.get bytes are a single base64url decode, the original bytes. esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:629-631 reads them as UTF-8 the same way.
- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/RawEmailSourceSanitizer.swift:264-290 — inner parts of an embedded raw RFC 822 blob are QP- or base64-decoded and read as UTF-8 (QuotedPrintableDecoder.swift:6-9). The part's charset header is ignored, and here the bytes really are in that charset.
- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/RFC2047Decoder.swift:6-9,159-185 — the charset table serves headers only. The file's own comment says Gmail usually returns header values already decoded to UTF-8.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:861-869 — the body is QP-decoded again whenever the part's header says quoted-printable.

**Trigger.** The part has non-ASCII bytes in a non-UTF-8 charset and is one of two rare kinds: a text/plain or text/html part Gmail serves by attachmentId instead of inline (outside measurement: about 3 MB, with a 300 KB body still inline; the code comment's ~25KB is unverified), or the inner QP/base64 part of a message body that is itself raw RFC 822 source.

**Impact.** In those rare messages, non-ASCII characters become U+FFFD in the stored body, bodyText, cleanedSnippet, chatPreviewText, the list snippet and search, and legacy CJK text in such a part is unreadable. Ordinary inline mail in windows-1252, ISO-2022-JP, Shift_JIS, GBK and the like is not affected. The recommended fix, decoding inline body.data with the declared charset, would itself produce mojibake on all such mail.

**Verifier.** Not from repo lines. Two outside tests measured inline body.data as UTF-8: google_workspace_mcp PR 1377 (16 charsets plus 580 real messages) and mcp-gee-sweet PR 816 (compared format=full with raw). The opposing gws-rust PR 327 used fixtures only. Separate and unverified: Gmail also removes the transfer encoding, but MessageProcessor.swift:861-869 QP-decodes a second time. MessageProcessorTests.swift:1272-1299 models body.data as still QP-encoded.

**Invariant risks**

- Body-materialization contract (CLAUDE.md sync section; MessageProcessor.swift:734-743): the decoder must never fail. If fetchLargeBodyContent returned nil for a charset it could not decode, the code would treat that as a deterministic per-part failure, persist the row without its body and advance the cursor.
- Inline body.data is UTF-8 that Gmail has already converted, so it must not be decoded by its charset label. A windows-1252 fallback after strict UTF-8 fails would turn a whole UTF-8 body into mojibake over one stray byte, for example the 0xBE that the second QP pass at MessageProcessor.swift:861-869 makes from '=be' in a URL.
- RawEmailSourceSanitizer.extractHTMLText feeds RichContentVerdictResolver at render time (RichContentVerdictResolver.swift:124). CacheVersioning.swift:19-27 requires a richContentVerdictEpoch bump for any change to it, and that bump re-runs the launch verdict backfill over every stored message.
- web replays rawSourceHTMLRecoveryCases from the golden corpus (corpus.golden.test.ts:115; rawSource.ts:254 is the web copy of decodePartBodyIfNeeded). A new charset case must ship together with the web change, and must avoid iso-8859-1 bytes 0x80-0x9F, where CoreFoundation reads Latin-1 and WHATWG reads windows-1252.

**Fix.** Add one pure decoder that never fails, decode(bytes:charsetLabel:). It tries strict UTF-8 first. Bytes that are ASCII, contain ESC and carry an ISO-2022 label go to that label's encoding. Otherwise it tries the label's encoding, looked up through RFC2047Decoder's table made internal, and finally the lossy UTF-8 used today. It never guesses windows-1252. Leave inline body.data as it is. On the attachment-backed paths in MessageProcessor and HTMLContentRecoveryService, run the existing QP pass on the raw bytes (a new Data overload of QuotedPrintableDecoder), then this decoder. Ship RawEmailSourceSanitizer.decodePartBodyIfNeeded in a second PR: decode the inner part to Data, apply its charset, bump richContentVerdictEpoch, and port rawSource.ts in the same change. No backfill: fixing stored bodies would mean fetching them again.

**First step.** Move the duplicated decodeBody, decodeTransferEncoding and looksQuotedPrintable code (MessageProcessor.swift:774-881, HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:639-820) into one shared pure decoder, behavior unchanged and pinned by the existing MessageProcessorLargeBodyFetchTests. Add no charset logic yet.

**Pinning test.** In MessageProcessorLargeBodyFetchTests: fetched windows-1252 'café' and Shift_JIS bytes, each with its label, decode correctly. UTF-8 bytes labeled windows-1252, and inline body.data, come out unchanged. Add a corpus raw-source case: an inner windows-1252 QP '=E9' part.

**Payoff.** Newly synced mail stops turning legacy-charset text into U+FFFD in bodies fetched by attachmentId and in inner parts of salvaged raw source. The inline path, which carries nearly all mail, is not touched.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#5` · low · maintainability · effort M · new

**Stored bodies carry no charset or decoder version, so a decoder fix cannot find or repair the damage**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Body parts are decoded as UTF-8 whatever charset they declare, and the decoded string is what gets stored. The part's charset, its transfer encoding and a decoder version are not stored anywhere. Nothing schedules a refetch. A body is rewritten only when the message is fetched again through the update path, or by on-demand HTML recovery, which uses its own duplicate UTF-8-only decoder. The damage can still be found: U+FFFD and ESC survive into bodyText and the HTML file. The proposed attributes would be nil on every row stored so far, so they cannot target that damage.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:774-779 — decodeBody runs String(decoding: decodedData, as: UTF8.self); no Content-Type charset is read
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:1181-1205 — ProcessedMessage carries htmlBody/plainTextBody strings and no charset, transfer encoding or decoder version
- esc-chatmail/Services/Models/Message+Extensions.swift:122-158 — Message stores bodyText, bodyStorageURI, snippets and richContentVerdict; no charset or decode-version attribute
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:629-645 — the on-demand recovery has its own copy of the UTF-8-only decode (getAttachment / decodeBody), separate from MessageProcessor
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Updates.swift:232-238 — a refetch rewrites the body file when it differs; lines 359-368 overwrite bodyText
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:170-177 — the mailbox starts at sign-in and brings back no earlier mail; 217-223: re-initial sync is capped at 30 days

**Trigger.** When a charset or quoted-printable decoder fix ships. Only rows already stored with non-UTF-8 parts are affected, plus damage that leaves no trace in the text, such as a transfer-decoding change that still produces valid ASCII.

**Impact.** After the fix, rows that are already damaged stay garbled until someone writes a repair pass.
