That pass would scan bodyText or the HTML files for U+FFFD and ESC, then refetch only those rows through the update path. The refetch count is the number of damaged rows, not 120k. The store holds mail only from sign-in onward, so S2 takes years of use. If only MessageProcessor is fixed, on-demand recovery keeps writing damaged HTML.

**Verifier.** Each cited location matches the code today. CacheVersioning.swift:10-41 versions only derived values. Recovery in the bubble loader runs only when bodyText is empty (MessageBubbleLoader+CompatibilityContent.swift:195-205), so it never heals rows that hold garbled text. Nothing strips U+FFFD or ESC, so a content scan finds the charset damage, which is what the auditor's own recommendation relies on. That makes the claim that the damage cannot be found wrong. The 120k refetch figure is also overstated. What remains is a missing repair pass plus a duplicated decoder.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1623 step 10 (the ESCChatmail 7 batch). No item covers charset or the body decoder; line 1492 (synchronous store load) gates any v7 attribute.

**Invariant risks**

- The repair must only update rows, never create them. MessagePersister.swift:603-617: saveMessages falls through to createNewMessage on .notPresent. A row deleted between the scan and the refetch would come back, against the rule that the mailbox starts at sign-in.
- The refetch belongs inside an incremental sync run, persisted at the orchestrator's save points with its ModificationTracker transaction and serializer-wrapped rollups. Its failures must never enter SyncFailureTracker buckets or freeze the cursor (drain rule). Never fetch over the network while holding an account-work lease (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:405-414: sign-out waits on leases it cannot cancel) or inside the exclusive .maintenance run.
- Share only the pure bytes-to-String decode. MessageProcessor.fetchLargeBodyContent (744-772) throws on transient failures to keep the body-materialization contract, while the recovery copy (HTMLContentRecoveryService.swift:622-636) swallows every error. Merging the fetch code would persist body-less rows behind an advancing cursor.
- Do not bump either CacheVersioning key. The update path already re-stamps the verdict whenever it saves HTML (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:402-411) and rewrites chatPreviewText. A richContentVerdictEpoch bump would put every bubble behind the loading pill and re-run backfills over the whole mailbox. Any v7 attribute needs the == nil disjunct and the async store load.

**Fix.** Fix the decoder first, then repair without a schema change. (1) Move both decoder copies (MessageProcessor 774-881, HTMLContentRecoveryService 638-827) into one pure MIMEBodyDecoder: base64 to bytes, quoted-printable decoded on bytes, charset read from the part's Content-Type through RFC2047Decoder's charset map, UTF-8 as the fallback. Add golden-corpus cases that web also passes. (2) Add a launch repair pass shaped like RichContentVerdictBackfill (a lease per batch, a keyset cursor, a migration key that embeds a decoder version). It queues the IDs whose bodyText or cleanedSnippet holds U+FFFD or ESC, in account-scoped defaults. (3) Drain at most 10 IDs per foreground or processing incremental run, the way Phase 2b drains abandoned messages: fetch with fetchAbandonedMessages and persist update-only, outside the failure ledger and the cursor. No version bumps; v7 attributes are optional.

**First step.** Move MessageProcessor's decodeBody, decodeBase64Data, decodeTransferEncoding and looksQuotedPrintable, and HTMLContentRecoveryService's copies of them, into one pure MIMEBodyDecoder without changing behavior. Leave each caller's fetch-error handling where it is.

**Pinning test.** MIMEBodyDecoderTests: a windows-1252, ISO-2022-JP or Shift_JIS part decodes the same through MessageProcessor and through recovery (Revert-check: MIMEBodyDecoder). A drain test: a damaged row is rewritten, a deleted row is not recreated, and the cursor and ledger do not move.

**Payoff.** Once a charset fix ships, garbled non-UTF-8 mail already stored repairs itself, and on-demand recovery stops rewriting damaged HTML. One decoder instead of two cannot drift.

### `gap-mime-decoding-i18n#6` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**The canonical hash re-parses re-serialized, decoded names by splitting on every comma**

Area: MIME body decoding fidelity and internationalized mail. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

createMessageHeaders rebuilds each parsed To/Cc as `name <addr>` from the decoded, unquoted name, and makeConversationIdentity then splits on every comma. So a name like `"bob@old.example, Bob" <bob@new.example>` adds a phantom bob@old to the router hash and to the conversation rows. Message rows (one extract, no split) and web (parser tokens) do not add it. An encoded word that decodes to `<boss@…>` swaps in that address through the rebuild, but a plain quoted name `"<boss@…>"` already does the same when the header is parsed.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationManager.swift:271-278 — To/Cc rebuilt as `\(displayName) <\(email)>` from parsed, decoded names
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationIdentity.swift:166-168 — every From/To/Cc value split on each comma, then extractEmail per piece (177-178)
- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/EmailNormalizer.swift:39-41 — bracketed regex takes the leftmost <…@…>, including one inside a quoted display name; 127-131 sanitizeDisplayName decodes RFC 2047 and strips the quotes that protected the comma
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Participants.swift:27-28 — message rows rebuild the same string but CoreDataFactories.swift:271 extracts once, no comma split
- web/src/sync/persist.ts:166 — web hashes the parser's To/Cc tokens directly
- esc-chatmailTests/Conversation/ConversationIdentityTests.swift:22 — the golden corpus replays raw headers through makeConversationIdentity, not createConversationIdentity, so the production rebuild path is not pinned

**Trigger.** A To/Cc display name that, once unquoted or decoded, has an address-shaped string before a comma, and that address differs from the real one. No common mailer is known to write this. A sender can write it on purpose.

**Impact.** The message's 1:1 chat forks into a group chat whose title names a phantom member. iOS and web hash the message differently. In the comma case the reply is not misaddressed: the conversation rows name someone who is not on the message, so ReplyLinkedAddressPolicy sends it to the message's own people. Fixing the rebuild would not stop address substitution, because the parser already lets a quoted name substitute an address.

**Verifier.** I traced the comma mechanism and it is as described. On raw headers a quoted comma name gives no phantom, because the leading `"` blocks the bare-address match. Only the rebuild exposes it. The participant-hash repair pass recomputes the hash from conversation rows, which already hold the phantom, so it never heals the chat. The split migration that reads message rows runs only once. Severity is lowered for three reasons: real mail rarely does this, the harm is limited, and quoted-name substitution already happens when the header is parsed.

**Invariant risks**

- participantHash is canonical, and the fix re-keys existing chats that have a quoted-comma name, or a nameless bracketed address the bare regex rejects (EAI or IDN, dotless host, quoted local part). Nothing merges them back. fixAndMergeIncorrectParticipantHashes rehashes from the conversation rows the old router created (DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:146). The split migration is behind a flag (948), and its guard refuses the move (1162-1168). Expect a one-time fork, not a flip-flop.
- The router and the message rows must change together. If only createMessageHeaders is fixed, an encoded name that decodes to `<boss@x>` hashes to the real address. saveParticipants still rebuilds `name <addr>` and stores boss@x (MessagePersister+Participants.swift:27-43). ReplyLinkedAddressPolicy would then send a reply in a chat titled for the real person to the injected address.
- Never re-parse a decoded display name. EmailNormalizer.swift:111-115 says decoding comes after address parsing, so decoded text cannot inject `<addr>`. Both rebuild sites break that today, and any fix that still re-serializes, even with the quotes put back, keeps the hazard.
- Golden corpus parity: new conversationIdentityCases trigger web CI. The iOS replay (ConversationIdentityTests.swift:22) feeds raw headers, where a nameless `<étudiant@x.fr>` keeps its brackets and survives. It must go through the ProcessedHeaders path, or the test pins code that production does not run.

**Fix.** Move MessageProcessor.parseEmailAddresses into one shared static beside EmailAddressListParser. Add a core identity builder that takes [EmailAddress] for From, To and Cc plus the raw List-Id. It keeps today's per-entry Hide-My-Email skip, isBetterDisplayName ranking, List-Id branch and BCC exclusion. createConversationIdentity passes ProcessedHeaders' to and cc, plus the raw From parsed by that helper. The [MessageHeader] variant tokenizes through the same helper, with no comma split. Delete createMessageHeaders. In the same change, give MessageParticipantFactory an email-and-displayName overload and use it in saveParticipants for To, Cc and Bcc, so the rows and the hash cannot diverge. No store repair: document the one-time fork for affected chats.

**First step.** Add two conversationIdentityCases: To `"bob@old.example, Bob" <bob@new.example>`, and Cc `<étudiant@x.fr>` with no name. Switch the ConversationIdentityTests replay to build ProcessedHeaders with the shared parser and call createConversationIdentity. Confirm both cases fail before changing production.

**Pinning test.** Replay the corpus through createConversationIdentity on parser-built ProcessedHeaders, with two new cases (today: phantom bob@old, étudiant dropped). Web replays the same JSON. Add a persister test: an encoded name decoding to `<boss@x>` keeps the row and hash on the real address.

**Payoff.** The router, the message rows and web agree on who is on a message. No phantom group chats appear, and nameless internationalized or dotless recipients are no longer dropped from the chat and its replies.

### `gap-wall-clock-time#3` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Elapsed-time checks treat a future stamp as fresh: setting the clock back freezes polling, shields and cadences**

Area: The device's wall clock is the only clock: clock changes, skew and time zones. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Each cited age check computes Date() minus a stored wall-clock stamp, with no guard against a stamp in the future. After the clock is set back by S, each check stalls for about S and then recovers on its own. The Mac poll throttle skips every unforced trigger, label reconciliation is skipped, the 6-hour maintenance cadence is not due, an abandoned action's localModifiedAt holds Gmail's state out for S plus 30 minutes, and recovery of a stuck 'processing' row waits S plus 10 minutes. The finding overstates two parts: iOS re-stamps the poll stamp on every return to the foreground, and the daily database cleanup still runs the maintenance passes.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:247-252, 264 — unforced requests are skipped while Date().timeIntervalSince(lastSyncTriggerAt) < minimumSyncGap, and a negative value counts as under the gap; :66-70 start() forces only when it creates a new loop
- esc-chatmail/App/AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:65-68, 101-105 — the Mac keeps the session running in the background and restarts it only on wake or activation, so activation with a loop already running stays unforced; iOS stops the session in the background, so its next start is forced
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1002-1005 — skips when now − lastReconciliation < interval; :391-395 passes Date().timeIntervalSince1970; :1063-1064 writes Date() as the stamp
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:40-47 — the 6-hour cadence is due only when now − lastRun ≥ interval; but DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:54 has the daily cleanup task run the same runMaintenanceCleanup without checking that cadence
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor+LabelOperations.swift:55-70 — a future localModifiedAt never counts as stale; PendingActionProcessor.swift:332-347 abandons without clearing the marker, PendingActionQueries.swift:425-438 dismisses by deletion and also leaves it; PendingActionProcessor.swift:61-68 recovers stuck rows only when lastAttempt < now − 10 min
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundActivitySchedulePolicy.swift:37-41 — the only clamp in the code: a stored due date further than one interval ahead is pulled in to now + interval

**Trigger.** A backward step of the device's wall clock by S (a manual change, or turning automatic time back on after the clock was set ahead, as people do to skip game timers) after the stamps were written. Automatic NTP corrections are normally seconds and do nothing visible. The poll freeze also needs the process to keep its in-memory stamp across the change, which in practice means the Mac app left running.

**Impact.** The freeze lasts about S and then ends on its own; nothing is lost and nothing wedges for good. Mac: no periodic polling for about S, until a system wake, Mailbox > Sync, a send or a quit. iOS: no polling effect, because a forced start re-stamps the time. On both platforms the hourly label reconciliation pauses, a local change Gmail rejected stays on screen longer, and stuck-action recovery is delayed. The 6-hour maintenance pause is mostly covered by the daily cleanup task, which on the Mac is scheduled through the clamped policy. The effects matter only when S is large, such as days after a clock set ahead is corrected.

**Verifier.** Every cited line matches the code today. No significantTimeChange or clock-change handler exists, and SyncClock reads Date(). HistoryProcessor.clearLocalModifications(for:) is never called, so the staleness backstop really is the only release for an abandoned action's marker. Three corrections to the original claim: the maintenance passes still run from the daily cleanup; the poll freeze is Mac-only; and the trigger is rare and its effects end by themselves. That makes this low rather than medium. Recommendation stands: a monotonic clock for in-process gaps, and one future-stamp clamp like dueDate's.

**Invariant risks**

- SyncClock.now() has to stay on the wall clock. SyncFailureTracker.swift:418 and :529 persist it as lastSuccessfulSyncTime and AbandonedSyncMessage.nextRetryAt. GmailAPIClient.swift:77-80 deliberately keeps its circuit breaker and time budget on Date(), so that FakeSyncClock's now(), which advances on every sleep, does not trip the StubURLProtocol retry tests. Add a separate monotonic member and leave now() as it is.
- localModifiedAt is two things. It is the pending-window guard (scalability review, 'Keep intact'), and it orders events (PendingActionProcessor.swift:418 compares `<= createdAt`, ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:277 uses `<`). Treating a future stamp as stale would let Gmail's state overwrite actions still in the queue. Stamping it again would write into the sync context and change the outcome of both comparisons.
- Query floors are not cadences. lastSuccessfulSyncTime and installTimestamp must never be stamped again to now: CLAUDE.md says never to move the mailbox start over a retained store, and doing so skips the mail in between. At most, clamp them downward to min(stamp, now) inside SyncTimeCalculator.
- In the abandoned-message drain, the `nextRetryAt == nil` and `state == nil` disjuncts are load-bearing on SQLite, so a clamp for a future deadline may only add a disjunct. Treating a future lastAttempt as stuck is safe only because recovery runs inside the exclusive .pendingActions run (PendingActionsManager.swift:473-484), and every action type is an idempotent label change; none is a send.

**Fix.** Two parts, and nothing new is written on a read path. (1) In-process: ForegroundSyncCoordinator keeps lastSyncTriggerAt as a ContinuousClock.Instant read from an injected closure that defaults to ContinuousClock.now. SyncClock.now() stays on the wall clock. (2) Persisted cadences: add one pure helper, WallClockCadence.isDue(lastRun:interval:now:futureTolerance:), that returns due when lastRun is more than a few minutes ahead of now. Use it in IncrementalCleanupSchedule.isDue, shouldSkipLabelReconciliation and SendAsAliasRefreshPolicy. Each one's existing mark-after-success stamps the time again, so the helper needs no write. Add an `OR lastAttempt > now + tolerance` disjunct to both stuck-processing predicates. Leave localModifiedAt, the query floors and nextRetryAt alone.

**First step.** In ForegroundSyncCoordinator, inject a monotonic `now` closure that defaults to ContinuousClock.now and store lastSyncTriggerAt as a ContinuousClock.Instant. This removes the Mac polling freeze. The state lives only in memory on the MainActor, and nothing persisted changes.

**Pinning test.** In ForegroundSyncCoordinatorTests, inject a fake monotonic clock and check that throttling follows monotonic time alone. Add pure tests: IncrementalCleanupSchedule.isDue, shouldSkipLabelReconciliation and SendAsAliasRefreshPolicy each report due for a stamp one day in the future. Each test carries a Revert-check naming WallClockCadence.isDue.

**Payoff.** After the clock is set back, Mac polling, label reconciliation, the 6-hour maintenance and stuck-action recovery no longer pause for the size of that backward step. The trigger is rare and the fix is cheap and isolated.

### `gap-wall-clock-time#5` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Day labels and relative dates never refresh: no day, clock or time-zone change is observed**

Area: The device's wall clock is the only clock: clock changes, skew and time zones. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Partly confirmed. Conversation rows (iOS list and Mac sidebar) and iOS bubble timestamps get their relative label from TimestampFormatter.format, which reads Calendar.current and Date() each time the body runs. A row's body only re-runs when its ConversationSnapshot changes or the row remounts, and the snapshot holds no time-relative field. Nothing observes a day, clock or time-zone change. So after midnight, mounted rows that get no new mail keep the old label, for example a bare "3:42 PM" for yesterday. The Mac time-line staleness is a documented, accepted decision. The time-zone claim is not established.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Utilities/TimestampFormatter.swift:22-41 — Today/Yesterday/weekday decided from Calendar.current and Date() at call time; fixed 'h:mm a' / 'MM/dd/yy' patterns
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ConversationRowView.swift:169-170,400-402 — row time is Text(TimestampFormatter.format(date)) computed in body; row inputs are snapshot, IDs, loader, metrics, palette
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationSnapshot.swift:7-17 — Equatable snapshot of stored fields only (lastMessageDate, unread, snippet...), nothing that changes with the day
- esc-chatmail/Views/Main/View+ConversationListLifecycle.swift:9-11 — the Mac sidebar stays mounted for the whole sign-in
- docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:397 — documented decision: the time line's label is computed when the row is drawn; 'Today' becomes 'Yesterday' at the next redraw after midnight
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatTranscriptRunPolicy.swift:33-45 — separator placement depends only on the two message dates and the calendar, not on now, and is recomputed in the ForEach each time the transcript is evaluated

**Trigger.** Midnight passes while list rows stay mounted and their conversations get no new mail. Common cases are a Mac sidebar left open overnight or an iOS app resumed from suspension the next day. A row refreshes when it scrolls out and back, when its snapshot changes, or when it remounts.

**Impact.** Cosmetic only. Next morning, rows for yesterday's mail can still show a bare time, which reads as today. "Yesterday" rows do not turn into weekdays, and weekday rows do not turn into dates. No data, sync or function is affected. The open Mac chat's "Today" lines behave the way the Mac UI plan already accepts.

**Verifier.** No observer of NSCalendarDayChanged, significantTimeChange, the clock-change or the zone-change notifications, and no TimelineView, exists under esc-chatmail/ or esc-chatmailTests (git grep found nothing). The ChatTimestampSeparator part restates a documented decision (docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:397). Separator placement does not depend on "now", so "splits days at the old zone's midnight" was not shown. Whether Calendar.current, SwiftUI's calendar environment or the static DateFormatter pick up a new zone is unmeasured. Severity goes from medium to low: the effect is a stale label only.

**October review.** docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:397 records that the Mac transcript's time-line label is computed when the row is drawn. That is accepted for the transcript only. docs/scalability-review.md has no item on this.

**Invariant risks**

- ConversationSnapshot equality and the publishVisibleItems funnel: a day field in the snapshot, or a forced reloadConversationWindowFromStore/replaceAll at midnight, rebuilds the snapshot of every row in the window on the main thread (scalability item conversation-list-window-full-refetch). Keep the day out of the data path.
- MacMailboxDetail is Equatable on the selection alone and stores only fixed values (MacMailboxDetail.swift:8-27). Passing the epoch through it, ChatView, MessageBubble's init or MessageBubbleLoadSignatureComponents would re-evaluate every open bubble or restart its load. Only leaf views should read it, from the environment.
- Mac transcript rows must not change height after they mount. If ChatTranscriptRunPolicy.placement (ChatMessagesView.swift:362, calendar: .current) depended on the epoch, a time-zone change would add or remove time lines in an open transcript. Only relabel single-line leaves.
- A stale clock value must never be used as 'now': after a missed notification, newly drawn rows would get wrong labels, which is worse than today. Keep Date() as the source of now. Also, CI's Swift 6.2 makes a memberwise init private when a view has a plain private var, so leaf views use @Environment or an explicit init.

**Fix.** Refresh only the label leaves and leave data and layout alone. (1) Make TimestampFormatter pure: format(_:now:calendar:). Count calendar days the way ChatTimestampSeparatorPolicy.dayForm does; today's 24-hour count (TimestampFormatter.swift:34-37) labels last Wednesday "Wednesday" when today is Wednesday. The formatters take calendar.timeZone. (2) Add a @MainActor CalendarDayClock that publishes an Equatable CalendarDay (start of today, time zone, locale). It updates on NSCalendarDayChanged, NSSystemClockDidChange, NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange (after resetSystemTimeZone) and app-did-become-active, and skips values equal to the last one. (3) Set it as an environment value from a wrapper view around ContentView in rootContent. (4) A new row-timestamp leaf view, MessageMetadata and ChatTimestampSeparator read it and still pass Date() as now. Do not use TimelineView. Switching to localized date patterns is a separate product decision.

**First step.** Extract a pure TimestampFormatter.format(_:now:calendar:) that counts calendar days like ChatTimestampSeparatorPolicy.dayForm. Keep format(_:) as a wrapper that passes Date() and Calendar.current. Pin it with fixed-date tests in an America/New_York calendar.

**Pinning test.** TimestampFormatterTests (fixed now and calendar): yesterday 3:42 PM reads "Yesterday"; a week-old same weekday reads a date. CalendarDayClockTests: NSCalendarDayChanged after advancing an injected now publishes a new day; becoming active on the same day publishes nothing.

**Payoff.** After midnight, or a clock or time-zone change, mounted list rows, the always-open Mac sidebar and open transcripts show the right day labels. The cost is one re-render of a few text views per day.

### `gap-wall-clock-time#6` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Optimistic sends and dateless messages put device time into a server-time order**

Area: The device's wall clock is the only clock: clock changes, skew and time zones. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

An optimistic send stamps internalDate and the conversation's lastMessageDate with device Date(), and its rollback snapshot's createdAt is device time too. The transcript sorts by internalDate, so with clock skew S the reply sits among messages received within S of it until the echo replaces it, and a retained Not-sent row keeps that position for good. Rollback decides supersession by comparing server internalDate with device createdAt. An INBOX arrival is protected by the hasInbox guard, so only rare non-inbox cases depend on the skew. The dateless fallback is practically unreachable.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:245, 289, 1831 — message.internalDate = Date(); conversation.lastMessageDate = Date(); snapshot createdAt = Date()
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:358-362 — transcript sorts by internalDate, then id
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1609-1616, 1912 — supersession is server internalDate > device createdAt; archive restore is also refused while conversation.hasInbox
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:9-15, 57-64 — sync reactivates on INBOX/SENT/fromMe; the rollup unarchives whenever hasInbox
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:63, 107-108 — lastMessageDate is recomputed from the stored messages, so the list's device date lasts only until the echo
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:53-58 with esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:20 — the Date() fallback sits behind format=full fetches, which always carry internalDate

**Trigger.** The device clock is set by hand, minutes off Google's (automatic time keeps skew under a second). Bubble order also needs a message in the chat within S of the reply. The archive cases also need a Compose or Forward send to an archived chat that rolls back before the barrier.

**Impact.** Cosmetic. A reply bubble sits out of place until its echo lands, and the conversation list position is wrong until then too. A Not-sent bubble stays out of place. On a failed compose to an archived chat, the archive restore can go either way. With a slow clock, a message already in the chat counts as newer, so the chat the user archived stays unarchived. With a fast clock, a SENT-only message from another client during preflight does not count as newer, so the chat is re-archived over it. Inbox mail arriving during preflight still unarchives the chat in every case.

**Verifier.** I read the stamps, the transcript sort, both rollback paths (1579-1617, 1116-1167), restoreConversationState and the rollup. The claimed re-archive over newly arrived mail is blocked for INBOX mail: applyArchiveState unarchives the chat and restoreConversationState returns while hasInbox is true (1912). For lastMessageDate, the echo's rollup recompute heals the list. The internalDate fallback is defensive because fetches request format=full; that claim relies on Gmail's API behavior, not on repository code. No document records accepting skew.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:228 — the Review correction says "optimistic sends stamp a local now", but only to keep isFromMe rows out of the recovery bound (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:955-959). No item covers transcript order, list order or rollback supersession.

**Invariant risks**

- Switching supersession to arrival order flips a pinned rule. A message synced during preflight whose internalDate is older than the tap must not count as newer, so the pre-send archive comes back (GmailSendServiceOptimisticFailureTests.swift:1885-1911; OptimisticUpdates.swift:1620-1631).
- A refetch of a dateless message breaks the classification contract in MessageProcessor. A throw becomes .bodyFetchFailed, which freezes the cursor on a condition that never changes. A nil becomes .unprocessable and the mail is dropped (MessagePersister.swift:443-458). Leave the Date() fallback alone.
- Record createdAt also orders records (OptimisticUpdates.swift:642, 1552; MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:88). An offset-only stamp that moves backwards between two taps swaps bubbles and chain order, so clamp it to lastMessageDate. A new record attribute would need a new model version.
- Compute the stamp inside the gate and the anchored turns, after adoptStoredArchiveState, with no await and no fetch on the main thread. Keep writing only lastMessageDate and snippet, never hasInbox. Keep the offset in memory, not in account-scoped defaults. Leave conversation.createdAt on device time (its grace period is measured in device time).

**Fix.** Keep the supersession rule and the MessageProcessor fallback; fix the stamp. Inside createOptimisticMessageWithoutCleanupInterleaving, after the anchor resolves, compute one stamp: max(now(), conversation.lastMessageDate + 1 ms) when that lies within a bound (say 15 min) of now, plus a server offset only if the sync-window fix builds one (in memory, reset on NSSystemClockDidChange). Use it for message.internalDate, conversation.lastMessageDate, ConversationFactory's initialLastMessageDate and both snapshots' createdAt (passed in, not Date()); the fallback snapshot at 1962 takes message.internalDate. Inject now: @Sendable () -> Date into GmailSendService. Supersession then compares one clock without changing its rule.

**First step.** Add a pure OptimisticSendStampPolicy.stamp(now:lastMessageDate:) with the bounded clamp and its unit tests. Then add now: @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init to GmailSendService.init and route lines 245, 289, 1213 and 1831 through one computed stamp.

**Pinning test.** In GmailSendServiceOptimisticFailureTests, an archived non-INBOX chat whose last message is dated now()+120 s: the optimistic reply sorts last and records createdAt == internalDate; rolled back, the archive returns. Revert-check: message.internalDate = now(). Add a clock-set-back tap-order case.

**Payoff.** On a slow or reset clock, replies land at the bottom (keeping the tail-append fast path) and failed sends to archived chats restore the archive; fast clocks need the offset.

### `sync-persist-path#5` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Persistence order across batches is arbitrary, but conversation routing depends on order**

Area: Message fetch, processing and persistence path. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Incremental sync gathers new IDs in a Set, hands Array(set) unsorted to the fetch phase and chunks by 50; only each fetched group is sorted by internalDate. With only archived epochs for a participant set, a non-reactivating arrival processed first commits a new active shell that a later INBOX/SENT message joins; the reverse order reactivates the old epoch for both. Across chunks, hash order rather than time picks the epoch. Each message is routed once, and both outcomes are ones the pinned epoch rule already yields chronologically.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/HistoryCollectionPhase.swift:40,64,83,96 — `var allNewMessageIds: Set<String>`, `formUnion(newIds)`, returned as `Array(allNewMessageIds)` on both exits
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:313-315 — `messageFetchPhase.execute(input: historyResult.newMessageIds, ...)` with no sort; BatchProcessor.swift:56 chunks it in that order (`messageBatchSize = 50`, Constants.swift:90)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:245-259, 332-334, 376-378 — `chronologicallySorted` applied per fetched group only; retry successes persist in later, separate calls
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:14, 21-29 and Persistence/MessageConversationRouter.swift:29-32, 56-58 — reactivation only for INBOX/SENT/from-me; an active match always wins, an archived one is returned only when reactivating
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationCreationSerializer.swift:44-73, 107-132 and Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:212 — no match commits a new shell at once with `archivedAt = nil`, so a later INBOX message selects it over the archived epoch; ConversationMerger.swift:145-153 merges only `archivedAt == nil` duplicates
- docs/scalability-review.md:609-623 and 1625, ConversationIdentity.swift:150-154, esc-chatmailTests/Conversation/ConversationRoutingPolicyTests.swift:211-243 — new epoch on a non-INBOX arrival is documented, test-pinned, and listed as an open product decision

**Trigger.** An incremental slice with more than 50 new IDs in which one participant set whose conversations are all archived receives both a reactivating message (INBOX, SENT or from-me) and a received message without INBOX at fetch time (skip-inbox filter, or archived on another device before this one synced), and the two fall in different 50-ID chunks. In the same chunk they are persisted chronologically. Listing paths (initial sync, recovery, reconciliation) are deterministic but process the newest chunk first.

**Impact.** Whether the new mail joins the reactivated old chat or a fresh epoch (older history left behind in the archived one) is decided by Set iteration order for that process, not by time. No message is lost or duplicated and no duplicate active chats result; the same split already happens by design whenever the non-INBOX message is chronologically first. Archived epochs are never merged, so the outcome is permanent. The cost is unpredictable, non-reproducible routing in catch-up slices and a determinism contract that holds only per call.

**Verifier.** Read every cited file whole. No guard found: the orchestrator passes the Set-derived array straight through, and the merger folds only active duplicates. Lowered to low: epoch minting on non-INBOX arrival is deliberate, test-pinned and an open product decision (scalability-review step 12), so nondeterminism only changes which design-legal topology results. "Run to run" is overstated: creation routes once; existing rows reroute only for List-Id repair (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:698-701). Per-process Set order is Swift behavior, not code read.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:609-625 non-inbox-arrival-epoch-growth (the epoch rule, still open, step 12 at line 1625). Ordering across chunks is not covered there.

**Invariant risks**

- Each attempted ID lands in exactly one disposition bucket. The ordered de-duplication needs one seen-set for the whole slice, across all pages. Without it, an ID added again on a later page is fetched and persisted twice. Keep the per-page excludedSendEchoIDs admission (HistoryCollectionPhase.swift:55-63).
- Do not sort the whole slice by internalDate: history records carry none (GmailAPIModels.swift:95-106), so it would mean fetching every message first and losing the 50-ID chunks and batch saves. Do not buffer retry successes either: fetchBatch persists first-attempt successes before it rethrows an account-scoped abort (MessageFetcher.swift:332-341).
- The epoch rule is an open product decision that iOS and the web must keep in parity (scalability-review.md:619-623, step 12). ConversationRoutingPolicyTests:211-243 pins a new epoch for a non-INBOX arrival. Leave shouldReactivateArchivedConversation and selectParticipantHashConversation alone.
- Routing must stay in saveMessages' sequential persist loop (MessagePersister.swift:291-304), never in the concurrent preparation. The cursor, checkpoint and ledger staging are unchanged: this fix only reorders.

**Fix.** HistoryProcessor.extractNewMessageIds should return [String] in first-seen record order (an array plus a seen set). HistoryCollectionPhase should accumulate an ordered array with one seen-set for the whole slice, so an ID repeated across pages appears once. Leave BatchProcessor, fetchBatch, the per-group chronologicallySorted, retry persistence and the routing rules untouched. This brings iOS into line with the web, whose JS Set keeps insertion order and whose slices deliberately follow history order (web/src/sync/incremental.ts:105-119, 502-516). Document on HistoryCollectionResult.newMessageIds and saveMessages: order is chronological within a call, history order across incremental chunks, newest page first on listing paths, and retry successes persist after their chunk. Update HistoryProcessorTests' Set comparisons.

**First step.** Change HistoryProcessor.extractNewMessageIds (HistoryProcessor.swift:50-79) to return [String] in first-seen record order. Make HistoryCollectionPhase.swift:40,64,83,96 accumulate an ordered array plus one seen-set for the whole slice. Turn HistoryProcessorTests' Set expectations into ordered arrays.

**Pinning test.** HistoryCollectionPhaseIntegrationTests: two history pages with 30 or more IDs, one ID repeated across them. Assert newMessageIds equals the exact first-seen array. Revert-check: a Set in HistoryCollectionPhase. With 30 IDs a Set preserving order by chance is negligible.

**Payoff.** Routing in catch-up slices that span several chunks becomes reproducible and matches the web's history-order slices. A random per-process input stops deciding permanent epoch splits, at negligible cost.

## Send and queued actions (10)

### `networking#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**messages.send is one in-process JSON request capped at 60 s, so a slow or backgrounded upload ends as "Delivery unknown"**

Area: Networking and Gmail API client. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

The send session copies the read session's configuration and changes only waitsForConnectivity, so messages.send keeps the 60 s resource timeout. Attachments are base64-wrapped at 64 columns into an in-memory MIME string, base64url-encoded again and posted as one JSON body to users/me/messages/send: about 1.83x the attachment bytes, roughly 46 MB at the 25 MB budget. A post-barrier timeout or cancellation is classified ambiguous, and iOS background expiry cancels even an admitted request. The resulting state is kept indefinitely and offers only Check Delivery.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:116-117,148-152 — read session sets request timeout 30 s and resource timeout NetworkConfig.resourceTimeout; createSendSession copies session.configuration and sets only waitsForConnectivity = false
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:247,369-371 — resourceTimeout is 60.0; sendMessage endpoint is users/me/messages/send (git grep finds no /upload, uploadTask, background session or didSendBodyData anywhere in the app)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/MimeBuilder/MimeBuilder+MultipartMessage.swift:68,76 with Services/Send/GmailSendService.swift:133 and Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:71-73 — attachment base64 at lineLength64 appended to a String, converted to Data, base64url-encoded again, then JSON-encoded into httpBody
- esc-chatmail/Services/Retry/RetryStrategy.swift:114-145 with GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:107-133 — NSURLErrorTimedOut and cancelled are not pre-transmission errors, so sendMessage rethrows them as ambiguousDelivery; GmailAPIClient.swift:483-492 throws without a retry when allowsRetransmission is false
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:133-141,471-480 and Platform/UIKitOutboundBackgroundTaskManager.swift:13 — beginBackgroundTask expiry cancels the worker even after admission; with the barrier persisted the outcome is handleAmbiguousOutcome
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:389-392, Views/Chat/FailedSendRecoveryPolicy.swift:52-57 and ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:1611-1618 — ambiguous state is 'retained indefinitely and is never auto-retried'; the only action is Check Delivery, which runs an incremental sync and then tells the user to check Gmail's Sent folder

**Trigger.** A send with attachments whose whole request (connect, upload, Gmail's response) exceeds 60 s: about 4 to 5 MB of attachments at 1 Mbit/s uplink, the full 25 MB below about 6 Mbit/s. On iOS, also any upload still in flight when UIKit's background allowance (about 30 s) expires after the user locks or leaves the app, for example three unresized photos (about 9 MB, a 16 MB body) under about 4.5 Mbit/s. Text-only sends are unaffected. The Mac lease never expires, so the Mac sees only the 60 s cap.

**Impact.** The bubble ends as "Delivery unknown" for a message whose body never fully reached Gmail. That state is permanent unless a sync echo arrives. It has no Edit and Resend, only Check Delivery, so the user must check Gmail's Sent folder and compose the message and re-pick the attachments by hand. Nothing tracks bytes sent, so a truncated upload cannot be told from a committed send.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited location plus the retry engine, error detector, MIME builder, background lease, recovery UI and docs. Found no guard: no per-request timeout override, no byte-progress tracking, no upload path, no size cap below 25 MB, and images are re-encoded only above 4096 px. Changes: the ratio is about 1.83x, not 1.78x. Classifying expiry as ambiguous is documented and deliberate; the unscaled 60 s cap is only pinned by a test. Not run: URLSession timeout behaviour and Gmail's JSON body limit.

**October review.** Not in docs/scalability-review.md: rate-limit-pacing (line 398) only keeps messages.send off the retrying paths. The rules that apply are in CLAUDE.md, "Outbound send (non-idempotent; never resend)".

**Invariant risks**

- Non-idempotent send (CLAUDE.md, Outbound send): 'fewer body bytes sent than expected means Not sent' would be a new definite error class. If the byte count ever undercounts, Edit and Resend sends the mail twice. Two ways that could happen: CFNetwork re-sends the POST in a fresh transaction, or no metrics are delivered when the task is cancelled. StubURLProtocol cannot show either, so the rule has to be measured on the real network stack, and a send with no per-transaction metrics stays ambiguous.
- Admitted sends are drain-only (OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:41-42 and 219-225; cancelAndAwaitAll at 237-251 waits with no bound). Today the 60 s resource timeout is what bounds a sign-out's drain on the auth-transition gate, so a longer send timeout lengthens that drain. Later chat replies to the same conversation also wait behind the upload in OutboundConversationSendSequencer, which has no timeout. A background URLSession would escape both the drain and the generation fences.
- Transmission barrier: the spool write, and any resumable POST that creates an upload session, must happen before checkCancellation() + beforeTransmission(), never between the barrier and the request. Resuming or re-PUTting a session after a failure is a retransmission path, which CLAUDE.md forbids: cold recovery only converts markers.
- uploadType=media cannot carry threadId, so replies need multipart or resumable metadata, and messageId: must stay in the MIME so sync can match the echo. The spool is account data: never the temp directory, and it must be removed on every outcome, by teardown and by a launch sweep. GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests.swift:467 pins the send session's resource timeout equal to the read session's, so that test must be changed on purpose.

**Fix.** Phase it; change no error class first. (1) Give sendSession its own timeoutIntervalForResource (NetworkConfig.sendResourceTimeout, about 300 s) in createSendSession, keeping the 30 s idle timeout as the stall detector. (2) Only after measuring against a loopback server: run the send through data(for:delegate:) collecting URLSessionTaskMetrics; a pure policy calls it definitely unsent only when metrics arrived, every transaction's countOfRequestBodyBytesSent is below the body length and no response arrived, otherwise ambiguous; a new GmailMessageSendError case maps to the existing post-barrier retained Not sent. (3) Separately: /upload multipart (carries threadId) from a spool written before the barrier; resumable status queries only after measuring Gmail; no background session.

**First step.** Add NetworkConfig.sendResourceTimeout and set it in GmailAPIClient.createSendSession(basedOn:) beside waitsForConnectivity = false, with a why-comment naming the sign-out drain bound. Update GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests.swift:467 to pin the new value.

**Pinning test.** GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests: production sendSession's timeoutIntervalForResource equals NetworkConfig.sendResourceTimeout and exceeds the read session's, request timeout unchanged (Revert-check: createSendSession). Phase 2: a loopback server stalling mid-body yields definite Not sent; full body without response stays ambiguous.

**Payoff.** Attachment sends progressing past 60 s complete instead of ending as permanent 'Delivery unknown'; phase 2 makes truncated uploads, including iOS background expiry, Not sent with Edit and Resend.

### `outbound-and-actions#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**Send transport holds the whole message in memory several times over and must finish in 60 s; slow or backgrounded uploads end as terminal Delivery unknown**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Confirmed as written. A send reads each attachment whole, base64s it into one MIME String, converts to Data, base64url-encodes the whole MIME again (plus three replacingOccurrences passes), and JSON-encodes that as httpBody: about 1.83x the attachment bytes. It goes out as one data task on sendSession, whose configuration is the read session's with only waitsForConnectivity changed, so the 60 s resource timeout bounds the entire upload. A timeout, or the iOS background-expiry cancel of an admitted worker, is post-barrier and recorded as ambiguous.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/ErrorHandling/FileSystemErrorHandler.swift:128 — Data(contentsOf: url); reached per attachment from GmailSendService+Attachments.swift:13 through AttachmentPaths.swift:346-348
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/MimeBuilder/MimeBuilder+Alternative.swift:179-180, 216 — per-attachment base64 String appended to one String, then mime.data(using: .utf8); MimeBuilder.swift:109 routes every reply here, MimeBuilder+MultipartMessage.swift:68-69, 76 is the same shape
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/APIError.swift:115-120 (called from GmailSendService.swift:133) — base64EncodedString plus three replacingOccurrences over the whole MIME; GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:71-73 JSON-encodes it into httpBody
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:117, 148-152, 367 — timeoutIntervalForResource = NetworkConfig.resourceTimeout (Constants.swift:247, 60.0); createSendSession copies the configuration and sets only waitsForConnectivity = false; one transport.data(for:) call; line 69 builds the production client with these defaults
- esc-chatmail/Services/Retry/RetryStrategy.swift:114-145 and Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:107-133 — timedOut and cancellation are not pre-transmission, so ambiguousDelivery; Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:135-141, 491-503 — expiry cancels an admitted worker and the outcome is recorded ambiguous
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/FailedSendRecoveryPolicy.swift:52-58 and Services/Send/OutboundMessageCoordinator.swift:533-535 — Delivery unknown offers only Check Delivery, which is an incremental sync; Services/Utilities/ImageProcessor.swift:9, 32-36 — photos up to 4096 px are attached unrecompressed; Services/Send/OutboundAttachmentContextBuilder.swift:76 enforces the 25 MB budget at send

**Trigger.** Any send whose attachments total more than a few MB when the uplink sustains less than about 0.25 Mbit/s per attachment-MB for 60 s (iOS and Mac), or, on iOS only, when the app is backgrounded or the phone locked before the upload finishes. The ordinary case is three or four 12 MP photos (attached unrecompressed, roughly 8-12 MB, a 15-22 MB body) on cellular; the worst is the 25 MB budget (about 46 MiB body, 6 Mbit/s needed).

**Impact.** The request never completes, so Gmail delivers nothing, but the bubble ends as terminal Delivery unknown. Its only action is Check Delivery, which runs a sync and then tells the user to check Gmail's Sent folder; there is no Edit and resend. Content and attachments stay on the row, so nothing is lost, but the user must recompose (or Forward the bubble, which hits the same limit). Memory is about 34 + 46 + 46 MiB held across the upload at the budget, about 45 MiB for a 10 MB set: unmeasured, and a jetsam concern only near the top of the budget.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited line; all match. No guard found: git grep finds no upload endpoint, upload task or background URLSession, and no request-level timeout override. No doc records the 60 s bound as a decision; GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests.swift:455-467 pins timeout parity only as read settings carried over. The post-barrier ambiguity itself is deliberate and stays. Mac lease never expires, so the expiry half is iOS-only. Not verified: real upload timing, and whether Gmail rejects a 46 MiB JSON raw body outright.

**Invariant risks**

- Never resend: the upload must stay one request on sendSession with allowsRetransmission:false. The temp-file write, metadata and token must come strictly before beforeTransmission (GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:66-80). A background URLSession, or resumable-upload resume PUTs, would add retransmission by the system or by our code and new response classes (308). Each would need explicit classification, because a misclassified one is a duplicate-send hazard.
- Admitted sends are drain-only. OutboundTaskRegistry.cancelAndAwaitAll (OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:237-251) awaits them while the auth-transition gate is held, and the conversation's send turn is held until transmit returns (ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:395-407). A longer resource timeout makes both sign-out and the next reply wait longer, so the cap needs a named constant. Never cancel an admitted send to shorten that wait.
- The 120 s circuit breaker (GmailAPIClient.swift:359-364) throws `lastError ?? APIError.timeout`, and the 401 refresh path continues without setting lastError (444-456). Once an upload can take more than 120 s, a definite 401 rejection comes back as APIError.timeout, which is classified ambiguous (Delivery unknown) instead of Not sent.
- The temp MIME file is account data. Create and remove it inside the registered send, sweep it at launch and in clearMailDerivedCaches (AuthSession.swift:975), and have its remover refuse any path outside its own directory (the PastedImageFile.remove precedent). Keep one MimeBuilder definition writing through a sink, so the deterministic Message-ID header and the bytes cannot drift from the String build.

**Fix.** Phase it, keeping the barrier, marker and ambiguous classification untouched. 1 (S): give sendSession its own timeoutIntervalForResource (named cap, e.g. 10 min) and rely on the 30 s idle timeout for stalls; make the 120 s breaker never turn a definite 401 into APIError.timeout. 2 (M): one MimeBuilder definition writing to a sink; stream attachments in 48-byte-multiple chunks into a temp file before beforeTransmission, then one upload(fromFile:) to upload/…/messages/send?uploadType=multipart (threadId in metadata), allowsRetransmission:false. Remove the file on every exit; sweep at launch and in clearMailDerivedCaches. 3: iOS background is a separate decision (BGContinuedProcessingTask on iOS 26; reject background URLSession).

**First step.** In GmailAPIClient.createSendSession set timeoutIntervalForResource from a new NetworkConfig.sendResourceTimeout, assign lastError before the 401 path's continue (GmailAPIClient.swift:456), and deliberately update the resource-timeout equality in testSendSession_productionClient_doesNotWaitForConnectivityButKeepsReadSettings.

**Pinning test.** GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests: the send session's resource timeout is sendResourceTimeout while reads keep 60 s; a 401 then breaker trip throws a definite error (needs an injectable breaker clock). MimeBuilder: file-sink bytes equal the String build for 0/47/48/49-byte attachments.

**Payoff.** Multi-photo sends on slow uplinks (every Mac send, iOS while foreground) deliver instead of ending terminal Delivery unknown, and send memory stops scaling with attachment size.

### `outbound-and-actions#3` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**A pending action's five retries are spent in one burst inside the exclusive store run; a minute of 5xx or 429 abandons the queue head, then each action behind it**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

The loop refetches the oldest pending/failed row (retryCount < 5, no due time) straight after an in-run sleep of 2/4/8/16 s. Each executor call is three HTTP attempts (1 s, 2 s backoff), so 15 consecutive 5xx, rate-limit or fast transport failures abandon the head in about 45 s; after a 30 s sleep the next row follows roughly every 75 s. Only auth, revoked credentials, quota and cancellation stop the run without spending budget. The exclusive run is held throughout: foreground sync parks behind it, a BGTask sync returns .blocked.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionProcessor.swift:151-168 — fetchNextPendingAction: status pending OR (failed AND retryCount < maxRetries), oldest createdAt first, fetchLimit 1, no time predicate; the model's PendingAction entity (ESCChatmail 6.xcdatamodel/contents:85-100) has retryCount and lastAttempt, no next-retry attribute
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionProcessor.swift:237-258 and 339-353 — a retryable failure writes retryCount+1 and 'failed', or 'abandoned' at 5; then sleeps min(2*2^retryCount, 30) s inside the run and returns .continueRun, so the 30 s sleep also runs after the abandonment
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionProcessor.swift:4-8, 262-273, 307-318 — header comment says a run-level condition must not burn budget; only authenticationError/credentialsRevoked/quotaExhausted map to stopRun; non-APIError errors (raw URLError, TokenManagerError) return shouldRetry true; APIError uses isRetriableSameRequest (rateLimited, timeout, networkError, 5xx per Services/ErrorHandling/APIErrorRecovery.swift:41-52)
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManager.swift:63-64, 815, 826, 846, 871-903 — maxRetries 5, baseRetryDelay 2 s; isConnected read before the loop only; the while loop runs inside the task registered with the exclusive .pendingActions run, ended only after the task returns
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:116-118, 395-398, 420-439, 471-512 with Services/Config/Constants.swift:244-260 — waitsForConnectivity true, 30 s request / 60 s resource timeout, 3 attempts with 1 s then 2 s backoff, 120 s total budget; a breaker-tripped 429 and a 5xx both end as a thrown retriable error after three attempts; transport errors are rethrown raw
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:122-131, 162-176 and Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:265-267, 316-319 — a foreground sync that finds the boundary held waits for idle and asks again; a background sync returns .blocked(by:). Services/PendingActions/PendingActionQueries.swift:345-360 — banner Retry resets status and retryCount; Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:810-836 with HistoryProcessor+LabelOperations.swift:55-70 — after 30 min the local-modification guard lapses and reconciliation re-adds INBOX

**Trigger.** The app is running, an action is queued or made while NWPath reads satisfied, and every request fails for about 45 s (Gmail 5xx, 403 rateLimitExceeded, a tripped 429 breaker, or TLS/DNS/refused connections on a captive or dead network), about 80 s (429 with no Retry-After), about 8 min (30 s timeouts on a dead path) or about 10.5 min (path lost after the run started). A path already unsatisfied when the run would start spends nothing.

**Impact.** Queued archive, Report Spam, read-state and star changes stop being sent automatically: each row becomes 'abandoned', the list shows "N changes didn't reach Gmail", and only the banner's Retry (budget reset to 0) revives it. If the user does not retry within 30 minutes, label reconciliation restores Gmail's state locally, so an archived chat returns to the inbox. Sync is held off for the length of the burst (about 75 s per abandoned row on fast failures, up to 10 min per row on timeouts), which costs little during an outage sync would also fail in.

**Verifier.** Read processor, manager, queries, executor, retry engine, RetryStrategy, run coordinator, foreground coordinator, model v6. No guard found: no other retryCount writer, no in-loop connectivity check, no due-time column. Not a documented decision, and not in the prior review. Tightened: foreground sync is parked and re-requested, not dropped; abandonment is recoverable through the banner. A failed pre-request token refresh also spends budget. Durations are computed from constants, not run. Severity sits at the low edge of high.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1514 covers abandoned-row surfacing, a neighbouring item. Step 10 batches schema changes into ESCChatmail 7. Neither covers the retry burst.

**Invariant risks**

- Strict FIFO: the auditor's 'select only due rows' lets a later markUnread or unstar overtake an earlier markRead or star on the same message (PendingActionProcessor.swift:158 is oldest-first today), which inverts Gmail's final state. Gate the whole queue on the head instead.
- A transient stop that spends no budget wedges the whole queue for good behind one row that keeps getting a 5xx. Keep a bounded per-row budget, spent at most once per out-of-run cycle.
- A new out-of-run gate must be added to every gate site: scheduleProcessing, processAllPendingActions (called at every foreground start), clearPendingTask, currentOutcome's stale-verdict mapping to .skipped, and resetRetryStateForAccountTransition and stopMonitoring. Otherwise it hot-loops, or the old account's backoff gates the replacement account's queue.
- Keep network processing in the exclusive .pendingActions run, not the uncancellable lease that teardown drains. Never bump localModifiedAt to stretch the 30-minute guard, because clearLocalModifications clears only markers <= createdAt. Any nextRetryAt goes in the batched ESCChatmail 7, never in v6.

**Fix.** No schema change at first. In processAction, send transient failures (isRetriableSameRequest, raw URLError, unknown errors) to a new .stopRun(.transientFailure(retryAfter:)). That path spends at most one retryCount unit, or none if the monitor now reads offline, drops the in-run sleep and ends the run, which frees the exclusive boundary. In PendingActionsManager, add a fourth bounded timer modelled on scheduleQuotaRetry: injectable base about 30 s, cap about 15 min, honours Retry-After, reset on .completed. Wire it into every gate and both account-boundary resets. Keep processing strictly oldest-first. Later, in ESCChatmail 7, persist nextRetryAt and hold the whole queue on the head's due time.

**First step.** Add .transientFailure(retryAfter:) to PendingActionRunStopReason and to the private processing outcome. Route retriable APIError and URLError failures there in processAction, spending one unit with no sleep. Add the quota-style timer with an injectable sleeper.

**Pinning test.** PendingActionsManagerTests, with a serverError(503) executor and an injected sleeper: one execute per cycle, retryCount 1, isBoundaryHeld() false while the timer waits. A transition reset cancels the timer. markRead then markUnread on one message never run out of order.

**Payoff.** A one-minute Gmail 5xx or 429 blip, or a captive network, no longer abandons queued archive, spam and read changes. Sync no longer parks behind backoff sleeps taken inside the run.

### `background-energy#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Background wakes are inbound-only: the pending-action queue has no background owner and its conflict shield lapses after 30 minutes**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

BGTask workers run only the incremental sync. On a cold background launch nothing drains PendingActions: the manager starts its network monitor lazily, and the restore hook rescans only parked work. The conflict shield is localModifiedAt's age alone (30 min), not whether a live PendingAction names the message. So label reconciliation, which also runs on app-refresh budgets, re-adds INBOX and resets isUnread to Gmail's value on queued archive and read changes. The rollup then clears archivedAt. Report Spam is not re-inboxed: a local SPAM label skips the message.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:314-317 — the worker calls only executor.performIncrementalSyncForBackground; no pending-action drain
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManager.swift:154-170, 377-407 — the network monitor starts only in ensureInitialized; authenticationDidRecover rescans only if hadParkedWork, deliberately so it cannot race a cold BGTask launch
- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:454-468 — the only lifecycle drain is at foreground session start, then a forced follow-up sync
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor+LabelOperations.swift:55-70 — the shield checks age > maxLocalModificationAge only (Constants.swift:200, 1800 s); no PendingAction lookup
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:576-583, 809-861 — Gmail's 100 newest non-spam messages from 24 h; a stale marker lets it re-add INBOX (833-835) and overwrite isUnread (856-858); a local SPAM label skips the message (824-828)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:57-64 — a rollup with hasInbox clears archivedAt and hidden, which unarchives the chat

**Trigger.** Archive or mark-read made offline, or cut off by suspension. The system then kills the process, and a background wake runs label reconciliation (TTL 20 min, or 1 h when quiet) more than 30 minutes after the action. The message must be among Gmail's 100 newest from the last 24 h. The same revert can happen in the foreground when the immediate sync wins the race against the startup drain.

**Impact.** Gmail and other devices do not see the action until the next foreground. Locally archived chats come back in the inbox and read mail turns unread. On foreground the drain runs, and the forced follow-up sync re-applies the action through history, so the visible revert lasts about one sync cycle. Abandoned actions are not stranded: retries run within the same run.

**Verifier.** The code matches the claim, with corrections. Spam is not reverted, because a local SPAM label makes reconciliation skip the message. The authentication retry backs off from 30 s to at most 5 min, not 15-60 min; only the quota retry waits 15-60 min. Mitigations: a warm process resumes its drain task or gets a connectivity edge during a background wake. This is not documented as a decision: the scalability review assumes "localModifiedAt blocks remote label replay during the pending window", and clearLocalModifications already asks about live PendingAction rows while the shield does not.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:93 (review correction: the localModifiedAt guard lapses after 30 min); related, not built: bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored, step 8 (label reconciliation still runs under .appRefresh)

**Invariant risks**

- Calling processAllPendingActions from the BGTask worker runs ensureInitialized (PendingActionsManager.swift:154-170). That starts the network monitor and spawns an unstructured recover/requeue task, which takes the exclusive .pendingActions run. The background sync takes its run without waiting (SyncEngine.swift:510), so it then returns .blocked and the slot is burned. This is the race authenticationDidRecover's hadParkedWork gate (377-407) exists to prevent; keep that gate.
- BGTask expiration would not stop a drain started that way. The run's task is unstructured (494), acquirePendingActionRunTask parks in waitUntilIdle, which cannot be cancelled, and a retryable failure sleeps up to 30 s (PendingActionProcessor.swift:254) inside a refresh window of about 30 s. Use acquireRunWithTask together with withTaskCancellationHandler, as SyncEngine.swift:289-293 does.
- A label change that history processing skips is lost for good, because the cursor still advances past it. That includes the excluded-mailbox delete branch (LabelOperationProcessor.swift:105-117). So add the live-action check to label reconciliation only, OR'd with the age check, which covers the gap between the local save and the enqueue.
- A failed read of PendingAction rows does not mean 'no live actions'. On that failure, repair nothing and return .incomplete, so that lastReconciliationTime is not recorded. The drain's outcome must never change the BGTask's success value, its backoff or the sync cursor.

**Fix.** Ship two separate changes, the shield first. (1) In SyncReconciliation.processReconciliationMismatches, inside the same perform, fetch the live PendingAction rows (pending, processing, failed) as dictionaries. Find their targets with executedTargetMessageIDs, moved into one shared helper. Skip a message when its age shield holds OR a live action names it. If that fetch fails, repair nothing and return incomplete. Leave LabelOperationProcessor and MessagePersister on the age check alone. (2) Add a budgeted drainForBackgroundTask that skips ensureInitialized, respects the park, quota and auth gates, takes acquireRunWithTask, forwards cancellation, caps the number of actions and never sleeps a backoff. Call it in performAuthoritativeSync after the auth guard and before the sync, and ignore its outcome. Leave out the scene-background assertion.

**First step.** Move PendingActionProcessor.executedTargetMessageIDs into a shared helper. Then add the live-action fetch and the OR'd skip to processReconciliationMismatches, where a failed fetch returns incomplete. Ship that alone, before touching BackgroundSyncManager.

**Pinning test.** SyncReconciliationTests: a message archived and read locally, stamped two hours ago, with a live archiveConversation action naming it, and a Gmail stub saying INBOX and UNREAD. Reconciliation leaves both alone. With the action abandoned, INBOX comes back. Revert-check: the live-action skip.

**Payoff.** Archived and read chats no longer come back after a 30-minute gap. Gmail and other devices see queued actions at the next background wake, not the next time the app is opened.

### `outbound-and-actions#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Delivery unknown never converges when Gmail did not receive the message: nothing looks up the deterministic Message-ID**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Mechanism confirmed. A post-barrier timeout, dropped connection, 5xx, cancellation, background expiry or cold restart writes the ambiguous marker; only a synced echo carrying the deterministic Message-ID consumes it. Nothing else downgrades or removes it: Check Delivery is an incremental sync, Edit and Resend requires notSent, and no lookup by Message-ID exists. While it lives, its conversation is skipped by merges, row repair and re-homing (a blocked pass retries every cleanup), and every SPAM/DRAFT/TRASH history arrival is fetched in full. Indefinite retention is a documented choice, so severity is medium.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:389-405, 1343-1371 — recordAmbiguousRemoteSend is documented 'retained indefinitely and is never auto-retried'; cold recovery converts an in-flight record to ambiguous and only logs for one already ambiguous. :485-525 is the only writer of the notSent marker and no ambiguous path calls it.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:133-141, 471-503, 589-614 — background-time expiry cancels an admitted request ('durable marker makes cancellation ambiguous'); post-barrier ambiguous errors and cancellation go to handleAmbiguousOutcome, which also marks the attachments uploaded.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundMessageCoordinator.swift:533-535 and esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:1611-1618 — checkDelivery is performIncrementalSync; a row still deliveryUnknown afterwards only raises 'Check Gmail's Sent folder before sending again'.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/ChatReplyDraftStore.swift:188-192, 216-220 and esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesView.swift:1000-1022 — recover and forwardRecoveryContext throw notDefinitelyUnsent unless the state is notSent; the row's menu offers Check delivery and Forward, with no edit, resend or delete.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor.swift:101-136, esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:423-431 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:164-199, 1019-1025 — an in-flight or ambiguous marker admits every excluded-label candidate on a history page; every record of any state anchors its conversation; a blocked pass leaves its flag clear and retries (the contact-link hash alone is still written in place, :180-184).
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:116-117, 148-151, 367, esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:247 and esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:107-133 — the send session copies a 60 s whole-resource timeout, the send is one data(for:) request, and a timeout or non-pre-transmission transport error is classified ambiguous.

**Trigger.** A send fails ambiguously after the barrier without reaching Gmail: the 60 s whole-request timeout on the single-shot base64 upload (large attachment on a slow uplink), a stalled or dropped connection, background-time expiry while the upload is still running, or a process kill after the admission marker was saved.

**Impact.** The bubble reads Delivery unknown permanently. It cannot be edited, resent or dismissed, so the user checks Gmail and writes the reply again, re-adding attachments (Forward of the row is the only in-app shortcut). For each stuck row, its conversation is never merged, row-repaired or re-homed, a cleanup pass it blocks reruns at every cleanup, and sync fetches every spam, draft and trash arrival in full. There is no data loss, no duplicate send and no cross-account effect.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited site plus the orchestrator, API client and cleanup callers; found no guard, expiry or downgrade path, and git grep for rfc822msgid returns nothing. Changes: severity high to medium (no data loss, honest UI, cost is mostly the documented never-retry decision; scalability-review.md:1496 says never delete these records). Contact-link hash is still given to anchored chats. Caveat on the fix: search absence is not proof of non-delivery, and history sync already covers the found case.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1496 (Hygiene, "Not-sent and delivery-unknown send records are re-walked…"). It notes that records "live until the user acts or an echo arrives" and that they should never be deleted or auto-retried. It covers the main-actor re-walk only, is not built, and offers no convergence path.

**Invariant risks**

- Legacy ambiguous records must never become retryable. The cold path converts pre-04d76ce6 (2026-08-11) sends, whose MIME carried another Message-ID, and stamps the deterministic ID on them locally (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:734-752, 1405-1428). An rfc822msgid miss therefore proves nothing for them, and no stored field tells them apart today.
- Non-idempotent send: never touch in-flight records, which the recommendation includes. An in-flight marker belongs to a live send until cold recovery converts it. Downgrading it mid-upload would offer Edit and Resend while Gmail can still commit the request. Only terminal ambiguous records qualify, after a quiet period far past the 60 s resource timeout.
- Sync staging and the account boundary: the probe runs inside the exclusive incremental run. A found echo persists only through MessagePersister.saveMessages in the run's context, and the downgrade is staged for the orchestrator's save point. API errors and cancellation give no verdict, and account-scoped errors abort the run. No write may come from a probe answered after an account transition.
- The downgrade must equal retainDefinitelyUnsent's effects: notSent marker, attachments .failed, forward envelope withoutRecoverySource (:587-591, 514-517). It must be compare-and-set from ambiguous only. A new marker string instead would need every reader updated (deliveryState defaults to .none, so a missed reader shows the row as delivered; isLocalMarker; HistoryProcessor; the MessagePersister+Helpers marker list).

**Fix.** Probe, never retransmit. In ESCChatmail 7 (step 10), add an optional OutboundSendMutationRecord.admittedAt, set in recordRemoteSendState's in-flight transaction; records without it (legacy MIME, pre-version) stay ambiguous. At the end of ReconciliationPhase (not under appRefresh, a few records per run), for ambiguous records admitted at least 1 h before the run started, list `rfc822msgid:<id> in:anywhere`. Hit: fetch and saveMessages in the run's context, which consumes the marker. Empty: stage a compare-and-set from ambiguous to notSent in the sync context, through a helper factored out of recordRemoteSendState (attachments failed, forward source cleared), committed at the orchestrator's save point. Error or cancellation: no verdict; account-scoped errors abort the run. Never probe in-flight records.

**First step.** Write a pure DeliveryUnknownProbePolicy with unit tests, before touching sync or the schema. Eligible: ambiguous marker, admittedAt set, at least 1 h before the run started, not app refresh. Verdict: hit means persist, empty means downgrade, error or cancellation means none.

**Pinning test.** A run test with MockGmailAPIClient: an ambiguous record over 1 h old with an empty rfc822msgid list becomes notSent, and ChatReplyDraftStore.recover then succeeds. Legacy (no admittedAt), recent, list-error and cancelled records stay ambiguous; a hit is consumed.

**Payoff.** A Delivery-unknown row that Gmail provably never received becomes Edit-and-Resendable. Its excluded-label full fetches stop, and the user can act to release the conversation anchor. Duplicate sends still need an explicit user resend.

### `outbound-and-actions#4` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**A queued action's local effect is guarded by a 30-minute timestamp, not by the queue, and the action row is saved separately from the change it describes**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Archive/read/star save the change on a background context, then insert the PendingAction in a separate viewContext save; nothing recovers a marker with no action row. Sync protects a local change only while localModifiedAt is under 30 minutes old and never asks whether an action is still live. When a sync runs before the drain (BGTask syncs never request one; foreground start requests sync first), label reconciliation re-adds INBOX and restores unread on recent messages and un-archives the conversation. It self-heals once the drain and a following sync run.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/MessageActions.swift:256-275, 433-445 — the read/archive/star change is saved on a new background context and returns the Gmail ID; only afterwards is pendingActionsManager.queueAction awaited (several actor hops later)
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManager.swift:666-681, 705-717 — the action row is inserted and saved on coreDataStack.viewContext; a failed save is a Log.error. NSManagedObjectContext+Perform.swift:30-39 — saveOrLog does not roll back, so the unsaved row stays in the view context
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/HistoryProcessor+LabelOperations.swift:55-71 and Services/Config/Constants.swift:198-200 — hasPendingLocalModification returns false once the marker is older than 1800 s; no PendingAction lookup. ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:273-282 restores only a marker newer than the sync context's, so it does not cover a stale one
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:576-583, 809-861 — lists up to 100 Gmail messages of the last 24 h, skips only fresh markers, else re-adds or removes INBOX and overwrites isUnread; 823-828 skips the INBOX re-add when the local row carries SPAM
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:53-64 — a rollup with hasInbox clears archivedAt and hidden (the chat returns). Services/Sync/LabelOperationProcessor.swift:104-108, 131-134 — a later history label removal is applied once no fresh marker blocks it (the self-heal)
- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:449-466 — sync is requested first, the drain in a later Task, then a forced sync after the drain. Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:317 — the BGTask worker only calls performIncrementalSyncForBackground. PendingActionsManager.swift:163-168, 389-406 — drains are otherwise scheduled by connectivity regain and parked-auth recovery

**Trigger.** A queued archive or mark-read older than 30 minutes (offline triage, or the app suspended before the drain finished) on a message among Gmail's 100 most recent of the last 24 hours, with label reconciliation due (20 minutes after history changes, 60 minutes when quiet), and a sync taking the run before the drain: a cold BGTask launch, or a foreground start where the sync wins the race. Separately, a process kill between the mutation save and the action-row save.

**Impact.** Archived chats return to the list and read mail shows unread again until the queue drains and the next sync replays Gmail's history; after a background refresh that lasts until the app is next opened. Report Spam is not reverted by reconciliation. No lasting divergence while the action stays live. A kill between the two saves leaves an archive, read or star Gmail never receives: after 30 minutes it is silently undone on recent mail and stays divergent on older mail.

**Verifier.** Read every cited site plus rollup, label processor, run coordinator and foreground/background entry. Code is as described; no queue-liveness guard exists. Changed: the revert is transient and limited to the recent-100/24h window; spam is skipped; a failed action-row save is not rolled back, so the row rides the next viewContext save; connectivity regain can drain in a warm background wake; cited BackgroundSyncManager lines 452-455 do not show the no-drain claim. The TTL itself is documented.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:93 (archive/spam batchModify "Review correction" notes the 30-minute lapse only as a reason to cap requeue age); :1654 "localModifiedAt is cleared". No item covers reconciliation reverting a live action or the two-save enqueue.

**Invariant risks**

- Never drain the queue from inside a sync run or a lease. The drain needs the exclusive boundary (SyncRunCoordinator.swift:190-192, PendingActionsManager.swift:473-505), so it would deadlock.
