In BGAppRefresh its backoff sleeps of up to 30 s (PendingActionProcessor.swift:247-256) and the BGTask-slot race described at PendingActionsManager.swift:378-388 also argue against it.
- Do not drop the 30-minute escape or widen liveness to every guard. A failed marker clear or an abandoned action would then diverge for good, and LabelOperationProcessor.swift:104-108 skips the whole history item, so unrelated label changes would be lost as the cursor advances.
- A failed PendingAction read is never 'no live actions'. It must fail closed: processingFailed, outcome .incomplete, so lastReconciliationTime is not recorded. Reconciliation must stay a read inside the sync context and never save it.
- The outbox createdAt must be >= the markers it covers, because clearLocalModifications clears only localModifiedAt <= createdAt (PendingActionProcessor.swift:416-421). The combined save stays inside the conversation's turn under the held lease and asks for no gate. The manager signal goes after the perform.

**Fix.** Sync side first, additive. In SyncReconciliation.processReconciliationMismatches, inside the perform that fetches local messages, read live PendingAction rows (pending, processing, failed under maxRetries) and their target IDs via PendingActionProcessor's executedTargetMessageIDs, made a shared nonisolated helper. Skip INBOX/UNREAD repair for those IDs, in addition to the fresh-marker skip. A failed read sets processingFailed and changes nothing. Optionally give MessagePersister+Updates' preserve check the same set. Keep LabelOperationProcessor and the 30-minute escape unchanged. Then the outbox: insert the PendingAction in MessageActions' background context and save it with the mutation, with createdAt at the marker's date, roll both back on failure, then signal the manager. Add no drain inside a run.

**First step.** Turn PendingActionProcessor.executedTargetMessageIDs into a nonisolated helper that returns live actions' target IDs for a context and throws on a failed read. Call it in processReconciliationMismatches and skip INBOX/UNREAD repair for those IDs.

**Pinning test.** SyncReconciliationTests: a message is archived and marked read locally, with localModifiedAt 31 minutes old and a live archive+markRead row naming it, while Gmail reports INBOX+UNREAD. After reconciliation it is still archived and read. Revert-check: the live-action skip.

**Payoff.** Archived chats no longer come back, and read mail no longer turns unread, after a BGTask or launch sync while actions are queued. A process kill between the two saves can no longer lose an action.

### `outbound-and-actions#5` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Unsent text is not durable: New Message and Forward store nothing, and reply autosave and the tap-to-bubble window queue on a global mutex**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The compose half stands: ComposeViewModel keeps recipients, subject, body and attachments only in memory, and nothing persists or restores a compose sheet, so a process kill with New Message or Forward open loses it. The reply half is narrower than stated. Text autosaved before the tap stays in ChatReplyDraft until the optimistic save removes it in the same transaction, and a save is also scheduled on scene-inactive. Only text typed since the last completed autosave is memory-only during a gate hold. Gate latency is a documented cost and a prior review item.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ComposeViewModel.swift:30-31, 352-365 — subject and body are @Published only; presentationDidDisappear calls discard(), which clears attachments; the file (read whole) writes no draft to any store
- esc-chatmail/Views/Main/ConversationListView.swift:171-173 and Views/Compose/ComposeView.swift:196 — the New Message sheet is built with mode .newMessage and discards on disappear; git grep finds no call site for .newEmail and no SceneStorage/NSUserActivity restoration in esc-chatmail
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:348-351, 1345-1351, 1369 — the 350 ms debounced reply save runs through performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation and writes nothing while composerState.isSending
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/ChatReplyDraftStore.swift:152-158 and Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1464-1472 — the stored draft is removed inside the optimistic-message save: "A crash leaves either the draft or the durable send"
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatView.swift:254-256 — scenePhase != .active calls viewModel.scheduleReplyDraftSave()
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:351-381 and docs/scalability-review.md:928-930, 1558 — maintenance takes the gate once per pass ("waits for at most one pass"); bubble lag behind the gate and a send holding the gate while it waits for a turn are already recorded

**Trigger.** iOS reclaims the suspended app, or it crashes, while a New Message or Forward sheet holds typed content. For chat replies: process death during a cleanup-gate hold, which loses only the text typed since the last completed autosave (including a reply typed and tapped within that window).

**Impact.** At relaunch the New Message text and recipients, or a forward's note and recipients, are gone with the picked attachments. A chat reply loses at most its unsaved tail, or all of a reply typed and tapped inside the debounce. During a gate hold a tapped reply shows an empty field and no bubble until the holder finishes; that lag is the prior review's item, limited to one maintenance pass per hold.

**Verifier.** Read ComposeViewModel whole, the reply draft path, the serializer, the gate's holders and the coordinator. Guards the auditor missed: the scene-inactive reply save, the draft removed atomically with the optimistic save, and runFullCleanup being one-shot (InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:275-280). The compose gap is new and no doc records it as a decision. The shared/exclusive gate fix is unproven: optimistic creation awaits inside the gate (OptimisticUpdates.swift:58-62). Hold times were not measured.

**October review.** Compose drafts are in no doc. Gate holds: six-hour-maintenance-inside-sync-run (scalability-review.md:926-934; step 9 built per-pass holds), participant-split-migration-walk (:951-961, open), version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation (:1053-1057, open)

**Invariant risks**

- Shared/exclusive gate breaks gate-then-turn anchoring: a send suspends inside the gate (alias load and turn wait, GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:58-66, 106), so sends are not serialized by the main actor. Shared holders would also still queue behind an exclusive cleanup pass (DataCleanupService.swift:371-381), so the latency is not cut.
- Account boundary: a new store entity must join accountScopedEntityNames (AuthSession.swift:170-183), and every write must check authSession.userEmail == draftAccountEmail as reply drafts do (ChatViewModel.swift:1369-1370). A file-based draft would be a new on-disk store of mail data that needs sign-out cleanup, tombstones and the Mac tripwire.
- Attachments saved with no owner match AttachmentPredicates.orphaned (message == nil AND replyDraft == nil). The lease is in memory only, so after a relaunch the daily deleteOrphanedAttachments batch-deletes those rows (DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:94-108) and the file sweep then removes the local_ originals.
- Send transaction: remove the compose draft in the optimistic save and restore it in the rollBackToComposer save, never at admission. Otherwise a crash leaves both a Not-sent message and a draft. Writing a ChatReplyDraft outside the gate breaks the cleanup anchor snapshot (DataCleanupService.swift:351-361). Never edit the shipped v6 model.

**Fix.** Keep the gate as it is: shared mode breaks anchoring and still waits behind exclusive passes. Shorten the gate holds through the open review items instead. For compose, add a ComposeDraft entity in a new model version. It stores JSON (mode, recipients, subject, body, StoredForwardEnvelope, recoveredMessageID) and owns its attachments through a new Attachment.composeDraft inverse. Save it on a debounce and on scene-inactive, inside performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation, with the reply draft's account, isSending and hasDiscarded checks. Delete it in persistOptimisticSendMutationAndGraph's save and restore it in the rollBackToComposer save. Delete it on Cancel, swipe-away or send, not on onDisappear alone. Re-present the sheet after the launch restore has authenticated.

**First step.** Cut ESCChatmail 7 (a new version directory plus the .xccurrentversion bump; v6 untouched) with ComposeDraft and an optional Attachment.composeDraft. Add the entity to accountScopedEntityNames, add composeDraft == nil to AttachmentPredicates.orphaned, and pin the v6-to-v7 lightweight migration with a test.

**Pinning test.** ComposeDraftStoreTests on TestCoreDataStack: type into ComposeViewModel and await the save. On a fresh context, assert that recipients, body and draft-owned attachments come back. deleteOrphanedAttachments keeps them. The optimistic save removes the row, and rollBackToComposer restores it (Revert-check).

**Payoff.** New Message and Forward text, recipients and attachments survive jetsam, a crash or a Mac quit. Reply drafts keep their anchor and FIFO guarantees, with no gate redesign that would not have cut the latency anyway.

### `invariant-enforcement#4` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Never-resend at messages.send depends on defaulted parameters and catch-all error classification**

Area: Invariant enforcement, complexity budget and change safety. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The gap is narrower than claimed. The only production send route passes the Message-ID and the barrier, because it calls through ComposeSendServicing, whose requirements have no defaults. The real client sends with retransmission off. Unknown failures that are not APIError are already treated as ambiguous. What remains: an APIError case missing from both switches falls to `default:` and is treated as definite, both in isAmbiguousSendFailure and again in mapSendError. A future ambiguous case would therefore show as "Not sent" with Edit and Resend. The GmailSendService defaults and a barrier-free protocol overload, used only by tests, still let a new direct caller skip both.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:116-132 — an APIError not in the list hits `default: return false` (definite); any other error type returns `!ConnectionErrorDetector.isPreTransmissionError(error)`, so it is ambiguous unless proven pre-transmission (RetryStrategy.swift:114-153 is an allowlist that defaults to false).
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService.swift:144-177 — GmailMessageSendError.ambiguousDelivery becomes SendError.ambiguousDelivery. A raw APIError reaches mapSendError only after the client called it definite, and mapSendError again lists serverError/timeout/decodingError/networkError, then `default: .apiError`. Both switches must miss a case for it to go wrong.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:13-36, 361-390 — protocol requirements with no defaults; the one caller passes `MimeBuilder.messageId(forOptimisticMessageID:)` and the barrier. Lines 329-335: a nil `transmissionAdmission` falls back to the durable `recordRemoteSendAdmission`, so that default is the safe one.
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClientProtocol.swift:94-100 — a protocol-extension `sendMessage(rawMessage:threadId:)` that passes `beforeTransmission: {}`; it is called only from GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests.swift:144-320. GmailSendService.swift:51-52, 92-93 default `messageId` to nil and the barrier to `{}`.
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:237-241 — `allowsRetransmission: Bool = true`; GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:94-98 is the only caller passing false, and every other caller is a read or a label change that is safe to repeat.
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/FailedSendRecoveryPolicy.swift:45-50 — `.notSent` offers Edit and Resend, which is where a misclassified ambiguous send could be sent a second time.

**Trigger.** Someone adds an APIError case for an outcome that may have reached Gmail, the retry engine throws it on the send path, and it goes into neither isAmbiguousSendFailure nor mapSendError. Or new code calls GmailSendService.sendNew/sendReply directly, relying on the defaulted messageId and barrier.

**Impact.** Latent; no current path misclassifies. If the trigger happens, a send Gmail may have committed is kept as "Not sent", and the user's explicit Edit and Resend can deliver it twice. A direct caller that relies on the defaults gets a random Message-ID, so its echo never matches, and no durable admission marker.

**Verifier.** Read every cited line. Refuted parts: "a new error type after the barrier" is already handled safely by the fallback for non-APIError errors. The orchestrator's defaults are safe: the disposition applies only before the barrier, and a nil admission closure writes the durable marker. The retransmission default is right for every other endpoint. APIError.networkError is thrown only on the History path. All 13 cases classify correctly today, and GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests pins each one. No doc calls the `default:` deliberate. isAccountScopedSyncAbort is about sync and outside this finding.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md:98-102 "Outbound send (non-idempotent; never resend)" lists the ambiguous classes by hand. Not an item in docs/scalability-review.md: only rate-limit-pacing's "Keep intact" (line 398) mentions messages.send.

**Invariant risks**

- Flipping the `allowsRetransmission` default to false on `performRequestWithRetry`, instead of making it required, would strip 5xx and timeout retries from every read and label change (GmailAPIClient.swift:424, 483-487). Transient errors would then become `.failed` verdicts that freeze the sync cursor and abandon pending actions.
- The rule 'anything unclassified is ambiguous' must apply only after the barrier. Pre-barrier failures arrive raw via `transmissionNotStarted` (GmailSendService.swift:146-147), and `TransmissionBarrierState.isPersisted` plus the disposition decide them. Calling them ambiguous would record delivery-unknown with no admission marker, and offline replies would lose Edit and Resend.
- Pre-transmission URLErrors, `RetryCancelledBeforeRetransmission`, 401, 429 and the rate-limit 403 must stay definite. The new property must not replace the retry engine's own retransmission test (GmailAPIClient.swift:483-486). Treating those cases as 'conservatively ambiguous' regresses `testSendMessage_persistentNoDataPathRefusal_failsDefinitelyNotAmbiguous` and `testProductionOfflineSend_notConnectedToInternet_retainsMessageAsNotSent`.
- Removing the `messageId` default must not add a fallback ID, because only `MimeBuilder.messageId(forOptimisticMessageID:)` lets sync match the echo. Keep the nil default of `transmissionAdmission`: its fallback is the durable `recordRemoteSendAdmission`. If `isAccountScopedSyncAbort` is touched, keep exactly auth, revoked and quota (sync invariant).

**Fix.** Add one exhaustive `APIError.nonIdempotentSendProof` (no `default:`; history-only cases count as may-have-committed) beside `recoveryAction` in APIErrorRecovery.swift. `isAmbiguousSendFailure` and `mapSendError` both read it, and `mapSendError` keeps its messages. Invert the last catch in GmailSendService.sendMessage: only pre-transmission errors and `RetryCancelledBeforeRetransmission` become `.apiError`, anything else `.ambiguousDelivery` (no change for the real client). Then make `messageId: String` and `beforeTransmission` required on ComposeSendServicing, GmailSendService and GmailAPIClient, delete the protocol-extension overload, and make `allowsRetransmission` required, with reads passing true. Leave the orchestrator's isPersisted matrix alone and update CLAUDE.md:102. `invalidData` also covers a 2xx error body (GmailAPIClient.swift:271-274): keep it definite here.

**First step.** Add an exhaustive `APIError.nonIdempotentSendProof` beside `recoveryAction` in APIErrorRecovery.swift. Route `GmailAPIClient.isAmbiguousSendFailure` and `GmailSendService.mapSendError` through it without changing behavior. Run GmailAPIClientRetransmissionTests, GmailSendServiceTests and GmailSendServiceOptimisticFailureTests.

**Pinning test.** Add `APIErrorClassificationTests.testNonIdempotentSendProof_coversEveryCase`, a table over every APIError case like `testRecoveryAction_coversEveryCase`. Add a GmailSendServiceTests case: MockGmailAPIClient throws an unknown error after the barrier, expecting `.ambiguousDelivery`. Revert-check: the inverted catch.

**Payoff.** The compiler then enforces the never-resend rule: no new APIError case or new send caller can skip the classification, the deterministic Message-ID or the barrier. Behavior today is unchanged.

### `mac-platform#3` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Quit is the Mac's routine exit, but it waits only for sends; an owed draft save dies with the process**

Area: macOS target architecture and platform shim layer. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The Mac quit decision looks only at outbound sends. With none in flight it returns .terminateNow, and AppKit exits without running another async task. A reply draft is written only by a Task that starts 350 ms after the last composer change and then takes the cleanup-sensitive gate. So any reply text still waiting for that save at Cmd-Q (or at a window close, which also quits) is lost without warning. In practice the window is the 350 ms debounce. Gate holds that last long enough to matter are rare on the Mac, and a send that holds the gate already delays the quit.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Platform/MacAppDelegate.swift:26-47 — applicationShouldTerminate asks AppLifecyclePolicy.terminationDecision(hasOutstandingSends:) only; with no send it returns .terminateNow, and there is no applicationWillTerminate
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:348-350 — composerState.objectWillChange debounced 350 ms on RunLoop.main before scheduleReplyDraftSave; :1313-1318 the save is a taskManager Task; :1345-1351 it runs inside performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:253-258 — hasOutstandingSends covers every send from reserve() to finish, including the preflight, which holds the gate; so a quit with a gate-holding send waits (up to 10 s) and a queued draft save can run then
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:371-383 — each maintenance pass takes the gate on its own, so a waiting save is queued behind at most one pass
- docs/scalability-review.md:928 — maintenance measured at about 0.55 s total at S3 on an M5 Pro, S2 about a third, with the gate held for the longest pass: not seconds to tens of seconds
- docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:167 — the owner treated losing this same unsaved tail (the text since the last 350 ms autosave) on a fast A, B, A switch as a bug and fixed it, so the loss is not an accepted cost

**Trigger.** Cmd-Q, or closing the mailbox window, within about 350 ms of the last keystroke in a reply field, with no send in flight. Continuous typing without a 350 ms pause keeps resetting the debounce, which widens the gap. A rarer case: quitting while a sub-second maintenance or launch-repair batch holds the gate.

**Impact.** The reply text typed since the last debounced save (usually a few characters, at most the run of typing since the last pause) is missing from the draft at the next launch, with no warning. Losing a whole reply would need a gate hold that lasts through the typing and is still running at quit. On the Mac that is not realistic in steady state.

**Verifier.** The mechanism is real: only one participant (sends) drains at termination, and nothing in the repo is documented as accepting the loss of a draft at quit. Three corrections. The claim of "seconds to tens of seconds" of gate hold at S2 contradicts the review's measurement. The queued-send trigger is mostly covered, because the quit waits for that send. "The whole reply" overstates the loss. Not measured: whether SwiftUI calls onDisappear before the window-close quit's 0-delay terminate. The fix (flush owed saves inside the terminateLater wait) is still cheap.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:213 "Quitting" (waits for sends only); docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:167-171 (A, B, A unsaved-tail fix, sibling case)

**Invariant risks**

- A sidecar draft file is a second durable copy outside the store. It is mail-derived account data that sign-out's clearMailDerivedCaches does not know about, and it can bring back a reply that was already sent. ChatReplyComposerDirectory.UnpersistedSend and the single-writer draft ownership exist to stop exactly that, and saveMergingUnsentReply's merge rules would be skipped.
- Writing the draft outside the cleanup-sensitive gate at quit, to avoid the wait, breaks the store-wide snapshot that cleanup reads. Merge, dedup and empty-shell passes skip conversations that a ChatReplyDraft anchors (DataCleanupService.swift:371-383), and the rule that a queued save reads the composer only after the gate (ChatViewModel.swift:1365-1368) would no longer hold.
- Flushing through any path except startReplyDraftSave and saveReplyDraftWithoutCleanupInterleaving drops their guards: isSending, ownsDraft generation, account email, and the no-op for an off-screen composer in scheduleReplyDraftSave. A stale or empty save then deletes a newer draft, or a draft from another account is written.
- The quit must still be requested from the run loop (MacMainWindowCloseObserver), with a single reply from a single main-actor task, and the wait must not cancel or touch any send. The 350 ms Combine debounce on RunLoop.main probably does not fire while AppKit holds .terminateLater in modal-panel mode (not measured), so the flush cannot rely on it.

**Fix.** Leave the send wait as it is and add drafts as a second participant under the same deadline. (1) Add a @MainActor ReplyDraftWriteTracker. It counts gated draft writes, starting the count in ChatViewModel.startReplyDraftSave and handOffUnsentReply and ending it when each task returns, cancelled ones included, and offers a cancellation-aware waitUntilIdle. (2) Add ChatReplyComposerDirectory.flushPresentedDraftsForTermination(). It calls scheduleReplyDraftSave() on every presented composer now, skipping the 350 ms debounce but keeping every guard. (3) applicationShouldTerminate flushes first, then asks terminationDecision(hasOutstandingSends:hasOutstandingDraftWrites:). One terminateLater task waits for both and replies once. Every write stays under the cleanup gate. No sidecar file. On timeout the app logs and quits.

**First step.** Add ReplyDraftWriteTracker, a counter with a cancellation-aware idle wait modeled on OutboundTaskRegistry.waitUntilOutstandingSendsFinish (OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:265-284). Wrap the tasks of ChatViewModel.startReplyDraftSave (:1313-1318) and handOffUnsentReply (:1182) in it. Nothing changes until the delegate asks it.

**Pinning test.** In ChatViewModelTests: type a reply, call flushPresentedDraftsForTermination, wait for the tracker to go idle, then assert draftStore.load holds the text with no 350 ms elapsed (Revert-check: the flush). Add AppLifecyclePolicyTests for the decision's two inputs and a timed-out wait test using FakeSyncClock.

**Payoff.** Cmd-Q, or closing the window, within about 350 ms of typing no longer silently drops the end of the draft. Ordinary quits stay instant, and the quit becomes one bounded drain that later participants can join.

### `outbound-and-actions#6` · low · maintainability · effort M · new

**The send lifecycle is an implicit state machine spread over a dozen holders, persisted as sentinel strings and driven from the main actor**

Area: Outbound send, compose and the pending-action queue. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

One send's state does span the registry entry, a three-flag relay, two one-shot actors, a sequencer turn, a background lease, composer flags and an UnpersistedSend count; durable state is three sentinel strings in remoteCommittedMessageId; outcomes are decided by three catch arms. But the reservation, turn and lease are released structurally (a defer, one watcher, an unconditional tail), only UnpersistedSend is ended by hand, and no leak path exists. Each send makes four to six synchronous commits on the main actor, one of them the deliberate linearization point.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendModels.swift:5-29 — three sentinel constants; deliveryState decodes them, and a nil message ID with a nil thread ID means sending
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:73-86 — sync matches the three sentinels with an IN predicate on remoteCommittedMessageId (HistoryProcessor.swift:102-116 matches two of them the same way)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:326-339, 471-578 — admission is recorded in the registry, the relay, the barrier actor and the admission actor in sequence; three catch arms branch on isPersisted, the disposition and relay flags; turn.finish() and lease.end() run unconditionally at 577-578
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:179-182, 186-225, 237-251 — one watcher finishes the reservation when the background task returns (OutboundMessageCoordinator.swift:354-359 is the defer before hand-off); admitTransmission saves the marker without yielding the main actor; cancelAndAwaitAll waits with no bound until entries is empty
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:1012, 1026, 1051, 1136, 1178, 1196 — UnpersistedSend begun at the tap and ended at five separate sites in four functions
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:368-370, 565-573, 755-757, 897-900, 1471-1473 — @MainActor viewContext saves at creation, before transmission and at reconcile; a private-queue context saved inside performAndWait for each marker write

**Trigger.** A future edit to the send path that adds an early exit before the worker exists, reorders the four admission writes, or adds a reader of remoteCommittedMessageId that forgets the markers; separately, any of a send's four to six commits issued while a sync save holds the store's writer.

**Impact.** No failure today: no leak path was found, and 110 tests in the three send suites pin the outcome matrix. What remains is change risk on the non-idempotent path, and a main-thread wait per commit bounded by one concurrent sync save, which nobody has measured. If a background send task ever failed to return, sign-out would wait forever at cancelAndAwaitAll (AuthSession.swift:846), which is worse than the latched reopen the finding names.

**Verifier.** Read the coordinator, orchestrator, registry, sequencer, lease and directory whole, plus sendReply and the marker writers. Changed: release is mostly structural; the four resources end at four different points by design, so 'one owner, one release' does not fit; the admission save is synchronous on purpose (CLAUDE.md:111), so only later marker writes could move off main. Checked the merge task and post-send sync for a leak: none. Severity lowered: no failure, nothing measured.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md "Outbound send (non-idempotent; never resend)" records the invariants, not this refactor. Nearest review item: docs/scalability-review.md:1496, the cold send-record walk on main. It is a different defect and is not built (fetchAllOptimisticSendMutationRecords has no predicate).

**Invariant risks**

- The in-flight marker save is the linearization point and must not yield the main actor (OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:186-226). It shares one transaction with the forward-recovery chain consumption (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:593-731). If it became an awaited background write, closeAdmission could land in .persistingAdmission and stop being able to cancel, so a sign-out would have to drain a send that then transmits.
- Outcome matrix: before the barrier, ambiguousDelivery and cancellation always roll back. retainAsNotSent applies only with positive evidence (teardownRequested, backgroundTimeExpiredWithoutTeardown), and markPersisted is set before the request (ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:321-340, 471-575). A state machine that merges the relay flags or reorders these writes can read a post-barrier failure as pre-barrier. The rollback then gives the content back to the composer, and the user can send it twice.
- Each reader matches a different subset of the sentinels. MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:73-86 matches all three markers; HistoryProcessor.swift:102-105 only inFlight and ambiguous; DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:1105-1108 nil or inFlight. Cold recovery maps nil to Not sent and inFlight to delivery-unknown. Collapsing them all to isLocalMarker changes HistoryProcessor's admission of excluded echoes. An integer column needs a v7 mapping or backfill with dual reads, not a lightweight migration.
- Cold recovery runs synchronously on main in the auth-change turn, before the foreground sync starts (esc_chatmailApp.swift:409-442), and turns every nil record into Not sent. Made async, it could convert a live send's pre-admission record and offer Edit and resend on a message about to transmit. Also, `context.perform` closures that capture non-Sendable values compile on local Swift 6.4 and fail on CI's 6.2 (CLAUDE.md Traps).

**Fix.** Change no schema and keep the admission write on main. 1. Extract a pure OutboundSendFailurePolicy from the three catch arms (ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:471-575). It maps error class, isPersisted, disposition, teardownRequested and backgroundTimeExpiredWithoutTeardown to recordAmbiguous, retainNotSent or rollBack. One catch switches on it and calls the existing handlers in their current order, admission resolution included. 2. Add one typed OutboundSendRecordState decoder in GmailSendModels.swift (preAdmission, inFlight, ambiguous, notSent, committed). deliveryState and the snapshot's has*/remoteCommittedResult derive from it. Named predicate builders reproduce each reader's exact subset. 3. Before moving any post-barrier write off main, measure recordRemoteSendState under a concurrent S2 sync save.

**First step.** Write OutboundSendFailurePolicy and its exhaustive truth-table test first. Then replace the three catch arms in executeInBackground with one catch that switches on the policy, leaving every handler, admission resolution and the unconditional turn/lease tail unchanged.

**Pinning test.** OutboundSendFailurePolicyTests: an exhaustive table over error class, barrier state, disposition, teardown and expiry, with a Revert-check naming the policy. Plus a repositorySource test that the sentinel constants and remoteCommittedMessageId appear only in allow-listed files.

**Payoff.** The non-idempotent outcome matrix becomes one exhaustively tested function and the marker encoding one decoder. A new error class or reader can no longer misroute a send silently. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Sync durability, pacing and background budget (14)

### `background-energy#1` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**A 30 s app-refresh grant is budgeted in history pages, not time, and commits only at the end**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The app-refresh budget is only counts (3x100 history records) plus two flags, with no deadline. Under .appRefresh the run still lists up to 500 IDs for the missed-message check and fully fetches the missing ones, and runs the TTL-gated label reconciliation. Those results, the cursor, the checkpoint and the ledger are written only at the final save. When the slice has no destructive records, history-phase messages and labels are already saved every 50 messages, after label processing. So an expired refresh loses the reconciliation work and the cursor advance, not everything, and the next refresh replays the slice.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundMailboxSyncBudget.swift:7-35 — the budget is a page limit, a page size and two flags (allowsExpensiveRecovery, allowsStoreMaintenance); there is no time limit
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58 and IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:348-382 — when allowsIntermediateContextSaves is true (:1067-1087, false only for deletes, TRASH/SPAM/DRAFT label adds, or adds without labels), each 50-message batch is saved and again after label processing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/ReconciliationPhase.swift:55-79 with SyncReconciliation.swift:135-141 — the missed-message check lists min(500, max(100, hours*50)) IDs and fully fetches the missing ones into the context without saving
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:471-512,1008-1021 — cursor, checkpoint, counter, ledger and lastReconciliationTime are written only by the final save, after a cancellation check; :505 records the successful-sync time only for an untruncated slice
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/BatchProcessor.swift:56-57,115-116 and GmailAPIClient.swift:515-527 — cancellation is checked between batches and a retry sleep throws on cancel, so the unwind after expiry is short apart from an in-flight Core Data perform; BackgroundSyncManager.swift:257-263 completes the task after the worker returns
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/HistoryCollectionPhase.swift:55-64 — IDs already stored are not skipped, so a replayed slice fully fetches its messages again

**Trigger.** An S2/S3 refresh after hours with no granted refresh, whose backlog is more than the 300-record slice. The slice is truncated, history replays oldest first, and the newest up to 500 messages show as missing. The same applies to a slow cellular network when the 20-minute label-reconciliation TTL has lapsed (about 100 metadata GETs at 10 at a time).

**Impact.** A refresh of this kind can go past its roughly 30 s grant. On expiry the newest mail fetched by the missed check is rolled back, along with the cursor advance. The next refresh replays the same slice and fetches the same messages again, which costs battery and quota. The oldest messages of the slice have usually been saved already. Nothing is lost: a processing task or the next foreground sync completes the work. Background sync posts no notifications, so what users see is chats that stay stale until the first foreground sync.

**Verifier.** This is the known open item bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored: step 8 has no Built entry, and step 9 only took maintenance off refresh. Corrections: (1) "Nothing committed" is wrong when the slice has no deletes or trash/spam moves. (2) The unwind is bounded except for an in-flight perform. (3) waitsForConnectivity matters mainly on a cold launch, because NetworkMonitorService starts with _isReachable=true (SyncHelpers.swift:167) and SyncEngine.swift:512 otherwise skips the run when offline. (4) The abandoned drain is capped at 50, paced, and usually empty.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md `bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored` (lines 433-459) and Suggested order step 8 (line 1603); step 9 (line 1607) built only its maintenance half. The rest is on open, unmerged PR 451 (branch claude/scalability-step-8, head 8abdc4f4).

**Invariant risks**

- A deadline or early stop inside MessageFetchPhase or label processing advances the checkpoint over a partial set of IDs, and splitting the final save separates the cursor, ledger, counter and rollups. Shrinking a slice is safe only through the existing page limit, which stages nextPageToken.
- Deferred missed-message IDs must be stored before the resume cursor (SyncReconciliation writes it to defaults mid-run) or lastSuccessfulSyncTime moves past them. Any new account-scoped default (deferred IDs, an expiry marker) must be removed in AuthSession.clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults.
- IDs refused only by the budget (a 429 not waited out in PR 451, short timeouts) must hold the cursor without a strike. Otherwise three refreshes trip the maxConsecutiveSyncFailures escape hatch and abandon fetchable mail. A skipped drain must stage nothing, because the drain alone owns retryCount.
- A background read session must be built from the injected session's configuration, so StubURLProtocol tests still route through the stub. It must never replace sendSession or change allowsRetransmission. Add no early checkpoint save.

**Fix.** Merge open PR 451. It already gates the drain, label reconciliation and missed-message fetches behind BackgroundMailboxSyncBudget.allowsDeferrableWork, keeps deferred missed IDs in an account-scoped default, and stops app refreshes waiting out 429s. Do not add a wall-clock deadline inside phases, and do not chunk the final save. On top of it: make the refresh's missed-message check one 100-ID list call that leaves missedMessageReconciliationCursorKey alone. Shrink the next refresh's slice from 3x100 to 1x100 after an expired or overlong one, using a default cleared in clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults. Keep IDs refused only by the budget out of the strike counter. A background read session with waitsForConnectivity=false is a separate, later step.

**First step.** Rebase PR 451 (claude/scalability-step-8, head 8abdc4f4) on main. Rerun IncrementalSyncCursorTests, DeferredMissedMessageFetchTests and BackgroundSyncManagerTests, then merge it before writing any deadline or slice-shrinking code.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: an app refresh over four history pages and 300 missed IDs makes one list call and no missed-ID, drain or metadata GET. It stages checkpoint p3 and no reconciliation time. After a recorded expiry, the next refresh lists one history page.

**Payoff.** An app refresh does only its history slice and commits it, so a backlog drains across refreshes instead of replaying. Each refresh is spared up to 550 full GETs and 100 metadata GETs.

### `background-energy#4` · medium · performance · effort M · new

**New mail is found only by a fixed 60 s poll that never adapts, and an empty tick still costs two requests, a store commit and a notification fan-out**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The fixed 60 s loop is real, and the only thing that changes it is the session starting or stopping. On iOS it runs only while the scene is active: going to the background stops it. On the Mac it keeps running while the window is hidden or minimized, and pauses only for system sleep. A tick with no new mail still makes a history.list call and a missed-message messages.list call (the second is a documented safety net), and once an hour it also runs label reconciliation (up to 101 requests). It always restamps the failure-counter row, so the context saves, and posts two notifications that refetch the open chat's window. Low Power Mode, thermal state and Low Data Mode are never read. Push is declared but not built.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:45-46, 214-224 — periodicInterval 60 / minimumSyncGap 30; the loop is Task.sleep then triggerSync("foregroundPeriodic"), with no other cadence input
- esc-chatmail/App/AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:58-68, 101-105 — an iOS background returns stopForegroundSyncAndArmBackgroundTasks; a Mac .background returns .none; on the Mac only systemWillSleep stops the loop
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:384-400, 425-432, 526-531, 994-1005 — the missed-message check runs every sync "by design"; the counter is staged on every run; the cleanup hold is followed by .syncCompleted; a quiet sync forces label reconciliation hourly
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureCounterCheckpointStore.swift:157-162, 205-209 — apply() always sets updatedAt = now, so hasChanges in CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:85 is true and the run commits
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:576-596 — the hourly label reconciliation is one list call plus up to 100 getMessageMetadata calls
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+Reconciliation.swift:120-147 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:233-234 — each .syncCompleted reloads the open chat's window page; the incremental cleanup always posts .conversationCleanupFinished

**Trigger.** The Mac app open, or minimized or hidden, while the Mac is awake: about 60 ticks an hour with no mail. On iOS this happens only while the app is in the foreground, including in Low Power Mode or Low Data Mode.

**Impact.** On an idle Mac, each hour brings about 120 requests, plus up to 101 from the hourly label reconciliation, and 60 store commits. Each commit is a persistent-history transaction kept for 7 days. Each hour also brings 60 rounds of chat-window refetch and reply-addressing refresh. The cost is flat in mailbox size and stays the same whatever Low Power Mode or thermal state says. On iOS the only freshness outside the foreground is BGAppRefresh.

**Verifier.** Correct as written: the 60 s sleep, the counter's updatedAt write, the cleanup hold, the two posts, isExpensive being only logged, and push not being built (mac-app-plan.md:122). Corrected: iOS does stop the loop in the background. The per-sync messages.list is deliberate (code comment; scalability review correction at line 445). The audit missed the hourly reconciliation and the chat-window refetch. Closing the window quits the app (decision 7). App Nap and idle sleep would lower the counts, but neither was measured. Nothing records the 60 s cadence as accepted: mac-app-plan.md:743 lists it as a Phase 3 re-rank item.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:203-209 (PR B "When sync runs": keep syncing while hidden or minimized, 60 s cadence accepted) and :743 (Phase 3: re-rank for the all-day 60 s loop, not started); related: scalability-review.md:1495 (persistent-history purge)

**Invariant risks**

- Suppressing .syncCompleted or .conversationCleanupFinished on quiet runs breaks three things. AbandonedPendingActionsModel uses .syncCompleted as its periodic recheck (AbandonedPendingActionsModel.swift:21-29). ChatViewModel refreshes reply addressing on both posts (ChatViewModel.swift:375-393), and a quiet run can still refresh send-as aliases or adopt contact links (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:222, DataCleanupService+ContactUnification.swift:49). And CLAUDE.md requires every DataCleanupService run to announce its end.
- "Write nothing" must still run failureTracker.commit, because lastSuccessfulSyncTime is history recovery's floor and sets the missed-message window (SyncFailureTracker.swift:317-321). It must also keep the ModificationTracker commit and consume, and must add no save outside the orchestrator's save points. Setting an equal value still marks the row dirty, so the check has to come before the assignment, inside the stores' perform blocks.
- Stopping the loop while the Mac window is hidden or minimized would reverse a recorded decision (mac-app-plan.md:207; AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:65-68). The loop can sleep longer but must never stop. Skipping or thinning the per-sync missed-message list call would also remove the documented safety net (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:384-389; the review's correction on bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored).
- The idle backoff must reset on any of these: a run with mail or label records, needsFollowUp, a forced trigger (the post-send echo, a user refresh, activation, wake), and stop() or start() across an account transition. Replacing the sleep must swap periodicTask within one main-actor turn, because scheduleImmediateFollowUp refuses while periodicTask is nil (ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:290). Otherwise backlogs stall, echoes converge late, or a new account inherits the old account's long interval.

**Fix.** Three independent steps, cheapest first. (1) Make a quiet run commit nothing. SyncFailureCounterCheckpointStore.stage skips apply when the compatible row already holds that count and email and there is no duplicate. AccountPersister.setAccountHistoryId assigns only when the value changes. Keep failureTracker.commit (lastSuccessfulSyncTime), the ModificationTracker commit and both notifications. (2) Pass a run summary (new messages, label records, needsFollowUp) through the ForegroundSyncPerforming completion. A pure SyncCadencePolicy takes app state (active, inactive or hidden), Low Power Mode, thermal state, constrained path and the quiet-run count. It lengthens the sleep through an injected SyncClock with tolerance and never stops it. It resets on any change or forced trigger and re-arms on activation and power notifications. (3) Record a push decision: build a users.watch relay or drop aps-environment.

**First step.** In SyncFailureCounterCheckpointStore.stage, skip apply (and so the updatedAt write) when the compatible row already has the target count and accountEmail and there is no duplicate. In AccountPersister.setAccountHistoryId, assign only when account.historyId differs. Change nothing else.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests on a .sqlite TestCoreDataStack: after a clean run, a second run with an empty stubbed history.list produces no NSManagedObjectContextDidSave from the sync context, yet lastSuccessfulSyncTime advances and a held-then-clean run still resets the counter; Revert-check names both guards.

**Payoff.** A quiet Mac hour drops from 60 store commits and history rows to none; hidden, idle or Low Power polling falls from 120 requests an hour to a few dozen.

### `background-energy#5` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Connectivity has three owners and three definitions; sync's is a racy cached flag that pre-empts the session's own wait and never triggers a sync**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Three NWPathMonitors run, with two rules between them. Sync and pending actions count only .satisfied as online. Send counts anything but .unsatisfied, a documented choice. Sync's actor flag is written through a new nonisolated Task for each path update, and those Tasks run in no guaranteed order, so a reordering could leave it false until the next path update. The preflight skips the run even though the read session waits for connectivity itself, and no sync is started when the path comes back. The next try is the 60 s tick or the next activation or wake.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncHelpers.swift:167-176,196-197 — _isReachable starts true; each update does Task { await self?.setReachable } from a nonisolated @Sendable closure; reachable = path.status == .satisfied
- esc-chatmail/Services/Utilities/NetworkMonitor.swift:48-58 with PendingActionsManager.swift:163-169 — second monitor, .satisfied only, written synchronously under a lock; a false-to-true edge schedules pending-action processing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundNetworkPathMonitor.swift:44-64 — third monitor: .requiresConnection and unknown statuses count as usable, with the reason documented
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:512-516 — the preflight returns .skippedNoNetwork; GmailAPIClient.swift:114-121 — the read session has waitsForConnectivity = true and a 60 s resource timeout
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:214-224,269-271 — a skipped run becomes .skipped and nothing is queued; only the 60 s periodic loop retries
- esc-chatmail/App/AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:102-105 — systemDidWake and applicationDidBecomeActive start the session with an immediate sync, which meets the same gate

**Trigger.** The app (iOS foreground or Mac session) asks for a sync while the cached flag reads false: right after leaving airplane mode, during Wi-Fi reassociation at Mac wake, while an idle VPN On Demand tunnel reports .requiresConnection, or (rarely) after two path updates whose Tasks run out of order.

**Impact.** Common case: the first sync after the connection returns comes up to 60 s late, while pending actions resume at once. VPN On Demand: sync and pending actions are held until some other connection brings the tunnel up. Rare case: a flag left false on a stable link skips every sync, pull-to-refresh included ("Network unavailable"), until the next path update or a relaunch. Background runs map the skip to .failed and get a 60 s or 120 s backoff retry, so the background is not affected.

**Verifier.** Read all three monitors, the gate, the coordinator, the Mac lifecycle wiring, the background .failed handling and the session configuration. Corrections to the original finding: "three definitions" is really two rules. A skipped sync at wake happens only if the flag is false when didWake arrives; at wake the flag can just as well still read true, and then waitsForConnectivity covers the outage. Activation also retries without the throttle once 30 s have passed. The Task reordering follows from Swift's semantics but was not reproduced, and how closely NWPath updates arrive was not measured. No doc records the sync gate's .satisfied rule as deliberate.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md:114 (Outbound send: OutboundNetworkPathMonitor.isUsable, the send-only rule); docs/mac-app-plan.md:205 (sync immediately on wake). docs/scalability-review.md has no item on connectivity monitors.

**Invariant risks**

- Do not relax the sync preflight beyond skipping a known-unsatisfied path, and do not drop it because the session waits anyway. The read session waits for connectivity (GmailAPIClient.swift:118) with a 60 s resource timeout, 3 retries and a 120 s retry cap (Constants.swift:247-260). A run started offline would hold the exclusive SyncRunCoordinator boundary for minutes. Pending-action runs (PendingActionsManager.swift:500-502) and store maintenance would park behind it, a BG refresh would return .blocked, and mid-run fetch timeouts would become .failed ledger verdicts.
- The send gate must stay as it is. It sits before the transmission barrier, and its waiters register under the same lock as the state, so no wakeup is lost and cancellation is handled (OutboundNetworkPathMonitor.swift:98-124). The send session keeps waitsForConnectivity=false. Folding the send monitor into a new service without keeping its manual satisfied instance for unit tests (lines 22-24) would make every hosted send suite wait on the host machine's real network.
- A sync started by a became-usable edge must go through ForegroundSyncCoordinator.triggerSync with force: false, and only while periodicTask != nil and canAccessMailbox. Otherwise it would sync after the iOS scene goes to the background or while the Mac sleeps, bypass the 30 s minimum gap on a flapping link, or call SyncEngine directly from the monitor queue.
- NWPathMonitor cannot restart after cancel(), and PendingActionsManager.stopMonitoring() cancels it (line 508-509, NetworkMonitor.swift:66-67). On a shared service that would kill connectivity for sync and send for the rest of the process. AppNetworkMonitor's single, unsynchronized onConnectivityChange slot cannot serve as a multi-subscriber edge source: a second subscriber would overwrite pending actions' callback.

**Fix.** Do it in stages. (1) Replace NetworkMonitorService's per-update Task with lock-protected state written synchronously in pathUpdateHandler. Count nil (no update yet) as usable, and map status through OutboundNetworkPathMonitor.isUsable, so the preflight skips only a known-unsatisfied path. Keep that skip, because a run started offline holds the exclusive boundary for minutes. Inject it into SyncEngine.init through a protocol. (2) Give it a became-usable stream that more than one caller can subscribe to. ForegroundSyncCoordinator subscribes in start(), cancels in stop(), and calls triggerSync(force: false). (3) Optionally fold AppNetworkMonitor in, with no stop() a consumer can call. Leave the send monitor and its unit-test instance untouched.

**First step.** In esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncHelpers.swift, make NetworkMonitorService keep an optional status under an NSLock, written inside pathUpdateHandler. Answer through OutboundNetworkPathMonitor.isUsable, and give SyncEngine.init a protocol-typed parameter so tests can inject a manual path.

**Pinning test.** New SyncEngineConnectivityTests with a manual path source: unsatisfied returns .skippedNoNetwork; requiresConnection and not-yet-reported start a run; unsatisfied then satisfied reads usable. ForegroundSyncCoordinatorTests: an edge after a skip starts one sync, none after stop(). Revert-check comments on both.

**Payoff.** Sync starts as soon as the path returns (Mac wake, airplane mode off) instead of up to 60 s later. VPN On Demand users sync, and a flag stuck false can no longer skip every sync.

### `networking#5` · medium · scalability · effort M · known-open

**No shared request pacing or interactive priority; the 429 breaker never sees the bulk path, and label reconciliation spends about 100 GETs to read two label bits**

Area: Networking and Gmail API client. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Real and still unbuilt: bulk message GETs run 15-wide with a one-attempt client budget, so rate-limit backoff exists only in MessageFetcher's per-batch 0.5/1/2 s ladder (jittered, Retry-After-aware). Nothing paces across batches or callers, and IDs that outlast the ladder become cursor-blocking failures. The breaker skipping that path is deliberate. Low-severity additions hold: 403 rate-limit retries bypass the breaker, and client backoff has no jitter. Overstated: no request queue exists, so interactive calls are not delayed locally; label reconciliation's ~100 GETs are a documented, TTL-gated cost with no failure shown.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:391-411 — comment says breaker checks precede recordBackoff on purpose so concurrent 429s at maxRetries 1 do not trip it; a final-attempt 429 throws at 407-409, before recordBackoff at 411
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:154 and :492-505 — getMessage(format: "full", maxRetries: 1); the batch ladder is 0.5 s doubling, raised to Retry-After when given, plus 0-25% jitter; :394-413 exhausted IDs join fetchFailedIds (blocking)
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:533-537 and :471-507, Services/Retry/RetryStrategy.swift:41-47 — 403 rateLimitExceeded maps to .rateLimited, is retried through shouldRetry with a plain doubling sleep, never calling recordBackoff or shouldAbort; GmailAPIClient+History.swift:69-75 the history path aborts instead
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:183-188 and Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:986-1006 — the reconciliation cost (one list plus ~100 metadata GETs) is written down as the largest steady-state consumer, and the 20 min / 1 h gate is the chosen mitigation
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:580-583 and :664-681 — one list of 100 IDs from the last 24 h, then format=metadata GETs in chunks of 10, reading only INBOX and UNREAD from labelIds
- docs/scalability-review.md:386-408 and :1603 — rate-limit-pacing item calls the ordering deliberate and says "Do not route maxRetries-1 429s into RateLimitTracker's breaker"; step 8 ("Add shared 429 pacing") has no Built note

**Trigger.** Large fetch passes only, and only when Gmail actually answers 429 or 403 rate-limit: a re-initial sync with no sign-in before it (capped at 30 days, Constants.swift:217-223), history recovery after a long absence, or a multi-thousand-record incremental backlog. Batches are 50 IDs with serialized persistence between them (Constants.swift:90), which lowers the sustained rate; how often 429s occur was not measured.

**Impact.** IDs still rate-limited after the roughly 3.5-4.5 s ladder (or a Retry-After capped at 60 s) become blocking fetch failures: the cursor or checkpoint holds, the slice is fetched again next run, and sync reports warnings. Later runs, the escape hatch and the abandoned drain recover it, so it degrades and does not lose mail. Interactive calls share only server quota and the breaker with sync; pending actions requeue on rateLimited. Reconciliation costs about 100 GETs at most every 20 minutes, with no failure shown.

**Verifier.** Every cited line reads as described. No limiter exists (git grep for bucket/limiter finds only the C4 comment), and there is one shared client and tracker (GmailAPIClient.swift:69, :83). Changed: "breaker never sees bulk" is deliberate, not a defect; "no interactive priority" has no present mechanism because nothing queues; reconciliation is an accepted, documented cost, and its 429s do reach the breaker (default three-attempt budget). No fields parameter anywhere, confirmed. Medium rests on the known-open pacing item alone.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:386 `rate-limit-pacing`; Suggested order step 8 (line 1603) "Add shared 429 pacing", no Built note. Reconciliation cost is a documented TTL decision (Constants.swift:183-188, IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:986-1006).

**Invariant risks**

- Non-idempotent send: a limiter inside performRetryingRequest would wait between sendMessage's beforeTransmission() and the request. A cancelled wait throws a bare CancellationError, which isAmbiguousSendFailure (GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:112) turns into ambiguousDelivery for a send that never left the device.
- The breaker ordering is deliberate (GmailAPIClient.swift:391-411), and testBudgetOfOne_rateLimited_carriesRetryAfterWithoutSleepingOrRecordingBackoff pins it. Feeding 429s at maxRetries 1 into RateLimitTracker trips its 120 s breaker for every caller, sends included. The history path must keep aborting on a 403 rate limit (testHistoryRateLimit403AbortsRunAsRateLimited).
- Sync partition rules: if the limiter refuses for any reason other than real task cancellation, fetchOnce puts the ID in .failure and it is classed as permanent, which spends the escape hatch. Waits must give way to cancellation so quiescence and BG expiry can drain them. A pending action holding a lease must not queue behind bulk work, because teardown waits for leases. A 30-60 s ladder is longer than BGAppRefresh's budget of about 30 s.
- Reconciliation: replacing the per-ID GETs with INBOX/UNREAD list filters would read a message missing from a truncated or lagging search result as a removed label, and archive it locally. Today processReconciliationMismatches touches only IDs it actually read (SyncReconciliation.swift:802).

**Fix.** Leave RateLimitTracker, the engine's breaker ordering and sendMessage as they are. Add a standalone actor, GmailBulkRequestPacer, that takes an injected SyncClock. It keeps an in-flight budget that halves on .rateLimited (429 or 403 rate limit) and decays back up to 15, plus a shared not-before deadline taken from Retry-After. Only bulk callers acquire it: MessageFetcher.fetchOnce and getMessageMetadata (the abandoned drain and reconciliation). Interactive loads, pending actions and sends never do. A wait throws only on task cancellation. It holds no account data, so it is not a participant in the account boundary. Separately, on the message path, have a 403 rate limit record backoff and check the breaker only when it will actually sleep, and add jitter on top of any Retry-After, never below it. Keep reconciliation's per-ID GETs.

**First step.** Write GmailBulkRequestPacer as an actor over SyncClock, with acquire/release, onRateLimited(retryAfter:), onSuccess and time decay. Unit-test it under FakeSyncClock with nothing wired to it. Then have MessageFetcher.fetchOnce acquire it through an injected default.

**Pinning test.** In GmailAPIClientRetryBudgetTests, using the real client, StubURLProtocol (with a new in-flight high-water mark) and FakeSyncClock: after a 429 carrying Retry-After, fetchBatch sends nothing before the deadline and its peak concurrency drops. Add a Revert-check naming the pacer acquire.

**Payoff.** During large re-syncs and recoveries, sync stops hitting a rate-limited Gmail again and again, so fewer IDs run out the ladder into cursor-blocking failures and repeat passes. How often 429s happen is unmeasured.

### `startup-lifecycle#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Entering the background stops only the timer: the in-flight sync run is neither drained nor protected, and a background task that meets the frozen run reports success**

Area: App startup, launch passes and scene lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

On iOS .background the app only stops ForegroundSyncCoordinator's periodic and deferred tasks and arms BGTasks under an assertion that ends with the arm. The run in flight is a separate unstructured task holding SyncRunCoordinator's exclusive run; nothing cancels it (cancelSync has no caller) or keeps the process alive for it, so a run longer than the suspension grace freezes holding the boundary. Every incremental run, background ones included, is kind foregroundIncremental, so a BGTask resumed beside the frozen run gets .blocked(by: foregroundIncremental), returns success and schedules no catch-up.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:384-388 — .stopForegroundSyncAndArmBackgroundTasks calls foregroundSyncCoordinator.stop(reason:) then armBackgroundTasksForSceneBackground(); nothing else runs on .background (AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:59-64)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:76-83,115 — stop() cancels periodicTask and deferredSyncTask only; each trigger runs in its own unstructured Task, so the cancellation never reaches a started run
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:209-213 and SyncRunCoordinator.swift:224-231 — cancelSync()/cancelForegroundRun(); git grep finds callers only in tests. beginBackgroundTask appears only in the send manager and SceneBackgroundAssertionLatch
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:316-319,518 — a held boundary returns .blocked(by: activeRunKind); prepareIncrementalSync starts every incremental run, background included, as kind .foregroundIncremental
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:115-120,188-196,342-347,452-456 — the assertion wraps only the arm task; handlers re-arm ordinary cadence at entry; .blocked by a non-nil kind other than pendingActions/maintenance returns true with no retry (pinned by BackgroundSyncManagerTests.swift:1517-1532)
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:359-364,494-500 and MessageFetcher.swift:347-387 — a retried request frozen past the 120 s wall-clock budget throws on resume; a fetch batch has no such deadline and reissues requests

**Trigger.** Leaving the app while an incremental run still needs more than the few seconds iOS allows after backgrounding (catch-up after hours or days away, history recovery, a 10x500-record slice; likelier at S2/S3 where message writes are slower), with the process surviving suspended until the next BGAppRefresh or BGProcessing delivery.

**Impact.** That refresh or processing slot does no mailbox sync, yet completes as success with no 5-minute catch-up; only the ordinary cadence re-armed at handler entry remains. It repeats until the frozen run unwinds: a run frozen in one retried API call fails at first resume, one frozen in a fetch batch can need several wakes. On return to the foreground the fresh sync waits behind the stale run. No data loss; the app has no notifications, so the visible cost is a stale list on open.

**Verifier.** Read every cited path; all are as described. No scene-phase or UIApplication observer touches the run, and no doc records this as accepted. The 'active mailbox sync satisfies the task' decision is test-pinned but assumes a live run. Tightened: launch passes take non-exclusive leases (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:264-266, 473-478), so they never cause .blocked. Not observed: suspension timing, and whether the handler or the resumed run's failure wins the first-wake race.

**October review.** none; nearest is bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored (docs/scalability-review.md:433), which does not cover a run frozen at backgrounding

**Invariant risks**

- Every incremental run, background ones included, is .foregroundIncremental today (SyncEngine.swift:518; no production run uses .background). A naive cancelForegroundRun() from a refresh handler would kill a BGProcessing run going on at the same time. Background runs must take .background first.
- UIKit's expiration handler must end the assertion synchronously (SceneBackgroundAssertionLatch.swift:8-15). You cannot await or hop to the SyncRunCoordinator actor there, so the 'cancel and await' has to happen before expiry (cancel at a soft deadline). At expiry the only step is a synchronous cancel through a MainActor-held Task handle.
- A BGTask handler that waits for the boundary must use the cancellation-aware, generation-checked acquireRunWithTask/parkUntilIdleOrCancelled, never waitUntilIdle or acquireRun. Otherwise an expired task is completed only when the frozen run ends, and a wait that spans an account transition would not refuse.
- Cancellation must stay a thrown CancellationError, with a ModificationTracker rollback and no per-message verdict. The post-run store maintenance also starts after backgrounding, because scheduleImmediateFollowUp returns false once stopped, so the guard must cover the whole trigger task. History recovery has no checkpoint, so cancelling it loses its unsaved listing.

**Fix.** Three steps, in order. (1) Background runs take kind .background: prepareIncrementalSync takes a kind, and shouldScheduleRetryWhenBlocked keeps treating .background as satisfied. A foreground-kind holder during a BGTask is then provably stale. (2) When performIncrementalSyncForBackground is blocked by a foreground kind, it calls cancelForegroundRun(), takes the boundary through a generation-checked, cancellation-aware acquireRunWithTask(kind: .background, for:), and runs its budgeted slice. (3) An iOS guard with an injected assertion closure covers any foreground trigger task in flight at backgrounding or started after it. It releases when the task ends, cancels at a soft deadline, and at expiration cancels synchronously through a Task whose withTaskCancellationHandler forwards to the run. Launch passes need nothing: their leases never hold the boundary.

**First step.** Add a kind parameter to SyncEngine.prepareIncrementalSync and pass .background from performIncrementalSyncForBackground. Then deliberately update the BackgroundSyncManagerTests pins: .background stays satisfied, and the foreground kinds are treated as stale.

**Pinning test.** SyncEngine test: a foreground-kind run that waits until cancelled holds the boundary. performIncrementalSyncForBackground cancels it, takes .background and returns .completed. Cancelled while waiting, it returns promptly. Revert-check: the cancelForegroundRun call. A guard test with a spy assertion pins release and synchronous cancel.

**Payoff.** A background wake that meets a frozen run syncs instead of reporting false success. Most catch-up runs finish under the assertion, so the list is fresh on open.

### `sync-engine#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**A held cursor is retried at once, so the three-strike escape hatch can be spent in seconds on transient failures, and abandonment is silent**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

A run with any blocking fetch or persist failure stages count+1 and returns needsFollowUp; the foreground coordinator starts the next run at once with force, so run one plus two follow-ups reach the three-strike threshold in one chain. The cursor then advances and the IDs go to the drain: five single attempts over at least 17 hours, then the row is deleted. No app code observes the abandonment notification. Strikes need history.list to succeed; a full outage spends none.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:412-427, 540 — a run with failures proposes incrementedFailureCount(after: activeFailureCount) and stages it with no time term; a held run returns needsFollowUp: wasTruncated || !advancePlan.shouldAdvance
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:47, 247-252, 294-303 — maxImmediateFollowUpRuns = 3; the continuation is triggered with force: true, which skips the 30 s minimumSyncGap check; the limit (3 follow-ups) is above the 2 needed to reach strike three
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:229-259, 298-321, 540-551 — hatch at count >= maxConsecutiveSyncFailures marks deferred rows abandoned; commit stamps lastSuccessfulSyncTime and posts .syncMessagesAbandoned (git grep: declared SyncEngine.swift:8, observed only in tests); row deleted at retryCount 5, backoff 15 min x4 capped at 12 h; the comment at 546-548 paces the drain against back-to-back syncs, the strike counter has no such pacing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:61-64, 194-201, 410-414 — one client attempt plus three retries at 0.5/1/2 s per 50-ID batch; retriable failures left on the final attempt become exhaustedRetryIds and join fetchFailedIds
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:251-255, 512-516 — the completion runs only for a run that succeeded and recorded a result; a run is refused when the network monitor reports no network. HistoryCollectionPhase.swift:47 — listHistory throws, so a failed list ends the run before any strike is staged
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/ReconciliationPhase.swift:55-79 and SyncTimeCalculator.swift:68-74 — every run also lists mail after lastSuccessfulSyncTime minus 300 s and re-fetches IDs missing locally, without gating the cursor; the finding did not count this net

**Trigger.** App in the foreground. history.list succeeds while messages.get or a body fetch for at least one ID fails all four attempts in each of three back-to-back runs: per-user rate limiting during a large catch-up (each run re-fetches the whole frozen slice at 15-way concurrency, with no skip for stored IDs), a message-specific 5xx, or a large message timing out on a slow link. About 15-30 s for a small slice with fast errors; several minutes with 30 s timeouts, a Retry-After, or many failing batches. Offline and full outages do not trigger it.

**Impact.** The hold-and-retry protection lasts one chain of runs, not three spaced attempts. The affected mail is skipped by the cursor and normally arrives late through the drain: on the next sync if the fault has cleared, otherwise 15 min, 1 h, 4 h and 12 h later. The missed-message check also re-fetches it, but only while it is within about 5 minutes of the last successful sync. A message that fails all five drain attempts is dropped from the app with only a log line. The user sees nothing beyond a "Sync completed with warnings" status.

**Verifier.** Code is as cited; the only run-level throttle is the full-disk backoff. Lowered to medium: the usual outcome is late mail, and loss needs five more spaced failures. Two recommendations contradict docs/scalability-review.md: line 396 keeps rateLimited a per-message verdict, and line 1638 lists deletion after 5 attempts as already sound. The follow-up timing and the unobserved notification are new. Nothing was executed; how often Gmail fails messages.get this way is unmeasured.

**October review.** Related only: rate-limit-pacing (docs/scalability-review.md:386-408, step 8, not built). Line 1638 ("Already sound": ledger rows deleted after 5 attempts). Strike pacing and the held-run chain are not in the review.

**Invariant risks**

- Do not let exhausted 429, 5xx or timeout failures spend no strike, and do not add them to isAccountScopedSyncAbort. A message that always fails would then freeze the cursor for good, which is the wedge the escape hatch exists to prevent (Constants.swift:134-136). That predicate also feeds MessageProcessor's body buckets and MessagePersister, and rate-limit-pacing says to keep rateLimited as a per-message verdict.
- Stage the strike time in the syncFailureCounter.v1 row in the run's context. It then commits or rolls back with the ledger and the cursor, and sign-out removes it with SyncCheckpoint (AuthSession.swift:182). Never keep it in UserDefaults or memory. Keep payload version 1 and make the new field optional, because decodeCount resets any other version to zero.
- Spacing strikes without spacing the held reruns multiplies full re-fetches. A frozen slice re-GETs every ID, and a held initial sync or history recovery re-lists its whole window. So space strikes on the incremental slice path only. A missing or backward-moving clock must count as a strike, or the hold becomes a wedge.
- Keep needsFollowUp. BackgroundSyncManager's 5-min catch-up and the skip of processing-task maintenance (SyncEngine.swift:312) depend on it for held runs. Add a separate field. StoreMaintenanceAfterSyncSourceTests pins the source line `completion(result.needsFollowUp)`.

**Fix.** Two changes, in this order. (1) Add IncrementalSyncResult.hasDurableContinuation: true only for a truncated slice whose plan advanced. SyncEngine passes that, not needsFollowUp, to the foreground completion. A held run then queues no immediate run and waits for the 60 s loop; the background path keeps needsFollowUp. (2) On the incremental slice path only, count a strike only when about 5-10 min have passed since the last one. Put this in one pure policy with an injected SyncClock, and store lastStrikeAt as an optional field in the syncFailureCounter.v1 payload, staged with the count. A missing lastStrikeAt or a backward clock counts. Do not exempt transient errors from strikes. Separately, show the user a count from .syncMessagesAbandoned, and hash the message ID logged at SyncFailureTracker.swift:542.

**First step.** Add hasDurableContinuation to IncrementalSyncResult: wasTruncated && advancePlan.shouldAdvance on the slice path, false on the fallback, recovery and deferral returns. Pass it to the completion at SyncEngine.swift:255 and update the StoreMaintenanceAfterSyncSourceTests pin.

**Pinning test.** In IncrementalSyncCursorTests with FakeSyncClock: three back-to-back failing runs stage count 1 and hold; advancing the clock past the spacing reaches the hatch (Revert-check: spacing check). testFailureCounterSurvivesFreshTrackersAndAdvancesOnlyAtThreshold must advance the clock between runs. A SyncEngine test: a held result queues no continuation.

**Payoff.** The three strikes spread over ten or more minutes, so a rate-limit burst or a brief 5xx no longer sends mail to the 17-hour drain. Held runs also stop re-fetching back to back.

### `sync-engine#3` · medium · scalability · effort M · known-open

**No pacing or run-level backoff on the Gmail read path: 15-way bursts, a 3.5 s retry ladder, and a 60 s loop that replays the whole slice**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Confirmed: full GETs fan out 15 wide, one attempt each; a 429 is retried per 50-ID batch on a 0.5/1/2 s ladder (or Retry-After), nothing carries to the next batch, and the client breaker is deliberately bypassed. Only a full disk backs off a run. Wrong in shape: a quota or history refusal aborts the next run at its first request. The whole-slice replay is the held slice's: an immediate forced follow-up re-fetching every ID, capped at three passes by the escape hatch.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:141-154, 347-356 — task group bounded by maxConcurrentMessageFetches (15), getMessage(format: "full", maxRetries: 1); three retry passes per fetchBatch with calculateRetryDelay (0.5/1/2 s, or Retry-After when larger); no state survives to the next 50-ID batch
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:391-411 — on 429, `attempt >= allowedAttempts` throws rateLimited before rateLimitTracker.recordBackoff; the comment at 391-394 says this ordering is deliberate
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:181-189 — the first account-scoped error (quota) sets runAbortError and calls group.cancelAll(), so a replay while quota is still out stops within the first 15 requests
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:313-316, 412-432, 540 — every ID in historyResult.newMessageIds goes to the fetch phase with no stored-row filter; a failing run raises the durable failure count; needsFollowUp is true whenever the slice is held
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:214-224, 286-304 — the periodic loop triggers every 60 s whatever the last outcome; a run that reports needsFollowUp gets an immediate forced follow-up, up to maxImmediateFollowUpRuns (3)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:349-363 — only the insufficient-storage arm records a backoff; SyncFailureTracker.swift:229-232 holds the cursor until maxConsecutiveSyncFailures (3), then abandons and advances

**Trigger.** Per-message 429s (or 403 rateLimitExceeded) that outlast the 3.5 s ladder during a large catch-up slice, most plausibly when two devices on the account catch up at once. No 429 was observed; one device's sustained rate, limited by persistence between 50-ID batches, is near Gmail's per-user budget, not clearly over it.

**Impact.** A throttled slice is fetched up to three times back to back, about 5 units per already-stored message on each extra pass (roughly 20,000 wasted units for 2,000 IDs), inside the window that is throttling it. The three strikes are spent in that one episode, so throttled but fetchable IDs go to the abandoned ledger and arrive late through the 50-per-sync drain. A quota abort costs about one request a minute while it lasts, then one replay of the batches already stored.

**Verifier.** Read MessageFetcher, GmailAPIClient (+History, +Messages), SyncEngine, ForegroundSyncCoordinator, IncrementalSyncOrchestrator, the fetch, history and reconciliation phases, BatchProcessor, SyncFailureTracker and SyncStorageBackoff. No stored-ID filter and no sync quota backoff exist. Guards found: first-response abort on quota, three-strike escape hatch, three-follow-up cap. docs/scalability-review.md:386-408 lists the pacing item as open; step 8 (line 1603) is unbuilt. Severity stays medium on structural cost; the unbounded 60 s whole-slice replay is not real.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:386-408 `rate-limit-pacing` (step 8 at :1603, no Built note; no limiter exists in code). Skip-stored: `bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored` review correction :445. Run-level 429/quota backoff and held-slice immediate replay are new.

**Invariant risks**

- Send barrier and breaker: a limiter in GmailAPIClient.performRetryingRequest (also used by sendMessage, GmailAPIClient+Messages.swift:78-90) puts an await between beforeTransmission and URLSession. Sending maxRetries-1 429s to RateLimitTracker trips the 120 s breaker (GmailAPIClient.swift:391-394).
- Cancellation is never a per-message verdict. fetchOnce returns errors as values, and isRetriableError calls CancellationError non-retriable (MessageFetcher.swift:151-159, 194-209). If a pacer throws CancellationError or any non-retriable error while the parent task is not cancelled, the ID becomes a blocking failure and an escape-hatch strike.
- Skipping stored IDs: OutboundSendMutationRecords that hold only a marker (inFlight/ambiguous/notSent) are matched by the RFC Message-ID from the full payload (MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:66-115). Exempting record-named IDs is therefore not enough. Deferred IDs may have stored rows (bodyWriteFailed). If skipped IDs count as persisted, recordSuccessfulRun resets SyncStorageBackoff.
