- The run-level backoff is account-scoped plain state. Write it before endRun and reset it in resetStorageStateForAccountTransition (resetSyncStorageState) on every AuthSession path. A refusal reported as alreadyInProgress while the boundary is idle makes triggerSyncAfterCurrent spin. rateLimited must stay out of isAccountScopedSyncAbort.

**Fix.** Four steps, in order. (1) ForegroundSyncCoordinator: queue an immediate forced follow-up only for a truncated slice that advanced, never for a held one (split IncrementalSyncResult.needsFollowUp; background sync keeps the union). (2) Add a pacer owned by MessageFetcher (an actor that waits on SyncClock): Retry-After held across batches, AIMD width starting at 15, about 40 GETs/s. Never put it in GmailAPIClient's shared engine or RateLimitTracker. (3) Give SyncEngine a run-level backoff for quotaExhausted and for held runs whose failures were all rate-limited. Record it before endRun, reset it at account transitions, and report refusals as skipped. (4) On held replays only, skip GETs for committed rows. Refetch deferred-ledger IDs, IDs named by a record, and everything while a marker record exists. Skipped IDs count as unattempted, not persisted.

**First step.** Split IncrementalSyncResult.needsFollowUp into hasContinuation (a truncated slice advanced its checkpoint) and isHeld. Keep needsFollowUp as their union for BackgroundSyncManager. ForegroundSyncCoordinator's completion queues an immediate forced follow-up only when hasContinuation is true.

**Pinning test.** ForegroundSyncCoordinatorTests: a held, non-truncated result queues no immediate continuation (completion returns false); a truncated, advanced slice still does. Revert-check names the held guard. MessageFetcherTests through StubURLProtocol and FakeSyncClock: batch 1's Retry-After delays batch 2.

**Payoff.** A throttled catch-up stops re-fetching its slice three times within a minute and spending all three escape-hatch strikes, so fetchable mail stops landing in the abandoned drain, which retries on an hours-long schedule.

### `sync-engine#4` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**A BGAppRefresh slice still runs the drain, missed-message fetches and label reconciliation, and commits its cursor only in the last save**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

`.appRefresh` changes only the history slice (3 pages x 100) and skips initial-sync fallback, history recovery and store maintenance. The orchestrator still runs, before its only cursor-committing save: full fetch of every added message, the abandoned drain (up to 50, empty in steady state), the missed-message list plus full fetch of every missing ID (up to 500 on a backlog), and TTL-gated label reconciliation (list + ~100 metadata GETs). Cancellation before that save drops cursor, continuation, ledger, counter; a destructive record also disables batch saves and the post-label flush.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:282-287, 312 — the budget reaches the run only as historyPageLimit, historyPageSize and allowsExpensiveRecovery; allowsStoreMaintenance gates only the maintenance asked for after the run
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:172, 329, 397-400, 553 — allowsExpensiveRecovery guards only the initial-sync fallback and history recovery; the abandoned drain and the reconciliation phase run unconditionally
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/ReconciliationPhase.swift:5-8, 55-79, 89-101 — input is skipLabelReconciliation alone; missed IDs are full-fetched in the same run through BatchProcessor.retryFailedMessages
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:135-141, 580-583, 662-675 — missed-message budget of 100 to 500 IDs in 100-ID pages; label pass lists 100 and GETs metadata ten at a time
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:434-446, 471-491, 1014-1021 — continuation or cursor staged, then one final save behind Task.checkCancellation; reconciliation time recorded only after it
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58 with IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:348-382, 1067-1087 — per-batch save and post-label flush both skipped when any record deletes, adds a label-less message, or adds SPAM/DRAFT/TRASH

**Trigger.** A BGAppRefresh launch (about 30 s, which also covers cold launch and auth restore) whose fetches plus the optional tail overrun: a backlog after an absence (a 300-record slice plus up to 500 "missed" IDs, since a truncated slice leaves lastSuccessfulSyncTime unmoved, SyncFailureTracker.swift:317-325), or an S2/S3 store where each fresh sync context pays the hub fault. Not observed: no background task was run.

**Impact.** The next run lists and full-fetches the same history window again (nothing skips stored IDs) and repeats label reconciliation, whose timestamp was never recorded. A non-destructive slice that expires in the tail keeps its messages, label changes and rollups; a destructive one keeps nothing. An expired task schedules nothing beyond the ordinary cadence (BackgroundSyncManager.swift:318-320). The app has no push or notifications, so the cost is wasted background work and a staler mailbox on open until a processing task or foreground sync finishes the slice.

**Verifier.** Read orchestrator, phases, SyncReconciliation, BackgroundSyncManager, budget, config. No deadline guard, no skip of stored IDs, no test pins an app-refresh skip. docs/scalability-review.md step 8 is unbuilt; only the maintenance half (step 9). Tightened: drain is empty in steady state (fast path, 5-try backoff); the missed list is 1-5 pages; a non-destructive slice also keeps the post-label flush. The prior review says not to add an early checkpoint save: skip the tail instead. Expiry and iOS throttling are unmeasured.

**October review.** bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored, docs/scalability-review.md:433-459 (Review correction at 445: keep the one list call, defer only the fetches). Suggested order step 8 (line 1603) is not built. Only the maintenance half is built (step 9, line 1607; SyncEngine.swift:312, BackgroundMailboxSyncBudget.swift:33). The intermediate-save part is the separate open item no-intermediate-saves-destructive-slice (lines 484-505).

**Invariant risks**

- Committing the slice before reconciliation breaks the missed-message window. failureTracker.commit(recordsSuccessfulSync:) moves lastSuccessfulSyncTime to now (SyncFailureTracker.swift:317-322), and the window starts there minus 5 min (SyncTimeCalculator.swift:68-74, 104-121). The safety net goes empty, and deferred IDs drop out of every later window. The review also forbids an early checkpoint save (scalability-review.md:443).
- Deferring the fetches but keeping the normal list path loses IDs. The list call writes the missed-message cursor to UserDefaults at once instead of staging it (SyncReconciliation.swift:200-204, 279, 335). The next run resumes past pages whose IDs were never fetched.
- A skipped label pass must return .notRequested, never .completed. Otherwise finalizePersistence records lastReconciliationTime (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1019-1021), and the TTL suppresses the next foreground pass. A skipped drain must stage nothing, because only the drain owns retryCount.
- Narrowing allowsIntermediateContextSaves per ID does not work as stated, because a context save is all-or-nothing. It would need partitioned fetches, which break saveMessages' chronological sequential order and can expose a message that a later record deletes or excludes (commit 55e3a209). Leave it to its own item.

**Fix.** Replace performSync's three loose parameters with one IncrementalSyncWorkPolicy value that BackgroundMailboxSyncBudget maps to; foreground keeps today's behaviour. Under app refresh: skip the abandoned drain, return .notRequested for label reconciliation, and run the missed-message check as a one-page probe that does not resume, writes no defaults cursor and fetches nothing. If the probe finds missing IDs or has another page, commit with recordsSuccessfulSync false so lastSuccessfulSyncTime keeps the window, and report it so BackgroundSyncManager arms a processing task without a catch-up retry. Keep the single final save. Leave intermediate-save narrowing to its own item.

**First step.** Add an IncrementalSyncWorkPolicy value (.foreground, .processing, .appRefresh). Thread it from SyncEngine.performIncrementalSyncForBackground through prepareIncrementalSync into IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.performSync, replacing the three loose parameters. Then gate the abandoned drain at IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:329 on it.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: given a retryable abandoned row, one history message and a list page naming an unstored ID, an appRefresh run fetches only the history message, makes no metadata GETs, writes no missed cursor, keeps lastSuccessfulSyncTime; revert-check the guard.

**Payoff.** The work an app refresh does after history drops from up to about 650 requests to one list call. The slice's single save then lands well inside the roughly 30 s window.

### `sync-engine#5` · medium · scalability · effort L · known-partial

**Initial sync and history recovery still restart from page 1, and one failing message makes the whole window run again**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Confirmed: the window checkpoint stores only windowStart. The list page token and failure IDs are run-local, and every listed ID is fetched format=full and prepared again with no stored-row filter. A killed, expired or thrown run restarts at page 1 with no strike. Corrections: a held attempt repeats the whole window at most twice more, back to back, because the third strike abandons the failing IDs and advances. Backgrounding only suspends a foreground run, which resumes with its token; a restart needs process death, BGTask expiry or a run-level throw.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageListPaginator.swift:44-66,123-124,169-170 — pageToken is a local var starting nil; failedIds and persistenceFailures are run-local accumulators
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncWindowCheckpointStore.swift:29-37,99-102 — payload is version + windowStart only; startHistoryId and pageToken are always written nil
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/BatchProcessor.swift:56-64, MessageFetcher.swift:154, MessagePersister.swift:252 — every listed ID goes to fetchBatch, getMessage(format: "full"), then prepareMessagesConcurrently; no existence filter
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:832-859,901 and InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:458-478 — a held attempt stages a strike, keeps the frozen window and unset/expired cursor, and reports needsFollowUp; SyncFailureTracker.swift:229-281 with Constants.swift:136 — at 3 strikes the deferred rows are abandoned and the cursor advances
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:47,76-83,286-304 — up to 3 forced immediate follow-ups; stop() cancels only the periodic and deferred tasks, not the active run (SyncEngine.swift:209 cancelSync has no caller in the app or tests)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:217-223 and SyncTimeCalculator.swift:58-64 — the 30-day cap binds only a re-initial sync with no sign-in before it; recovery's last-sync branch is deliberately uncapped; docs/scalability-review.md:1603 — step 8 has no Built entry

**Trigger.** Mainly history expiry after an absence longer than Gmail keeps history, where the recovery window is the length of the absence. The 30-day re-initial sync needs a store reset with no sign-out (recovery ladder, Reset Mailbox), which is rare; a sign-in's window is minutes. The pass then restarts at page 1 if the process dies while suspended, a BGProcessing task expires, an account transition cancels it, or a list, quota, auth or full-disk error throws. Separately, a message that fails every fetch or persist attempt holds the pass.

**Impact.** Each restart lists the window again and full-fetches and re-processes every message already saved; kills and expiries add no strike, so nothing bounds the repeats. A persistently failing message costs three whole-window passes back to back before the escape hatch. At S3 a 30-day window is about 6,600 GETs per pass (arithmetic), roughly 2-7 minutes at the prior review's estimated rate, so "never finishes" is overstated. Newest mail and in-window label and read state still arrive on each pass. History-driven deletions, spam and trash moves, and changes to older mail wait for the cursor.

**Verifier.** Read both orchestrators, the paginator, BatchProcessor, MessageFetcher, SyncEngine, ForegroundSyncCoordinator and the window store whole. No guard refutes the mechanism; step 8 is an open item, not an accepted decision. Changed: added the 3-strike bound (the tracker's ledger design relies on the re-scan), narrowed "backgrounding" to process death or expiry, noted the 30-day trigger is rare, softened the impact (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:420-432 refreshes labels on re-fetch). Throughput is the prior review's estimate, not measured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:186 initial-sync-no-durable-checkpoint (Review correction :198) and :360 history-recovery-no-checkpoint (:372); Suggested order step 8 at :1603 has no Built entry. Only the window freeze is built (step 2, commit 0176013c, SyncWindowCheckpointStore).

**Invariant risks**

- Pre-scan watermark. A resumed run that advances to its own fresh profile.historyId (InitialSyncOrchestrator:475/497/519, IncrementalSyncOrchestrator:856) skips mail that arrived after the first attempt and sits above the token. Store the first attempt's watermark and limit its age: commit() stamps lastSuccessfulSyncTime=now (SyncFailureTracker:321), so if that watermark has expired, the next recovery starts after the gap, and reconciliation only looks back 24 h.
- Failure IDs travel with the token. Today they are only run-local (MessageListPaginator:123-124,169-170). If a page save stages the token without the accumulated fetch- and persistence-failed IDs, the clean branch of planHistoryAdvance (SyncFailureTracker:214-226) and recordFailure's replace delete the deferred rows, and the cursor advances past messages that were never stored.
- A rejected list token must not wedge sync. listMessages has no token classification (GmailAPIClient+Messages:8-17; only invalidHistoryPageToken exists, for history). A 400 then throws at run level with no strike, every later run resumes the same token, and sync is wedged permanently.
- Window and staging rules. A held completion must keep the window row: step 2 clears it only in the advancing save (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator:851-856), and the 2026-10 correction's 'clear on held' would let the window slide. The store only stages into each page's save, never saves itself. A v1 row means re-list from page 1, never 'no failures'.

**Fix.** Give SyncWindowCheckpointStore a v2 payload: windowStart, the first listing attempt's watermark (startHistoryId column) and capture time, the list pageToken, carried failed and resolved-tracked IDs, and listingComplete. MessageListPaginator takes a start token and hands pageCompletion the page's nextPageToken and accumulated failures; both orchestrators stage them before each page's saveAsync. Resume only a same-account v2 row under about 24 h old; otherwise re-list from page 1 with a fresh watermark and the same windowStart. Union carried failures into the completion retry; advance to the stored watermark. A held completion keeps window and watermark, so the next attempt retries only the ledger. Classify a rejected list token; clear it durably and restart.

**First step.** Add a narrow APIError.invalidListPageToken classifier to listMessages (4xx, the request carried a token, the message or reason names pageToken) and pin it through StubURLProtocol. Do this before any list token is persisted, so a stale stored token can never wedge sync.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: page 1 holds a fetch-failing ID; cancel at page 2's list. The next run lists first with the staged token, GETs no page-1 ID, retries the failing one and keeps historyId frozen while it fails. Revert-check: the page stage call.

**Payoff.** An interrupted recovery or re-initial sync resumes at its last saved page, and a held attempt re-fetches only the failing IDs instead of about 6,600 full GETs per pass at S3.

### `sync-engine#6` · medium · maintainability · effort M · new

**The commit protocol is written three times by hand, and part of the sync state sits in UserDefaults outside it**

Area: Sync engine architecture and durability. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Incremental sync, history recovery and initial sync each hand-order the same commit sequence (plan, stage counter, stage checkpoint or cursor, roll up and save inside the serializer, then tracker commit); a fourth, finalizeSync, is dead. Phases get the raw context; MessageFetchPhase saves it per batch, orchestrator-gated, with no cursor state staged, but skipping the serializer's read-state preservation. Of four UserDefaults sync values only the missed-message cursor is written ahead of the run's save. Background runs register as foregroundIncremental; performInitialSync and cancelSync have no production callers.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:411-508 and 829-894 — incremental and recovery each write out planHistoryAdvance, failureCounterStore.stage, checkpoint clear or setAccountHistoryId, rollups plus saveAsync inside performThrowingSyncMutation, then failureTracker.commit; only the incremental path goes through finalizePersistence (1008-1022) with its cancellation checks
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:398-527 with 187-237 — third hand-written copy (three branches each staging counter and cursor, then the same rollup/save/commit tail); incrementedFailureCount at 546-549 duplicates IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:981-984; AccountPersister.swift:148-166 finalizeSync is a fourth variant with no callers
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58 — batchCompletion calls context.coreDataContext.save() directly, gated by allowsIntermediateContextSaves; recordFailure is staged only after the loop (61-73). Every other sync-context save runs inside ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:188-200, which first calls preserveNewerLocalReadState (215-284)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncReconciliation.swift:195-204 and 335 — the cursor is written to defaults straight after listing, before findMissingMessages (159) and the phase's fetch; 519-526 — a failed or mistyped local fetch returns ids as all missing; Phases/ReconciliationPhase.swift:81-85 — recovery failures are logged, not cursor-gating
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AccountPersister.swift:129-139 — setAccountHistoryId uses try? and logs a warning when no Account is fetched; esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:2008-2020 — comment recording the leftover missed-message cursor that refetched a wiped mailbox's mail, and the removeObject that now clears it
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:209-237 and 518 — cancelSync and performInitialSync (its only caller is SyncEngineStorageAdmissionTests.swift:90); every incremental run, background included (278-290), begins as .foregroundIncremental; SyncRunCoordinator.swift:3-18 declares .background and .foregroundInitial, which no production code assigns

**Trigger.** Development-time: the next change to one of the three finalization paths, or a new sync value added to UserDefaults. The runtime holes need a capped reconciliation window (more than 100 to 500 new messages since the last successful sync) in a run that fails before its save, or a failed Core Data read.

**Impact.** No active cursor bug: the three paths agree today, and the Account cursor, counter, checkpoint and ledger still commit in one save. The cost is drift risk on the path where a mistake silently skips mail; the ordering is kept by convention, CLAUDE.md prose and the cursor test suites. The runtime effects found are low and in the safe direction: the safety net can skip one missed-message page, a failed lookup refetches up to 500 messages, and a failed Account fetch replays history while the run reports success.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited site; all are as described. Mitigations found: HistoryAdvancePlan and commit(_:) are typed, the checkpoint stores never save, IncrementalSyncCursorTests uses failing-save contexts, the batch save is gated by allowsIntermediateContextSaves, and the sign-out leak is fixed (AuthSession.swift:2020). Nothing documents the triplication as deliberate. The prior review's "commit atomically" still holds; its line-1517 item is a different cursor defect. Medium stands only as structural debt.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: not listed. Related only: Hygiene "Missed-message reconciliation resume cursors pile up in UserDefaults" (line 1517, still open) and no-intermediate-saves-destructive-slice "Keep intact" (line 496)

**Invariant risks**

- The counter, checkpoint and cursor are staged only into the final save. Staging the strike before the post-label flush brings back the one-high crash gap (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:422-424). The window freeze (SyncWindowCheckpointStore.stageFreeze) is the one deliberate early commit.
- Gate-then-turn: the final rollups and save run inside the conversations' serializer turns. runIncrementalCleanup takes the cleanup-sensitive gate (DataCleanupService.swift:234). If post-commit work is folded into the turn, it hangs against a send that holds the gate.
- Tracker success effects (ModificationTracker commit, failureTracker.commit with recordsSuccessfulSync false on a truncated slice) happen only after the save succeeds. The defaults writes come after the save but before endRun, so quiescence orders them ahead of clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults.
- Moving the cursor or lastReconciliationTime into SyncCheckpoint means the store-retaining paths of clearAccountScopedSyncDefaults (AuthSession.swift:2015-2021) no longer clear them. Separately, incremental's flush reads without claiming, while initial and recovery claim: unifying the two changes which conversations the final save rolls up.

**Fix.** Keep behavior unchanged, in three steps. (1) Make setAccountHistoryId throw and match the account email. Delete finalizeSync, cancelSync and cancelForegroundRun, share incrementedFailureCount, and run background syncs as .background. (2) Have SyncReconciliation return its cursor update, written after the save beside recordReconciliation. A failed ID lookup fetches nothing and keeps the cursor. Keep both values in the injected defaults. (3) Extract SyncRunCommit, which owns the context, the ModificationTracker transaction and the serializer turns. It offers saveIntermediate (inside the turn, refused once finalize stages) and finalize (counter, checkpoint or cursor, rollups and save, tracker commits, post-save writes), with gate-taking cleanup after the turn. Migrate recovery, then initial, then incremental. Decide whether recovery posts .syncCompleted (today it doesn't).

**First step.** Make MessagePersister.setAccountHistoryId throwing: fetch by the account email, and throw on a failed fetch or no row. Update its three call sites, delete the uncalled finalizeSync, and pin with a cursor-suite test that a failed Account fetch commits nothing.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: reconciliation lists a capped page with nextPageToken, the final save is scripted to fail; assert the missed-message cursor in the suite's defaults is unchanged and the next run re-lists it. Revert-check: the post-save cursor write.

**Payoff.** One place encodes the counter, checkpoint, cursor and tracker order for all three runs, so a mistake on the path that silently skips mail fails tests instead of review.

### `sync-persist-path#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**A held, cancelled or expired history slice is redone in full: stored messages are re-downloaded, re-parsed and re-labelled**

Area: Message fetch, processing and persistence path. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Every message ID of a history slice goes to a full-format fetch with no stored-row filter; preparation runs before the existing-row lookup; the update path re-reads the body file and resets labels. Cursor and continuation commit only in the final save (deliberate), so an expired, killed or aborted run, or a held slice (two more passes at most), re-downloads rows that per-batch saves already stored. The drain (at most 50, backoff-paced) and reconciliation run under every budget. The cost is wasted work and stale background refresh, not loss; app-refresh slices are capped at 3x100 records.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:35-58 — all slice IDs go to BatchProcessor.processMessages with no existence filter; the context is saved per batch only when allowsIntermediateContextSaves
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:154 — getMessage(id:, format: "full", maxRetries: 1) for every ID; GmailAPIClient.swift:119 sets reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData, so nothing is served from an HTTP cache
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Updates.swift:232-238, 420-432, 610-613 — a refetch reads the stored body to compare (rewrite skipped when identical), sets labels = nil and re-adds them, and re-tracks the conversation for rollup
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:329, 397, 434-452, 471-491 — drain and reconciliation run unconditionally; checkpoint and cursor are staged only into the final save; a held slice leaves the checkpoint where it was
- esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:107-110, 136, 142 — app-refresh slice is 3 pages of 100 records (comment: so a continuation can commit before expiration); 3 consecutive failures escape; drain capped at 50 per sync
- docs/scalability-review.md:433-445, 1512, 1603, 1607 — same item already recorded (bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored under Will degrade; stored-ID skip under Hygiene and marked optional); step 8 has no Built note, step 9 built only the maintenance half

**Trigger.** BGAppRefresh or BGProcessing expiry, process termination or an account transition mid-run, a daily-quota or full-disk abort, or one message that keeps failing (the slice is processed three times, then escaped). Plain app suspension does not cancel a foreground run: backgrounding only stops the periodic loop, and SyncEngine.cancelSync has no caller.

**Impact.** A full app-refresh slice (about 300 full fetches, up to 50 drain fetches, about 100 reconciliation calls) that does not finish in its window starts from zero on each refresh until a foreground or processing run completes it. A catch-up slice of up to 10x500 records is downloaded up to three times when one message keeps failing. Battery, data and quota are wasted and the app opens stale after a multi-day gap. No data loss, no cursor corruption, no permanent wedge. Whether a 300-record slice actually exceeds the window is estimated, not measured.

**Verifier.** Read every cited path whole; the code is as described. High lowered to medium: bounded, self-healing in the foreground, and the expiry estimate is unmeasured. Rate-limit 403s are retriable (GmailAPIClient.swift:536-539); only daily quota aborts. The missed-message check already filters stored IDs (SyncReconciliation.swift:510-531). Fix hazard: skipped stored IDs must still be tracked for rollup, because a cancelled run rolls back its ModificationTracker transaction (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:588-590).

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored (433-449; Review correction 445) and Hygiene item at 1512. Step 9 (1607) built the maintenance half (BackgroundMailboxSyncBudget.allowsStoreMaintenance). MessagePersister+Updates.swift:227-238 built the identical-body rewrite skip. Not built: the stored-ID skip, the label-set diff, and app-refresh gating of the drain and label reconciliation.

**Invariant risks**

- Deferred ledger and failed reads: a skipped deferred ID counts as persisted, and then recordFailure's replace (SyncFailureTracker.swift:132-137) or the clean advance's deleteDeferredRows removes its row. A stored row can still be one whose update failed (bodyWriteFailed). Exempt the deferred IDs. A failed existence, ledger or record read must skip nothing, never count as 'stored'.
- Send echoes: an echo saved while its anchor was unresolved (shouldConsumeAfterPersistence false, MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:216) is consumed only when a later refetch goes through the update path (Updates.swift:580-590). Exempt IDs where remoteCommittedMessageId equals the ID, and rows whose stored messageId equals MimeBuilder.messageId(forOptimisticMessageID:) of a marker record.
- Rollups: a killed run's batch saves (MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58) store rows without a rollup recompute, and its ModificationTracker transaction is lost. Today the refetch rebuilds it by re-tracking the conversation (Updates.swift:610-621). Skipped IDs must re-track their conversation objectIDs, or stale unread and hasInbox rollups stay.
- Counts and the safety net: skipped IDs must stay out of successfulCount, because newMessagesCount feeds SyncStorageBackoff.recordSuccessfulRun, which lifts the full-disk backoff when a run stored mail. Listing missed messages without fetching them is unsafe: the resume cursors are saved at list time, and the window starts at lastSuccessfulSyncTime minus 5 min. A committed slice moves that time, so the found IDs fall out of the window.

**Fix.** Filter in MessageFetchPhase, before BatchProcessor (MessageListPaginator shares BatchProcessor). Per 500 IDs, run one indexed `id IN` dictionary fetch on the sync context that returns id, conversation and messageId. Skip stored IDs, except deferred-ledger IDs and IDs a live OutboundSendMutationRecord names (by remoteCommittedMessageId, or by a marker record's RFC Message-ID). If any read fails, skip nothing. Record skipped IDs as persisted but leave them out of successfulCount, and track their conversations in the transaction. Separately, add a budget flag so an app refresh skips the drain and label reconciliation, leaving the reconciliation time and needsFollowUp unchanged. Keep the missed-message check whole: it already fetches only absent IDs.

**First step.** Write a failing IncrementalSyncCursorTests case: save stored rows for two of a slice's three IDs, run performSync with a MockGmailAPIClient that records getMessage calls, and assert that only the unstored ID is fetched. Then add the filter helper in MessageFetchPhase.

**Pinning test.** IncrementalSyncCursorTests: stored IDs are not fetched but count as persisted, and the cursor advances. Deferred-ledger and send-record IDs are still fetched. A failed existence read fetches everything. Skipped rows' conversations are re-tracked. Revert-check names the filter.

**Payoff.** A redone or held slice fetches only unstored and failing IDs. Expired app refreshes make progress instead of re-downloading about 300 messages, and a held 5,000-record slice is not downloaded three times.

### `sync-persist-path#6` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**The cursor escape hatch counts runs, not messages, and cannot tell a bad message from a bad environment**

Area: Message fetch, processing and persistence path. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

One per-account counter takes a strike per run with any blocking ID (429/5xx/timeout surviving a ~4 s ladder, non-ENOSPC write or Core Data errors, 4xx/decode). The deferred set is replaced each run, so at strike 3 that run's failing IDs are abandoned whatever their own history. A held run forces up to three immediate follow-ups, so the strikes can be spent back-to-back. Abandoned rows get five single-GET drain attempts over at least 17 h, then are deleted; the notification has no observer. Full disk, auth and quota abort without striking.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:412-419 and 981-984 — any failing ID in the run increments the single account-level count (saturating at 3) handed to planHistoryAdvance
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:132-137 and 229-261 — deferred rows absent from this run are deleted; at count >= 3 every deferred row is flipped to abandoned with no per-ID or failure-class test
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:47 and 286-304, with IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:540 — a held run reports needsFollowUp and the coordinator forces up to 3 immediate follow-ups (force: true bypasses the 30 s gap)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageFetcher.swift:61-64, 194-201, 410-414 and esc-chatmail/Services/ErrorHandling/APIErrorRecovery.swift:17-24, 41-52 — rateLimited/timeout/network/5xx are same-request retriable and, once exhausted, join fetchFailedIds; only auth, revoked credentials and quota abort the run
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessagePersister.swift:577-582, 620-633, 650-660 — out-of-space and entityCreationFailed throw run-level aborts; body-fetch failures, other I/O errors and generic creation errors return .failed
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:298-310, 540-551, 565-569 and esc-chatmail/Services/Config/Constants.swift:136-148 — abandonment posts .syncMessagesAbandoned (git grep: declaration, post and tests only); the 5th failed drain attempt deletes the row; backoff 15 min, x4 per attempt, capped at 12 h

**Trigger.** History listing succeeds but message GETs (or non-full-disk local writes) fail past the ~4 s ladder in three consecutive runs, which a single foreground trigger chains back-to-back through forced follow-ups. A permanent drop additionally needs five failed drain attempts spaced 15 min, 1 h, 4 h and 12 h apart.

**Impact.** Mail is passed by the cursor for transient, non-message reasons and then arrives only through the drain (50 IDs per run, one unretried GET each); this usually heals within a run or two. A message whose failure persists across the five drain attempts (4xx/decode defect, persistent per-ID 5xx or body-fetch failure, lasting local write error) is removed from the ledger with only a log line: no row, no UI, and no later backstop, because the abandoning commit resets lastSuccessfulSyncTime and the missed-message window starts 5 minutes before it.

**Verifier.** Read tracker, fetcher, persister, orchestrator, reconciliation and foreground coordinator. Corrections: full disk and model mismatch already abort (MessagePersister 620-629) and an offline run is skipped, so "local failures" is narrower; the auditor missed the immediate follow-up chain. Environment-only permanent loss is unlikely given the 17 h spacing. The prior review keeps 429 per-message (line 396) and calls the bounded ledger sound (line 1638); neither covers per-run counting or the silent terminal delete.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1638 'Already sound': the failure ledger is bounded and rows are deleted after 5 attempts. That is a size bound, not accepted loss. enospc-bodyless-rows and sync-out-of-space-backoff (1255-1297, step 6, built) kept only full-disk failures from using strikes.

**Invariant risks**

- Making transient or network failures never strike brings back the permanent cursor stall the escape hatch exists to prevent. One message with a persistent 5xx, timeout or body-fetch failure would hold the cursor forever, and on a non-terminal slice it would also hold every later page.
- Changing needsFollowUp itself breaks BackgroundSyncManager's catch-up scheduling and the background maintenance gate (SyncEngine.swift:312), and CLAUDE.md says not to key the foreground on it. Add a separate held-for-retry signal instead.
- A per-ID strike count cannot reuse retryCount, which the drain owns, so it needs a new attribute and therefore ESCChatmail 7, never an edit to version 6. recordFailure must still replace the deferred set and never truncate it, and counters must be staged only into the run's context, with success effects applied only through commit().
- A kept terminal row must stay out of the drain predicate and its paced-row count, whose nil disjuncts are load-bearing. It must never be 'deferred', because a clean advance deletes those. Count it by retryCount >= cap rather than by state, because a re-scan can turn it back into deferred and then abandoned. It stays in AuthSession's account-scoped wipe list, and a Retry must rewrite rows only under the account-work lease, never racing the run's staged ledger.

**Fix.** Keep the run-level hatch. (1) At the drain cap, stop deleting rows. Write retryCount = cap and a terminal state "exhausted": a String value, so no model change, and the existing `retryCount <` term already excludes it, in old builds too. Clear such a row once a Message with its id exists. Show the count in a banner like AbandonedPendingActionsModel's, with Retry and Open in Gmail. (2) In the drain, only message-scoped verdicts spend retryCount; timeout, network, 5xx and 429 failures only stamp the backoff. (3) Add a held-for-retry flag to IncrementalSyncResult. SyncEngine passes `needsFollowUp && !held` to the foreground completion, so held runs are not chained by force; background stays unchanged. (4) Optionally, space strikes with an optional `lastStrikeAt` in the counter payload.

**First step.** In SyncFailureTracker.stageAbandonedRetryOutcome (lines 540-551), replace the delete at the cap with retryCount = cap and a new AbandonedSyncMessage.State.exhausted. Update the two tests in AbandonedMessageRetryTests that pin deletion at the cap, giving the reason.

**Pinning test.** AbandonedMessageRetryTests: after a fifth failed drain attempt the row is exhausted, not offered by fetchRetryableAbandonedMessageIds, and counted by the banner's query (Revert-check: the delete). ForegroundSyncCoordinatorTests: a held, untruncated run queues no immediate continuation; a truncated one still does.

**Payoff.** Skipped mail can no longer vanish with only a log line, and one foreground trigger during a brief Gmail 5xx/429 burst no longer spends all three strikes.

### `background-energy#2` · low · reliability · effort M · new

**A foreground run frozen by suspension keeps the single-flight boundary, and the next background wake treats it as an active sync and yields**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

On iOS, scene-background cancels only the coordinator's periodic and deferred tasks. The run task is never cancelled, and the only background assertion covers the arm's pending checks. A run still in flight therefore freezes while it owns the exclusive boundary. Both the foreground and the background incremental entries register as .foregroundIncremental (.background is never used), so a later BGTask on the still-suspended process can find that stranded run, read `.blocked(by: .foregroundIncremental)` and complete with success. That wake syncs nothing and gets no catch-up retry. The cadence re-armed when the handler started still stands, and the next activation queues its sync behind the resumed run.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:386-388 — background does stop(reason:) then arms the tasks; nothing cancels or holds the active run
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:76-83 — stop cancels periodicTask and deferredSyncTask only; :122-131 and :162-176 the next activation sees alreadyInProgress and queues behind the current run
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:116-120 — the scene-background assertion is ended in the arm Task's defer, once the pending checks and submits finish
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:518 — prepareIncrementalSync, shared by both entries, always uses kind .foregroundIncremental; :316-319 blocked reports activeRunKind()
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:188-196 — handlers re-arm refresh/processing at entry; :342-345 and :452-456 blocked by a foreground kind returns true with no catch-up retry
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:494-500 — a failed request after a suspension longer than 120 s is not retried, because the budget is measured with Date()

**Trigger.** iOS only. The user leaves the app while a forced activation sync (or a continuation) still has work left. The process then stays suspended, not jetsammed, until a BGTask wakes it. On that wake the handler, which has only fast hops before beginRunWithTask on a warm process, must take the boundary before the resumed run unwinds. Which side wins that race is not established from code.

**Impact.** One discretionary background wake is spent and reported as success, with no 5-minute catch-up. It is not lost cadence: the ordinary refresh/processing requests were re-armed when the handler started. Nothing is lost: a resumed run that trips the 120 s budget fails like a cancellation, and the cursor and ledger rules keep its uncommitted work safe to redo. At the next open the activation sync waits for the resumed run and then runs, so mail is no staler than if the wake had never come.

**Verifier.** The code is as cited. cancelSync and cancelForegroundRun have no caller, and no beginBackgroundTask covers sync. Corrections: "schedules nothing" overlooks the re-arm at handler entry. "Work discarded" is not data loss, and the auditor's own fix (cancel at expiry) rolls back the same way. "Stale at next open" is wrong, because the activation queues behind the resumed run. Jetsam of a suspended process removes the stranded run. Whether a frozen run outlives several wakes is not shown, which is why severity is low, not medium.

**Invariant risks**

- A BG handler that waits behind the run with waitUntilIdle (parkUntilIdle at SyncRunCoordinator.swift:321 ignores cancellation) keeps an expired BGTask from being completed, because BackgroundTaskCompletionLatch waits for the worker to return. CLAUDE.md records that exact hang as the reason parkUntilIdleOrCancelled exists, so any such wait must be cancellable.
- UIKit's expiration handler has to end the assertion before it returns (SceneBackgroundAssertionLatch.swift:31-35, OutboundSendBackgroundLease.swift:31-34). Awaiting the run's rollback there gets the app killed by the watchdog. The handler cancels the run and ends the assertion at once, and the run finishes unwinding when the process next runs.
- Store maintenance is asked for after stop(): with periodicTask nil, scheduleImmediateFollowUp returns false (ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:290), so SyncEngine.swift:261-262 starts the passes. A lease ended at the sync's endRun leaves them unprotected. Asking for them from inside the run deadlocks (CLAUDE.md), so the lease has to span the outer Task and be cancelled through it.
- Reusing PlatformOutboundBackgroundTaskManager on the Mac would hold a .userInitiated activity on every 60 s run. That activity disables idle sleep (ProcessActivityOutboundBackgroundTaskManager.swift:25-30), which goes against the decided pause on system sleep (AppLifecyclePolicy.swift:12-14). Keep the sync lease iOS-only.

**Fix.** Two steps, in this order. (1) Thread a run kind through SyncEngine.prepareIncrementalSync, start performIncrementalSyncForBackground's run as .background, and make shouldScheduleRetryWhenBlocked true for .foregroundInitial/.foregroundIncremental: a wake blocked by a foreground run then schedules the 5-minute catch-up and reports false, while .background stays satisfied. (2) iOS only: hold a UIKit background task per foreground-entry run, begun synchronously when SyncEngine admits it and ended after endRun and any post-chain maintenance; expiration cancels the run's registered task and the outer task, then ends the assertion at once (OutboundSendBackgroundLease's shape). No-op on the Mac. Any wait in the BG handler must be cancellable. Leave the Date()-based retry budget alone.

**First step.** Add a kind parameter to SyncEngine.prepareIncrementalSync and pass .background from performIncrementalSyncForBackground. Make shouldScheduleRetryWhenBlocked return true for both foreground kinds, and update testModelV3Executor_activeMailboxSyncSatisfiesTaskWithoutCatchUp and testBlockedBackgroundSync_schedulesRetryOnlyForPendingActions.

**Pinning test.** BackgroundSyncManagerTests: blocked by .foregroundIncremental returns false with retryBackoffs == [catchUpRetryDelay], and .background still succeeds. SyncEngine: a parked background run reports activeRunKind() == .background; a lease spy's expiration cancels the run, leaves the cursor unchanged and ends the lease once.

**Payoff.** A wake that meets a frozen foreground run gets a 5-minute catch-up instead of a silent success. A run still going at backgrounding either finishes or rolls back, instead of freezing while it holds the boundary.

### `invariant-enforcement#5` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Cursor staging is correct by five agreeing copies, not by the types that hold the context and the cursor**

Area: Invariant enforcement, complexity budget and change safety. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

It is true that the cursor, ledger, counter and checkpoint commit together only because five orchestrator sites call things in the right order, and that behaviour tests pin this, not the types. The rest is overstated. MessageFetchPhase's batch save only runs when the orchestrator allows it, and it happens before any cursor-coupled staging, so it commits messages ahead of the cursor, which is the safe direction. The flag that defaults to true guards a different rule (no mid-run flush when history deletes local messages), not the cursor. A hand-made plan cannot move the cursor. What is really left is hygiene: dead APIs that bypass the plan, and one wrong comment.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AccountPersister.swift:142-166 — `finalizeSync(historyId:in:)` sets the cursor and saves with no plan or terminal-slice check. Its doc comment presents it as the atomic finalize, and `git grep 'finalizeSync('` finds no caller in the app or the tests.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:57-64, 393-397 — `recordSuccess()` and `reset()` write UserDefaults success/failure state directly. Only SyncFailureTrackerTests calls recordSuccess, and CLAUDE.md:79 already forbids both inside a run.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58, 65-72 — the batch save runs only when the orchestrator's `allowsIntermediateContextSaves` is set, and before `recordFailure`. The comment says the deferred rows commit with the final save.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:348-377, 415-446 — the intermediate flush saves after the deferred and drain staging but before the plan, the strike count, the checkpoint and the cursor are staged. So the deferred rows commit early and the MessageFetchPhase comment is wrong, but harmlessly. The terminal check is an `if nextPageToken` beside `setAccountHistoryId`.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:175-191, 288-326 — `HistoryAdvancePlan` has an internal memberwise init, but `commit` only writes UserDefaults keys, the drain latch and a notification. The cursor is set separately.
- esc-chatmailTests/Sync/IncrementalSyncCursorTests.swift:577-618, 863-931 — the cursor stays frozen through five non-terminal slices and advances only on the terminal one. A failed final save commits no cursor, checkpoint or success state.

**Trigger.** Someone calls the dead `finalizeSync`, `recordSuccess()` or `reset()`, or adds a new finalize site (for example the unbuilt step 8 resume points) without copying the plan, stage, save, commit order.

**Impact.** Nothing fails today. If one of those APIs were misused, the cursor could advance past mail that was never fetched. Two things limit that. Each sync re-checks recent mail since the last successful sync and fetches what is missing (SyncReconciliation.swift:119-166, 492-507). And IncrementalSyncCursorTests (49 tests), which CLAUDE.md:96 says to extend for any sync change, pins the ordering.

**Verifier.** I read SyncPhase, MessageFetchPhase, AccountPersister, SyncFailureTracker, both checkpoint stores, both orchestrators in full, and the cursor tests. The five sites are as described. Only MessageFetchPhase saves inside Phases/. The batch saves and the flush run before any cursor-coupled staging, by design (SyncFailureTracker:68-70), so CLAUDE.md:77 is not broken in substance. The dead code is real and worth deleting. The rewrite into a SyncRunTransaction type is a style choice with no failure shown, so I lowered the severity to low.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md:77-79 (the convention and its ban on recordSuccess/reset); docs/scalability-review.md:1637 "Already sound" (cursor, ledger and counter commit atomically); step 8 (line 1603) not built

**Invariant risks**

- Commit order. `failureTracker.commit`, the ModificationTracker commit/consume and `committedModificationTransaction = true` come after the final save and before the post-save cancellation check (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:493-507, 1014-1017). A unified `finalize()` that can throw between them rolls back a transaction that has already committed (CLAUDE.md:94).
- `commit(advancePlan, recordsSuccessfulSync: !historyResult.wasTruncated)` (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:503-506). A finalize that always records success writes `lastSuccessfulSyncTime` on a non-terminal slice, and that key is the floor of history recovery and reconciliation (CLAUDE.md:88).
- Initial sync and recovery advance to the pre-scan `profile.historyId` with no history slice (InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:329-335, IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:856). Their page saves commit the frozen window on purpose (InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:299-324). A token that demands a terminal `HistoryCollectionResult`, or a ban on staging before finalize, breaks both and blocks step 8's page-token resume.
- Serializer and gate. Rollups and the final save stay in one `performThrowingSyncMutation` (CLAUDE.md:92). Initial sync's `runFullCleanup(in: context)` saves the sync context under the cleanup gate (InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:106, DataCleanupService.swift:200-215), so a transaction that holds turns across the whole run hangs. Keep the `makeSyncContext` seam and the source pins (IncrementalSyncCursorTests.swift:171-191, StoreMaintenanceAfterSyncSourceTests.swift:20-24).

**Fix.** Do the hygiene now and put off the type. In one change, delete `MessagePersister.finalizeSync` (it has no callers) and `saveAccount`'s `saveHistoryId` parameter. Its default of `true` writes the cursor with no plan, and every caller passes false. Delete `recordSuccess()` and `reset()` with their three tests; `testCommit_appliesSuccessStateOnlyWhenCalled` keeps the coverage. Drop the clause in CLAUDE.md:79 that names them. Give `HistoryAdvancePlan` a `fileprivate init(outcome:)`. Make `setAccountHistoryId` throw when its Account fetch fails or finds nothing, instead of using `try?` (CLAUDE.md:84). Correct the comment at MessageFetchPhase.swift:65-66. Do not wrap the context, because every callee takes the raw context. Build any advance token as part of step 8, and have it accept both a terminal-slice proof and a completed-listing proof.

**First step.** Delete `finalizeSync` (AccountPersister.swift:142-166) and `saveAccount`'s `saveHistoryId` parameter, removing the five `saveHistoryId: false` arguments. Build, then run AccountPersisterTests, InitialSyncOrchestratorTests and IncrementalSyncCursorTests through `./Scripts/codex-test.sh -only-testing`.

**Pinning test.** A `repositorySource` test over AccountPersister.swift and both orchestrators: `historyId =` is assigned only in `setAccountHistoryId`, `finalizeSync` and `saveHistoryId` are absent, and `setAccountHistoryId(` keeps exactly its three call sites. Revert-check: restoring `finalizeSync`.

**Payoff.** Removes four APIs that write the cursor or the sync-success state without a plan, one of them through a `true` default. The only behaviour change is that a failed Account read now aborts the run instead of committing.

## Store write costs at scale (12)

### `gap-change-propagation-pipeline#1` · high · performance · effort M · known-open

**Sends write on the view context, and PersonFactory pins their Persons there for the process**

Area: From one store save to every observer: merge, cache invalidation and UI. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

An optimistic send builds its graph on the main-queue view context. Its From row sets participant.person to the self Person through the same factory the scale harness measured reading all 120,000 of the user's participations at S2, so each send can fault that hub on main. This happens with or without PersonFactory. What the pin adds is that the self Person and the recipients stay registered in the view context. After that, every merged save that touches them refreshes them, and the open chat re-maps its outgoing rows. On the list side the self Person is cheap, but each recipient fans out across that person's conversations.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1247-1257 — @MainActor; the From participant (the user's address) is created with MessageParticipantFactory.create(in: viewContext); Dependencies.swift:116-121 builds the service with the view context
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:26-33,83-89,290 — Persons are stored strongly in an NSMutableDictionary in context.userInfo; participant.person = person maintains the Person.messageParticipations inverse
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleHubFaultTests.swift:212-213 — the same factory path (MessagePersister) in a fresh context: 'a new message reads all 120,000 of the user's participations' (XCTExpectFailure)
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:182,541-548 — the view context merges automatically; only resetStore clears the PersonFactory cache on it
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:239-257 — any refreshed Person invalidates every cached row whose sender email matches; VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:32-43 re-fetches and re-maps them on the view context
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationIdentity.swift:75 — the user's own addresses are dropped from conversation participants, so ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:235-244 walks only note-to-self chats for the self Person, and k conversations for each pinned recipient

**Trigger.** Any send at S2/S3, on the main thread; the cold first send after launch is the worst case. After the first send, every sync save that adds a message involving the user or a recipient pinned this session, while a chat is open.

**Impact.** At S2 a send realizes up to about 120k MessageParticipant objects on main. The review measured 100 ms warm and 3.8 s cold on an M5 Pro, but for both hubs together (217k objects); a send reads only the self hub, and an iPhone is slower. This is a hitch on send, and can be a hang. After that, the open chat re-fetches and re-maps up to its 300-row window of own rows on main for each such save, and each pinned recipient re-triggers the existing person-change-conversation-fanout item.

**Verifier.** Every cited line holds. Three corrections. (1) The per-send fault does not depend on the pin: without it the Person is fetched fresh, with its participations unread. (2) SyncContextPageObjectRelease.swift:15-18 says a refresh re-faults the self-Person hub, so a merge likely drops the 120k set; the Person stays pinned for the process, its participations probably do not. (3) The list walk is cheap for the self Person. Not documented as a decision; inverse-tomany-hub-fault-tax covers sync contexts and label writes, not the send's main-thread write.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: inverse-tomany-hub-fault-tax (510-534; v7 fix, step 10 at 1623 not built) and person-change-conversation-fanout (895-917; step 5 "Not built yet" at 1561). New here: the send path's main-thread instance, the view-context PersonFactory pin, and the transcript's Person-driven re-map.

**Invariant risks**

- Moving creation to a private context breaks the unsaved-anchor cases: a temporary-ID conversation (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:92-98) and the includesPendingChanges lookup on the view context (:1182). It also breaks the same-turn local-send tail append, which needs the optimistic row inserted in the view context (VirtualScrollState+TailAppend.swift:31-34, 54-79), and the view-context rollback and draft paths (:417-479, :1443-1486). Any second creation route must keep the gate, then the turn, and must not ask for the gate inside the turn.
- Refreshing the self Person with mergeChanges false after each send changes the 120k-participation fault on main from once per merge to every send. The refresh also posts a refreshed Person, which both observers treat as a display change today. So it must never ship before the observer filter, and it should wait for ESCChatmail 7.
- The observer filter has to compare every Person field the consumers read. The chat row reads email, displayName and avatarURL (ChatMessageRowModel.swift:411-451); the list snapshot reads email and displayName (ConversationSnapshot.swift:64-70). Merged refreshes carry no changed-key delta, so compare current values with the row or snapshot, never with changedValues alone. A filter on email and displayName only would leave an open chat's avatars stale.
- Self MessageParticipant rows must stay, because strictParticipantSetIdentity needs complete From/To rows: v7 drops only the inverse. Dropping the PersonFactory cache after a send must keep resetStore's resetViewContextState cleanup (CoreDataStack.swift:521-547), which is the cross-account guard.

**Fix.** Ship in this order, inside existing code paths, with no schema change. 1) Filter both observers: VirtualScrollState.refreshedCachedMessageIDs counts an updated or refreshed Person only for rows whose senderInfoDisplayName or senderInfoAvatarURL differs from its current values; conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges skips a Person whose email=displayName fingerprint entry the window's snapshots already hold, then person-change-conversation-fanout's window-scoped fetch bounds k. 2) Drop PersonFactory's view-context cache in a defer after each optimistic creation (hygiene). 3) Leave the self hub fault to ESCChatmail 7's inverse-less self edge. Do not move creation to a private context, or refresh the self Person per send: that faults the hub on every send.

**First step.** Add a --performance case to ScaleHubFaultTests that drives the real createOptimisticMessage on the S2 store's main-queue context. Wrap its self-hub fault and registered-object assertions in XCTExpectFailure naming inverse-tomany-hub-fault-tax. The send path is not in the harness today.

**Pinning test.** A VirtualScrollState change-observation test: one local send's objectsDidChange (self and recipient Persons updated through the inverse) re-maps only the appended row, and so does a merged refresh of an unchanged Person. A displayName or avatarURL change still re-maps. Revert-check: the filter.

**Payoff.** Each send in an open chat, and each merged sync, stops re-fetching and re-mapping up to 300 rows on main. The send-time self-hub fault gets a measured harness case for v7.

### `sync-persist-path#1` · high · scalability · effort L · known-open

**Every message write still faults mailbox-sized Label and self-Person inverse sets into the run's fresh context**

Area: Message fetch, processing and persistence path. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Confirmed from code. Model v6, still current, keeps inverses on Label.messages/Message.labels and MessageParticipant.person/Person.messageParticipations. Each incremental run and each history recovery builds a fresh background context. In it, the create path's addToLabels and participant.person writes (self not excluded), history label adds/removes and message deletes each read a hub's whole inverse set; the strict XCTExpectFailure harness still pins this (217,062 objects for one new message at S2). The update path nils and re-adds labels on every refetched row unless a local change is pending. ESCChatmail 7 is unbuilt.

- esc-chatmail/Models/CoreData/ESCChatmail.xcdatamodeld/ESCChatmail 6.xcdatamodel/contents:83,149,177,185 — Label.messages/Message.labels and MessageParticipant.person/Person.messageParticipations each declare an inverseName; .xccurrentversion:6 still names ESCChatmail 6.xcdatamodel, and the directory has no version 7
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Creation.swift:134-153 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:290 — saveParticipants then addToLabels per label on every new message; the factory sets participant.person = person, and MessagePersister+Participants.swift:16-46 saves From/To/Cc/Bcc with no exclusion of the owner
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Updates.swift:414-432 — unless shouldPreserveLocalMailboxState, existingMessage.labels = nil and every incoming label is re-added, with no comparison against the stored set
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:137,219,708 — makeSyncContext defaults to coreDataStack.newBackgroundContext() and is called once per incremental run and once per history recovery
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleHubFaultTests.swift:209-217,240-248,269-281 — XCTExpectFailure wrappers still on for a new message (97,031 INBOX members, 120,000 participations, 217,062 objects), a label removal (97,040) and a deletion (219,916)
- docs/scalability-review.md:516,534,1539,1623 — measurements on an M5 Pro (S2 100 ms warm / 3.8 s cold, +49 MB; S3 1,238 ms, +172 MB), a ~10x spread between harnesses, wrappers recorded as still on, and step 10 (ESCChatmail 7) with no Built entry

**Trigger.** Any sync run at S2 or above (foreground, BGAppRefresh, BGProcessing, history recovery) whose fresh context inserts a message, applies a history label add or remove on a system label, deletes a message, or refetches a stored row with no pending local change. Refetches of stored rows come from history replays and re-lists; the missed-message check filters stored IDs first (SyncReconciliation.swift:528-529).

**Impact.** Paid once per hub per run, on the sync context's queue, not the main thread. Prior measurement on an M5 Pro Mac: 100 ms warm or 3.8 s cold and +49 MB at S2; 1.24 s and +172 MB at S3, cold not measured; the review expects 2-4x slower on an iPhone and records a ~10x spread between harnesses. A single relationship fault cannot be cancelled part-way, so a cold background run spends that time out of the ~30 s app-refresh window before writing one message. No failure is demonstrated at S2; the cost grows linearly with INBOX size and mailbox size.

**Verifier.** All six cited locations read as described; nothing was run. No guard, cache or context reuse found; SyncContextPageObjectRelease refreshes page rows only. Not a deliberate decision: review step 10 is unbuilt. Tightened: the update path is the only hub write just in refetch-only runs, and the numbers are Mac-measured. Severity high rests on the structural clause more than on S2 timings. The same factory line runs on the view context for optimistic sends (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1252-1268), unmeasured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:510-534 `inverse-tomany-hub-fault-tax`; Suggested order step 10 (line 1623, no Built entry; step 4 harness built, wrappers still on, line 1539); line 1512 refetch item (HTML-write skip built at MessagePersister+Updates.swift:227-238, label diff not)

**Invariant risks**

- A failed Core Data read is never empty: fetchLabelsByIds returns [:] on a fetch error (LabelPersister.swift:36-41). A diff that takes that as the desired set strips every label, exactly as `labels = nil` does today (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:421-432), and the rollup then saves a zero unread count while the cursor advances. Resolve labels before the body write, and map a failed read to .lookupFailed, which becomes .failed (MessagePersister.swift:597-600).
- The diff must stay behind hasPendingLocalModification (Updates.swift:218,414) and compare Label objects, not ID strings. Duplicate Label rows are legal (LabelPersister.swift:42-45; LabelOperationProcessor.swift:81-83), and an incoming ID that has no Label row must not count as a difference, or every refetch writes. Guard the isUnread assignment too: an equal-value assignment still dirties the row (Helpers.swift:703-708).
- The v7 migration runs inside the launch watchdog. prepareProductionAppPersistence is @MainActor (AppStartupBootstrap.swift), and nothing in the app sets shouldAddStoreAsynchronously (review line 1492). Keep v7 additive: a new version directory plus the .xccurrentversion bump, v6 never edited, and a versionHashModifier on every index change. Backfill in a latched, cancellable maintenance pass, never a custom mapping over 120k-400k rows at launch. Optional flags read NULL, so their filters need an `== nil` disjunct.
- Stopping system-label writes still leaves the v6 join rows. Message.labels is Nullify, so a delete faults INBOX through them, and every in-memory `labels.contains { $0.id == "INBOX" }` reader (rollup snapshot, reconciliation, MessageActions) has to switch at the same latch. For self-Person, keep the self MessageParticipant rows (strictParticipantSetIdentity). Replace each Person.messageParticipations reader (EntityCleanup:531-536, Migration:596,723) and its Cascade rule with fetches.

**Fix.** Two stages. Now, with no schema change: in performExistingMessageUpdate, resolve the desired Label objects (incoming IDs that have rows; a failed read throws) before the body write. Remove only stored labels that are not desired, add only desired labels that are not stored, write nothing when the two are equal, and guard the isUnread assignment the same way. Then cut ESCChatmail 7 (step 10), after making the store load asynchronous: additive system-label flags on Message, read through MessagePredicates, filled by NSBatchUpdateRequest in a latched maintenance pass that also clears the system join rows (measure how in the harness first); an inverse-less MessageParticipant.person that keeps the self rows; harness wrappers removed in that change.

**First step.** Add a ScaleHubFaultTests case that refetches manifest.ordinaryConversationInboxMessageID with its stored labels through MessagePersister.saveMessages, under XCTExpectFailure. Then implement the label diff at MessagePersister+Updates.swift:413-433 and remove that wrapper.

**Pinning test.** ScaleHubFaultTests: refetching a stored INBOX message with unchanged labels leaves both hubs as faults and registers under 1,000 objects (Revert-check: the diff). MessagePersisterUpdateTests: a changed set lands exactly; a failed label read gives .failed with stored labels intact.

**Payoff.** Refetch-only runs (held-cursor re-scans, recovery re-lists) stop faulting the INBOX, UNREAD and category hubs (S2: 100 ms warm, 3.8 s cold, +49 MB). v7 extends this to inserts, relabels and deletes.

### `concurrency-model#3` · medium · performance · effort M · known-partial

**The main actor is still a store writer: synchronous saves wait for any background transaction**

Area: Concurrency model and Swift 6 readiness. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The main actor commits to the store synchronously: about four times per send (optimistic graph on the view context, pre-transmission check, admission and committed markers through performAndWait), a view-context draft save per 350 ms typing pause, each pending-action enqueue, and five launch-repair saves through performAndWait. SQLite has one writer, so each waits out any commit in flight on another context. That commit is batch-bounded except for conversation-wide archive or spam and a history slice that defers its saves. No commit was timed.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:16,347,563,608,671,727 — @MainActor class with five direct storage.saveIfNeeded(context) calls, not three; 537-541 comment says the preview passes 'rarely have anything to save' and only the verdict backfill was moved off main. esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:13-27 — saveIfNeeded is context.performAndWait { save }, and its comment says the launch repair passes call it from the main actor
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:54-66,369,565-573,755-757,1471-1473 — creation saves viewContext inside the cleanup gate and the conversation turns; pre-transmission viewContext.save(); @MainActor recordRemoteSendState saves a private context through performAndWait. esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:186-207 — admitTransmission runs persistMarker 'without yielding the main actor', documented as the linearization point. esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:299-303,326-336,414-418 — each of these is a MainActor.run hop per send
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:348-350,1347,1396 and esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/ChatReplyDraftStore.swift:71-73,104 — composer changes debounce 350 ms into a draft save that awaits the cleanup gate, then context.save() on the view context. esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManager.swift:671-680 — enqueue is viewContext.perform { saveOrLog }
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:201-215,234-251 — cleanup passes mutate and save inside performCleanupSensitiveMutation, the same gate optimistic creation and draft saves await asynchronously, so those two never block the main thread behind a cleanup commit
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:37,53-58 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1067-1087 — sync commits per 50-message batch unless the slice has a deletion, a label-less add or an excluded label, when its messages commit in one later save. esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/MessageActions.swift:485-487,840-844 — conversation-wide actions save inside a background context.perform
- docs/scalability-review.md:69,1053-1068,1656 — root cause 4 already names main-actor saves in ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator; item version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation cites line 347 'saveIfNeeded on main' with impact 'occasional main-thread hitches'; the V6 display-name refresh is listed under 'Checked and found not to be a problem' as upgrade-only

**Trigger.** A send, a typing pause, a pending-action enqueue or a launch-repair save that lands while another context is committing. A hang-sized stall needs a large concurrent commit: Archive or Report Spam of a conversation with thousands of messages while the user types or sends in another chat, or a catch-up history slice that contains a deletion or an excluded mailbox label, whose messages commit in one save. Otherwise the concurrent commit is a 50-message sync batch or a 10 to 25 row repair batch.

**Impact.** Usually a stall of one small commit on tap-to-bubble or at a typing pause; unmeasured, and likely a frame or two. A hang only where the main-side save meets a multi-thousand-row commit. Cleanup passes do not stall optimistic creation or draft saves on the main thread, since both await the cleanup gate; only the ungated marker saves and the enqueue can meet a cleanup commit. Launch-repair saves are rare: V6 is one-shot, and the title, preview and stranded-shell passes save only when they repaired something. The exception is the chat-preview batch save at line 347, a prior open item.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited site; all as described. Corrections: five coordinator saves on main, not three (347 is prior item version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation, still unbuilt; V6 is under 'Checked and found not to be a problem'). The wait is one commit, not a whole background transaction. The cleanup gate covers creation and draft saves. Main-actor admission is a documented linearization; the L rewrite is not justified unmeasured. Severity kept as structural debt; hang exposure is narrower than claimed.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:69 root cause 4; `version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation` (1049-1068), fix (1), cites line 347, not built; send, draft and enqueue saves not itemized

**Invariant risks**

- Send linearization: OutboundTaskRegistry.swift:186-226 writes the admission marker synchronously on the main actor, so closeAdmission, Task.checkCancellation and the background-time check (ComposeSendOrchestrator.swift:326-336) run in one turn with it. Awaiting a writer there puts a suspension inside the barrier, and an expiry that lands after the marker but before URLSession records an unsent mail as delivery-unknown.
- One context for drafts and the optimistic graph: the debounced save (ChatReplyDraftStore.swift:91-105), the draft removal inside the graph's save (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1448-1473), saveMergingUnsentReply and discard all use the view context. Moving only one of them leaves a stale registered draft that the object-trump merge policy writes back, losing reply text. Same-turn reads after creation (fetchMessageSync, adoptStoredArchiveState, onOptimisticMessagePersisted) also assume the view context.
- Lock order and the account boundary: a new serial writer is a third lock beside the cleanup gate and the conversation turns. It must be a leaf: nothing inside it may wait for the gate, a turn, the run boundary or a lease. Every write must be awaited inside its caller's gate, run or lease, so that teardown drains it. Otherwise it deadlocks, or old-account writes land after reopen.
- Launch-repair ordering: the preview batch's save and its checkpoint stay inside the cleanup-sensitive hold, with the checkpoint written straight after a successful save (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:322-351); a flag latches only after its save succeeds. A save seam that is then called off main must be built in a non-isolated type behind a lock (VerdictBackfillSaveSeam). ChatPreviewRepairTests.swift:843 builds its seam in a @MainActor suite.

**Fix.** Do not build a shared writer. (1) In ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator, send the five main-actor `storage.saveIfNeeded(context)` calls (347, 563, 608, 671, 727) through the existing `saveOffMainActor`. Each stays where it is (347 and 727 inside the cleanup hold), and each checkpoint or flag is written right after a successful save. (2) PendingActionsManager: persistAction, persistConversationAction and cancelPendingAction write through one `newBackgroundContext()` with `await context.perform`, still awaited inside the run or lease they hold. (3) Add signposts, carrying no identifiers, to the remaining main-actor writes, and measure them on S2 next to a 20k-message archive. (4) Keep the markers synchronous. Move drafts and the optimistic graph together, and only if the measurements show hangs.

**First step.** At ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:347, replace `storage.saveIfNeeded(context)` with `await Self.saveOffMainActor(context, using: storage.saveIfNeeded)`, and keep persistChatPreviewCheckpoint directly after it inside the hold. Then do the same at 563, 608, 671 and 727.

**Pinning test.** For each pass, a save seam behind a lock (like VerdictBackfillSaveSeam) asserts mainThreadAttemptCount == 0 and a checkpoint written after the save; Revert-check: saveOffMainActor. An enqueue with the view context dirtied stores its row and leaves viewContext.hasChanges true; Revert-check: newBackgroundContext.

**Payoff.** Takes every launch-repair and pending-action commit off main at low risk, including the 20k-ID JSON encode in a conversation action, and measures whether send and draft saves need more.

### `content-pipeline-cpu#3` · medium · scalability · effort M · known-open

**Each heuristic tweak is still a store-wide migration: two mailbox walks per bump, the preview walk under the send gate at background priority**

Area: HTML sanitization, DOM cleaning, text processing and preview builders. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Mechanism holds as cited: both completion keys embed the constants, bumped together in three commits since the prior review (two on 2026-10-27, one on 2026-11-17). Each bump re-arms two independent walks of every received row, each loading the body and running cleanedHTMLForProcessing. The preview walk derives 25 rows per cleanup-sensitive hold at .background priority, and optimistic send creation takes the same gate; its save is a performAndWait from the main actor. Both walks are checkpointed, cancellable and foreground-only, so this is bounded degradation, not failure.

**Evidence**
