**Invariant risks**

- Merging the walks reverses a recorded decision. RichContentVerdictBackfill.swift:14-20 and ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:433-439 keep the verdict pass separate: no gate, no pending deferral, its own running flag. The prior review's 'Keep intact' says 'The two passes stay independent'. Under the gate the verdict scan makes sends wait, and a deferred conversation would hold back verdicts.
- Deriving outside the gate is only safe if the pending-send read, the deferral and the checkpoint write all stay inside one hold (ChatPreviewRepair.swift:209-211, Coordinator:322-329, DeferredRetryAnchors.load). Otherwise a split or merge moves rows that the retry never finds. The apply step must also compare-and-set against the preview phase A saw, so it never overwrites a fresher preview written by ingest.
- A window on the preview pass leaves old rows on the old derivation for good: the loader shows the stored chatPreviewText unchanged (MessageBubbleLoader.swift:131-132). Healing it at load would add a writer outside the gate and make a row's text and height change after it mounts. This needs Kevin's decision or a per-row stamp in ESCChatmail 7.
- A pause or window must never set a completion flag it did not earn, never wait while holding a lease, and never stand in for an epoch bump. Rows outside a verdict window stay .unknown (never guessed) and heal through MessageBubbleLoader.swift:119-126.

**Fix.** Keep the two walks independent and make each one cheaper. (1) Save the preview batch through saveOffMainActor inside the gate hold, then persist the checkpoint. (2) Split each ChatPreviewRepair batch into two steps. Derive holds only the lease, stays cancellable and returns values keyed by message ID along with the preview it saw. Apply takes the gate, re-reads the pending sends, defers their conversations, compare-and-sets chatPreviewText, saves and persists the checkpoint. (3) Window RichContentVerdictBackfill, which already runs newest first: stop at a recency cutoff and set the flag. Older rows stay unknown until a bubble load stamps them. (4) Between batches, before taking a lease, stop without setting the flag under Low Power Mode or serious thermal state. Windowing previews is Kevin's call.

**First step.** In ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.prepareAndSaveChatPreviewBatch, replace storage.saveIfNeeded(context) at line 347 with `await Self.saveOffMainActor(context, using: storage.saveIfNeeded)`. Keep persistChatPreviewCheckpoint right after it, still inside the gate hold. Add the matching main-thread save test.

**Pinning test.** ChatPreviewRepairTests: hold derivation in chatPreviewRepairDidDeriveRow. Assert that a cleanup-sensitive mutation finishes meanwhile, and that a send record inserted there leaves the row's preview unchanged and its conversation in the persisted checkpoint. Also saveSeam.mainThreadAttemptCount == 0, Revert-check saveOffMainActor.

**Payoff.** Sends and draft saves stop waiting on HTML derivation at background priority, and the preview pass stops committing on the main thread. After a bump, eager verdict re-stamping covers only recent mail, not the whole mailbox.

**Pinning test.** The same harness case, unwrapped by the fix. After a New Message at S2, the viewContext's self Person messageParticipations is still a fault and fewer than 1,000 objects are registered. Revert-check: the private-context creation.

**Payoff.** Tapping Send no longer reads 120k (S2) to 400k (S3) self participations on main or pins them there. Until ESCChatmail 7, every send pays that read off-main while holding the gate.

A migration test on the S2 template decides whether dropping Label.messages keeps every join row in place. If it does, use the same shape: removeStaleLabels counts by fetch and mergeDuplicateLabels repoints by fetch. If not, denormalize as planned: first refactor label reads and writes behind one seam, then add a store-metadata latch, a dual write, and an NSBatchUpdateRequest backfill in the maintenance run.

**Payoff.** Removes 120,000 of the 217,062 objects one new message registers at S2, and the same from each deletion. The label half then removes the 97k INBOX read from inserts, relabels, archive and spam.

### `data-model#4` · medium · performance · effort L · known-open

**The canonical conversation rollup still materializes every message of each touched conversation as a full row, bodies included, twice per incremental run**

The snapshot never reads bodyText, but the full-row prefetch carries that inline, uncapped column. The second pass runs only when the history slice allows intermediate saves: no deletions, no TRASH/SPAM/DRAFT label adds, no messagesAdded without labelIds (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:1067).

**Verifier.** Opened every cited location; all are as described. No guard, cap, chunking or cache found on this path. Not a documented decision: docs/scalability-review.md lists it as open item rollup-full-conversation-materialization and step 11 is unbuilt. Tightened three points: the double pass is conditional on allowsIntermediateContextSaves; "commit nothing" overstates, since message batches are already saved; the work is off the main thread. **October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:536 `rollup-full-conversation-materialization` (review correction :548); step 11 "Bound rollups and list paging" :1624 has no Built entry. Code confirms: ConversationRollupUpdater.swift:150-157 prefetch, IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:350 still reads without claiming.

**Invariant risks**

- Never apply a snapshot built on a failed or partial read. hasInbox=false makes ConversationRoutingPolicy.applyArchiveState (ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:81-86) archive and hide the chat, and CLAUDE.md says a failed Core Data read is never empty. The sync callers at IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:365/479 also throw away updateRollupsForModified's false.
- Rollups run before the save, inside performThrowingSyncMutation, after preserveNewerLocalReadState has already written to messages in the sync context (ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:273-282). Stored queries, and any dictionary or propertiesToFetch fetch, miss unsaved inserts, label changes, re-homes and deletes. So exclude every dirty Message ID, add those rows back from memory, and treat a temporary conversation ID as overlay-only.
- Three SQL spellings go wrong on SQLite but pass on in-memory test stores: `isUnread == YES` is driven from byIsUnreadIndex (use MessagePredicates.unreadInInbox), `NONE labels` drops rows with no labels (use the visibleInChat SUBQUERY), and `conversation.id ==` scans. Also, MessagePredicates.chatExcludedLabelIDs and MessagePersister.excludedMailboxLabelIDs must stay the same set.
- If the messages prefetch is dropped while updateDisplayNameOnly still walks conversation.messages (:794, :762), one bulk prefetch becomes a fault per row. A bare claim makes finalize run updateDisplayNamesForConversations, which prefetches every message, for IDs tracked in both sets. Capping bodyText changes RichContentVerdictResolver's inputs and the bubble fallback, and breaks LegacyOutgoingBodyTextFallback.

**Fix.** Ship in two parts. (1) Intermediate flush: claim rollup IDs via claimPendingRollupConversations and add a matching claim for display-name-only IDs, so finalize redoes only re-tracked conversations, as initial sync and recovery already do. (2) Split ConversationRollupSnapshot.make into a pure reducer over value inputs. One grouped stored count routes large conversations to bounded inputs: MessagePredicates counts and fetchLimit-1 probes, a newest-first preview walk, all excluding every dirty Message ID and re-adding those from memory, plus a narrow sender query for titles. Small conversations keep today's prefetch walk. Use an id tie-break in both paths; apply nothing on any failed read. Leave bodyText to step 10.

**First step.** In IncrementalSyncOrchestrator's intermediate flush (:350), call claimPendingRollupConversations instead of modifiedConversations, add a ModificationTracker claim for display-name-only IDs, and pin it with an IncrementalSyncOrchestratorTests case that counts rollup calls per conversation across flush and finalize.

**Pinning test.** In .sqlite mode, conversations with unsaved inserts, INBOX removals, deletes, re-homes, SPAM rows and a blank newest preview give equal snapshots both ways (Revert-check: overlay); on S2, rolling up the largest chat leaves conversation.messages faulted.

**Payoff.** Each touched chat's rollup reads a few indexed rows, not every lifetime row (review estimate: 0.2-0.8 s and 5-25 MB per 1-3k S2 chat, twice per run).

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:276-291 — PersonFactory.findOrCreate (a cache hit after the batch prefetch), then participant.person = person, an inverse-maintained edge to Person.messageParticipations
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleHubFaultTests.swift:50-54 — measured: a new message also reads the sender's own messageParticipations (800 for a list sender), so the inverse read applies to every Person, not only self (212-213)
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:235-244 — on main, each updated or refreshed Person's conversationParticipations is walked, returning every conversation with no window or archived filter
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/PersonCache.swift:271-275 — invalidateEntry is one dictionary removal plus a locked generation bump, so the P awaited hops are negligible
- docs/scalability-review.md:1561 — person-change-conversation-fanout is listed as not built yet; line 520's v7 fix (b) covers only the self-Person edge

**Trigger.** A group row with about 100-500 visible To/Cc addresses has been shown, so the window fetch's participants.person prefetch has registered its Persons in the view context (an open chat's row cache does the same). Then any sync brings a message to or from those members. Reply-all forks multiply the conversations walked.

**Impact.** Sync side: each run registers about P times the group's history in extra objects. That is milliseconds warm and up to hundreds of milliseconds cold, not seconds per message. Main thread: each merged save can cost up to P to-many faults, plus one fault and a snapshot for each affected conversation. Estimated at tens of milliseconds for P around 100, possibly over 250 ms for P around 500 with forks. None of this was measured.

**Verifier.** Confirmed: no cap; one inverse read per Person (measured for sender and self); automatic merges into the view context (CoreDataStack.swift:182); the window prefetch registers Persons (ConversationWindowProvider.swift:41); the walk runs on main. Corrected: "seconds per message" is unsupported, because the cost is per Person per context. PersonCache hops are negligible, and the photo prefetch is detached. That an inverse-only change puts a Person in the updated set is standard Core Data behavior, not measured here. person-change-conversation-fanout's window fetch fixes the main-thread part for any P.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: person-change-conversation-fanout (lines 895-914; line 1561 lists it as not built yet). inverse-tomany-hub-fault-tax fix (b) at line 520 covers only the self-Person edge, and v7 (step 10, line 1623) has not been cut.

**Invariant risks**

- Replies read MessageParticipant rows (ReplySnapshots.swift:365-464). With a recipient cap, evidence.isComplete stays true, so ReplyLinkedAddressPolicy.rowsCanAnswer trusts the cut-down set and reply-all silently drops people.
- Hash parity: strictParticipantSetIdentity must match the header-derived identity, and nil means do not re-home. A 'truncated' flag would have to be honored by every reader of the rows (re-home passes at Migration:1128/1522, reply evidence, participant extractor), or chats fork.
- v6 has shipped, so removing the inverse or adding a flag goes only into ESCChatmail 7 (a new directory and the .xccurrentversion bump). Person.messageParticipations is Cascade (model v6:185), so merge and orphan cleanup must delete or re-point rows themselves.
- List rules: no FRC, publishVisibleItems stays the single funnel, SortKey stays canonical. Unsaved optimistic rows have temporary objectIDs, which name no stored row and must not go into an SQL `self IN`. PersonCache must not skip self (review correction, line 1322).

**Fix.** Drop the recipient cap and do two independent pieces. (1) Now, with no schema change, build person-change-conversation-fanout. In conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges, replace the conversationParticipations walk with one fetch on the observed context over the window's permanent objectIDs: `self IN %@ AND ANY participants.person IN %@`, using the notification's Person objectIDs and prefetching participants.person. Check rows with temporary IDs in memory. A Person change cannot bring a row from outside the window into it: search reads only Conversation attributes, and the contacts filter reads emails. (2) In ESCChatmail 7, choose the option of an inverse-less MessageParticipant.person, not the self-only row. Replace Person's Cascade rule and the three readers of messageParticipations with `person == %@` fetches. Leave PersonCache invalidation semantics alone.

**First step.** In ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift, rewrite conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges as a fetch scoped to the window's permanent IDs, plus an in-memory check of rows with temporary IDs. Extend the .sqlite suite in ConversationListViewModelTests before touching the model.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests on .sqlite: a Person in one window row and 200 other conversations (190 archived), and a sibling save that adds its MessageParticipant. Assert its conversationParticipations stays a fault and only that row is snapshotted again. Revert-check: conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges.

**Payoff.** Removes the main-thread to-many faults on every merged save, which grow with group size and history (estimated tens to hundreds of ms at P 100-500). The v7 choice removes the sync context's per-recipient reads.

### `startup-lifecycle#5` · medium · scalability · effort M · known-open

**Mailbox-wide launch passes are owned by the list view model and run only in the foreground session, with the preview pass still saving on the main actor**

Area: App startup, launch passes and scene lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator is built only by ConversationListViewModel and started from the list's onAppear. Its preview re-derivation and verdict backfill are keyed by chatPreviewDerivationVersion and richContentVerdictEpoch, bumped together on 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-17; each bump re-reads every received body, 25 rows per cleanup-sensitive hold and 10 per lease. No background task drives them and nothing gates on power; on iOS they advance only while the process runs. The preview scan runs oldest-first. Its batch save is a main-actor performAndWait, but only when a preview changed.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:103-109,488,513-516 — the view model constructs the coordinator (git grep finds no other constructor), starts the passes in onAppear, and cancels them only on a disappear without mailbox access (View+ConversationListLifecycle.swift:30)
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:115-128,396-397 — every .syncCompleted calls three passes; the completion keys embed chatPreviewDerivationVersion and richContentVerdictEpoch (CacheVersioning.swift:17,36; commit f3066969 changed both)
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:144-153,281-288,330-351 — a 25-row batch derives and saves inside performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation; the @MainActor method calls storage.saveIfNeeded(context) at 347; the verdict pass saves through saveOffMainActor (514,542-547) and takes no gate (493-495)
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:21-28 — saveIfNeeded is performAndWait and returns at once when the context has no changes; esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:54 — optimistic send creation takes the same cleanup-sensitive gate
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ChatPreviewRepair.swift:334,423-426,436-442 — the re-derivation scans every isFromMe == NO row ascending by ID and loads its HTML; RichContentVerdictBackfill.swift:63-68 scans the same rows descending; MessageBubbleLoader.swift:84-100 shows a stored preview as it is and recomputes only the verdict
- esc-chatmail/Services/DatabaseMaintenance/DatabaseMaintenanceService.swift:52-78 and esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundTaskScheduler.swift:32-40 — the registered background handlers are analyze, cleanup, the retired vacuum, sync refresh and sync processing; docs/scalability-review.md:1049-1071 lists this item with its fix unbuilt

**Trigger.** The first sessions after installing a build that bumps chatPreviewDerivationVersion or richContentVerdictEpoch (both bumped in 8e01d320 on 2026-10-27 and f3066969 on 2026-11-17), on an iOS mailbox at S2 or above; also the first upgrade onto either pass.

**Impact.** Per bump at S2 each pass reads and re-derives about 105k received rows while the app is in use. The prior review's unmeasured estimate is 10-35 minutes per pass, so on iOS it spreads over days of sessions; the Mac app keeps running and finishes while open. A reply's optimistic creation can wait behind one 25-row batch held at background priority. Stored previews of recent mail keep the old derivation until the oldest-first scan reaches them; verdicts self-heal per bubble load. Main-thread saves happen only for batches that changed a preview.

**Verifier.** Opened the coordinator, both pass types, the view-model wiring, save seam, gate, SyncRunCoordinator and task registries. Code matches the finding; the prior item is unbuilt and absent from 'Suggested order'. Tightened: iOS suspension already pauses the walk, so 'no pause on backgrounding' is no failure; on the Mac the process keeps running; main-actor saves are rare (hasChanges guard) and the verdict pass saves off main. No grep hit for Low Power or thermal checks. Durations unmeasured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1049-1071 `version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation` (fixes 1-4 unbuilt; absent from Suggested order 1530-1628). The app-level/BGProcessing ownership half is new.

**Invariant risks**

- Never run the passes inside an exclusive run (the daily cleanup's StoreMaintenanceCoordinator run, runStoreMaintenanceAfterSync). Their waitForCurrentSyncToComplete is SyncRunCoordinator.waitUntilIdle (SyncEngine.swift:327-329), which waits for the caller's own run. It also ignores cancellation (parkUntilIdle, SyncRunCoordinator.swift:321-326), so an expired BGTask parked behind a sync stays uncompleted.
- ChatPreviewRepair has no HTML-generation fence. With the boundary closed, loadHTML returns nil (HTMLContentHandler.swift:294-304), the row keeps its old preview and the checkpoint still advances (ChatPreviewRepair.swift:408-416, 436-442), so the pass latches complete without re-deriving. Under today's foreground ownership a held lease implies an open boundary. A background or app-level driver (cold BG launch, failed reopen) loses that.
- The preview checkpoint must still be written after the save and inside the cleanup-sensitive hold: the split and hash-correcting merge read DeferredRetryAnchors from it (DataCleanupService.swift:438-446). Moving the save off main must not move that write out of the gate closure. Reversing the scan direction changes the Checkpoint format those passes decode.
- Exactly one runner per pass. A VM-built coordinator left beside an app-level owner gives two in-memory checkpoints and cursors writing the same UserDefaults keys. The owner may start only once canAccessMailbox is true after AppStartupBootstrap's restore. A new BGTask identifier needs an Info.plist entry and a handler that is kept or retired forever.

**Fix.** Three changes, in order. (1) In prepareAndSaveChatPreviewBatch, save through the existing saveOffMainActor seam, keeping save, then persistChatPreviewCheckpoint, then invalidation inside the gate closure; route the coordinator's other main-actor saves the same way. (2) Before each lease, stop unlatched under Low Power Mode or thermalState >= .serious (injected closure); note each bump's cost beside both constants. (3) Fence ChatPreviewRepair on HTML generation like RichContentVerdictBackfill, then move only the three flag-keyed passes into one app-owned service, started when canAccessMailbox and re-armed by .syncCompleted, plus a power-requiring BGProcessing identifier entered through AppStartupBootstrap, outside any exclusive run, with a cancellation-aware idle wait. Recent-window bounding stays a product call.

**First step.** In ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.prepareAndSaveChatPreviewBatch (line 347), replace storage.saveIfNeeded(context) with await Self.saveOffMainActor(context, using: storage.saveIfNeeded), leaving persistChatPreviewCheckpoint and the cache invalidation after it, inside the gate closure.

**Pinning test.** In ChatPreviewRepairTests, mirror testCoordinatorBackfill_savesOffTheMainThread: a counting save seam sees zero main-thread saves for a batch that changed a preview, and a cleanup-sensitive mutation queued behind it reads the advanced checkpoint. Revert-check: saveOffMainActor in prepareAndSaveChatPreviewBatch.

**Payoff.** No main-thread commits across a bump's ~105k-row S2 pass; iOS can finish it overnight on power instead of over days of sessions, without warming phones in Low Power Mode.

### `sync-persist-path#2` · medium · scalability · effort L · known-open

**Conversation-derived state is recomputed by materializing the whole conversation, at six sites and twice per incremental run**

Area: Message fetch, processing and persistence path. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Sync rollups (updateRollupsForModified) fetch each touched conversation with every message row and label join prefetched, walk the set in ConversationRollupSnapshot.make and again for header names. Incremental sync calls it at the intermediate flush (skipped for destructive slices) and at finalize over the same unclaimed ID set. Rows are realized once per run context, so the second pass and the other sites mostly re-walk memory; the unprefetched ones (per-INBOX-removal walk, echo snapshot) add per-message label faults and an O(removals x messages) loop. All of it runs off the main thread.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupUpdater.swift:150-170 and 58-59 — SELF IN fetch prefetching messages, messages.labels, participants, participants.person with no limit or propertiesToFetch, inside context.perform; conversation.messages handed whole to ConversationRollupSnapshot.make; 794-821 walks conversation.messages again for header names
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:27-28 — loop over every message building a Set of label IDs per message
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:348-377, 454-491, 1067-1087 — flush runs only when allowsIntermediateContextSaves (no deletions or excluded-label adds in the slice); it and finalize both read modifiedConversations(in: modificationTransaction) with no claim between, so the same conversations are rolled up twice
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/LabelOperationProcessor.swift:68 and 210-247 — labels prefetched only for the touched message IDs; each item that loses INBOX calls refreshInboxIndicators, which walks all of conversation.messages reading each message's labels
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:384-388, 636, 721-728 — echo consumption builds a snapshot over all remaining messages with no prefetch; isOnlyMessage reads conversation.messages.count (after MessagePersister+Creation.swift:105 has already set message.conversation); the update path prefetches every message's labels per call
- docs/scalability-review.md:536-561 and 1624, esc-chatmailTests/TestSupport/ScaleStore/ScaleStoreShape.swift:46-48, esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncContextPageObjectRelease.swift:6-13 — prior item with its caveat that the second rollup reuses resident rows; step 11 (bounded rollups) has no 'Built' entry; the S2 seed shape has one 20,000-message chat and five of 2,000; page release exists only for initial sync and history recovery

**Trigger.** Any incremental sync that brings mail or label changes into a large conversation. The project's own S2 seed shape has one 20,000-message chat and five 2,000-message chats, so this applies at S2, not only S3. Worst case: many INBOX removals made in another client inside one large chat, up to 5,000 history records per foreground slice and 300 per app refresh.

**Impact.** Prior measurement (M5 Pro, synthetic store with 3-4 KB bodies): 174-186 ms and +166-182 MB per rollup of a 20k-message chat, with the rows staying resident until the run's context is released; an estimated 0.2-0.8 s for 1-3k chats. It runs on the sync context's queue, so it delays list convergence and holds those conversations' serializer turns, but blocks no main thread and changes no result. A remote bulk archive adds O(removals x conversation size) label reads, estimated at seconds to minutes per slice. Nothing was measured on a device and no failure was shown.

**Verifier.** Opened all six sites; the code matches. Still unbuilt: review step 11. Guards found: the flush gate, history slices capped at 5,000 records (300 under app refresh), and context.perform on a background context. The messages.count probe is PK-only and follows the inverse wiring at Creation:105, so it is hygiene, not a separate materialization. Severity lowered from high: degradation with a named cost, no failure, figures are Mac measurements and estimates. The 20k chat is part of the S2 seed shape.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:536 rollup-full-conversation-materialization (with :563 label-op-inbox-refresh-conversation-walk, :587 send-echo-rollup-unprefetched, :1500 isOnlyMessage; Suggested order step 11 at :1624, which has no Built entry)

**Invariant risks**

- The dirty overlay. Rollups run before the save, over unsaved inserts, label edits, reroutes and deletes. Count, dictionary and fetchLimit-1 reads miss these changes or merge them wrongly, and a wrong hasInbox archives a live chat through ConversationRoutingPolicy.applyArchiveState (ConversationRoutingPolicy.swift:52-86). The fix: exclude the dirty Message IDs (current or committed conversation, permanent IDs only), set includesPendingChanges=false, and add those messages back from memory, as MessageActions.applyInboxRollup does (MessageActions.swift:896-943).
- Every touched conversation must be rolled up before its save. The per-record walks and the echo's make(from:).apply can go only where the conversation is tracked and rolled up inside the serializer block before the save. createNewMessage (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:195) and the update path (+Updates.swift:587) throw away the conversations consumeRemoteCommittedSendMutation returns. Only deleteExistingMessageIfPresent tracks them. Drop the inline snapshot without tracking them, and the optimistic row's other conversation keeps a stale date and snippet.
- Claiming IDs at the intermediate flush. Finalize would then hold the serializer turn for, and roll up, only conversations that were tracked again after the flush, so every writer after the flush must track again (SyncReconciliation.swift:878-884 does). Display-name-only IDs need a claim of their own, or finalize walks the conversations claimed at the flush again through updateDisplayNamesForConversations.
- ConversationRollupSnapshot stays the single definition of the rule. INBOX, SENT and received are counted over every message; only the visible and preview inputs filter by excludedMailboxLabelIDs. Keep the ChatReplyDraft check on an empty rollup, the skip of equal-value writes, the list-title rules, and the rule that a failed read is never 'empty': on a read failure, fall back to the full walk and never apply a partial snapshot.

**Fix.** Land it in stages. (1) Remove the redundant recomputations. Drop refreshInboxIndicators and refreshConversationInboxIndicators, keeping the O(1) unread delta. Track the conversations that consumeRemoteCommittedSendMutation returns, and keep its in-memory check only for newly inserted conversations. Replace messages.count with a flag set when the conversation is created for this message. (2) Claim the rollup and display-name IDs at the intermediate flush; claimPendingRollupConversations already exists. (3) Build headerDisplayNamesByEmail only after the list-title early return. (4) Replace the messages and messages.labels prefetch with a bounded gatherer feeding a per-message reducer shared with make(from:): objectID-predicate counts, limit-1 newest rows, existence probes, a newest-first preview walk, a dirty overlay, and a fallback to the full walk when a read fails.

**First step.** Delete the refreshInboxIndicators call in LabelOperationProcessor and the update path's refreshConversationInboxIndicators. Rewrite testUpdateExistingMessage_removingInboxLabelRecomputesConversationInboxIndicators to assert the values after updateRollupsForModified. Then track the conversations the echo consumes.

**Pinning test.** ConversationRollupUpdaterTests: a .sqlite parity test of make(from:) against the bounded gatherer, with an unsaved insert, removal of the newest INBOX row, a delete, a reroute, an INBOX+TRASH row and a blank-preview newest row (Revert-check: dirty overlay). ScaleHubFaultTests: a registered-object bound for rolling up the 20k chat.

**Payoff.** A touched 20k-message chat stops costing about 175 ms and 170 MB per rollup, twice per run. A remote bulk archive stops costing O(removals × conversation size).

### `concurrency-model#4` · low · performance · effort M · known-partial

**One process-wide file lock is both the account fence and the body I/O mutex, and it sits inside every Core Data save and every row mount**

Area: Concurrency model and Swift 6 readiness. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

HTMLContentAccountBoundary is one process-wide NSRecursiveLock serving as both the account fence and the body-file mutex. Every context's didSave takes it, and a fresh chat row mount takes it about 5-7 times on the main actor, plus once per MessageBubble body evaluation. Holds on other threads are bounded: one body read or write, or one chunk of at most 100 unlinks. The multi-second S2 case is not a lock wait: the orphan sweep runs on the main actor itself, which the prior review already tracks as open.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:14-47 — one NSRecursiveLock; capture, isCurrent and perform all take it, and perform runs the caller's file operation while holding it
- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/CacheCoordinator.swift:138-150 — the didSave publisher (object nil, so every context) calls HTMLContentHandler.shared.captureAccountGeneration() on the posting queue before the plan is built; started in production at esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:210
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader+HTMLAnalysis.swift:5-21 with esc-chatmail/ViewModels/MessageBubbleViewModel.swift:37,85 and esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageBubble.swift:192-199,635-643 — cachedHTMLAnalysis takes the lock 2-3 times, runs in the view model's init and again in the first loadIfNeeded, and body's loadSignature calls htmlSourceSignature (lock, plus a stat on a cold signature cache) on every evaluation
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:399-417,453-468 — deleted-body removal takes the lock once per chunk of 100 and asks the store outside it; the comment records that every HTML read/write and every save take this lock and that a waiter waits a hundred unlinks at most (also docs/scalability-review.md:1600)
- esc-chatmail/Services/DatabaseMaintenance/DatabaseMaintenanceService.swift:6-7,68-77 and DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:114-141 — the sweep is a main-actor static method that calls cleanupOrphanedFiles synchronously, reached only from the daily cleanup task; docs/scalability-review.md:1024-1047 and :1588 track it as still open
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:192-204 — hasStoredHTMLFiles is called only when there is no Account row and no account-scoped row, inside performBackgroundTask

**Trigger.** A chat on screen (row mounts and body evaluations) or any context save that overlaps a lock hold on another thread: a body write or read during sync or recovery, or one chunk of a bulk-delete file reclamation. A whole-directory hold on another thread needs a sign-in over a store with no rows but leftover body files, such as after a store reset.

**Impact.** Each main-thread acquisition can wait for one in-flight hold: a single body write (milliseconds, longer on a slow disk) or one chunk of up to 100 stat-and-unlink pairs (estimated tens of milliseconds, not measured). The result is frame hitches when scrolling a chat during a bulk delete, and saves delayed by the same bound. No ordinary path makes the main thread wait seconds on this lock.

**Verifier.** Code matches the citations; row mounts take the lock more often than stated. Overstated: the multi-second stall is the tracked main-actor sweep; hasStoredHTMLFiles runs only on a row-less store; calculateStorageSize, cleanupOldFiles and deleteAllHTML have no app callers. The lock's place in every save is already documented (CLAUDE.md, review line 1600), with holds deliberately bounded. Apple documents pthread mutexes, which NSRecursiveLock wraps, as QoS-promoting, so "does not donate priority" is doubtful. No hold time was measured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1024 `html-orphan-sweep-main-thread` (step 7 "Not built" :1588, as `html-orphan-sweep-main-actor`); bulk-delete half built :1567, :1600 (HTMLContentHandler.swift:425-472). Fence/mutex split itself is new.

**Invariant risks**

- Closing must drain. closeAccountWork() (HTMLContentHandler.swift:187-194) runs synchronously at AuthSession.swift:405, before the tombstone rename, and relies on this lock to wait for any file I/O already running. Make the admission check lock-free and re-check only after the operation, and a write admitted before the close can land after the rename. saveHTMLResult then recreates the missing Messages directory (:266-274) and writes the old account's body into it, and hasStoredHTMLFiles counts that file.
- Deleted-row reclamation reads the file's date under the lock just before unlinking it, and relies on every body write taking the same lock (:407-417). Per-file or unlocked I/O must keep a path's stat-and-unlink and its write-and-cache-update mutually exclusive. Otherwise a body stored again is unlinked, or fileSignatureCache keeps a stale 'missing' that htmlFileExists and RichContentVerdictResolver trust.
- The store is asked before the boundary lock is taken, never while it is held, and a failed read removes nothing (CLAUDE.md, CacheCoordinator note). A chunked sweep's `id IN` check must follow both rules. It must also keep the nil-generation skip (DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:125) and the Mac tripwire guard (HTMLContentHandler.swift:651-657).
- Moving the sweep off main without chunking it backfires. The main-thread close (AuthSession.swift:405) and the post-time capture in every viewContext save (CacheCoordinator.swift:148) would wait for the whole walk, and cancelling the maintenance run could not shorten it. Replacing NSRecursiveLock with an unfair or read-write lock also drops reentrancy: audit for nested perform first.

**Fix.** Keep file operations behind a lock that close can drain; never make them lock-free. Steps, in order: (1) Close html-orphan-sweep-main-thread: make cleanupOrphanedHTMLFiles nonisolated and replace cleanupOrphanedFiles with a chunked HTMLContentHandler sweep shaped like deleteHTML(forDeleted:). List file names; for each chunk of 100, check cancellation and the generation, call liveMessageIDs with no lock held, then in one perform skip files wasWrittenAfter(sweepStart) and unlink and invalidate the rest. Keep the tripwire first; a nil generation or a failed read removes nothing. (2) Make hasStoredHTMLFiles a first-entry probe that still throws on errors other than a missing directory. (3) Optional: let capture/isCurrent read state from an OSAllocatedUnfairLock that is written only while the I/O lock is held.

**First step.** Make DatabaseMaintenanceService.cleanupOrphanedHTMLFiles nonisolated. Add HTMLContentHandler.deleteOrphanedHTML(expectedGeneration:startedAt:chunkSize:liveMessageIDs:isCancelled:), copying deleteHTML(forDeleted:)'s loop: the store is asked per chunk outside the lock, and the file date is checked under it.

**Pinning test.** In HTMLContentAccountBoundaryTests, chunkSize 2: a reopen inside liveMessageIDs stops later chunks; cancelling after one chunk stops the sweep; a throwing read and a body written after the start are kept. DatabaseMaintenanceServiceTests: the remover runs off main (Revert-check: nonisolated).

**Payoff.** Takes the only multi-second lock hold (estimated 0.5-3 s at S2) off the main actor; on the Mac daily cleanup runs inside the open app, so that hang is visible.

### `invariant-enforcement#6` · low · maintainability · effort M · new

**One-shot migrations and launch repairs accumulate with no upgrade floor, no shared mechanism and no retirement**

Area: Invariant enforcement, complexity budget and change safety. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

About a dozen one-shot passes each keep a hand-written UserDefaults latch, and nothing records an upgrade floor, so legacy branches cannot be retired. Once the flags are latched, the extra cost at runtime is close to zero: each sync's hold reads a few flags. The contact unification pass is not a migration and is deliberately placed in that hold. Two of the five launch repairs run once per launch by design. The archive-migration latch fires only on an empty store. The RFC 2047 pass, which runs on upgraded stores, does latch after a failed fetch. The only heavy cost is the split walk, which the prior review already lists as an open item.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:106,275-281 — runFullCleanup, and with it the archive migration, runs only behind hasDoneDuplicateCleanupV1, before the profile fetch and before anything is stored. So the unconditional latch at DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:55 fires on an install's empty store and has no effect.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:454,469,494,517-528 — the RFC 2047 pass reads with `(try? context.fetch(...)) ?? []`, so a failed fetch leaves nothing to change. NSManagedObjectContext+Perform.swift:12 then returns true, the flag latches, and the claim at DataCleanupService.swift:244-246 does not hold for fetch failures.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:230-252 with DataCleanupService+ContactUnification.swift:48-53 and ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:173-183 — the steady-state hold is one map comparison plus four flag reads. Unification is an ongoing pass whose position is required, not a one-shot.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:94-126,575-578,618-624 — the list-title and missing-preview repairs run once per launch by design. The sync-completion re-arms return early once their pass has latched. Lines 24-26 and 684 hold a completion flag that is written and read only by tests.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Dependencies/MigrationFlagStore.swift:8-13 — the shared abstraction is four get/set calls, with no registry, no ordering and no record of the build that last ran.
- docs/scalability-review.md:947-957,972,1621,1655 — the split walk still runs inside the sync run and is not built. Exposure is limited to stores upgraded from before V2 and to syncs where an anchor blocks the latch.

**Trigger.** An upgrade from a build that predates a pass, which runs each unlatched pass once inside the sync run under the gate. A rare SQLite fetch error during the RFC 2047 pass. The prior split item while an anchor blocks its latch.

**Impact.** Debt in hygiene and change safety. Each new pass rewrites its own latch semantics, and two of them latch on failure. Compatibility code cannot be shown dead; CLAUDE.md keeps LegacyOutgoingBodyTextFallback for direct upgrades. Recurring gate delays come only from the split item, which is already tracked. Enforcing a floor by resetting the store would cost the user their mail history, because nothing backfills older mail.

**Verifier.** I read every pass and its latch. The archive-migration latch claim is true in code, but the latch can only fire on an empty store. The auditor missed the RFC 2047 pass, whose `try?` fetches latch on failure. The cost the auditor attributes to each sync and launch is a set of guard no-ops, and two of the counted passes are deliberate repairs that run once per launch. The 148 'legacy' mentions in 49 files are counted correctly. I found no record of the build that last ran (searched for CFBundleVersion). Severity is lowered because every heavy runtime cost belongs to the split item, which is already tracked.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md `participant-split-migration-walk` (lines 947-972; step 9 "Not built", line 1621) covers only the cost part. CLAUDE.md Traps: `LegacyOutgoingBodyTextFallback` "must stay" for direct upgrades.

**Invariant risks**

- Contact unification is not a one-shot pass. It must stay the first step of every sync run's cleanup, including the initial sync's full cleanup before any mail is routed (DataCleanupService.swift:203-205 and 235-237; +ContactUnification.swift:17-24). If it is folded into a registry or the hold moves out of the sync run, mail is hashed with a map the stored conversations do not carry yet, which forks chats.
- If completion moves to store metadata, or keys are renamed, without importing today's UserDefaults latches, every pass re-runs on every upgraded device. That includes the split walk, estimated at 40-90 s at S2 with the gate held. The passes would also re-run after a recovery-ladder reset. Nothing is gained, because defaults and the store already start and die together (FreshInstallHandler.swift:55-56, 171-181). Running the archive migration on a populated store would also archive every send-only chat: `!hasInbox` at +Migration.swift:33, and sends never set hasInbox (OptimisticUpdates:291).
- A floor enforced by resetting the store loses mail for good: nothing backfills, and a reset re-lists only `initialSyncMaxWindow`. CFBundleVersion cannot name the build a pass was introduced in either: it is `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` = 1 (Info.plist:40, project.pbxproj:247), and Xcode Cloud assigns the shipped number.
- A shared runner must latch only when the pass itself reports completion after its own save. A trivially successful save does not count: `performSaveIfNeeded` returns true when there are no changes (NSManagedObjectContext+Perform.swift:12). Each hold must stay self-contained: no plan carried across a gate release, and the chat-preview checkpoint written inside the hold. The runner must never ask for the gate while it holds a conversation's turn, or while it holds a lease and waits on the exclusive run.

**Fix.** Keep the latches in MigrationFlagStore under today's keys. Keep every pass where it runs now and in the same order; unification stays first in each sync cleanup and outside any registry. First fix the failure latches: RFC 2047's `(try? fetch) ?? []` becomes a do/catch that returns nil. Delete the archive migration, which only ever runs on a fresh install's empty store. Then add a declarative `OneShotMigration` table (key, a monotonic epoch the code owns, owner) and one `PassOutcome` that a shared helper alone turns into a latch. Seed a completed-epoch value from the existing latches. Retire passes below a declared floor, never by resetting the store. Leave the split walk to its tracked item.

**First step.** In DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:454, 469 and 494, replace the three `(try? context.fetch(...)) ?? []` reads with a do/catch that returns nil and skips the flag write, as in repairAddressShapedPersonDisplayNamesIfNeeded:600-608. Add the fetch-failure test.

**Pinning test.** RFC2047HeaderTextRepairMigrationTests: a context whose fetch throws leaves hasDecodedRFC2047HeaderTextV1 clear, and a later run decodes (Revert-check: the do/catch). Plus a repositorySource test that every migrationFlags key in esc-chatmail/ is in the registry.

**Payoff.** Stops a transient fetch error from permanently skipping a repair, deletes one dead and hazardous pass, and gives later passes one latch rule and a floor for retiring them, without re-running anything.

## Main-thread cost in the list, transcript and reader (23)

### `chat-transcript-ui#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**The scroll window keeps only 10 rows behind the last-appeared row in either direction, so a tall viewport loses on-screen rows**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

Every row's onAppear sets `scrollPosition` to that row's index once it is more than 2 rows away. Scrolling down, that is the bottom-edge row B. The window must then cover [B−10, B+30), from one default configuration used on every platform, and if it does not, a fresh 40-row window replaces it. Once scroll-up slides have left the window at [P−10, P+30), scrolling back down removes rows below B−10 from the ForEach. In a viewport showing more than about 11 rows (Mac's dense rows, iPad), those rows are on screen.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+WindowLoading.swift:259-260 — startIndex = scrollPosition − bufferSize, endIndex = scrollPosition + visibleItemCount + bufferSize, with no direction or viewport input
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+WindowLoading.swift:262-306 — a covered range is a no-op; otherwise loadWindow replaces with exactly that range. Only extendsWindowOnOverlap unions, and only replayHeldVisibleIndex passes it (VirtualScrollState.swift:451)
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState.swift:349-370 — markIndexVisible: outside the holds, any index more than 2 from scrollPosition becomes scrollPosition, then updateVisibleMessages(). Called from every row's onAppear (ChatMessagesView.swift:396-397)
- esc-chatmail/Services/VirtualScroll/VirtualScrollConfiguration.swift:36-41 — the one default (20/10/50/5); ChatMessagesView.swift:22-27 builds VirtualScrollState with no configuration, and the Mac reaches the same view (MacMailboxDetail.swift:43 passes bubbleStyle .mac)
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageBubbleStyle.swift:94-102,213-218 — Mac bubble padding 6/6 and row spacing 2, against 10/10 and 8 on iOS: a one-line Mac row is about 30pt, so a 700-900pt chat column shows well over 11 rows
- esc-chatmailTests/VirtualScroll/VirtualScrollStateTests.swift:4943-4980 — pins the sliding replace for normal scrolling, justified by 'SwiftUI re-anchors it while the reader drags' (measured on the iPhone simulator). No test feeds bottom-edge indexes for a tall viewport; VirtualScrollState.swift:271-278 records the related walk-forward under programmatic shifts

**Trigger.** On the Mac (or iPad), in a chat of short messages: scroll up until the top edge is more than ~30 rows above the tail, so the window becomes [P−10, P+30) rather than reaching the tail, then scroll back down. The first replacement drops N−11 of the N on-screen rows.

**Impact.** While the reader scrolls down through history, rows at the top of the viewport leave the data source. Shown rows vanish, and content shifts or rubber-bands. Each move of 3 or more rows brings new rows on screen and starts another replace, so the transcript likely creeps toward the tail. Unaffected on most iPhones (about 10 rows visible); borderline on Pro Max.

**Verifier.** Checked for guards. Neither the ±2 dead zone nor the initial-anchor or programmatic holds apply during a user drag. preloadPrevious fires below 5 rows from the start and the replace below 10, so slow scroll-up settles into 40-row slides. No documented decision covers viewport size: the deliberate sliding replace was measured on iPhone only. Not established from code: how SwiftUI redraws when rows leave the ForEach while on screen. Rows leaving while on screen is certain from the arithmetic; the walk-forward is likely.

**Invariant risks**

- The sliding replace for ordinary scrolling is a measured decision (VirtualScrollStateTests.swift:4943-4980, testMarkIndexVisible_withoutHold_slidesWindowAsBefore). Extending the window on every step grew it to the cap and front-trimmed rows above the reader (iPhone simulator, 11 of 40 slow drags). The auditor's [minRealized − screenful, maxRealized + screenful] is that growth again.
- The programmatic-scroll deferral has its own copy of the range. replayHeldVisibleIndex computes index − bufferSize to decide whether a replay would prepend (VirtualScrollState.swift:439-443). A symmetric (±30) or wider range in updateVisibleMessages that is not mirrored there prepends rows at rest after a keyboard shift, the bug deferredLeadingReplayIndex exists for.
- The initial-anchor hold and head parking must stay as they are. markIndexVisible stays a no-op during the hidden pass (VirtualScrollState.swift:352), while markRowRealized and markRowUnrealized stay ungated in onAppear/onDisappear (CLAUDE.md, ChatMessagesView.swift:396-418). Never move the window from a realization event, and keep scrollPosition parked at the window head (WindowLoading.swift:173, InitialLoad.swift:290).
- Main-actor cost is tied to the configuration. A normal replace re-fetches and re-maps every row on the view context (resolveRowsOnViewContextThrowing, RowCache.swift:32-60). Moving to ±30 or a bigger Mac visibleItemCount makes every 3-row step heavier. It also changes the initial window, the rebase floor and the maxWindowSize clamp (VirtualScrollConfiguration.swift:31-33).

**Fix.** Keep the sliding replace, but make it never drop a realized row. Add a pure VirtualScrollWindowPolicy.requestedRange. It returns today's [P−buffer, P+visible+buffer) united with the absolute span of realizedRowIdentities, mapped through the current visibleMessages as the view maps rows (visibleRangeStartIndex + row.index), and capped at maxWindowSize by dropping the realized rows farthest from P. Use it in updateVisibleMessages and in replayHeldVisibleIndex. Realized rows always lie inside the current window, so the union adds no loads, prepends or preloads. The covered check and every iPhone outcome (realized rows already inside today's range) stay the same. Only which rows a replace keeps changes. Do not make the buffer symmetric or enlarge the Mac configuration instead.

**First step.** Write the failing case in VirtualScrollStateTests: config 3/1/3/0, window 10..<15, rows 10-14 realized through ChatTranscriptIdentityPolicy.rows, then markIndexVisible(14). Today the state publishes 13..<18, dropping realized rows 10-12.

**Pinning test.** testMarkIndexVisible_scrollingDownTallViewport_keepsRealizedRows asserts 10..<18 is published, with a Revert-check naming the realized-span union in the policy. A parity test asserts that realized rows 13-14 give exactly today's 13..<18.

**Payoff.** Mac and iPad readers scrolling back down through history keep every row on screen, with no jumps or creep toward the tail. iPhone behavior, load counts and the measured holds stay unchanged.

### `web-content-rendering#1` · high · reliability · effort M · new

**No web view recovers from WebContent process termination, and the pool re-issues dead views as ready**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

No navigation delegate implements webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate and nothing else tests liveness. The reader's needsReload compares only recorded content and signature, so a dead view is never reloaded. A pool entry's didFinishInitialLoad is never cleared: checkout hands the view out as ready, adoption marks paint confirmed and drops the placeholder, check-in re-hosts it. Only a memory warning, LRU eviction, a key change or an account transition removes it. What WebKit shows after an unhandled termination was not measured; the app's policy would not stop a reload of the base URL.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:455-517 — the live coordinator implements decidePolicyFor, didFinish, didCommit, didFail and didFailProvisionalNavigation only; `git grep webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` (and ProcessDidTerminate) over the whole repository returns nothing, and the other three delegates (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1916-1938, BaseEmailWebView.swift:288-319, EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:622-647) have no such method either
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1451-1479 and 1484-1499 — checkout guards on key, didFinishInitialLoad and isCheckedOut only, then returns entry.webView; checkin re-hosts the same web view. didFinishInitialLoad is set true at 1741 and 1749 (and the test seam at 1892) and is never set false
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:336-345 and 358-362 — adoptAlreadyLoadedContent sets hasConfirmedPaintForCurrentLoad = true with no paint check, then completeAdoptionCallbacksIfActive calls onAdoptedPrerendered and onLoadFinished; esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/FullEmailReaderView.swift:195-197 sets webViewPainted = true, which removes the snapshot placeholder (line 112)
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailWebViewLoadCoordination.swift:34-36 and 45-47 — needsReload compares lastLoadedContent and lastLoadedReloadSignature only; loadReadiness then returns deferred 'no-pending-reload', so updateWebView and onLayoutChange never reload a dead view
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1048-1050, 1167-1172, 1509-1521 — the only unprompted pool clear is the memory-warning callback; a visible-row warm that finds a same-key entry keeps it and returns; esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:320-350 — the scene-phase handler only drives sync, nothing empties the pool on background
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:113-115 and 148 — .other and .reload are allowed, and any other non-link navigation type with an https URL falls through to .allow; esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/EmailSenderBaseURLResolver.swift:22 — the base URL is https://<From domain>/

**Trigger.** The WebContent process of a reader or pooled web view dies while the app itself survives: the app suspended with a warm pool (visible email cards warm up to four off-screen web views after 200 ms, EmailContentSection.swift:131-143) or with the reader open, and the system reclaiming memory; or a page that crashes WebKit. Mostly iOS; the Mac has no jetsam, so only crashes apply there.

**Impact.** The full-email reader shows an empty web view with its placeholder already removed. For a pooled message every reopen gets the same dead view until four other messages are warmed, a memory warning arrives, the content or width changes, or the app relaunches. A live, non-adopted reader stays empty until dismissed. No data loss. Narrower than reported: a preview fallback card gets a new web view when its row remounts, and the snapshot renderer fails after its 5 s timeout. "Shows the sender's site" is unverified.

**Verifier.** Read all four delegates, the pool file whole, load coordination, reader view and session, and the scene-phase handler. No guard found; not in CLAUDE.md or the prior review. Changed: the base-URL reload is the auditor's unmeasured reading, and by my recollection WebKit keeps no history item for loadHTMLString, so an empty view is likelier; preview cards self-heal; stickiness is bounded. Not observed: a real process kill, what WebKit then shows, or how often it happens.

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: FullEmailWebViewManager and FullEmailReaderAccountBoundaryRegistry are participants. The terminate handlers may only drop state. They guard the coordinator's isInvalidated so a scrubbed reader does not reload, and the pool's handler never re-warms: a re-warm is new account work with no captured generation (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1086-1091, 1852-1854).
- Pool ownership: a checked-out entry belongs to the reader, whose coordinator is then the delegate (FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:66), so the pool's delegate never hears of its termination. Skipping check-in alone leaves an isCheckedOut entry that clear() keeps (1509-1513) and that blocks every warm of that message (1178-1180). The reader must have the pool drop the entry by web-view identity, and teardown of a checked-out entry stays the fail-closed scrub (1789-1791).
- Navigation policy: the app's own loadHTMLString arrives as .other with the sender's base URL, and allowing .other and .reload is pinned (FullEmailWebViewManagerTests.swift:1402-1406). The auditor's 'cancel any main-frame load the app did not start' needs navigation tracking, which the hand-off of a view from the pool's delegate to the reader's and the scrubs' delegate-less blank loads would defeat. Cancel .backForward only: no code in the app calls reload() or goBack().
- Reload loop and paint gate: updateWebView calls loadContentIfReady on every update (FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:83-88), so the one-shot latch must leave the signature recorded after a second termination, or a page that crashes WebKit reloads forever. Reset through resetLoadedSignatureAfterFailure so paint confirmation re-arms, and keep a late didFail for the dead navigation from resetting the new load. Emptying the pool on background also drops the prepared payloads, and nothing warms them again until rows remount (EmailContentSection.swift:110-112).

**Fix.** Implement webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate in all four delegates; that alone stops WebKit's own reload, whose target was never measured. Reader Coordinator: guard isInvalidated; set isLoading false; if adopted, clear adoptedPrerenderedMessageId and call a new FullEmailWebViewAdopting.discard(messageId:webView:) (drops the entry by identity, keeps the prepared payload, no teardown); call onLoadFailed, then resetLoadedSignatureAfterFailure and loadContentIfReady, once per reload signature. WarmNavigationDelegate: an onTerminate closure removes the idle entry through removeEntry; no re-warm. BaseEmailWebView: the same one-shot reload. Snapshot session: finish with navigationFailed(WKError(.webContentProcessTerminated)), no new enum case. Add .backForward to navigationDecision's cancels. Leave .other/.reload allowed and the pool alive on background.

**First step.** Add WarmNavigationDelegate.webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate firing an onTerminate closure that has FullEmailWebViewManager remove the entry only if entries[id] === entry and it is not checked out, keeping preparedPayloads; pin it with a manager test first.

**Pinning test.** Manager: prepaintAfterExplicitOpen, markInitialLoadFinishedForTesting, call the entry's navigationDelegate terminate method; assert no entry, checkout nil, payload kept. Reader coordinator (iOS): adopt, terminate twice; assert discard once, one reload, onLoadFailed fired, reclaim false. Revert-check each.

**Payoff.** A killed WebContent process no longer leaves the reader blank with its placeholder gone, or recycles a dead pooled view; WebKit's unmeasured reload toward the sender's domain is closed.

### `caching-memory#6` · medium · performance · effort M · known-open

**Every persisted message invalidates the user's own address, forcing a Contacts re-query before row loads**

Area: Caching architecture and memory management. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

createNewMessage invalidates PersonCache for every participant, the user's own address included, which bumps that address's generation. AliasManager's cache is valid only while the fingerprint of the account's own addresses is unchanged, so the next alias read reruns ContactsSelfAliasProvider, which keeps no cache; concurrent readers each rerun it. Separately, every incremental run calls setAliases, which always reruns it, persist or not. A row reads the rollup cache synchronously first, so only rows that missed wait, showing the stored title meanwhile. None of it runs on the main thread.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Creation.swift:208-211 — awaits PersonCache.invalidateEntry for every participant email of a created message; MessagePersister+Participants.swift:17-46 collects From/To/Cc/Bcc with no exclusion of the user's own address. CacheCoordinator.swift:267-274,431-438 plans every updated Person in a save, with no changed-value check, and invalidates each email again
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/PersonCache.swift:271-275 — invalidateEntry calls ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker.shared.invalidate(email:), which stamps a new generation on that address (ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker.swift:64-75)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:33-48,71-77,100-115 — getAliases returns the cache only when the fingerprint over the account's raw addresses is unchanged; a miss awaits cacheAliases, which calls selfAliasProvider.aliases; the fingerprint is stored only after that await, so concurrent callers each call the provider; setAliases calls cacheAliases unconditionally
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:67-117 — no cache; returns [] at once unless Contacts access is authorized or limited; otherwise one unifiedContacts predicate query per address form, then enumerateContacts over the whole address book when a Gmail address matched no card
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:222-223,1028-1038,1053 — every incremental run calls refreshSendAsAliases, and both its in-TTL branch and its refresh branch call AliasManager.setAliases; ForegroundSyncCoordinator.swift:45,217 runs the periodic sync every 60 s
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ConversationRowView.swift:89-97,119-123,209-212,370 — the row's body reads the rollup cache synchronously and starts loadParticipants only on a miss, showing the fallback name until then; ParticipantLoader.swift:181-196,481-500 awaits the aliases ahead of the loader's own cache lookup

**Trigger.** Contacts access granted (without it the provider returns at once). Then: every incremental sync run, every 60 s in the foreground, reruns the provider once through setAliases, with or without new mail. After any stored message that names one of the user's addresses, each alias read that follows reruns it again: a row load that missed the rollup cache, the chat header, a send, the next run. The whole address book is enumerated only when a Gmail address of the account is on no contact card.

**Impact.** Redundant Contacts queries at least once per sync run, each O(address book) in the no-card case. Contact names and photos on rows whose rollup entry was invalidated arrive later by one provider run per concurrent reader, serialized on the provider's actor; the row shows its stored title and initials meanwhile. No main-thread block and no effect on data. The cost of a run was not measured; 50-300 ms for 1-5k contacts is the prior review's estimate.

**Verifier.** Read all cited code plus ContactsSelfAliasProvider, ParticipantRollupCache, ConversationRowView, AliasManagerTests. No guard found: the provider has no cache, AliasManager no single-flight, the review's three tests are absent, step 13 has no Built note. Corrected: rows check the cache before loadParticipants; without Contacts access the provider returns at once; setAliases reruns it every run regardless of persists. Person under NSUpdatedObjectsKey is inferred and not needed. Medium at its low end; cost unmeasured.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1310-1335 `self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist`, Review correction at :1322; Suggested order step 13 (:1626) not built; AliasManager.swift unchanged

**Invariant risks**

- Optimistic hashing parity (CLAUDE.md, Outbound send): getAliases(from: viewContext), awaited inside the cleanup-sensitive gate (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:54-106), must still read Core Data when cold or after invalidate(). A setAliases shortcut or single-flight join must never return a set computed for a different raw account list, or the chat forks.
- Account boundary: cacheAliases writes cachedAccountAliases after its provider await (AliasManager.swift:100-115), so an invalidate() at sign-out (AuthSession.swift:873) can already be overwritten by the old account. A stored in-flight Task makes that worse unless invalidate() bumps an epoch, drops the task, and the write-back checks the epoch.
- Review correction :1322: do not filter self out of MessagePersister+Creation.swift:208-211 or PersonCache.invalidateEntry. Note-to-self rollups depend on the self address's per-email generation, and a real alias change must still call rollupDependencyTracker.invalidateAll().
- Contacts-edit edge: on iOS, the one proven signal for an edit to the user's own card is ContactsResolver.invalidateCache(for:) (EditContactView.swift:199-213 invalidates every address on the card), which shares tracker.invalidate(email:) with PersonCache. Dropping per-email generations wholesale loses it. A CacheCoordinator changed-value filter runs in didSave, where values are committed and changedValues() is empty, so it would also drop real name changes.

**Fix.** Fix AliasManager only, per the review correction. In ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker, add a contact-card generation map bumped by a new invalidateContactCard(email:), which ContactsResolver.invalidateCache calls and invalidateAll clears. Add selfAliasFingerprint(for:), built from the global generation, the auth status and those card generations, never PersonCache's per-email ones. AliasManager keys validity on that fingerprint plus Set(raw), captured before the provider await. When both match, setAliases returns the cache. The provider runs once per raw set through a stored Task, which invalidate() drops by bumping an epoch that also guards the write-back. Leave MessagePersister and CacheCoordinator unchanged.

**First step.** Add invalidateContactCard(email:) and selfAliasFingerprint(for:) to ParticipantRollupDependencyTracking, its tracker and the AliasManagerTests stub. Switch ContactsResolver.invalidateCache(for:) to the new call, then move AliasManager's two validity checks to the new fingerprint.

**Pinning test.** AliasManagerTests with a real tracker and a counting provider stub. invalidate(email:) of the account address, then getAliases, stays at one provider call; same-set setAliases stays at one; invalidateContactCard makes two; concurrent reads share one call; invalidate() mid-call discards the late result.

**Payoff.** Takes the Contacts query, an address-book walk where a Gmail address is on no card, out of every sync run, every row load after a persist, and New Message's gate-held anchor step.

### `chat-transcript-ui#2` · medium · performance · effort M · known-partial

**Scrolling history and every arriving message re-materialize the whole window on the main actor**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

While the reader scrolls, the window settles at about 40 rows, from 10 above the appearing row to 30 below it. Every 3-row step falls outside that range and replaces the window. The replace re-fetches all 40 rows on the main queue (SELF IN plus three prefetches) and re-maps them, although 37 are cached. It also clears the by-index memo, so ChatMessagesView.body (not only the row body) runs one main-thread OFFSET fetch per step. Sync arrivals and echoes still take the known-open main-queue reload: two COUNTs, an OFFSET object fetch and a re-map, usually of 20-40 rows and at most 300.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+WindowLoading.swift:259-262,295-305,469-473 — the coverage range is scrollPosition-bufferSize to +visible+buffer; the slide passes reusesCachedRows only when extendsWindow (keyboard replay), so a replace calls resolveRowsOnViewContextThrowing for every ID
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState.swift:360-368 with esc-chatmail/Services/VirtualScroll/VirtualScrollConfiguration.swift:36-41 — a step of 3 or more rows moves scrollPosition and calls updateVisibleMessages; buffer 10 and visible 20 give a 40-row window that the next 3-row step leaves (preload needs distance under 5, but the replace triggers at 7)
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:7-14,32-60 — setMessageWindow clears resolvedRowsByAbsoluteIndex; SELF IN fetch with participants, participants.person and attachments prefetched, then ChatMessageRowModelMapper.map, on viewContext
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesView.swift:37-42,120-124,1054-1070 with esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:96-123 — the session forwards scrollState's objectWillChange, and body calls senderGroupingMessages, which calls rowForGrouping(window.end): fetchOffset=index on viewContext for every historical window it publishes
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+Reconciliation.swift:13-18 with esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:276-296 and esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+WindowLoading.swift:144-153 — a dataset change in a followed chat runs loadLatestWindow(forceViewContext: true): a COUNT, then an OFFSET Message fetch (batch 20) mapped to objectIDs plus a COUNT, on the viewContext. The window keeps its accumulated rows up to maxWindowSize (300)
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+TailAppend.swift:32-34 and docs/scalability-review.md:1561 — sync inserts and the echo deliberately keep the full reload; keyset paging and the lookahead are recorded as not built

**Trigger.** Two triggers. First, scrolling through history in any chat: each step of 3 or more rows replaces a window of about 40 rows. Second, an incoming message or send echo while the chat follows the latest window. The main-thread lookahead's OFFSET cost grows with the depth of the window end, and the reload's COUNTs grow with the size of the conversation.

**Impact.** Each 3-row scroll step puts about 8 SQL statements and a 40-row re-map on the main thread. In chats under about 1k messages that cost is probably small; it was not measured. In 10k-20k chats the per-step OFFSET lookahead (the prior review estimated 20-40 ms on device at OFFSET 10000) hitches roughly every 3 rows. Arrivals there cost about 70-150 ms each, which is the prior review's estimate.

**Verifier.** Every cited path holds. Corrections: the steady window is about 40 rows, not 300. The lookahead that fires on every slide comes from ChatMessagesView.body (senderGroupingMessages). The row-body lookaheads at lines 338/349 normally go unrealized, because the window reaches 10 rows above and 30 below the appearing row. Neither the sliding replace nor the re-map of every row is a documented decision, so reuse is open. The sync and lookahead parts are the prior review's open "Will degrade" items. The slide's page and COUNT run off main. No timings were taken. Ordinary chats are not shown to hitch, so the severity is medium.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: chat-grouping-lookahead-offset (l.769), chat-reconcile-main-count-offset (l.744), step 5 built objectID predicates (l.1543) / "Not built yet" (l.1561), step 11 keyset (l.1624). Slide re-map of 37 cached rows is new.

**Invariant risks**

- Dataset reloads (loadLatestWindow, reloadHistoricalWindowClamped, the dataset-change retry at WindowLoading.swift:232-242, the deferred .range replay at Reconciliation.swift:62-67) are the documented healing path for rows changed without a precise notification (TailAppend.swift:20-22, testSyncTailInsert_followingLatest_takesFullReload). 'Reuse cached rows on every load' deletes it. Only current-window rows are trusted (RowCache.swift:62-68), so resolveCachedRows' trust-everything rule must not be used.
- A published neighbour ID goes stale when a visible insert lands between the window end and it while a historical window is preserved (ChangeObservation.swift:77-86). Line 123-125 clears only the index memo there. Neighbour IDs must be cleared at that point and evicted like window rows, and the index < totalMessageCount guard must stay so latest windows never look ahead.
- Widening page.messageIDs to carry neighbours breaks loadWindow's exact-count check (WindowLoading.swift:461) and the preloads' disjointness check (648, 743). The injectable MessagePageLoader needs new optional fields instead. The sliding replace itself is deliberate (testMarkIndexVisible_withoutHold_slidesWindowAsBefore): do not turn it into an extension.
- The arrival fixes stay separate. An in-place sync tail append must exclude the echo, which is an insert plus the optimistic row's delete in one sync save; sync owns that replacement and display identity must persist. Auto-read must still go through resolvePendingInsertedMessageEvents. A background reload cannot see unsaved optimistic rows (CLAUDE.md outbound send; ensureVisibleMessage forces the viewContext).

**Fix.** Make two changes now and leave the third to step 11. (1) Slide: in updateVisibleMessages, pass reusesCachedRows: true for the replace as well, so only rows outside the current window are fetched and mapped. Every dataset reload keeps the full re-map. (2) Lookahead: the page loaders fetch one extra row on each side in the same OFFSET query, into new optional page fields. Store those neighbour IDs with the window, deriving them from trimmed IDs on preloads and setting nil for latest and tail-append. rowForGrouping resolves them by ID through resolveCachedRow and keeps the OFFSET fetch only as a fallback. Evict and clear the IDs wherever the index memo is. (3) Arrivals (background count plus pending fold, sync tail append) and keyset paging stay with step 11.

**First step.** In VirtualScrollState.updateVisibleMessages (WindowLoading.swift:304), change `reusesCachedRows: extendsWindow` to `true` and update its comment. Add a main-queue variant of FetchCountingContext that records each Message fetch's fetchOffset and the number of IDs in its SELF IN.

**Pinning test.** VirtualScrollStateTests, using a main-queue counting viewContext. A 3-row slide replace maps only the new rows (one SELF IN of 3 IDs). A window row updated beforehand shows its new value. After a historical publish, rowForGrouping(window.end) runs no fetchOffset>0 fetch. Revert-checks name reusesCachedRows and the neighbour fields.

**Payoff.** Each history scroll step of 3 rows maps 3 rows instead of 40 and runs no body-time OFFSET fetch on the main thread, on iOS or the Mac (start-1). Arrival reloads stay as they are until step 11.

### `chat-transcript-ui#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Reveal and anchoring rest on undocumented LazyVStack behaviour, compensated by timers, with two of three OS paths never run**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The transcript is ScrollView{LazyVStack}. The reveal relies on SwiftUI behaviour: rows calling onAppear under the cover, where scrollTo lands, and size-change anchors. The coordinator infers that behaviour from geometry and corrects it with probes, a nudge, a past-end correction and a watchdog. The blank-open cause was never reproduced, so the fix rests on a hypothesis. No test mounts the view on any OS; 124 unit tests cover the coordinator's decisions. Every failure is bounded: at most about 4 s hidden, then a reveal, and a blank reveal clears on the first scroll.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesCoordinator.swift:2340-2342 — 'the most plausible mechanism for that report, not an observed one: the device-side cause was never reproduced'
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesCoordinator.swift:196-200,1001-1007,2124-2152 — a 3 s reveal time limit plus a 1 s watchdog grace end every hidden pass with a reveal; the timers only pace re-probes, and geometry onChange (ChatMessagesView.swift:504-510) drives the handler directly
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesView.swift:1187-1209 — role anchors from iOS 18; below that the single .top anchor the transcript always used. #available(iOS …, *) is true on macOS, so the Mac takes the modern branches
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatTranscriptScrollAnchorPolicy.swift:7-18 — under the .top anchor chats 'open slowly, and sometimes blank', bounded by the pass's time limit: the documented cost that remains on iOS 17.x
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatTranscriptOffsetShifter.swift:20-26 — the inset shift is gated to iOS 26+ (measured in the 26.5 and 27.0 simulators); earlier versions keep the coordinator's existing scroll-to-bottom path
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState.swift:281-285 — the at-rest prepend is deferred (deferredLeadingReplayIndex), a guard; VirtualScrollStateTests.swift:4943-4946 — 11 of 40 measured a rejected extend-on-every-step design, not current code

**Trigger.** A chat open on an OS whose LazyVStack realization or scrollTo behaviour differs from the iOS 26/27 simulators the mechanism was measured on. That is chiefly iOS 17.x, which keeps the old .top anchor, or a future OS release. It is not a layout pass that outlasts the 16-150 ms waits: those waits only pace re-probes, geometry changes call the handler directly, growth resets the retry budget, and a deadline bounds the pass.

**Impact.** The worst case is a spinner for up to about 3-4 s, or a reveal that is off the newest row or blank until the first scroll. It is not data loss and not a wedge. A regression would show only as always-on warnings in the device log, because CI does not mount the view. There is also an ongoing cost: each new scroll feature has to fit into the reveal, follow and shift state machines.

**Verifier.** I read the coordinator whole, the view and the policies. Corrections: VirtualScrollState 281-285 is a guard, and the 11/40 figure measured a rejected design. "Two of three OS paths never run": CI runs none of the view's paths, and the Mac takes the iOS 18/26 branches. The older forks keep behaviour that shipped before. The waiting trigger is wrong. Blank-open fixes came in three rounds (Sep 29-Oct 12), with none since. High needs a concrete failure under common conditions; this has bounded fallbacks, hence medium.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:730 (Keep intact: "Leave ChatTranscriptRealizationPolicy row realization untouched"); CLAUDE.md Traps, hidden initial-anchor pass bullet; docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:613 Risks

**Invariant risks**

- The realization record has to stay where it is. markRowRealized and markRowUnrealized live in each row's onAppear and onDisappear, keyed by the ForEach display identity so the echo swap does not remount the row (ChatMessagesView.swift:396-418, CLAUDE.md, scalability-review.md:730). Moving to collection-view reuse and willDisplay, or deleting the 'below iOS 18' unrealize after a floor raise, silently breaks the nudge's out-and-back (VirtualScrollState.swift:246-248).
- The bottom inset and anchor contract. The composer overlay's measured height is the transcript's bottom inset and must never become a safeAreaInset.
