ChatBottomInsetPolicy assumes the .top size-change anchor after the reveal (ChatTranscriptScrollAnchorPolicy.swift:22-25). Rows must not change height after they mount. A collection view's contentInset and self-sizing cells change all three.
- Mark-read gating. A message is auto-marked read only when the chat is revealed, uncovered and in an active window, and the anchor counts as visible for following (ChatTranscriptPresentationPolicy.swift:110-122, ChatMessagesCoordinator.swift:653-680). A new container that reads the anchor as visible under the cover marks mail read that nobody saw. On the Mac, any new AppKit view in the chat that takes drags or mouse-downs needs MacFileDropForwarder and must not take clicks away from the attachment drag source or Quick Look.
- Hosted harness hygiene. VirtualScrollState fetches on the view context from the main actor (rowForGrouping), so the harness must use stack.makeMainQueueViewContext() or ConcurrencyDebug traps. Appear marks the chat read, and the Mac test host's container is real, so inject MessageActions (via MainQueueMessageActionsCoreDataStack), the contact loaders and a temp-rooted HTML handler. Wait by wall-clock deadline. A floor raise goes through Xcode, never a hand edit of pbxproj, and ships to TestFlight on merge.

**Fix.** Do not replace the container now: a collection view breaks most transcript invariants for a bounded, unreproduced failure. Stage it. First make the reveal observable: a defaulted `onInitialReveal` outcome closure on ChatMessagesCoordinator (confirmed, time limit, attempts exhausted, watchdog, user scroll), called in completeInitialReveal and the user-scroll reveal, threaded through ChatMessagesView's init. Then add a hosted iOS suite mounting ChatMessagesView over a seeded TestCoreDataStack, asserting a confirmed reveal; CI's iOS 26 runs it. Second, ask Kevin whether to raise the iOS floor (18 removes the .top branch; 26 also the shifter gate), set in Xcode, deleting only #available else-branches. Reconsider UICollectionView only if field warnings show fallback reveals.

**First step.** Add `onInitialReveal: (InitialRevealOutcome) -> Void = { _ in }` to both ChatMessagesCoordinator inits. Call it from completeInitialReveal (mapping fallbackReason to a case), from handleUserScrollInteraction's reveal and from the empty-conversation reveal. Pass it through ChatMessagesSession and ChatMessagesView's init with a nil default.

**Pinning test.** ChatTranscriptRevealHostedTests (#if os(iOS), default plan): mount ChatMessagesView over 60 seeded text rows (makeMainQueueViewContext) with mountInTestWindow; wait by deadline for onInitialReveal; assert .confirmed and newest row realized. Revert-check: deleting the onAppear markRowRealized call forces a fallback reveal.

**Payoff.** The reveal stops being an unobserved hypothesis and becomes a property CI checks on the shipping runtime. It catches an OS release that changes LazyVStack behaviour. With a floor raise, two never-run code paths can be deleted.

### `chat-transcript-ui#4` · medium · performance · effort M · new

**The transcript is one invalidation domain, and each row body takes the HTML file lock and hashes message text on the main thread**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Accurate today: the session forwards every scroll-state and coordinator publish, and ChatView observes Conversation and passes a new closure each pass. MessageBubble is not Equatable and gets a fresh onSendRecoveryAction, so every realized row's body runs on unrelated changes. Each body takes the process-wide HTML lock through htmlSourceSignature (a stat when the cache misses), even though cachedHTMLSourceSignature exists so mounting a row does not stat. Card rows add two more lock takes and five SHA-256 digests, a cost already removed from the row model.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesView.swift:37-42,77,365-381,473-482 — both objectWillChange publishers forwarded; @GestureState drag flag in the row-building scope; per-pass onSendRecoveryAction closure literal
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageBubble.swift:44,80-83,199,635-643 — non-Equatable struct holding closures; body computes loadSignature via htmlContentHandler.htmlSourceSignature
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:15,32-47,526-570,764-790 — one NSRecursiveLock; cachedHTMLSourceSignature documented 'mounting a chat row must not stat'; the uncached form body uses stats on a miss
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailContentSection.swift:47-67,103-110,371-380 — loadKey/warmFullEmailKey computed in body: two lock reads, five SHA-256 + String(format:) per byte
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/ChatMessageRowModel.swift:97-109,279-280 — team replaced per-row SHA-256 'so MessageBubble body recomputation does not hash message text'; ChatMessagesCoordinator.swift:1316,1994-2000 unguarded takeover publish and the 'every realized bubble re-evaluated' note; ChatView.swift:9,87-93 @ObservedObject Conversation plus a new closure each pass
- docs/scalability-review.md:1034 — the planned off-main orphan sweep takes the boundary lock per chunk, not for the whole sweep

**Trigger.** Each drag start and end (@GestureState plus the unguarded takeover publish), keyboard height changes, re-probes of the hidden pass, any visibleMessages publish (one row's attachment or send state), and any merged save that changes the open Conversation (rollups on new mail or mark-read). Lock waits happen only while background work holds the HTML boundary: sync body writes, bubble, preview and warm reads, launch re-derivation and backfill reads after an epoch bump, and 100-unlink chunks that reclaim files of deleted rows.

**Impact.** Every realized row's body runs again on events that have nothing to do with it, and each pass takes the global HTML lock 1–3 times per row on the main thread. A take waits for at most one critical section held off main: one body read or write, or one 100-unlink chunk, which can run to tens of ms. The cost scales with realized rows, not mailbox size, though contention rises during S2/S3 backfills. None of this was measured. The claim that a planned off-main sweep would hang main for the whole sweep is wrong: that plan takes the lock per chunk.

**Verifier.** Read every cited line. Correct as described: forwarding, the non-Equatable bubble, the per-pass closures, body-time lock reads, a stat on a cache miss, and the five digests. Found more support: the no-stat cachedHTMLSourceSignature built for mounting rows, and the per-row SHA-256 the team removed from the row model, which is still in EmailContentSection. Corrected the orphan-sweep clause. Steady state is mostly cache hits costing microseconds per row. No body counts or lock waits were measured. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or the scalability review accepts this.

**October review.** Not in docs/scalability-review.md. Related only: html-orphan-sweep-main-actor (line 1034), whose per-chunk off-main plan, once built, would put lock waits against these body reads.

**Invariant risks**

- Equality must compare the whole ChatMessageRowModel, not loadSignatureComponents. The stored verdict is kept out of the load signature on purpose, and a verdict stamped while the row is mounted must still re-render it without restarting its load (MessageBubble.swift:115-120; ChatMessageRowModel.swift:244-249; CLAUDE.md rich-content verdict trap).
- Removing htmlSourceSignature from the body needs a replacement trigger. Without one, rows go stale after recovery, raw-source saves and refetch rewrites, the three posters of contentSourceDidChangeNotification (HTMLContentRecoveryService:449, CanonicalEmailContentLoader:202, MessagePersister+Updates:643). A placeholder that changes after the first load ('unknown', then the real value) doubles every row's load through MessageBubbleViewModel's appliedContentSignature gate.
- An Equatable bubble keeps the closures from an older pass. performSendRecovery writes ChatComposerFocus and viewModel state, so actions must read state when called (the MacMailboxDetail rule). LoadTaskID must keep message.id because of the echo swap under one ForEach identity. Keep ChatTranscriptRowLeadIn unconditional and update the text pins in ChatBubbleStyleSourceTests.
- Any signature read moved into the load must use the captured accountContext.htmlContent generation, never the nil-generation overload the body uses today. The revision counter must stay per row (the bubble's view model), never on ChatMessagesSession or VirtualScrollState, or the single invalidation domain comes back. Moving to @Observable breaks the ObservableObject convention and the Combine sinks.

**Fix.** Three changes, in this order. (1) Make rows skippable. Move every value input of MessageBubble into one synthesized-Equatable Inputs struct: the whole ChatMessageRowModel, prefetchedSenderName, the one-to-one flag, contactRefreshToken, runPlacement, transcriptWidth, isNewestInTranscript and style. == compares only that struct. The closures go through a session-owned object that reads state when called. Add .equatable(), as MacMailboxDetail does, and guard the takeover publish at ChatMessagesCoordinator:1316. (2) Replace the body's htmlSourceSignature with a per-row revision: MessageBubbleViewModel subscribes to contentSourceDidChangeNotification for its loadingMessageID and bumps a @Published counter. (3) Key EmailContentSection's two tasks on a Hashable struct of loadSignatureComponents plus that revision. Skip @Observable.

**First step.** Bundle MessageBubble's value inputs into one synthesized-Equatable Inputs struct. Route its two closures through a session-owned action object that reads state when called. Show the row through .equatable(), as MacMailboxDetail does.

**Pinning test.** MessageBubbleInputsTests: bubbles differing only in closures compare equal; differing isNewestInTranscript, contactRefreshToken or storedRichContentVerdict do not. MessageBubbleViewModelTests: a contentSourceDidChange post for loadingMessageID bumps sourceRevision; another ID's does not. Source pin: no htmlSourceSignature( in bubble views.

**Payoff.** Drags, keyboard moves, sends and merged saves re-run only the rows that changed. No row body waits on the global HTML lock behind off-main body I/O. Unmeasured.

### `chat-transcript-ui#5` · medium · scalability · effort M · new

**Row loads queue behind each other: DOM parses run on a shared actor every row hops through, and producers ignore row cancellation**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

ParsedEmailProvider runs the full DOM parse inside its actor with no suspension point. With includePreviewImages, that parse also sanitizes the HTML and parses it a second time. Every card row's preview build goes through that one actor, so the parses run one after another. Every bubble and preview load's generation check also waits on that actor. RenderedMessageCache producers run in unstructured tasks, so a row's cancellation never stops them. Rows the reader has already flung past keep queuing parses ahead of the rows the reader stopped at.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/EmailDOM/ParsedEmail.swift:297-322 — actor method: generation guard, cache lookup, then `try ParsedEmail.parse(...)` synchronously with no await; parse (98-123) builds the SwiftSoup document, plain text, summary and, if asked, EmailPreviewImageExtractor (sanitize + second DOM query)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader.swift:174-187 — isAccountWorkContextCurrent awaits renderedMessageCache, htmlContentRecoveryService and parsedEmailProvider; called at 66/71/109 and again in each facet
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSourceLoader.swift:144-160,189-196 — the card preview source is built in a RenderedMessageCache producer that calls parsedEmailProvider.parsedEmail(includePreviewImages: true); there is no cancellation check on this path
- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/RenderedMessageCache.swift:630-640 — `Task { await producer() }` then `await work.task.value`: no cancellation handler, so the producer runs on after its waiter is cancelled
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader+HTMLAnalysis.swift:139-155 — the bubble loader itself parses only rows with attachments, calendar invites or a missing HTML hint
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageDisplayPolicy.swift:101-113 — a known stored verdict routes at mount without the load; esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailContentSection.swift:86-106 — a card shows EmailContentPlaceholder until previewPipeline.loadPreview returns

**Trigger.** Opening a newsletter or list (`l|`) chat in which most rows are cards: the first open in a session, or after a memory warning or RenderedMessageCache eviction (20 MB, and preview sources hold the canonical HTML). Also flinging through such a chat, where cancelled rows still enqueue their parses.

**Impact.** Visible card rows keep their placeholder until every parse queued ahead of them has finished on one serial executor, and the parses for rows already scrolled past are ahead of them in that queue. Cards then pop in late, swapping placeholder height for card height. Rows that wait on the load (unknown verdict, forwarded, incoming HTML with no stored preview) stay on the pill for longer. Plain-text rows and rows with a known verdict render at mount, so their delayed loads cannot be seen. Parse times were not measured.

**Verifier.** Corrected the scope: the main parse source is card preview builds, not bubble loads, and plain-text rows show no visible delay. The full-email warm task does not use the parse actor: it takes the preferHTML branch, which returns before the parse (SourcePreparation:100), and it checks cancellation (OriginalEmailSourceLoader:576). Re-classifying rows that already have a stored verdict is the documented design (the load is authoritative and re-stamps stale verdicts). That work runs off any actor and does not delay rendering, so on its own it is low. Prior review covered only the provider's memory.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md "parsed-email-cache-no-byte-cap" (adjacent memory item, still open: count limit 256 and FIFO at ParsedEmail.swift:265-266 and 424-427; its Keep intact already requires close to drain in-flight parses). Design intent: MessageBubbleLoader.swift:11-14.

**Invariant risks**

- The close must still drain. Today the synchronous parse on the actor is the drain: closeAccountWorkAndClear (ParsedEmail.swift:364-368) cannot run in the middle of a parse (315-322). Once parses are detached, every parse must stay registered until it unwinds. The same goes for producers that RenderedMessageCache.cancelInFlight/cancelAllInFlight drop, which is already a gap: close awaits only inFlight.values (RenderedMessageCache.swift:550, 786-803). Otherwise old-account HTML outlives sign-out.
- A cancelled producer's output must never be treated as a result. Once producers observe cancellation, one cancelled mid-run can return a degraded value, such as a placeholder analysis built with no canonical HTML. That value must not be stored, handed to joined waiters (who today pass on isCurrent(snapshot) alone, line 623), or memoized by htmlAnalysisCache.setValue (MessageBubbleLoader+HTMLAnalysis.swift:80-88, which has no Task.isCancelled check).
- Re-validate after the new await. invalidate(messageId:) (ParsedEmail.swift:350-357) and a store for another source signature can now interleave with a parse. Gate the store on the in-flight entry still being this work, not on a new per-message generation map: the review flags such a map as a growth item and pruning it per key as an ABA hazard. Re-check accepts(expected) and re-prune stale signatures before storing, and re-check accepts(expected) again before returning.
- CI builds with Swift 6.2, which rejects a non-Sendable capture in a @Sendable closure: the injected parser (ParsedEmail.swift:256, 267) and every capture of the detached task must be @Sendable. EmailDocument is not Sendable, so it must be created and used up inside the task. The audit's other suggestion, trusting the stored verdict and verifying later, is not part of the fix. Routing at mount is already built (MessageDisplayPolicy.swift:101-113). Moving the check to idle would drop a documented trigger of RichContentVerdictRefresher, and the cards would still wait.

**Fix.** Stage 1, ParsedEmailProvider only, protocol unchanged: run each parse in a Task.detached registered per ParsedEmailKey (work id, requested facts, waiter count); the actor only dedups, caches and stores. Admit two or three parses at once through a cancellation-aware, newest-first permit. Store only if the entry is still that work's and accepts(expected) holds, re-pruning other signatures then; invalidate drops the entry from the dedup map. closeAccountWorkAndClear cancels and awaits every parse still running, abandoned ones included. Stage 2, RenderedMessageCache: count waiters, cancel a producer when the last leaves, keep cancelled producers registered until they unwind, and never return or memoize their value. Skip the lock reads and the verdict change.

**First step.** Add ParsedEmailProviderTests with an injected parser that blocks until released: a generation check answers while a parse is blocked, two keys parse at the same time, and close waits for the blocked parse and stores nothing. Then move the parse into the registered Task.detached.

**Pinning test.** ParsedEmailProviderTests with a gated parser: isAccountGenerationCurrent answers within a deadline while a parse is blocked; two keys' parses both start; close awaits the blocked parse and caches nothing. Revert-checks name the detached parse and closeAccountWorkAndClear's drain.

**Payoff.** Card previews in a newsletter chat parse in parallel instead of one at a time. Generation checks stop waiting behind parses, and rows already flung past stop delaying the visible ones. Not measured.

### `content-pipeline-cpu#6` · medium · performance · effort S · new

**The Forward sheet sanitizes and wraps the forwarded email on the main actor**

Area: HTML sanitization, DOM cleaning, text processing and preview builders. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

ComposeViewModel is @MainActor and updateForwardedPreviewHTML calls HTMLSanitizerService.wrapHTMLForDisplay synchronously from ComposeView's onAppear and its color-scheme onChange. The input is the whole stored original HTML with a header spliced in, with no size cap. The chain is a SwiftSoup parse and outerHtml, a Character-wise URL attribute scan, up to 30 whole-document regex replacements, the CSS passes, then a second SwiftSoup parse and outerHtml (the wrapper's default .domPreferred). The result is cached per appearance, so it runs once per presentation and once per light/dark change.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ComposeViewModel.swift:8-9,226-245 — @MainActor class; updateForwardedPreviewHTML calls HTMLSanitizerService.shared.wrapHTMLForDisplay inline; the guard at 235 skips only when a preview for the same appearance already exists
- esc-chatmail/Views/Compose/ComposeView.swift:219-223,229-231 — onAppear runs setupForMode() then updateForwardedPreviewHTML; onChange(of: isDarkMode) runs it again
- esc-chatmail/Services/Compose/MessageFormatBuilder.swift:208-245 — buildHTMLForward returns the entire originalHTML with a header inserted after <body> (or wrapped in <html><body>), so the input always has document structure and no length bound
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLSanitizerService.swift:4,73-89,180-193 — plain final class with synchronous methods and no isolation; wrapHTMLForDisplay runs sanitize() then displayWrapper.wrapHTMLForDisplay with the default headSerialization
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLDisplayWrapper.swift:13-16,156-162,328-344 — the code's own comment puts one SwiftSoup parse at 50-200 ms on large newsletters and gives the reader a .stringOnly path to avoid it; .domPreferred (the forward path) does SwiftSoup.parse + outerHtml
- esc-chatmail/Services/EmailDOM/EmailDOMHTMLSanitizer.swift:94-109 and esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLTrackingRemover.swift:95-125 — first SwiftSoup parse, select("*") attribute pass and outerHtml; then 2 + 11 + 7 + 10 stringByReplacingMatches passes over the whole document whenever it contains "<img"

**Trigger.** Tapping Forward on a message that has stored HTML (the preview is skipped only when there is no stored HTML or an inline attachment's Content-ID cannot be emitted verbatim), and again each time the appearance changes while the sheet is open. Cost grows with that one message's HTML size, not with mailbox size.

**Impact.** The main thread is blocked once as the Forward sheet appears, for a time proportional to the forwarded body. With two SwiftSoup parse/serialize round-trips at the 50-200 ms each that the code's own comment gives for large newsletters, plus the regex and character scans, a large marketing email plausibly exceeds the 250 ms hang threshold; small emails stay a short hitch. Not timed. No data or correctness consequence.

**Verifier.** All six cited locations read as described. No guard, cap or off-main hop was found. Not in CLAUDE.md or docs/scalability-review.md, so it is new. One imprecision: the DEBUG-only, iOS-only HTMLRenderingDebugView.swift:73-75 also calls the sanitizer on the main actor. ComposeViewModelTests.swift:131-135 pins the synchronous publish, so the fix changes that test. Adjacent main-actor work on the same tap (ChatViewModel.swift:1847-1867 reads the body from disk) is outside this finding. Hang duration is inferred, hence medium confidence.

**Invariant risks**

- The second half of the recommendation, making the sanitizer's entry points async, would add suspension points to HTMLContentLoader+SourcePreparation.swift:101-102,143,214,246. The caller contract says to re-check the account generation after every await before a result is cached. Keep HTMLSanitizerService synchronous; it is already used off the main thread there.
- The nil-HTML branch is not an empty state. ComposeView.swift:414-429 shows a 160-point plain-text fallback, while the web view at :401-407 is 240 points tall. Showing that fallback while the preview is built would flash the forwarded email's plain text and then jump in height. It needs a separate 'preparing' state.
- Results can arrive out of order. The SwiftSoup parse cannot be cancelled, so a light-to-dark-to-light toggle can publish the wrong appearance unless the result is checked against the latest request (and against hasDiscarded). Also, BaseEmailWebView's reload signature includes isDarkMode (BaseEmailWebView.swift:236-247). Passing it the environment's value while the old HTML is still shown makes WebKit reload twice, the first time with the wrong background. Pass the appearance the HTML was built for.
- The work must run in a Task.detached: a plain Task inherits the main actor. Hand it only Strings, a Bool and a @Sendable static builder. Capturing the non-Sendable HTMLSanitizerService hits the trap where CI's Swift 6.2 and the local 6.4 disagree. The preview must stay out of HTMLContentLoader and RenderedMessageCache, which take part in the account boundary. Send must neither wait for the preview nor use it: send uses the raw forwardedHTMLBody (OutboundMessageCoordinator.swift:577-581).

**Fix.** Keep HTMLSanitizerService synchronous. In ComposeViewModel.init, inject a @Sendable (String, Bool) -> String preview builder. Its default is a static func that makes today's exact wrapHTMLForDisplay(.preview) call, so the output is identical. updateForwardedPreviewHTML records the appearance asked for and returns early if a preview for it is already published or being built. Otherwise it cancels the previous task and runs the builder in Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated). The result is published on the main actor only if its appearance is still the latest asked for and the sheet has not been discarded. Publish a state (plainText / preparing / html with its appearance). ComposeView shows a 240-point placeholder while preparing and passes the HTML's own appearance to BaseEmailWebView. Send is unchanged.

**First step.** Add the injected @Sendable preview builder to ComposeViewModel.init, with a static default that reproduces today's HTMLSanitizerService.shared.wrapHTMLForDisplay(..., displayPurpose: .preview) call. Then convert testUpdateForwardedPreviewHTML_cachesWrappedPreviewAndRefreshesForColorScheme to await publication with a waitUntil bounded by a deadline.

**Pinning test.** In ComposeViewModelTests, a builder blocked on a semaphore: updateForwardedPreviewHTML returns with the state .preparing; after release, waitUntil .html. A second test asks for light then dark, finishes dark first, and expects dark at the end. Revert-check: Task.detached in updateForwardedPreviewHTML.

**Payoff.** Takes a one-time main-thread stall off the opening of the Forward sheet and off each appearance change. On large newsletters that stall plausibly passes 250 ms. The preview output stays byte-identical.

### `conversation-list-ui#1` · medium · performance · effort M · known-open

**Rows with a contact photo, and any row that just received mail, always miss the participant rollup cache, so the main-context name load is the steady state**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

ParticipantRollupCache stores no photoInfo when any photo carries bytes, and production photos always do, so a photo row's full lookup is always nil and its .task(id:) reloads on each appearance. The loader's pre-snapshot checks pass [:] header names, matching only entries cached without From names, so the load runs the snapshot on the view context: participant walk plus an unbounded DISTINCT sender fetch. Every created message also bumps each From/To/Cc/Bcc address's generation, evicting rollups that name them. Chat-header loads take the same path on every chat open.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantRollupCache.swift:318-329 — cacheablePhotoInfo returns nil unless every photo has imageData == nil; 42-44 a photo lookup returns only photoInfo; 286-290 a non-nil header-name request (including [:]) must equal the cached names; 223-227 a moved dependency fingerprint evicts the entry.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ProfilePhotoResolver.swift:200,250-255,296 — prefetch, avatar-file and Contacts paths all return ProfilePhoto(imageData: data, url: nil); only a non-file, non-data stored URL (280) is byte-free. Dependencies.swift:413-416 builds the production loader with no photoLoader override.
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ConversationRowView.swift:356-358 — with a participant hash, needsParticipantLoad is `cachedFull == nil`, never consulting uncachedLoad; 119-123 and 209-212 make it the .task(id:) key; 370-377 the task calls loadParticipants with conversationContext, which ConversationListView.swift:198 and MacConversationSidebar.swift:116 pass as viewContext.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantLoader.swift:186-209 — both pre-snapshot checks pass headerDisplayNamesByEmail: [:]; 211-217 then fetchConversationParticipantSnapshot, which (403-432) runs context.perform on the caller's context; 233-245 the post-snapshot upgrade re-resolves photos and stores photoInfo nil again. ChatViewModel.swift:1756-1763 calls the same load on every chat open.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationParticipantExtractor.swift:232-244 — DISTINCT (senderEmail, senderName) dictionary fetch over every message of the conversation, no limit; the ESCChatmail 6 model has no index covering the sender columns (byConversationAndDateIndex at contents:163 only).
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Creation.swift:208-211 — each created message calls PersonCache.invalidateEntry for every From/To/Cc/Bcc address (MessagePersister+Participants.swift:15-48), which bumps that address's rollup generation (PersonCache.swift:271-275). docs/scalability-review.md:1561 lists row-header-distinct-sender-scan as not built yet.

**Trigger.** Each appearance (scroll-in, and probably pop-back) of a non-list row whose top four participants include a Contacts photo and whose conversation holds an explicit From name for one of them; every chat open of a conversation with From names, photo or not; the next body evaluation of any cached row naming an address on a newly persisted message.

**Impact.** One view-context perform per trigger, with an unbounded DISTINCT read of that conversation's messages on the main thread. That is sub-millisecond for ordinary chats and an estimated 5-40 ms hitch for 2k-20k-message chats at S2/S3, paid on every appearance instead of once per 300 s TTL. Photo avatars are decoded from Data again on each fresh mount (CachedAsyncImage has no decoded-image cache), so a row can show initials first. No data loss and no hang.

**Verifier.** Read all cited files whole plus CachedAsyncImage, AliasManager, the dependency tracker and the model's indexes; found no guard, cap or off-main path. Prior review item row-header-distinct-sender-scan is listed 'Not built yet' (line 1561); photo and per-persist causes are new. Severity lowered to medium: per load under ~1 ms for ordinary chats, 5-40 ms only for 2k-20k-message chats (prior review's estimate, unmeasured). Not run: .task re-firing per List appearance and row state discard are SwiftUI behavior.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:869-893 `row-header-distinct-sender-scan` (Review correction at :881); Suggested order step 5 lists it "Not built yet" at :1561. The photo-row cache bypass and the `[:]` pre-snapshot mismatch are new causes that make this miss happen far more often than that item says.

**Invariant risks**

- Core Data context rules. A background context cannot resolve the window's unsaved conversations, which have temporary IDs (the review correction at :881). Defaulting to CoreDataStack.shared.newBackgroundContext() would read the wrong store under TestCoreDataStack and in the Mac test host. A context built by hand must set NSMergeByPropertyObjectTrumpMergePolicy. Its perform block may capture only Sendable values, or Swift 6.2 rejects it (the CI trap).
- Header-name freshness. ParticipantLoader.swift:193/205 pass `headerDisplayNamesByEmail: [:]` on purpose (2b4f5bc9, "Fix participant header cache invalidation"). Deleting a message bumps no address generation (CacheCoordinator.swift:287 only evicts body caches). If that check is loosened to nil, a deleted or re-headed From name would show stale for up to the 300 s TTL.
- The photo-memory rule is deliberate (9d822c79; ParticipantRollupCache.swift:323; pinned by testLoadParticipants_doesNotRetainRawPhotoPayloadsInRollupCache, which expects photoCounter == 2). Putting Data in the 600-entry rollup would keep avatar bytes alive after ProfilePhotoResolver evicts them, after a memory warning, and after sign-out, because the rollup is invalidated only lazily, by fingerprint, via PersonCache.clearCache. Any decoded-image cache would be account data and must be cleared in ProfilePhotoResolver.closeAccountWorkAndClear.
- Per-persist invalidateEntry (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:208-211) is the only signal that a new From name has arrived. The review's correction to self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist keeps it for the self Person too. Bounding the DISTINCT scan to the newest N messages changes which name wins (testLoadParticipants_olderFullerVariantStillUpgradesShortLatestName). Persisting the name at ingest needs ESCChatmail 7 and must be staged into the orchestrator's context.

**Fix.** Three steps. (1) Build the known-open fix. For permanent IDs, fetchConversationParticipantSnapshot reads on a private-queue context built on the passed context's coordinator: merge policy set, a value snapshot returned, one load in flight per objectID. Temporary IDs keep using the passed context. Do the same for resolveSenders. Keep the `[:]` header revalidation: it catches From names that were deleted or changed (2b4f5bc9), and it is cheap once off main. (2) Let photo rollups hit without holding bytes: cache which email fills each photo slot, refill the photos from a nonisolated peek of ProfilePhotoResolver's NSCache, and treat a slot that is gone as a miss. (3) Keep the per-persist invalidation. Leave bounding the scan, or persisting names at ingest, to ESCChatmail 7.

**First step.** Add a snapshot-context factory to ParticipantLoader.init. By default it makes a private-queue context on the passed context's persistentStoreCoordinator, with NSMergeByPropertyObjectTrumpMergePolicy. Route fetchConversationParticipantSnapshot through it whenever the objectID is not temporary.

**Pinning test.** ParticipantLoaderTests with a counting factory: a saved conversation's snapshot runs on the factory context, off main, with identical names (contested case); a temporary-ID one uses the passed context; a photo rollup's second load calls photoLoader once. Revert-check comments.

**Payoff.** Takes the unbounded DISTINCT sender scan off main for every row appearance and chat open (est. 5-40 ms warm per large S2/S3 chat); photo rows stop reloading on scroll-in.

### `conversation-list-ui#2` · medium · performance · effort M · known-open

**Search and the Contacts/Other filters are synchronous main-thread scans of every active conversation, restarted from offset 0 on each debounced keystroke**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Real, with scope narrowed. Search ANDs CONTAINS[cd] on displayName and snippet onto archivedAt == nil; SQLite evaluates it over every unarchived row, synchronously on the view context after each 150 ms debounce. Snippet is uncapped (cleanedSnippet, Int.max) except for newsletters and forwards, which store the subject. Under search only about `limit` rows are materialized. Contacts/Other test membership in Swift over 500-row OFFSET batches from offset 0; that reaches the whole active set only when matches are sparse, and paging repeats it with a larger batch.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationWindowProvider.swift:141-160 — "(displayName CONTAINS[cd] %@) OR (snippet CONTAINS[cd] %@)" ANDed onto archivedAt == nil; :40-41 fetchBatchSize = min(pageSize, limit) with participants and participants.person prefetched; :93-118 loop starts at fetchOffset 0, candidateBatchSize = max(limit x 5, limit, pageSize), and stops once `limit` rows pass the Swift check.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:521-538 — debounced-search and filter-state callbacks reset the limit and reload; :574-597 fetchWindow is called synchronously on the @MainActor view model (esc-chatmail/Views/Main/View+ConversationListLifecycle.swift:23 passes viewContext); :588 a short window latches hasLoadedAllConversationWindow, which :600-605 uses to skip backfill rescans; :562-563 paging grows the limit and reloads from scratch.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationFilter.swift:42-49 — search and .contacts/.other need the in-memory candidate scan; :54-61 .contacts with an empty contact cache is skipped; :67-74 only .unread has a store predicate.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationFilterService.swift:22-27 — contactEmailsCache didSet calls onFilterStateChange under any filter; :98-109 membership is normalize + Set.contains per participant; :140-152 search re-check is Foundation range(of:) over displayName and snippet.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/MessageProcessor.swift:883-922 — cleanedSnippet is built with maxLength: Int.max; esc-chatmail/Services/Models/Message+Extensions.swift:100-113 — forwards and newsletters preview the subject, everything else prefers cleanedSnippet; esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:110-113 and esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:618-625,712-714 write Conversation.snippet with only a trim.
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleQueryPlanTests.swift:424-429 — on the S2 store the window query finds unarchived rows through an index and sorts all of them in a temp B-tree per window; docs/scalability-review.md:819-867 — both items sit under "Will degrade" with timings marked as estimates, and :1530-1628 does not list either as built.

**Trigger.** Each debounced search keystroke (150 ms) under any filter; switching to Contacts (or Other) when fewer than about 100 matches sit near the top of the list; each page under such a sparse filter; a contact-cache change while it is selected. Felt only at S2-scale active conversations (8-12k) and up.

**Impact.** The main thread stalls while typing in search, or when switching to or paging a sparse Contacts filter. The prior review estimates 150-500 ms per keystroke and 0.3-0.6 s per sparse scan at S2, over a second at S3. None of this was measured, and the cost is lower for newsletter-heavy mailboxes. No data is lost and the list recovers when the fetch returns. S1 is unaffected.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited location; code matches. Bounds the auditor missed: fetchBatchSize 50 limits materialization under search; the loop stops at `limit` matches; `.contacts` with an empty cache is skipped; a short window latches hasLoadedAllConversationWindow, so live changes do not rescan. Not a documented decision and not built. Severity lowered to medium: the prior review files both under "Will degrade", and timings are unmeasured and mix-dependent. Snippet evidence should cite MessageProcessor.swift:889, not compactListText.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:819 `contacts-other-filter-main-scan` and :843 `list-search-contains-uncapped-snippet` (Review correction :855), under "Will degrade / Main-thread UI hot paths". The built list for step 5 (:1541-1561) names neither, and step 11, keyset list paging (:1624), is not built.

**Invariant risks**

- Pending/persisted merge (review :806): a background context cannot see the view context's unsaved conversations (optimistic sends) or resolve their temporary IDs. Merge pending rows on the main thread, and set hasLoadedAllConversationWindow (ConversationListViewModel.swift:588) from the scan's reached-end flag, not from window.count < limit. Otherwise a re-checked short window latches and backfill stops.
- An exact SQL `participants.person.email IN` does not match `EmailNormalizer.normalize` (lowercasing, Gmail dot and plus stripping, googlemail). mergeDuplicatePersons re-normalizes only duplicate groups (DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:432-448), so a legacy singleton row drops out of .contacts, and the Swift backstop cannot restore a row SQL never returned. Rewriting Person.email in place risks the canonical participant hashing.
- Snippet cap: one helper for Conversation.snippet only, used by every writer and by the guarded `!=` comparisons (ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:110-112, MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:712-714, GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:1909). Otherwise every rollup re-dirties the row. Never put it in MessagePreviewText.nonEmpty and never cap Message.cleanedSnippet. A heal pass outside the serializer turns overwrites a newer sync or send snippet under the object-trump merge policy.
- Managed objects never cross contexts, and CI's Swift 6.2 rejects non-Sendable captures in perform: ConversationFilterService.matches is @MainActor and cannot run in a background perform. Results need a query generation that also changes on NSInvalidatedAllObjectsKey (the store is destroyed at sign-out). A scan error must keep the current window: fetchWindow returns [] on error today, and the view model then latches all-loaded.

**Fix.** Ship it as three PRs. (1) No product change. Keep the exact .all/.unread fetch synchronous. Move only the needsInMemoryCandidateScan paths to one reused private-queue context (storage.makeBackgroundContext). That context applies a pure, Sendable ConversationVisibilityRule, shared with ConversationFilterService, and returns ordered persisted objectIDs plus a reachedEnd flag. On the main thread: drop stale generations, materialize those IDs with `self IN %@` plus prefetch, re-check them, merge the view context's pending rows, replay changes that arrived while the scan ran, and latch from reachedEnd. (2) .contacts/.other: resolve contact Person objectIDs in the background through Swift normalization, then filter with `ANY participants.person IN %@` / SUBQUERY count==0. (3) The snippet cap needs Kevin's decision; heal existing rows inside serializer turns. Leave keyset paging to step 11.

**First step.** Extract ConversationFilterService.matches into a pure, nonisolated ConversationVisibilityRule (search text, filter, normalized contact set), with no behavior change. Have both the main-thread check and fetchFilteredWindow call it. Existing ConversationWindowProviderTests and ConversationFilterServiceTests should stay green.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests with a fetch-counting view context: a search, or a switch to .contacts, runs no CONTAINS or offset fetch there. A superseded query's late result is dropped. The window matches the old synchronous one, pending rows included. Each test carries a Revert-check comment.

**Payoff.** At S2/S3, search keystrokes and Contacts/Other switches and pages stop blocking the main thread (the review estimates 0.15-1.5 s per event). The previous rows stay on screen until the new result lands.

### `conversation-list-ui#3` · medium · scalability · effort M · known-open

**The list window only grows, and every page, pop-back and removal re-reads and re-snapshots all of it from offset 0 on the main thread**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Confirmed from code. loadMoreIfNeeded adds 50 to an uncapped loadedConversationLimit and refetches the whole window on the main-queue view context: about limit/50 batch fetches, each prefetching participants and persons, then one snapshot per row that walks participants and normalizes emails. The same full reload runs unconditionally in onAppear (each iOS pop-back) and as the backfill after any removal while more rows exist. The limit drops back to 100 only on a search, filter or contact-email-cache change. Non-removal live updates stay incremental.

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:574-597 — the reload calls fetchWindow(limit: loadedConversationLimit) on the view context, listStore.replaceAll, publish, plus Set/filter passes over the window; 480-482 onAppear reloads unconditionally; 599-609 the backfill is that same full reload when visible count < limit and not all loaded.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationWindowProvider.swift:34-42,59-61 — three sort descriptors, fetchBatchSize min(pageSize, limit) = 50, prefetch of participants and participants.person, fetchLimit = limit, and the whole result iterated through the visibility filter.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationListStore.swift:25-34 — replaceAll builds a ConversationListItem for every row (10-11, 111, 122, 133: the linear scans and their 'few hundred rows' comment); esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationSnapshot.swift:57-79 — each snapshot walks participants, normalizes each email and sorts two sets.

- docs/scalability-review.md:796-817 — the same item (conversation-list-window-full-refetch) with the 15-25 ms / 150 ms estimates; 1624 — step 11 'Page the conversation list by keyset' carries no Built note; 1640 — 'window SQL takes about 1-2 ms at 30k conversations'. esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleQueryPlanTests.swift:424-429 — the temp B-tree sort is recorded and not asserted.

**Trigger.** A mailbox with more unarchived conversations than the loaded window (S2/S3; at S1 the window tops out near 1.5k rows) and a user who has scrolled several hundred to a few thousand rows down. Then each further page, each archive, spam report or mark-read under the Unread filter, and on iOS each pop-back from a chat. The deep window lasts until a search, filter or contact-email change, sign-out or process death, so a Mac session can hold it for days.

**Impact.** A main-thread stall per page, removal and iOS pop-back that grows linearly with the loaded window: about limit/50 × 3 SQL statements plus one snapshot build per row. The prior review's unmeasured estimates are 15-25 ms at 300 rows and about 150 ms at 3,000, so hitches while scrolling deep and near-hang reloads at a few thousand rows. At the default 100-row window it is a few milliseconds. The store's linear scans and the publish passes are O(window) but negligible next to the refetch.

**Verifier.** All cited code is as described; nothing caps or trims the window, and step 11 is unbuilt. Three small corrections. A contact-email cache change also resets the limit, under any filter. The Mac sidebar gets the same resets and simply lives longer. The temp B-tree sort is not the cost driver (the prior review puts window SQL at 1-2 ms at 30k), so the proposed index is secondary to keyset paging. Timings are unmeasured estimates.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md conversation-list-window-full-refetch (lines 794-817); Suggested order step 11 "Page the conversation list by keyset" (line 1624), which has no Built note. The code still does the full reload.

**Invariant risks**

- Prefix gap: upsertConversation puts a row that now sorts past the tail at the window's end (ConversationListStore.swift:122-125), with no trim at count == limit. An unpin or a lowered lastMessageDate then leaves a gap that today's full reload heals and a naive keyset append skips for good.
- The pending-change merge: unsaved optimistic rows exist only on the view context (testOptimisticUnsavedConversation_survivesReAppear). So the keyset fetch must stay there with includesPendingChanges on, and its predicate must give the same answer in memory and in SQLite: a NULL lastMessageDate sorts last, and the UUID tie-break must agree. Build it from SortKey, never a copy.
- The onAppear reload is today's only heal. Invalidate-all empties the store without a refetch (+ChangeObservation.swift:68-74), and the batch delete of empty conversations merges only into registered objects (DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:61-69), which leaves ghost rows. PerformanceRegressionTests also measures the fetch through repeated onAppear.
- A window cap trims rows out of the selection, because publishVisibleItems keeps the selection inside the visible rows. It also withdraws an open spam question and can drop the Mac's open-chat row. An index belongs in the one batched ESCChatmail 7 version (step 10), with a versionHashModifier.

**Fix.** Keep fetching on the view context.
1. Give ConversationListStore a boundary SortKey, the last row fetched from the store. While more rows may exist, upsert drops a row that sorts past the boundary instead of appending it. Trim moves the boundary.
2. Add a page fetch after the boundary for .all and .unread without search. Build its predicate beside SortKey: a nil-date disjunct and the UUID tie-break, with includesPendingChanges on. Filtered and search paths keep the full reload.
3. loadMoreIfNeeded fetches only the next page and backfill only the missing rows, and both append them.
4. onAppear reloads only when a windowIsCurrent flag is false: a new context, or after invalidate-all.
Defer the cap and the index to step 10.

**First step.** Add the boundary to ConversationListStore. Change upsertConversation to drop a row that sorts past it while the window is incomplete. Add a store test that unpinning past the tail still leaves a store-order prefix. Ship this before any keyset fetch.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests on .sqlite: an old pinned row and a full, incomplete window. Unpin it and page repeatedly. Assert the window equals a fresh full fetch's prefix and each page builds exactly pageSize snapshots (spy). Revert-check: upsert's boundary drop.

**Payoff.** A deep page, a backfill after a removal or an iOS pop-back costs one 50-row fetch instead of re-reading and re-snapshotting the whole window (the review estimates about 150 ms at 3,000 rows).

### `conversation-list-ui#4` · medium · reliability · effort S · known-open

**A Person change faults every conversation that person ever joined on the main thread, through the one ingestion path with no guard against the tombstoned-fault crash**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

Any Person in a merged update or refresh makes the change relevant. The handler collects every conversation of each such Person through conversationParticipations (no window, archived or prefetch limit) before applying anything; the store then reads archivedAt on each object singly, on the main thread, and builds a list item for each unarchived row that passes the filter. That initializer is non-failable and reads the non-optional Conversation.id. Nothing on this path checks isDeleted or materializes at fetch time, as the sibling-save path does against the crash it documents.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:116-127 — a Person under NSUpdatedObjectsKey or NSRefreshedObjectsKey returns true from isRelevantConversationListChange.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:88-94,235-244 — personAffected is built whole (flatMap over person.conversationParticipations, compactMap to .conversation, no restriction) before applyConversationChanges is called at line 94; no throttle or coalescing in between.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationListStore.swift:55-66,96-107 — per conversation: isSourceConversation (ConversationListViewModel.swift:619-621, archivedAt == nil), archived rows removed and skipped; the rest go to matchesVisibility, then ConversationListItem(conversation:). No isDeleted check.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationListItem.swift:14-17 — non-failable init sets stableID = conversation.id; esc-chatmail/Services/Models/Conversation+Extensions.swift:9 declares `@NSManaged public var id: UUID`. ConversationFilterService.swift:140-165: an object with nil values passes only filter .all or .other with empty search text.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:186-191 — sibling-save comment: a delete landing before a returned fault fires tombstones the row and the snapshot build crashes on its nil id; returnsObjectsAsFaults = false only there. esc-chatmailTests/Caching/CacheCoordinatorDeletedRowCaptureTests.swift:65-73 pins that a fault for a committed-deleted row reads nil values with no exception.
- docs/scalability-review.md:897-905,1561 — the fan-out is prior item person-change-conversation-fanout (k of 300-500 at S2, 50-300 ms estimated), listed under step 5 as "Not built yet"; the item says nothing of a crash.

**Trigger.** A background Person save merged into the view context (contact name or avatar from ContactsResolver.updatePerson, a better header name during sync, a person merge) for someone in hundreds of conversations at S2/S3. The crash also needs a background conversation delete (a ConversationMerger loser, a cleanup pass) to commit between that conversation's participant fault firing in the walk and its archivedAt read in the store loop, with the filter on All or Other and no search text.

**Impact.** A main-thread run of about 2k+1 single-row fault firings for a Person in k conversations, plus participant and person faults for each unarchived row: the prior review's estimate of 50-300 ms at k of 300-500, not re-measured, repeated for each Person saved after a Contacts grant. Negligible for a typical contact (k of 1-3). Separately, a rare trap on the nil UUID in the list's change handler; the race was not reproduced.

**Verifier.** Could not refute. All cited lines read as described; no guard, cap or coalescing found on the path. The fan-out is the prior review's open item (docs:1561, 'Not built yet'); only the crash exposure is new, and it is an unreproduced, narrow race. Tightened: archived rows stop at the archivedAt read; a tombstone is dropped before `id` under Unread/Contacts or a search; inserted/updated/refreshed Conversations are equally unguarded, so 'the one path' overstates.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:895-917 `person-change-conversation-fanout` (step 5 "Not built yet", :1561); the code walk at ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:235-244 is unchanged. The tombstone-crash half is new: the item never mentions it.

**Invariant risks**

- Window rows can be unsaved inserts. An optimistic conversation is a pending insert, and ChatViewModel.swift:316-317 gives one a permanent ID before any save. So `self IN window` in SQL, or a background-context fetch (step 5 says "move off main"; the correction at scalability-review.md:881 covers temp IDs), silently misses or cannot resolve them. Match pending rows in memory, as ConversationWindowProvider.fetchFilteredWindow:74-91 does.
- Managed objects never cross contexts, and the objectsDidChange pipeline owns live updates. The fetch must run synchronously on the observed context inside handleConversationContextChange, where the backfill path already fetches (ConversationListViewModel.swift:412,607,580). No FRC. publishVisibleItems stays the single funnel, and SortKey stays the canonical order.
- Copy the sibling-save fetch exactly: returnsObjectsAsFaults=false and shouldRefreshRefetchedObjects left at its default (ChangeObservation.swift:186-194). Forcing a refresh fights the automerge. A window-only fetch is correct only because Person writers change displayName/avatarURL and never email, sort key or filter membership (ContactPersistenceService.swift:42-50; the merge only re-normalizes email, DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:444-448). Keep it that way.
- In the failable init, read the ID through KVC (`value(forKey:"id") as? UUID`) before ConversationSnapshot(from:), and have upsert remove the row on nil, not just skip it, or a stale row stays. Never make Conversation.id optional: that is a model change needing ESCChatmail 7. A revert-check of the tombstone test traps the test host, so announce that crash run.

**Fix.** Rewrite conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges on the observed context, inside the handler. Inserted Persons keep the in-memory walk. Window rows (listStore.visibleItems) that are pending Conversations (insertedObjects/updatedObjects) are matched in memory, as fetchFilteredWindow does. The rest take one fetch: self IN persistedWindowIDs AND ANY participants.person IN persistedPersonIDs, with includesPendingChanges false, returnsObjectsAsFaults false, participants and participants.person prefetched, and refresh left at default. A window-only fetch is safe because Person writers change displayName/avatarURL, never SortKey or filter membership. Then make ConversationListItem.init failable: return nil when the row isDeleted or value(forKey:"id") as? UUID is nil, checked before the snapshot. replaceAll skips such rows, upsert removes them, and the two test callers are updated.

**First step.** Add the SQLite-mode regression test in ConversationListViewModelTests first: a strongly held Person in 200 conversations (190 archived, a small window). Change its displayName, then assert the window rows re-snapshot and person.hasFault(forRelationshipNamed: "conversationParticipations") stays true.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests (.sqlite, main-queue context): a Person in 200 conversations, window of 5. After a rename only the window rows' fingerprints change, conversationParticipations stays a fault and archived rows stay unfired (retainsRegisteredObjects). Plus: a tombstone yields a nil item and no row.

**Payoff.** A Person change costs three bounded SQL statements over the window instead of 2k+1 main-thread faults (k 300-500 at S2), and no ingestion path can trap on a tombstoned row.

### `gap-change-propagation-pipeline#3` · medium · performance · effort S · known-partial

**The transcript classifies every merged message in the process by firing faults on main**

Area: From one store save to every observer: merge, cache invalidation and UI. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The view context auto-merges every save. The transcript's gate checks types only, so any merged Message or Attachment in any conversation passes it. On its first membership check, belongsToCurrentConversation fires the fault of each merged message. For another conversation's message it then reads the UUID through KVC, which fires that Conversation's fault, even when both objectIDs are permanent. The method's own comment says it faults at most the message row. refreshedCachedMessageIDs also fires the fault of every changed Attachment. The repeated passes after that are in-memory only, and the boundary-cache scan covers about two rows, so both are negligible.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:182 — viewContext.automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent = true, so every sibling save reaches this observer
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:404-430 — the relevance gate checks object types only and never the conversation
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:454-475 — the comment says 'faults at most the message row', but a non-matching conversation falls through to value(forKey: "id") and fires the foreign Conversation's fault
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:38-43,90 with 535-544,574-591 — three unconditional passes over the inserted set (83/98/111 run only when the open chat itself gained a visible row); 210-221 read attachment.message for every changed Attachment
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+RowCache.swift:7-9,128-130 — the boundary memo is cleared on every window and holds only grouping-lookahead rows, which rowForGrouping also writes to resolvedRowsByID, so the ?? scan at :273-276/:382-385 is about two entries and only on a miss
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:53-58 — saves come per 50-message batch, or the whole slice lands in one final save when intermediate saves are off (scalability-review.md:488-490: 1k-3k messages)

**Trigger.** Needs a chat open on iOS, or a selected sidebar row on the Mac, where a selected chat stays mounted. A merged save must also insert many Messages or Attachments in other conversations: 50-message batch saves, 500-ID initial-sync or re-list page saves, or a catch-up slice with intermediate saves off that lands 1k-3k messages in one save. An ordinary incremental sync with a few new messages costs microseconds.

**Impact.** Cost on main is about one message fault, plus one Conversation fault per distinct foreign conversation, plus one fault per attachment, for each merged message. It is an upper bound of about two single-row reads per message (a row-cache hit is cheaper). That is roughly tens of ms for a 50-message batch and an estimated 100-300 ms on an iPhone for a 500-message save, more for a catch-up slice. It is not measured, and it adds to the merge hitch that no-intermediate-saves-destructive-slice already names.

**Verifier.** Confirmed the gate, the membership check, the attachment walk and the reader observer (FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:230-251, only while the reader is open). Corrected three points. Only the first membership call faults an object, so extra passes are in-memory. The boundary-cache scan is negligible. The cost scales with save batch size, not every save or store size. Not covered as sound or refuted in docs/scalability-review.md. Fix: skip the UUID fallback when both IDs are permanent, or run one SELF IN fetch.

**October review.** Not in docs/scalability-review.md (nearest: chat-reconcile-main-count-offset, which covers only the open chat's own inserts). Prior work: docs/archive/performance-reliability-plan.md:41,86 item U8, built in #94 (8d83cefb, 2026-07-03) as a type-only gate plus an objectID-only membership check. 0f351246 (2026-07-25) added the UUID fallback back, and that fallback fires the foreign Conversation's fault. The per-message Message faults were never removed.

**Invariant risks**

- Temporary IDs: an optimistic conversation's objectID is temporary, is never cached and changes when the conversation is saved. Deciding membership by objectID alone, or with a SQL `SELF IN` / `conversation ==` check, would miss that chat's rows. Keep the crash-guarded KVC UUID fallback whenever either ID is temporary or nil, as CLAUDE.md's objectID rule and transcriptPredicate (RowCache.swift:327-355) do.
- Deletions: a fetch never returns deleted rows, and Core Data may clear the inverse relationship before it posts the notification (ChangeObservation.swift:477-491). Objects under the deleted key must keep the committedValues path. Without it, deletions in the open chat stop triggering reconciliation and totalMessageCount drifts.
- Same-turn classification: the local-send tail append publishes in the notification's own turn, measured against the count from before the change (ChangeObservation.swift:91-103, TailAppend.swift:11-18). An async or background membership fetch would break that, and Message objects must not cross contexts.
- No new main-thread SQL on every merge: an unconditional fetch turns the common one-message merge from a row-cache fault into a SQL round trip. Also, an inserted attachment of a window message can arrive while its message is not registered in the view context, so attachment membership cannot simply be skipped.

**Fix.** First, with no new SQL: resolve the conversation's objectID and UUID once per notification and decide each Message once into a member set every pass reads. When both the open conversation's ID and the relationship's destination ID are permanent, decide by objectID alone, as transcriptPredicate does; keep the KVC UUID fallback only for temporary or nil IDs, and committedValues only for objects under the deleted and updated keys. Then, only if the scale harness shows the remaining message and attachment faults matter, add a thresholded, chunked objectID-result fetch (includesPendingChanges false) for faulted permanent-ID inserts and refreshes, leaving deletions and temporary IDs on the in-memory path.

**First step.** In VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift, write the pinning test first. Then change belongsToCurrentConversation to take the conversation objectID and UUID, resolved once per notification. When both IDs are permanent, it returns the objectID comparison alone.

**Pinning test.** VirtualScrollStateTests: SQLite stack, main-queue context with automerge and retainsRegisteredObjects, chat A open. Save 50 messages into conversation B from a background context. Assert B is unregistered or still a fault. Revert-check: the permanent-ID short-circuit.

**Payoff.** Removes one foreign Conversation fault per distinct conversation on large merges while a chat is open (nearly always on the Mac). Not measured. The mergeChanges call itself and the conversation-list observer are untouched.

### `web-content-rendering#2` · medium · performance · effort M · new

**Every rich row that rests on screen pre-renders its whole original email in a new WKWebView**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: confirmed (medium confidence).

Every HTML-preview row runs a warm task. 200 ms after mount (no scroll-idle check), if local HTML exists, the main-actor manager builds a screen-sized WKWebView, hosts it in an unhidden off-screen UIWindow and loads the original HTML; remote images and tracking pixels are not stripped on this path. Four stay pooled until LRU, memory warning or sign-out. Checkout needs the exact rounded width, but iOS warms at screen width, so a narrower iPad sheet should never match, and any miss pre-paints another off-screen copy.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailContentSection.swift:110-112, 131-143 — .task(id: warmFullEmailKey) on every section; 200 ms sleep from mount, then fullEmailOpener.warm with currentVisibleRowWarmWidthEstimate(). esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageContentView.swift:41-61 mounts the section for every showHTMLPreview row
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:960, 1152-1194, 1686-1724 — @MainActor manager; with adoption on (420-440: default on, launch-argument kill switch only) and width > 1 it creates an Entry: LayoutAwareWKWebView at width x host.preferredHeight(), host.host(...), loadHTMLString(html, baseURL:)
- esc-chatmail/Platform/OffscreenWebViewHost.swift:37-63 — one UIWindow in the active scene, frame x = -screenWidth - 100, isHidden = false, kept for the process; comment says it is placed so the render server composites it and WebKit paints
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1034, 1048-1063, 1509-1521 — capacity 4; observers are memory pressure (clear()) and the remote-image-fallback notification only; clear() has no other caller, and the app has no isLowPowerModeEnabled / thermalState use (git grep)
- esc-chatmail/Platform/FullEmailReaderWarmWidthSource.swift:8-16 and FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:270, 1455 — iOS warm width is screen.bounds.width ('the width of the reader sheet on an iPhone'); checkout requires entry.key == key with widthBucket = Int(width.rounded()); project.pbxproj:282 TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2"; View+AppSheet.swift:40 plain sheet(item:)
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentLoader+SourcePreparation.swift:89-102 — original/preferHTML path skips tracking removal, 'Remote http(s) images load directly via WebKit' (HTMLDisplayWrapper.swift:125 CSP has no img-src). FullEmailOpenSession.swift:430-463 with FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1197-1199, 1255-1298 — a miss tears down the mismatched entry and renders another off-screen copy, documented as helping only later opens

**Trigger.** Opening or scrolling any chat whose rows route to the HTML preview (newsletters, receipts, list conversations) and have local HTML: each such row that stays mounted 200 ms warms a web view, including during a slow scroll. On iPad the reader sheet is narrower than the screen, so the warmed width should never match; iPhone landscape probably misses too (not confirmed).

**Impact.** WKWebView creation on the main actor and a full HTML plus remote-image load per mounted rich row, with churn past the fourth; up to four pooled web views held through chat exit and backgrounding. Cellular data and tracking-pixel fetches for mail the user never opened (the preview path strips known trackers, this path does not). On iPad the warm work cannot be adopted and each open renders the email twice. No cost was measured; the process count is inferred.

**Verifier.** Read the warm path, host window, key, checkout, session width hook and original-HTML preparation. Guards found: 200 ms debounce, cancellation check before entry creation, exact-key de-dupe, LRU of 4, memory-pressure clear, local HTML only. Pre-rendering is deliberate (manager header, AGENTS.md) but absent from CLAUDE.md and the scalability review; the Mac plan fixed the same screen-width mismatch for the Mac only. Tightened: the debounce runs from mount, not scroll rest. The iPad miss is inferred from sheet sizing, not run.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:302 (Mac warms at the reader's own width; iOS kept the screen width, pinned by FullEmailReaderWarmWidthSourceTests). Not in docs/scalability-review.md.

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: FullEmailWebViewManager is a participant. Any new slot, debounce or release task must run inside warm()'s activeWarmOperations or prewarmTasks so clearForAccountTransition cancels and drains it (reopenAccountWork refuses while warms are outstanding). A release may tear down only entries that are not checked out, through teardown(); a checked-out entry goes only through scrubForAccountTransition.
- Warm and reader HTML must stay byte-identical (FullInteractiveEmailWebView, and htmlFingerprint in FullEmailWebViewPreRenderKey). Stripping trackers or blocking remote images only on the warm path makes every checkout a key_mismatch. The only way to stop tracking loads is to not pre-render unopened mail.
- A release that keeps prepared payloads must also drop the remembered warm widths (FullEmailRemoteImageFallbackBookkeeping). Otherwise handleRemoteImageFallbackDidWarm re-warms at the stored width and rebuilds an off-screen WebView after the release, even while the app is in the background.
- Tests: inject a background event source as MemoryPressureEventSource does, and never post UIApplication notifications to the default center, which clears shared caches in the host. Wrap UIKit tests in #if os(iOS). The iOS case of FullEmailReaderWarmWidthSourceTests pins the screen width and must change in the same change. On the Mac, keep the no-presentationSizing rule for the reader sheet.

**Fix.** In order: (1) iOS warm width = the reader's recorded width when measured at the current window width; with none, the window width only in a compact size class, else nil (iPad then warms HTML only, as the Mac does). (2) Add releaseIdleWebViews(): tear down non-checked-out entries, keep payloads, drop remembered widths; call it from an injected iOS background source and ChatView.onDisappear. (3) Pure FullEmailVisibleRowWebViewPolicy: one visible-row WebView slot (a new one replaces the last; explicit-open keeps LRU 4), none in Low Power Mode, thermal ≥ serious or inactive scene. No touch-down gesture. (4) Skip the explicit-open prepaint while a non-adopted live reader shows that artifact.

**First step.** Add a pure FullEmailReaderWarmWidthPolicy taking the window width, the horizontal size class and the recorded (windowWidth, readerWidth). Use it in FullEmailReaderWarmWidthSource.currentWidth on iOS, record the window width in prepareForMeasuredReaderWidth, and rewrite the iOS case of FullEmailReaderWarmWidthSourceTests.

**Pinning test.** FullEmailWebViewManagerTests: warming two messages as visible rows at 390 gives only the second a WebView entry, and both keep payloads. After releaseIdleWebViews, a UUID-named remote-image-fallback post rebuilds no entry. Revert-check names the slot and the width forgetting.

**Payoff.** Ends per-row WKWebView builds and tracker loads for unopened mail and frees pooled web views in the background. After the first open, iPad opens adopt instead of rendering each email twice.

### `web-content-rendering#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Preview snapshots are captured on timers with no completeness signal and cached for seven days**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

Capture is gated on WKWebView didFinish plus a fixed 1 s settle. Nothing checks that images succeeded, every successful render is stored, and nothing ever removes a stored snapshot. The key has no load-outcome or inline-attachment term, so an HTML-route card first rendered with fast-failing images is served for 7 days from creation. Each cold render builds a new WKWebView, two at a time, at least 1 s each. The card mounts at 180 pt and gets its real height (180-320) only after an async cache read.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:529-579, 622-627 — didFinish starts finishAfterLoadSettles: 250 ms and 750 ms sleeps, two height measurements, measured height floored at 180 then clamped, takeSnapshot; no check of any image's outcome
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:101, 442-457, 490-498 — maxConcurrentRenders 2; a new WKWebViewConfiguration and LayoutAwareWKWebView per session; a 5 s timeout fails the render
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotCache.swift:21-35, 117-121, 176-178 — key = preview key, HTML hash, width, dark, renderer version; age checked against createdAt (7 days); remove(for:) exists but git grep finds no caller outside the cache
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailPreviewSnapshotView.swift:129, 225-230, 271-273, 328-334, 403-404 — displayHeight starts at 180, is reset per request and set only after the awaited cache.load; every successful render is stored; a failed render sets didFail (MiniEmailWebView fallback) and stores nothing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/CIDSchemeHandler.swift:117-122, 144-155 and esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:118 — the handler awaits the on-demand fetch before answering; the transparent pixel is sent only for no matching row or a nil fetch; the read session has waitsForConnectivity = true
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailContentSection.swift:273-281, 333-347 and esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/FullEmailReaderView.swift:112-113, 199-208 — the snapshot view is used only for the .html payload; the reader shows the cached image only while !webViewPainted

**Trigger.** First render of an HTML-route preview card (one for which no native card was built) while offline or while image requests fail fast. The cache is cold on first view, 7 days after creation, after a dark-mode flip or a width change. Not "a cid image still downloading": the cid handler awaits the fetch, and one slower than 5 s times the render out, which stores nothing.

**Impact.** Affected cards show missing images for up to a week, across relaunches; tapping still opens the live reader, where the snapshot is only a placeholder until paint. Cold HTML cards fill at no more than two per second. A card taller than 180 pt grows after mount even on a warm cache. Newsletter, transactional, invite, reservation and deploy cards are unaffected.

**Verifier.** Code as cited. No guard found: no success check, no invalidation, no synchronous height source (only the MiniEmailWebView fallback has one, MiniEmailWebView.swift:40-42, 93-96). Not in docs/scalability-review.md beyond the 50 MB bound (line 1645). Corrected: didFinish, not the timers, gates capture; the cid-downloading trigger is wrong; scope is .html cards only; heights change only between 180 and 320. Unverified: that WebKit sends didFinish promptly when remote images fail offline. Nothing was run.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1645 — "Bounded disk caches" (Already sound) covers only the snapshot cache's 50 MB size bound; no item covers whether a capture is complete

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: the snapshot cache (closeAccountWorkAndClear, EmailPreviewSnapshotCache.swift:196-219) and the render scheduler (closeAccountWorkAndAwait, EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:308-344) are both participants. Any new in-memory tier, any pooled WKWebView (which holds its CIDSchemeHandler's message and the old account's WebContent memory) and any synchronous height memo must be cleared and drained there. The scheduler's reopen refuses while old work is outstanding, so a leaked render keeps previews closed until relaunch.
- Turning an incomplete capture, or a longer wait for images, into a render error sets didFail (EmailPreviewSnapshotView.swift:403). That swaps the card for MiniEmailWebView: a live, scaled WKWebView in the scrolling transcript, one WebContent process per card (AGENTS.md:139; docs/mac-app-plan.md:333). An incomplete render has to succeed and be shown. It must just not be persisted.
- The auditor's 'add inline-attachment availability to the key' would read message.attachments on the main-thread view context at mount, once per row (EmailContentSection.swift:357-368). It would also change loadTaskIdentity every time an attachment's state flips, which restarts .task and the render. The outcome has to come from CIDSchemeHandler instead, where a failed fetch is answered with a 1x1 pixel (lines 151-155) that document.images reports as loaded.
- If every broken image makes a render uncacheable, an email whose images are permanently dead (404 trackers) is re-rendered on every mount for good. The check has to skip invisible and tiny images and those outside the capture area, and keep incomplete renders for a bounded time. Heights must stay predictable too (AGENTS.md:139, EmailContentCard.swift:28-34): nothing may make a row's height depend on how its load turned out.

**Fix.** Leave the settle sleeps and the 5 s timeout alone: didFinish already waits for non-lazy images. Add a verdict instead of a wait. (1) CIDSchemeHandler counts, under a lock, the pixels it sends for a nil fetch or an unreadable local file. "No matching row" still counts as complete. (2) After the second height measurement the session runs a probe: images in the capture area, larger than 2×2, that are broken or not complete. A probe error counts as incomplete. The result gains isComplete. (3) An incomplete result is shown and never treated as a failure. store writes to disk only for complete results; incomplete ones go to a small in-actor memory tier (about 10 minutes) that closeAccountWorkAndClear clears. Pooling web views and a synchronous height memo are later, separately measured steps.

**First step.** Add isComplete to EmailPreviewSnapshotResult and an image-outcome probe next to HTMLPreviewSnapshotHeightMeasurementScript. Evaluate it after secondHeight in finishAfterLoadSettles. Pin it with real-renderer tests before changing EmailPreviewSnapshotCache.store.

**Pinning test.** EmailPreviewSnapshotCacheTests (iOS-only), two parts. Real renderer: a broken data: image gives isComplete false; a valid image or no images gives true. Stub incomplete result: shown, didFail false, and a fresh cache on that directory loads nil. Revert-check: the gate in store.

**Payoff.** HTML cards first rendered offline or with failed images heal on the next view instead of showing gaps for up to seven days. Render timing, heights and the MiniEmailWebView fallback stay as they are.

### `web-content-rendering#4` · medium · performance · effort M · new

**Body-size work and the process-wide HTML lock run on the main actor at row mount, at tap and per render**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Several main-actor paths do work that grows with body size, and nothing caps the body. Every bubble's body takes the process-wide HTML lock and stats the file on a signature-cache miss; a rich row does it two more times and SHA-256s bodyText each time its body is evaluated. warm() hashes and CID-scans the wrapped HTML on main for each visible rich row. Opening a warmed message runs preparedOpenArtifact synchronously: a body read on an NSCache miss, a trim, lowercase and scan, SHA-256 of the canonical body and of the wrapped HTML, and two bodyText normalizations. checkout repeats the hash and the scan. Snapshot scale detection and cid: file reads also run on main.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageBubble.swift:199, 635-643 — every bubble body evaluates loadSignature through htmlContentHandler.htmlSourceSignature (lock + stat on miss); EmailContentSection.swift:47-67, 74-81, 103, 110 add two more calls and SHA-256 of message.bodyText as .task ids
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:14-47, 253-279, 306-334, 526-570, 764-790 — one NSRecursiveLock guards writes, String(contentsOf:) reads and stats; the uncached signature stats on a miss, while the cached variant's comment says a mounting row must not stat
