- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/EmailReaderViewModel.swift:41-51 and esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1341-1396, 284-293, 454-484, 503-504 — reader init calls openSession → preparedOpenArtifact synchronously; when warmed: SHA-256 of wrapped HTML, currentHTMLSourceSignature (HTMLContentHandler.swift:580-601, 706-734; CanonicalEmailContent.swift:58-68), bodyText normalized twice (CanonicalEmailContentLoader.swift:410-445)
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:25-35, 609-648 and FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1135-1164, 1444-1450, 1626-1644 — checkout at makeWebView and warm() each run a CID scan plus SHA-256 of the wrapped HTML on the main actor
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:417-440, 477 with HTMLPreviewScaleCalculator.swift:25-75; EmailPreviewSnapshotView.swift:104-115 with EmailPreviewSnapshotCache.swift:21-47 — main-actor session init: 3 copies, 3 regex compiles and scans, a wrap (per snapshot-cache miss); the view's task id SHA-256s the preview HTML on every body evaluation
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/CIDSchemeHandler.swift:11, 59-85, 106-141 with WebKit WKURLSchemeHandler.h:38-40 (WK_SWIFT_UI_ACTOR) and FileSystemErrorHandler.swift:126-128 — the conformance infers @MainActor, the Task inherits it, and a local hit reads the whole file with Data(contentsOf:) on main

**Trigger.** Rich rows mounting or re-rendering, or a tap on a warmed message, when the HTML or bodyText is large (hundreds of KB to MB). Also: the main thread waiting on the HTML lock while sync writes or reads a large body or the orphan sweep holds it, and mail with many inline photos.

**Impact.** The cost scales with message size, not mailbox size. At typical bodies (under about 200 KB) each operation is sub-millisecond to a few ms. Bodies of 1 MB or more plausibly cause hitches over 16 ms at tap, and at rich-row mount and warm. A wait on the lock is bounded by one file operation, except for the main-actor orphan sweep, which is tracked separately. A hang over 250 ms needs unusually large bodies or bodyText. Nothing was measured.

**Verifier.** Every cited chain holds. Corrections: the open path hashes the wrapped HTML twice (prepared key, then checkout) and the canonical body once, not three more times. Snapshot regex work runs once per snapshot-cache miss, at most two at a time, not on each scroll. preparedOpenArtifact returns early when nothing is warmed. Added: MessageBubble takes the lock and stats for every row, warm() hashes on main, and the snapshot view hashes the HTML on every body evaluation. I found no size cap. The hang claim is unsupported.

**October review.** html-orphan-sweep-main-thread (docs/scalability-review.md:1024; still open per :1588) overlaps only the lock-wait part

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: every HTML read, write, stat and signature-cache access stays inside HTMLContentAccountBoundary.perform. Close waits on that lock, so a write outside it can land after the tombstone rename. Off-main warm work must stay inside warm()'s counted operation, re-checking both generations after every await, never in a fire-and-forget task. Only the HTML-derived CID scan may move off main: the availability half reads view-context Attachments.
- CID: WebKit raises if a scheme task is called after stop. Only the Data read may leave the main actor. The isActive check and didReceive/didFinish stay together on main, with no suspension between them. The isReadableStoragePath guard (the readableLocalURLValue rule) stays.
- Signature identity: CanonicalEmailContent.sourceSignature keys RenderedMessageCache, contentSourceDidChange and activeHTMLSourceSignature. renderSignature and EmailPreviewSnapshotCacheKey must stay byte-identical between the prepared and live paths, or the reader repaints and snapshot keys split. A stat token may only gate a fast path, taken under the same lock as the read; a mismatch falls back to today's content check and never means reusable.
- Bubble routing: view bodies using cachedHTMLSourceSignature (nil on a miss) get a new task id once the first load fills the cache, so every cold row loads twice. A stat in the mapper would stat the whole 300-row window on every re-map. A size cap with a plain-text fallback contradicts the stored RichContentVerdict (a card/text swap after mount) and the reader's deliberate rule of no plain-text fallback.

**Fix.** Keep the content signatures as the identity, and compute derived tokens once, off main. (1) warmOriginalEmailSource returns three tokens: the wrapped HTML's existing count:sha16 fingerprint, its referenced CIDs and, for .messageFile, a stat token read with the body under the boundary lock. The prepared entry stores them. (2) preparedOpenArtifact drops its tautological key rehash, compares raw inputs before normalizing, and skips the content hash when the stat token is unchanged (else today's check). It builds CID availability and renderSignature from the stored tokens. (3) Pass MessageBubble's one signature down. Precompute the EmailContentSection, session and snapshot keys byte-identically, and the preview width estimate in the pipeline. (4) CID: read Data detached, respond on main. No cap.

**First step.** Add the wrapped HTML's count:sha16 fingerprint and its referenced CID set to WarmedOriginalEmailHTML, computed in warmOriginalEmailSource (off main). Store them in the prepared-payload entry, and drop preparedOpenArtifact's expectedKey rehash, which always matches.

**Pinning test.** FullEmailWebViewManagerTests: inject a fingerprint closure that records Thread.isMainThread. After warm, preparedOpenArtifact and checkout call it zero times on main, and renderSignature equals EmailReaderArtifact.make's for the same source. Revert-check: preparedOpenArtifact.

**Payoff.** Opening a warmed email and scrolling rich rows stop doing body-size work on main. Today an open costs up to four HTML SHA-256s, two CID scans and two bodyText normalizations. Unmeasured.

### `chat-transcript-ui#6` · low · performance · effort S · new

**Every merged save is classified on the main actor, and non-member messages still fault their Conversation**

Area: Chat transcript architecture, scroll performance and complexity. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The mechanism is real, but its scope is smaller than claimed. With a chat open, every relevant merge calls belongsToCurrentConversation for each Message: once in each of three inserted-set passes, and in two refreshed-set passes. For a message of another conversation the objectID test fails, and the KVC `id` read then fires that Conversation's fault. So the doc's "faults at most the message row" is false for non-members. That fault fires at most once per distinct other conversation per merge, not once per message: later reads find the object already loaded. The rest is cheap work on object pointers.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:38-43,90 — two passes over the inserted set run before the window guard at :74, and a third runs at :90 (estimatedTotalCount calls visibleInsertedMessageIDs again); :267-283 and :376-386 call the membership check for each refreshed Message
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:454-475 — the doc says it 'faults at most the message row', but when the objectIDs differ, :470-473 reads `id` through KVC on the other conversation, which fires that conversation's fault
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:480-491 — committedValues fallback; for an inserted message it reads `id` again on the same Conversation, which is already loaded by then
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:164,183-191 — for every sibling save that touches conversations, the list already batch-fetches all of them on main, loaded in full with participants and persons prefetched
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Phases/MessageFetchPhase.swift:37,54-57 — sync saves once per 50-message batch when intermediate saves are allowed
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:182 — the view context merges sibling saves automatically

**Trigger.** A catch-up or history-recovery sync while a chat is open (on the Mac, a chat is always open). Each merged batch save that inserts messages into many other conversations triggers it, and so does a merged read-state or label refresh in another conversation.

**Impact.** Each merge costs at most one extra Conversation-row fault per distinct other conversation: either a row-cache hit or one fetch by primary key. On top of that come a KVC read and a committedValues dictionary per message per pass, and about ten Set unions. This is small next to what the same merge already pays on main: N message-row faults, which the design accepts, and the list's batch fetch of the same conversations. The cost grows with the size of a save, not of the store, so it is the same at S1 and S3. It is unmeasured, and on its own it is not a hitch at 50-message pages.

**Verifier.** The U8 fix (docs/archive/PR-DESCRIPTION.md:26) kept the UUID fallback from the start. Commit 56ac651d only switched it to KVC, so the doc comment overstated the fix from day one. No test asserts that no Conversation fault fires. The item is absent from "Already sound" and "Checked and found not to be a problem". Fault cost and save sizes are not measured. A fix has to keep the UUID fallback when currentConversationObjectID() is nil, not only when it is temporary. Severity drops to low: the cost is per conversation, not per message, it does not scale with the store, and it is a fraction of the merge cost already accepted.

**Invariant risks**

- An early `return false` on the first objectID mismatch skips the committedValues fallback (VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:477-491). A message deleted with its inverse cleared, or moved out of this chat on the viewContext, would stop counting as this chat's change, so no reconciliation runs and a stale row stays until post-sync validation.
- Permanent IDs only (the review correction to chat-transcript-uuid-join-offset-paging; cachedConversationObjectID never holds a temporary ID). The UUID fallback has to stay wherever either ID is nil or temporary, and it has to stay an optional KVC read: the Swift `id` property traps mid-merge (:466-469).
- A single classification pass must keep two populations apart. hasVisibleInsertion and the tail append count temporary-ID inserts; insertedMessageIDs, knownTotalCount and auto-read leave them out (:580, :609). Merging the two changes when messageDatasetGeneration bumps and breaks the tail-append count guard (TailAppend.swift:65-67).
- Classification must run synchronously on the viewContext inside the notification. changedValuesForCurrentEvent() and committedValues only mean something in that turn, knownTotalCount has to be computed before the bookkeeping (:91-92), and Message objects must never be carried into a Task or another context.

**Fix.** In belongsToCurrentConversation, resolve our objectID once, then check each candidate by objectID: the current `conversation` first, then the committedValues destination. Read KVC `id` only when our ID is nil or either ID is temporary. Do not return false after the first mismatch, because the committed-destination check must still run. Use optional KVC, never the Swift `id`. Resolve currentConversationObjectID() once per notification and pass it down. Leave the single per-notification classification for chat-reconcile-main-count-offset (scalability-review.md:744, still open), which rewrites this handler anyway. Production rarely needs the UUID path: ChatViewModel.init gives the conversation a permanent ID (ChatViewModel.swift:316-318), and Conversation UUIDs are random and never reassigned (CoreDataFactories.swift:193).

**First step.** At VirtualScrollState+ChangeObservation.swift:458-494, add a private helper. It compares a destination's objectID with ours and reads value(forKey: "id") only when either ID is nil or temporary. Call it for the current destination and the committed one.

**Pinning test.** VirtualScrollStateTests: with chat A open and automerge on, background-save a message into B; B must remain a fault in viewContext (Revert-check: the unconditional KVC read). Also: moving a window message to B on viewContext must still reconcile.

**Payoff.** While a chat is open (always on the Mac), each merged save no longer faults one Conversation per distinct other conversation, and the common path drops the trap-prone UUID read. Small, unmeasured.

### `conversation-list-ui#5` · low · maintainability · effort S · known-open

**The list's read model can only be built from view-context objects on the main actor, and each stored change is applied twice, unbounded by the window**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The cited code is as described, but two claims are overstated. The row value initializers are not actor-isolated and accept any context's Conversation; only ConversationListStore's [Conversation] API and the @MainActor filter closure pin reads to the view context. Double handling is conditional: objectsDidChange carries only inserts and conversations still registered in the view context, and the code accepts the duplicate pass. Confirmed: handleSiblingContextSave fetches every changed Conversation with a two-level prefetch on main with no window test, and each pass pays O(window) scans and an O(window) publish compare.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:171-211 — performAndWait on main: `self IN` all inserted+updated Conversation IDs, prefetch participants and participants.person, returnsObjectsAsFaults = false, then applyConversationChanges; no window or sort-key test before the fetch.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:34-41,160-163 — comments: the automerge only refreshes objects still registered, so objectsDidChange can carry no Conversation; a duplicate pass is acknowledged and left to publishVisibleItems's equality guard. No dedup between the two sinks (26-32, 43-62).
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationSnapshot.swift:32-47 and ConversationListItem.swift:14-17 — the only initializers take a managed Conversation, but neither type is @MainActor or tied to the view context; a background context could build them inside its own perform.
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationListStore.swift:25-46,96-126 — replaceAll/applyChanges take [Conversation]; each upsert does two linear firstIndex scans of visibleItems; the comment at 10-11 assumes a window of 'a few hundred rows at most' while ConversationListViewModel.swift:562 grows the limit by 50 with no cap.
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:78-113 — equal-value guards keep a conversation with an unchanged rollup clean, written specifically so it does not fan through the list's sibling-save handling and the merge.
- docs/scalability-review.md:1518 and 1640 — the off-window sibling fetch is already a lower-priority item (effort S, not recorded as built in 'Suggested order'); 'Already sound' says the list has no FRC and applies changes incrementally.

**Trigger.** A background-context save whose inserted or updated IDs include a Conversation, once the list view model has appeared (it stays subscribed across pushes and sheets). At most about 500 conversations per sync page save, usually a handful; conversations with unchanged rollups and no new message are not in the save.

**Impact.** A few main-thread milliseconds per ordinary sync save. During a large catch-up, tens of milliseconds per page: up to 500 rows fetched with participants and persons, snapshotted and inserted, then trimmed if they sort past the window. The second snapshot pass happens only for inserted rows and rows still registered in the view context. Hitch-level, no correctness failure; nothing was measured.

**Verifier.** All six citations read whole and match. Guard the auditor missed: equal-value rollup writes. The duplicate pass is an accepted, commented choice; whether window rows stay registered was not observable from code. The "read model is main-only" claim is API shape (store signature, filter isolation) plus the deliberate need to show unsaved view-context rows, not a type constraint. The measurable part is the prior review's hygiene item, so severity drops to low; the shared off-main reader is a design recommendation.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1518 (lower-priority item: a merged save's Conversation IDs are fetched and snapshotted even when they sort past the window, effort S, not built). Related: conversation-list-window-full-refetch (lines 796-817) and step 11's list keyset paging (line 1624), both open.

**Invariant risks**

- Optimistic sends write lastMessageDate and snippet on the view context (GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:289-290). Both window reads use includesPendingChanges=true, and the review says to keep unsaved rows. A background reader sees only the store, so the row would fall back to its saved state.
- An async result that lands after the list has been reloaded or cleared can bring stale rows back. After viewContext.reset() clears the list (ChangeObservation.swift:68-75; CoreDataStack.swift:541-548), it could show the previous account's rows. AuthSession does not quiesce such a reader, and it can fetch while destroyAllData has removed the store (CoreDataStack.swift:526-530).
- Visibility checks must run on the live Conversation with the main-actor filter. participantEmails leaves out list conversations and Hide My Email relays, and the search clause is a superset that is checked again in memory (ConversationFilter.swift:31-41). On CI's Swift 6.2, a perform block that captures the filter closure does not compile.
- Rows outside the window that now sort before the tail must still enter (testBackgroundSaveBringsOutsideWindowConversationIntoWindow). Skipping a row must clear hasLoadedAllConversationWindow before the backfill runs. SortKey stays the only comparator, with no copy in a predicate. Keep returnsObjectsAsFaults=false and the Person and refresh paths in objectsDidChange.

**Fix.** Build the prior review's S item instead of the background reader. Add one admission test to ConversationListStore: admit a row that is already in itemsByID, any row while the window holds fewer than the limit, and any row whose SortKey sorts before the tail. applyChanges uses it for both pipelines and returns skippedBeyondWindow; applyConversationChanges then clears hasLoadedAllConversationWindow before the backfill. In handleSiblingContextSave, split the fetch in two. First fetch the changed IDs with no prefetch (returnsObjectsAsFaults=false, includesPendingChanges=true) to read their sort keys. Then run the existing prefetching fetch for admitted IDs only, and snapshot only the rows it returns. Keep the main-thread apply and both subscriptions. Leave the background reader to step 11.

**First step.** Add ConversationListStore.admits(objectID:sortKey:limit:) and a skippedBeyondWindow result from applyChanges. Cover a full window in ConversationListStoreTests: a row past the tail is skipped, a row before the tail is admitted, and a window row that moves past the tail is still updated.

**Pinning test.** In ConversationListViewModelBackgroundSaveTests, fill a window of 3, then have one background save touch 50 past-tail conversations and one pre-tail. Assert that only the pre-tail row enters, no skipped row's Participant is registered in the view context, and loadMoreIfNeeded still reaches the skipped rows.

**Payoff.** Catch-up sync saves no longer fetch participants or build snapshots on main for rows past the window. Each save's main-thread cost then depends on the changed rows that are admitted, and paging still reaches the skipped rows.

### `conversation-list-ui#6` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**A failed window fetch is published as an empty mailbox and latches 'all loaded'; on the Mac nothing fetches again**

Area: Conversation list architecture and main-thread exposure. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

fetchWindow catches a view-context fetch error and returns []. reloadConversationWindowFromStore then latches hasLoadedAllConversationWindow (0 < limit), replaces the window with nothing and publishes; paging and backfill refuse while the latch holds. A failure on a paging step therefore blanks an already populated list. Only a search, filter or contact-set change, or onAppear, refetches; sync and pull-to-refresh do not, and live changes re-add only the conversations that change. The invalidate-all leg is teardown-only: the view context is reset only with the mailbox unmounted.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationWindowProvider.swift:49-65 — the do/catch around both fetch paths logs "Failed to fetch conversation window" and returns [], the same value as a genuinely empty store.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:580-594 — hasLoadedAllConversationWindow = window.count < loadedConversationLimit, then listStore.replaceAll(with: window) and publishVisibleItems(); :556 and :602 return early while the latch is set; :562-563 paging reloads the whole window, so a failure there empties a populated list.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:526-537 with esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationFilterService.swift:22-27 — a contactEmailsCache change calls onFilterStateChange, which clears the latch and reloads; :491-497 loads that cache 0.5 s after onAppear, so a failed first fetch is refetched when Contacts returns a non-empty set.
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:157-159 and :405-410 — performSync only starts a sync and reloads nothing; the latch otherwise reopens only when a trim proves more than loadedConversationLimit rows (100 by default) are in the store.
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:541-549 — the only viewContext.reset(); reached from destroyAndReloadAsync (:443, :449; FreshInstallHandler.swift:257) and resetStore (:531; AuthSession.swift:388, run at :1632). AuthSession.swift:854 sets isAuthenticated = false before the cleanup at :879, and ContentView.swift:21-26 mounts the mailbox only while canAccessMailbox.
- esc-chatmail/Platform/MacMailboxView.swift:26 and :192-214 — the Mac's selection is the view's own @State, kept for any conversation existingObject still finds unarchived; publishVisibleItems (ConversationListViewModel.swift:545-550) prunes only selectionService's Select-mode set.

**Trigger.** context.fetch throwing on the main-queue view context while the list is mounted (SQLite I/O or corruption error, out of memory): at onAppear, on a paging step, or on a backfill after an archive. Not observed, and expected to be rare on a healthy store. A view-context reset is not a trigger: its only callers run at fresh install, after sign-out has unpublished the mailbox, or before sign-in publishes it, and the store-load recovery ladder never resets the context.

**Impact.** The list shows an empty mailbox, then only the conversations later syncs touch, and it looks final. No data is lost. On the Mac the open chat stays selected, but the sidebar stays wrong until a search, a filter change, a Contacts change or a relaunch. On iOS a pop-back refetches, but an empty list has no row to push, and a Select-mode selection is cleared.

**Verifier.** Read all four reload call sites, the filter service, the list store, CoreDataStack's reset paths and AuthSession's sign-out order. Changed: dropped the invalidate-all and store-recovery trigger, which cannot fire with the mailbox mounted; the Mac's open-chat selection is not pruned; the contacts-cache load about 0.5 s after appear usually refetches after a failed first fetch, which the auditor missed. Not a documented decision: the docs' rule is that a failed read is never empty. No fetch failure was observed.

**October review.** No scalability-review item covers the error path. Related: conversation-list-window-full-refetch in docs/scalability-review.md (step 11, not built), whose keyset paging rewrites this same reload and should keep the failure rule.

**Invariant risks**

- The finding's 'after invalidate-all, schedule one reload' would fetch at a bad moment. viewContext.reset() runs inside destroyAndReloadAsync, between destroyAllData and loadStoresAsync (CoreDataStack.swift:441-446), when the coordinator has no stores, and :524-529 records that a fetch there traps. Only clear the latch and mark the reload owed; onAppear does the refetch.
- Never reload on every .syncCompleted. That would refetch and re-snapshot the whole window on the main thread after every sync: the cost of conversation-list-window-full-refetch in the scalability review, and the same harm as the FRC trap in CLAUDE.md. Reload only while a failed fetch is still owed.
- Keeping the old window after the search, filter or contact set changed would show rows the new query excludes. In that case clear the window, as a query that matched nothing would. publishVisibleItems must stay the only publish path, because it keeps the selection a subset of the visible rows.
- loadMoreIfNeeded raises loadedConversationLimit before it reloads. Left raised after a failure, backfillConversationWindowIfNeeded runs a failing full reload again on every relevant merged save. Put the limit back on failure.

**Fix.** Make fetchWindow throw. Keep its two deliberate [] returns (limit <= 0 and canMatchCurrentFilter false). reloadConversationWindowFromStore returns a Bool. On a throw it logs, sets windowReloadOwed and leaves listStore, the latch and the published items unchanged. The exception is a query that changed since the last successful load (search text, filter, or the contact set under .contacts/.other): then it clears the window, publishes, and leaves the latch open. loadMoreIfNeeded puts the limit back when the reload fails. To retry, add a .syncCompleted sink on ConversationListDependencies.notificationCenter (received on main) that reloads only while windowReloadOwed is set. The invalidate-all handler clears the latch and sets windowReloadOwed, and never fetches.

**First step.** In ConversationWindowProvider, add a fetch closure that defaults to context.fetch, and make fetchWindow throw. Add try at the seven test call sites (ConversationWindowProviderTests, ScaleQueryPlanTests). Then write the failing view-model test.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests, own NotificationCenter, initialLimit 2 / pageSize 1, three rows: onAppear shows two. Stubbed fetch throws: loadMoreIfNeeded keeps both rows. Stub recovers and .syncCompleted is posted: three rows show. Revert-check: the failure branch; HONEST SCOPE: a stubbed error, not real SQLite I/O.

**Payoff.** A passing read error no longer leaves the list empty with paging shut. The Mac sidebar comes back at the next sync, without needing a relaunch, a search or a filter change.

### `gap-change-propagation-pipeline#2` · low · scalability · effort S · known-open

**Every save reaches the list through two full pipelines, and nothing coalesces saves**

Area: From one store save to every observer: merge, cache invalidation and UI. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The didSaveObjectIDs pipeline batch-fetches every Conversation ID that a sibling save touched, with participants and persons prefetched. It snapshots each one and upserts it with O(W) scans before trimming, so its cost follows the number of conversations in the save. The prior review already lists this as a hygiene item. objectsDidChange repeats the work only for merged inserts and still-registered conversations. In sync, inserts arrive one per ConversationCreationSerializer shell save, so the duplicate is one row per save. Nothing coalesces saves, but each per-shell-save pass is small, and the shell saves themselves are deliberate.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:34-41,160-163 — a merge yields no Conversation in objectsDidChange for an object that is unregistered or deallocated; the duplicate pass is accepted and the equality guard suppresses it
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:179-196 — one `self IN` fetch of every inserted or updated conversation ID in the save, with prefetch, so the cost is sized by the save
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationListStore.swift:111-125 — two linear scans per upserted row, before the trim at ConversationListViewModel.swift:405; W starts at 100 (ConversationListWindowConfiguration.swift:28)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationCreationSerializer.swift:75-82,107-131 — each new conversation is committed in its own shell-context save, deliberately, so it is store-visible and publishes before its first message
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:367-386 — the page rollup and save; pages hold up to 500 IDs (Constants.swift:93)
- docs/scalability-review.md:1518 — the save-sized didSave pass is already filed under Hygiene

**Trigger.** A re-initial sync after a store reset (window up to 30 days), or a history recovery after a long offline period. One 500-message page save there touches hundreds of conversations, and is preceded by a run of one-conversation shell saves. Ordinary incremental saves touch only a few conversations.

**Impact.** An estimated low tens of ms on the main thread per large page save: a hitch, not the 250 ms hang claimed. On top of that, a few ms per shell save for two one-row passes, spread across the time the page takes to persist. Nothing was measured.

**Verifier.** I confirmed both subscriptions, that nothing debounces, and that each new conversation gets its own save. I refuted "two full pipelines" for large saves: a merge reports updates only for registered objects (the code's own comment says so), and the conversations in a page save were inserted by earlier shell saves, so objectsDidChange carries few of them. The shell saves are a documented design. The save-sized half is the prior review's hygiene item. The 250 ms hang estimate is not supported. I ran nothing.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1518 (## Hygiene / ### iOS: "Every merged save's Conversation IDs are fetched, snapshotted and inserted on main even when they sort far past the window"). It has not been built: ChangeObservation.swift:179-196 still fetches every changed ID, and ConversationListStore.swift:55-66 still upserts every row before the trim at ConversationListViewModel.swift:405.

**Invariant risks**

- Removing objectsDidChange's conversation pass for merged changes would leave registered rows stale. The didSave fetch keeps a registered object's in-memory values (default shouldRefreshRefetchedObjects, ChangeObservation.swift:192-194), so when that fetch lands before the automerge, only the merge's refreshed-objects pass corrects the row (102-104, 160-163). objectsDidChange is also the only path for the view context's own unsaved rows (own saves are filtered out at line 53) and for Person renames (116-127). The prior review's keep-intact note at scalability-review.md:907 says the same.
- Driving the list from didMergeChangesObjectIDs would bring back the stale unregistered-row bug. Automerge refreshes only registered objects (ChangeObservation.swift:34-41), which is why ConversationListViewModelBackgroundSaveTests runs with automerge off (lines 19-22) and pins didSave as the only path for those rows.
- A persistent-history consumer would be a new account-boundary participant. CoreDataStack.swift:173-178 records history that nothing reads and requests no remote-change notifications, and PersistentHistoryPurger deletes history after 7 days (the review plans about 1 day). A consumer's token would have to survive purges and be reset by sign-out, fresh install and the recovery ladder's store reset.
- A skip that leaves hasLoadedAllConversationWindow latched leaves rows unreachable (pinned by testApplyConversationChanges_trimAfterShortInitialWindow_reopensPaging). An SQL prefilter would be a second mirror of the CANONICAL SortKey (ConversationListItem.swift:31-37), so it must be a strict superset and keep temporary window IDs out of `self IN`. A timer debounce would widen the moment an archived row shows undimmed (ConversationListViewModel.swift:45-47).

**Fix.** Keep both pipelines. They complement each other: didSave covers unregistered rows, and the merge's refresh covers registered rows, which the didSave fetch returns without refreshing. Build the prior review's skip as a pure policy used in ConversationListStore.applyChanges. Skip a row that is not in itemsByID and passes isSourceConversation, before any visibility check or snapshot, when the canonical SortKey `<` puts it after the window's row at min(count, limit)−1. Do not skip when the window is known complete (hasLoadedAll and count < limit). Return the skipped IDs. When any row is skipped, applyConversationChanges clears hasLoadedAllConversationWindow, so backfill reloads any slot a removal in the same batch opened. Keep the single prefetching fetch. Do not add didMerge, a history consumer or a timer debounce.

**First step.** Add a pure policy and a window-limit/complete input to ConversationListStore.applyChanges. The policy skips out-of-window rows that sort after the window's last row and returns their IDs. Then make applyConversationChanges clear hasLoadedAllConversationWindow beside the trim reset whenever any row is skipped.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelBackgroundSaveTests, limit 2: window [A,B], with older C and D stored. One background save archives A and touches D, and the list must converge to [B,C]; by the code, today it stays [B,D]. A store test checks that a skipped row's participants relationship stays a fault.

**Payoff.** A row past the window's tail costs a sort-key comparison in both pipelines (older shell inserts during a re-sync included), not a snapshot and an O(W) insert. A same-batch removal no longer lets a past-tail row hide rows the window has not loaded.

### `gap-change-propagation-pipeline#4` · low · reliability · effort S · new

**Person name changes are announced before the save, cached across invalidations and invalidated silently after the merge**

Area: From one store save to every observer: merge, cache invalidation and UI. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

ParticipantRollupCache records the tracker fingerprint when it stores an entry, after the load's awaited read of the view context. The tracker is bumped before the save: findOrCreate's early post, and createNewMessage's invalidateEntry. It is bumped again after the save by CacheCoordinator, which posts nothing. So a row that reads before the merge can cache an old name as fresh, or a re-render can hit the entry before the last bump. The cache token ignores the snapshot's display-name fingerprint, so the merge alone does not evict the entry. The PersonCache half has no visible effect.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:94-97 — displayName improved and invalidatePersonCacheAndPostLater fired inside the persist block, before any save (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:378 uses the after-save variant)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantRollupCache.swift:175-183 — dependencyFingerprint taken at store time; ParticipantLoader.swift:446-476 stores only after the awaited resolver/photo work
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantRollupCache.swift:23-27 — token is participantHash, stored title, header names; the row's participantDisplayNameFingerprint (ConversationRowView.swift:218-227) feeds only infoKey, and hash rows reload only on a miss (356-358)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/CacheCoordinator.swift:431-437 — post-save PersonCache invalidation (tracker bump) with no notification to views
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantInfoResolver.swift:258-273 — Contacts, From-header and view-context Person names win; PersonCache is consulted only when none is real
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/PersonCache.swift:182 — getDisplayName (cited 198-208) has no production caller, only ParticipantCacheAccountBoundaryTests

**Trigger.** A new message improves a Person's display name. The person must have no Contacts card and no explicit From-header name in another conversation, such as someone the user has only written to, or a To/Cc-only member of a group. The row's load or re-render has to land between the pre-save bumps, the merge and CacheCoordinator's post-save bump.

**Impact.** This is cosmetic and depends on timing, and no one has seen it happen. Another conversation's row or chat header can keep the old name until the row re-renders. If the stale read was stored after the last bump, the old name stays for up to the 300 s TTL. The receiving conversation recovers: a change to its stored title changes the token, so its entry misses and reloads.

**Verifier.** The mechanism holds for the rollup cache, but the scope is narrower than the auditor claimed. A better name never reaches the screen through PersonCache, because the snapshot's view-context Person name wins over it. The cited getDisplayName is test-only code. MessagePersister+Creation.swift:208-211 also invalidates every participant before the save, so restricting CacheCoordinator's Person rule would remove few bumps. No list-wide refresh after a sync was found. The interleavings were not observed. Severity is lowered to low because the effect is cosmetic, transient and limited to Person-derived names.

**October review.** Not covered. Related: self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist (docs/scalability-review.md:1310-1326, correction at line 1322, not built) and person-change-conversation-fanout (line 897, listed as not built at line 1561).

**Invariant risks**

- CacheCoordinator posting .personDisplayInfoDidChange for every updated Person (CacheCoordinator.swift:267-274) would also post the user's own address on every message save. Linking a MessageParticipant updates its Person through the messageParticipations inverse (ESCChatmail 6 model:185), and ChatMessagesView.swift:1073-1082 refreshes on a sender match, so the open chat would reload its header and grouping keys on every sync save.
- Restricting the coordinator's Person rule to email or displayName changes is unsafe. A didSave notification cannot read changedValues, because the save cleared them. Relationship-only bumps are today's only post-save eviction when a new message brings a new From-header name, since row lookups pass nil header names (ConversationRowView.swift:252-259). The correction at scalability-review.md:1322 also keeps the self Person invalidated.
- A display-name fingerprint in the token needs exactly one definition, shared with ConversationSnapshot.participantFields, including its deliberate Hide My Email asymmetry. If the two drift, every row lookup misses without any error and the rollup cache stops working without failing a test.
- findOrCreate must only stage on its context's queue and must never save it, because only the orchestrator's save points may save the sync context. Staged emails survive a rollback (DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:1541-1560) and post on the next save, which is harmless. Keep createNewMessage's pre-save invalidateEntry: it is the self-alias item's subject.

**Fix.** Fix this in the cache, not in how notifications are posted. (1) Give the tracker a monotonic mark. ParticipantLoader captures it before fetchConversationParticipantSnapshot, and cacheParticipantInfo stores nothing if any source email or the global generation moved since then. This is RenderedMessageCache's pattern (RenderedMessageCache.swift:410-431), and the caller still gets its result. (2) Add the participants' display-name fingerprint to ParticipantRollupCacheToken, computed by ConversationSnapshot's function, and have the row's lookups pass snapshot.participantDisplayNameFingerprint. The merge's snapshot rebuild then evicts any entry built before the merge. (3) Make findOrCreate use invalidatePersonCacheAndPostAfterContextSave, as MessagePersister+Updates.swift:378 does. Do not make CacheCoordinator post, and do not restrict its Person rule.

**First step.** Add mark() and hasInvalidated(_:since:) to ParticipantRollupDependencyTracking, and to AliasManagerTests' StubRollupDependencyTracker. Capture the mark in ParticipantLoader.loadParticipants before the snapshot read, and pass it into the store guard of ParticipantRollupCache.cacheParticipantInfo.

**Pinning test.** In ParticipantLoaderTests, a contacts resolver suspends on its first lookup. Meanwhile the test renames the Person and calls tracker.invalidate(email:). After release, cachedParticipantInfo is nil and the next load returns the new name. Revert-check: the cacheParticipantInfo fence.

**Payoff.** Rows can no longer cache or show a name from before the merge as fresh, in any order of merge, bumps and posts. No notification traffic is added. The header still depends on post-save ordering, which is unmeasured.

### `gap-change-propagation-pipeline#5` · low · reliability · effort S · known-partial

**CacheCoordinator ties every save in the process to the HTML file lock and never hears some deletes**

Area: From one store save to every observer: merge, cache invalidation and UI. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The three mechanisms exist, but each costs little. CacheCoordinator's compactMap takes the HTML boundary's NSRecursiveLock on the saving thread for every save, before it knows whether the plan is empty. Each lock hold lasts one body read or write, or at most a 100-unlink chunk, so a main-queue save can wait a few milliseconds. The docs already record that every save takes this lock. iOS background-task cold launches never call start(), so files of rows deleted in those runs wait for the daily orphan sweep. The two Message batch deletes find almost nothing in steady state.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/CacheCoordinator.swift:147-153 — captureAccountGeneration() (takes the lock) runs before invalidationPlan(forSave:) and its isEmpty guard, for every NSManagedObjectContextDidSave (object: nil at 138)
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:32-47,399-417 — perform holds the lock across the operation; deferred deletes are chunks of at most 100 unlinks, and the comment already says every context's save takes this lock
- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:199-210 — CacheCoordinator.shared.start() is called only in initializeApp; AppStartupBootstrap.swift:235-237 prepareForBackgroundSync only restores auth (used by BackgroundSyncManager.swift:42-44)
- docs/scalability-review.md:1589,1600 — the docs say a background task's cold launch never reaches initializeApp, and that every save captures the generation under the HTML lock
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+EntityCleanup.swift:134-158,302-330 — the Message batch deletes post no DidSave; but MessagePersister.swift:639 never stores DRAFT messages, and the model's Conversation.messages cascades (ESCChatmail 6 contents:51), so both passes rarely find rows
- esc-chatmail/Services/DatabaseMaintenance/DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:54-88 — the daily cleanup runs those same passes and then the HTML and attachment orphan sweeps in the same run

**Trigger.** A view-context save, such as a send's optimistic row (scalability-review:1558), that lands while another thread holds the HTML lock for a body write, a body read or a deletion chunk. An iOS BGTask that cold-launches the app and runs a sync which deletes messages (Gmail-side deletes, TRASH/SPAM exclusion).

**Impact.** The main thread can wait for one file operation or a 100-unlink chunk, a few milliseconds and rarely over 16 ms. The main thread's body loads already wait on this same lock. Body and attachment files of rows deleted in a cold background launch stay on disk until the daily BGProcessing sweep. That matches how every delete behaved before step 7. No data is lost and nothing leaks across accounts. The 6-hour batch deletes leave almost nothing behind, and the daily run sweeps right after them.

**Verifier.** Cited lines match the code today. start() has a single caller. The background cold-launch path rests on the code's own model and the review's statement; no launch was observed. Changes from the original claim: the batch-delete trigger is close to empty (drafts are never stored, messages cascade with their conversation). The lock cost is bounded and already documented. The fixes still make sense: build the plan first, which skips the lock on saves with nothing to invalidate, and start the coordinator from the shared bootstrap. Severity drops to low.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md step 7, `deleted-message-file-reclamation` (1178-1204; built 1564-1568, 1597-1600). The cold-launch start and the batch deletes are not listed as left; line 1600 records only the save-takes-the-lock fact.

**Invariant risks**

- Capture at post time (CLAUDE.md, CacheCoordinator): the generation must still be captured on the posting queue inside the save, before .receive(on: .main). Reading a main-actor copy, or capturing at delivery, can stamp an old account's deletes with the new account's generation.
- The unit-test host stays idle (esc_chatmailApp.swift:184-191). A start() in App.init, BackgroundSyncManager.init or any path a test can reach makes the shared coordinator hear every test stack's saves. It must also start before auth restore, so that reopenHTMLContent retires captures made before the account was established.
- Deferred removals go only through the removers that ask first (DeletedRowFileReclamation: live-row check, deletedAt, local_ files left to the sweep). A batch-delete helper must read the rows' values before execute, never resolve deleted IDs afterwards, and never call deleteHTML(for:bodyStorageURI:).
- No Core Data work under the HTML boundary lock, and no change to the rule that close drains in-flight work (HTMLContentHandler.swift:32-63, 407-417). Splitting or bypassing the lock to make the capture cheap rewrites the account-generation fence for a low-severity gain.

**Fix.** Three independent changes. (1) In CacheCoordinator.start's compactMap (147-154), build invalidationPlan(forSave:) first and return nil when it is empty; only then call captureAccountGeneration(), still on the posting queue. Extract this as a nonisolated static savePlan(forSave:captureGeneration:) and leave the boundary lock alone. (2) Call CacheCoordinator.shared.start() in prepareProductionAppPersistence once waitForStoreToLoad succeeds, which is before restore, as in initializeApp. Guard it with !RuntimeEnvironment.isRunningUnitTests. initializeApp's call stays as a no-op (start() returns early once started); update the comment at esc_chatmailApp.swift:336. (3) Optional, lowest value: route removeDraftMessages and removeOrphanedMessages through their graph-delete fallbacks, in chunks, so a DidSave reaches CacheCoordinator.

**First step.** Move the compactMap body in CacheCoordinator.swift into a nonisolated static savePlan(forSave:captureGeneration:) that builds the plan before it calls the capture closure. Then add the counting test to CacheCoordinatorDeletedRowCaptureTests.

**Pinning test.** Observe the test context's DidSave and call savePlan with a counting capture: an insert-only save captures zero times, a message delete once (Revert-check: capture first). Add a repositorySource pin of start() in prepareProductionAppPersistence.

**Payoff.** Saves with nothing to invalidate, main-thread view-context saves included, stop waiting on body file I/O. Mail deleted in background-launched syncs frees its files right away, not after a daily sweep finishes.

### `web-content-rendering#6` · low · maintainability · effort M · new

**Four web view construction sites and delegates share no policy and no app-wide budget**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The four web views do share a policy layer. All four use LayoutAwareWKWebView, a CIDSchemeHandler, JS off, the sender base URL, and the sanitizer plus CSP wrapper. The two preview delegates repeat the same inline allow-.other/.reload rule without the scheme screen. That gap is inert: meta, iframe, script and form are stripped, and the CSP forbids scripts, frames and form actions. The real cost: a snapshot that times out (the 5 s limit includes remote-image loads) swaps the row to a live scaled WKWebView. Nothing caps those views app-wide or frees them under memory pressure. The 1,938-line manager file is hygiene.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailPreviewSnapshotView.swift:43-55, 383-405, 524-529 — any non-cancellation render error sets didFail and mounts MiniEmailWebView (a live BaseEmailWebView) with the snapshot task attached; after one automatic retry nothing more is scheduled
- esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:101, 490-498, 529-536 — the scheduler allows 2 concurrent renders; once a render is admitted, its load, the 1 s settle and the snapshot must finish within the 5 s timeout
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/BaseEmailWebView.swift:288-295 and esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:637-647 — the same inline rule twice; FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:94-115 has the javascript/vbscript/file screen, which only the reader and WarmNavigationDelegate (1928) call
- esc-chatmail/Services/EmailDOM/EmailDOMHTMLSanitizer.swift:11-16 — meta, iframe, frame, form, script are removed; esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLDisplayWrapper.swift:125 — CSP script-src/frame-src/form-action 'none' and no img-src limit, so remote images load directly
- esc-chatmail/Platform/LayoutAwareWKWebView.swift:25-31, 47-55 — the base type all four sites share; the one known escape through a preview's permissive .other (a dropped file on the Mac) was fixed here, once, for every kind
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1033-1050 — the pool is capped at 4 and cleared on memory pressure; the fallback web views have neither. The file is 1,938 lines and holds about 18 types

**Trigger.** A chat with several HTML-fallback preview cards opened on a slow network, where remote images keep a snapshot from finishing (load plus the 1 s settle) within the 5 s timeout.

**Impact.** Each failed visible card becomes a live scaled WKWebView, one WebContent process each, and stays that way until its row is unmounted. The count is bounded by the LazyVStack's realized rows (a handful at 120-320 pt per card), not by any app-wide cap. Memory pressure does not release them. Their height is reported 250 ms to 1 s after mount, which AGENTS.md:139 names as a scroll-stability risk. The difference in navigation policy is inert today, and the file's size is a breach of the project's one-type-per-file rule.

**Verifier.** Overstated parts of the original: "share no policy" is wrong, because all four share LayoutAwareWKWebView, CIDSchemeHandler, the base URL resolver and the sanitizer/CSP. Remote-content policy lives in the shared HTML pipeline, not in four configurations. No termination recovery exists anywhere that could diverge. "Unbounded" is really bounded by the viewport. Retry renders are capped at 2, and the timeout starts only once a render is admitted, so queued renders do not time out. Not listed as accepted in scalability-review. AGENTS.md:110 names the fallback as the design, while :131 discourages scaling full HTML in lists.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:333 (PR E spike, "Long chat": one WebContent process per live card, "one more reason to keep snapshots as the normal path"); not in docs/scalability-review.md

**Invariant risks**

- Reader and pool must render byte-identically (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:14-16). A shared factory or delegate base that changes the reader's config breaks adoption. Previews must never inherit navigationDecision's permissive tail: line 148 `return .allow`, x-apple-data-detectors and openExternally.
- Account boundary: a budget that holds web views or queued HTML closures is an account participant. It must drain in cleanupHTMLContent/reopenHTMLContent (AuthSession.swift:402-438). A wait for the budget inside a render must handle cancellation, or the scheduler's close, which awaits running tasks (EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:324-326), hangs sign-out. The reader's makeWebView is synchronous and cannot wait.
- Sign-out clears only WKWebsiteDataStore.default(), under a soft timeout (AuthSession.swift:1013-1031). A factory that adds a custom persistent store, or a shared non-persistent one that outlives the account, escapes that cleanup: cookies and cached remote images carry across accounts.
- The row must keep viewModel.displayHeight from mount (AGENTS.md:139; the transcript's reveal and anchoring cannot absorb a later height change). Any web view a factory makes must stay a LayoutAwareWKWebView with makeNonInteractive (Mac drag refusal, hitTest nil). Fileprivate token values (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:517-519) must stay in their issuer's file.

**Fix.** Skip the app-wide budget and the shared factory and delegate base. 1) In EmailPreviewSnapshotView's didFail branch (lines 43-55), replace MiniEmailWebView with a static card framed at viewModel.displayHeight. Keep the background snapshotLoadTask, so the retry still runs, and keep the enclosing Button, which already opens the reader (EmailContentSection.swift:274-277). That removes the only web views with no cap and no memory-pressure release, and their late height change. It is a visible change, so it needs Kevin's OK. 2) Add a pure EmailPreviewNavigationPolicy (scheme screen, then .other/.reload only) and call it from both preview delegates. 3) Split the manager file by pure moves.

**First step.** Ask Kevin what a failed HTML preview should show. Then, in EmailPreviewSnapshotView.swift:43-55, swap MiniEmailWebView for a static view at .frame(height: viewModel.displayHeight), keeping the background snapshotLoadTask(width:) and its retry identity.

**Pinning test.** repositorySource test: EmailPreviewSnapshotView names no MiniEmailWebView or BaseEmailWebView, and its failed branch is framed at displayHeight. Table test of EmailPreviewNavigationPolicy: javascript:/file: .other cancelled, base-URL .other allowed, .linkActivated/.backForward cancelled. Revert-check comments.

**Payoff.** Removes the only web views with no cap and no memory-pressure release, and their height change after mount. Closes the preview scheme-screen gap without a cross-cutting budget at the account boundary.

## Memory, disk and caches (10)

### `attachments-storage-disk#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**An attachment is one buffered base64-in-JSON response under a 60-second resource timeout: it cannot resume, costs several times its size in memory, and has no concurrency cap**

Area: Attachments, body files and disk lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

getAttachment buffers the whole base64-in-JSON body on the shared read session, which gives any transfer 60 seconds regardless of size, then makes two more full string copies before decoding; the thumbnail is a full bitmap decode of that Data. A timed-out transfer is repeated by the API client (two fit its 120 s budget) and again by the downloader (three rounds): up to six full transfers before `.failed`, and a failed card restarts on its next appearance. The post-sync sweep is serial; only view-driven downloads are uncapped.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient+Attachments.swift:9-13 — performGET decodes the whole AttachmentResponse, then Data(base64UrlEncoded: response.data); no file, no streaming
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:117 — timeoutIntervalForResource = NetworkConfig.resourceTimeout (Constants.swift:247 = 60.0) on the one read session; :367 transport.data(for:) buffers the body; :496-499 the retry loop stops once the next delay exceeds the 120 s budget (Constants.swift:260), which is after the second 60 s transfer
- esc-chatmail/Services/Retry/RetryStrategy.swift:88 — NSURLErrorTimedOut is a retryable connection error, so the API client itself repeats a timed-out attachment transfer (the part the auditor did not trace)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/AttachmentDownloader.swift:979-1000 — a second retry layer (3 attempts, 2 s and 4 s backoff) re-calls the whole download, although the comment at :809-810 says the API client is the single retry owner; :1008 marks the row .failed
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/AttachmentDownloader.swift:602-610 — the post-sync sweep awaits each download in a for loop (serial); :526-542 startDownloadOperation checks only acceptsNewDownloads, and esc-chatmail/Views/Components/Attachments/ImageAttachmentBubble.swift:77-80 starts an unstructured Task per appearing view for queued, failed or missing-file rows
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/APIError.swift:104-112 — two replacingOccurrences copies, a count loop, then the base64 decode; esc-chatmail/Services/Utilities/ImageProcessor.swift:20 and :57 — the thumbnail is made through PlatformImage(data:) and a redraw, a full decode of the image

**Trigger.** An attachment whose base64 JSON (about 1.37 times its size) cannot transfer in 60 seconds: about 5 MB at 1 Mbps, 11 MB at 2 Mbps, under 1 MB on a 128 kbps throttled plan. The missing concurrency cap applies only to view-driven downloads: rows whose files are missing or failed, or a chat opened before the serial sweep reaches it; concurrent downloads then share the link and each still has 60 seconds.

**Impact.** Those attachments end as failed after up to six 60-second transfers (about six minutes and roughly 45 MB of data at 1 Mbps), hold up the serial sweep for that long, and start again when the card reappears. They do arrive on a faster link, so nothing is lost. Transient memory is roughly four to five times the file size plus a full bitmap decode for an image thumbnail; this is arithmetic over the visible copies, not a measurement, and no crash is shown.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited line; the code is as described. Corrections: the API client also repeats timeouts, so six transfers, not three; the post-sync sweep is serial, so the missing cap bites only view-driven downloads; Gmail's JSON attachments.get offers no resume, so the fixable defects are the fixed deadline and buffering. Not in CLAUDE.md or the prior review (its eager-download item is policy, step 12, unbuilt). Lowered to medium: recoverable, memory failure unproven.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1102 attachments-eager-permanent-download (related, known-open, step 12 not built; it covers only sweep policy and network cost). docs/archive/consolidation.md:510-514 claims downloads went to at most 3 attempts, which AttachmentDownloader.swift:978-1001 makes stale.

**Invariant risks**

- Sync body contract. MessageProcessor fetches body parts over 25 KB through the same getAttachment. It treats APIError.invalidData and decodingError as deterministic (the message persists without the part) and every other error as a failure that freezes the cursor (MessageProcessor.swift:691-697, :756-769). Changing getAttachment, its errors, or the shared read session's 60 s resource timeout (GmailAPIClient.swift:114-121) changes that contract and lengthens the exclusive sync run under BGAppRefresh. Any new decode error or disk error needs an explicit bucket.
- Account boundary. Every download runs inside a registered startDownloadOperation, which cancelAndAwaitAllDownloads drains while the auth gate is held (AttachmentDownloader.swift:513-542). A background URLSession outlives that drain and can deliver account A's bytes after the next sign-in. Staging files must sit in Attachments/, which sign-out renames whole and the orphan sweep reaps. They must never be left in tmp (CLAUDE.md's rule for Opened copies). The URLSession temp file must be moved at once, and rollbackPartialDownload (:1223) must remove the staging files.
- A file's presence means it is valid. saveData writes atomically because needsRedownload trusts any file it finds (AttachmentPaths.swift:325-339). A streamed decode must write to a staging file and then rename it into place, then call applyBackupPolicy(toFileAt:). Staging names must not start with remote_ or local_, because isRedownloadable and isStoredUnderLocalID judge a file by its name. The scaled timeout must stay under orphanSweepRecentFileGracePeriod (1 h, :403).
- Wedges from the cap and the retry engine. A slot wait must resume when its task or its generation is cancelled. A slot must never be held across the nested recovery operation (:1042) or across waitForActiveDownload (:739), or teardown hangs. CID reads (downloadAttachmentData) must not queue behind the sweep. The file path must keep the 401 refresh, the 429 pacing and classify403 (GmailAPIClient.swift:372-469). Its session must be derived from the injected session's configuration, as sendSession is (:148-152), or StubURLProtocol tests reach the real network.

**Fix.** Keep getAttachment and the read session as they are: sync's body-part fetches depend on their errors. Add a protocol requirement, used only by AttachmentDownloader, that downloads to a file. It runs on a session derived from the injected session's configuration, with a resource timeout of clamp(60 s + 1.4×byteSize at 16 KB/s, 20 min). It goes through performRetryingRequest, with the transport parameterized and non-2xx bodies read back for classify403. Move the file into Attachments/incoming_<UUID>. Decode the "data" string in chunks into a second staging file, rename it atomically, then applyBackupPolicy. An undecodable body maps to APIError.invalidData. Remove the downloader's own retry. Limit the network and decode step to two cancellable slots, user requests first. No background URLSession.

**First step.** Delete the catch-block retry recursion in downloadAttachmentWithRetry (:978-1001) and keep its .failed write. GmailAPIClient then becomes the single retry owner the comment at :809 claims. Update testDownloadFailureAfterRetryBudgetMarksFailedAndCleansInFlight to expect one client call.

**Pinning test.** Real-client StubURLProtocol tests: resource timeout scales with byteSize and the stub's protocol classes carry over; the chunked decode equals Data(base64UrlEncoded:) across split quartets and escapes; cancelAndAwaitAllDownloads leaves no incoming_ file; a timeout costs one client call.

**Payoff.** Large attachments on slow or throttled links finish instead of ending failed after up to six restarts. Memory per download falls from several times the file's size to a fixed buffer.

### `attachments-storage-disk#3` · medium · scalability · effort L · known-open

**Disk use still has no ceiling: every attachment is downloaded eagerly on any network, and nothing evicts bodies, originals or previews**

Area: Attachments, body files and disk lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Mechanism holds; severity lowered. Every received attachment row is created queued with byteSize known, and the post-sync sweep (foreground and background runs) downloads each in turn with no size, type, network-cost or Low Data Mode test. Its only free-space guard is upstream: a sync run is refused under 200 MB free, but a started sweep never re-checks. Images of 1600 px or less are written twice. Bodies and files leave only with their row, the orphan sweeps or sign-out. No budget eviction, no storage UI.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:319-320 — byteSize set from info.size, then stateRaw set to "queued" for every attachment row; the only caller is MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:515
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/AttachmentDownloader.swift:577 and :602-610 — sweep fetches stateRaw == queued (or local_inline_) and calls performDownloadAttachment per row; :811 apiClient.getAttachment is reached with no size, type, path or free-space check in between
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:486 — schedulePendingAttachmentDownloads after every incremental run, the path performIncrementalSyncForBackground (:281-289) also uses; :504-508 storageAdmission refuses a run under 200 MB (SyncStorageBackoff.swift:42-50), the only free-space test upstream of the sweep
- esc-chatmail/Services/Utilities/ImageProcessor.swift:32-36 — scale >= 1.0 returns the input data; AttachmentDownloader.swift:864-866 saves that as the preview file beside the original
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:607 and :625 — calculateStorageSize and cleanupOldFiles defined; git grep finds no caller. Removal call sites are CacheCoordinator.swift:65 (deleted rows), DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:87 and :138 (orphans), AuthSession.swift:407 (sign-out)
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:115-119 — URLSessionConfiguration.default with no expensive/constrained restriction; SyncHelpers.swift:177-180 reads path.isExpensive only to log it; docs/scalability-review.md:1625 — step 12 carries no Built entry

**Trigger.** Any sync that persists a message with attachments, foreground or background, on any network path including cellular and Low Data Mode; disk growth is linear in mail received since sign-in, from S1 on.

**Impact.** App storage grows with every message and attachment received and is never trimmed while the row exists (the prior review's 9-17 GB at S2 is an unmeasured estimate). The only way to reclaim it is sign-out, which resets the local mailbox to the sign-in moment. Attachments the user never opens are downloaded over cellular. No failure by itself: a full disk is handled by the 200 MB sync gate and failed-write states.

**Verifier.** All six cited locations match today's code. Searched for a download policy, eviction, age pruning, network-cost or free-space checks and a storage screen: none, except the sync admission gate at 200 MB, which the auditor missed. Not a documented decision; step 12 is unbuilt. Lowered to medium: linear cost, no loss or failure, sizes unmeasured, and a mailbox starts empty at sign-in so growth follows incoming mail. The prior review filed it under "Will degrade".

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md `attachments-eager-permanent-download` (line 1104) and `html-bodies-no-retention` (line 1078, with its review correction at 1088); Suggested order step 12 "Add retention tiers" (line 1625), which has no Built entry

**Invariant risks**

- Rows the policy skips must not stay `queued`. Attachment has no fetchIndex (ESCChatmail 6 contents:10-25), and on every sync the sweep re-reads every queued row and faults in its message (AttachmentDownloader.swift:574-598). Eviction 'back to queued' (review line 1112) would also be downloaded again by the next sweep.
- Layout is reserved from metadata. A CID image with no dimensions is drawn .collapsed while queued (InlineImagePresentationPolicy.swift:20), and dimensions and state feed the bubble's analysis fingerprint (MessageBubbleModels.swift:58). Deferring CID images, or clearing width/height/pageCount on eviction, changes row heights after mount.
- Forward copies only files already on disk: a missing inline attachment fails the whole setup, and a missing regular one is silently skipped (ComposeViewModel.swift:201-220, ComposeAttachmentManager.swift:204-208). Skipping the preview write blanks image bubbles, because AttachmentThumbnailLoader.load reads only previewPath (:90-96).
- Fences on eviction and unlinking. Never touch local_ or local_inline_ files (AttachmentPaths.isRedownloadable). Run eviction as a registered download operation inside the daily .maintenance run, with a Mac tripwire case. Save the row before the unlink, and unlink through AttachmentCacheActor's generation check plus DeletedRowFileReclamation's two checks. calculateStorageSize holds the HTML boundary lock for its whole walk (HTMLContentHandler.swift:607-608), and OutboundNetworkPathMonitor (the send gate) must stay as it is.

**Fix.** Ship in three phases. Phase 1, with no model version: a pure AttachmentAutoDownloadPolicy gates the post-sync sweep. The sweep does not run on expensive or constrained paths (use a separate path reader and leave OutboundNetworkPathMonitor alone), does not run from an app refresh, and stops below a free-space floor re-read before each download. CID images and other images under a cap stay eager. Rows over the cap, video and archives are created with a new stateRaw "remote": the views' download-on-appear checks accept it and the sweep's predicate excludes it. Forward downloads missing files first. An unchanged preview is written as a clone, not left as a nil previewURL. Phase 2: age-budgeted eviction to "remote" in the daily maintenance run. Phase 3: bodies, only after ESCChatmail 7 adds bodyEvicted.

**First step.** Inject a path-cost reader and a free-bytes reader into AttachmentDownloader. Have enqueueAllPendingAttachments return early on expensive or constrained paths, and stop below a floor re-read before each download. Skip the sweep after an app refresh, following allowsStoreMaintenance. Change no row states.

**Pinning test.** In AttachmentDownloaderTests, the sweep makes no MockGmailAPIClient.getAttachment calls on a path the injected reader reports as expensive or constrained, and the rows stay queued. It downloads them on an unrestricted path, and downloadAttachmentIfNeeded ignores the gate. Revert-check: the policy check in enqueueAllPendingAttachments.

**Payoff.** Stops cellular and background downloads of attachments nobody opens, keeps the sweep from eating the sync's free-space margin, and removes duplicate previews. Later phases stop disk use growing linearly at S2.

### `attachments-storage-disk#5` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**Full-disk handling stops at the sync boundary: the attachment pipeline has no free-space floor, cannot tell out of space from any other failure, and drops inline parts silently**

Area: Attachments, body files and disk lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Sync has a 200 MB admission gate and aborts the run on an out-of-space body write. The attachment side has neither. Every synced row starts queued, and the post-sync sweep fetches each one with no free-space or size check. saveData returns a bare Bool, so a full-disk write only marks the row failed and the loop moves on. An inline part whose write fails has its row deleted, with no verdict returned. The message is still inserted, and no recovery path exists without the row.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/AttachmentPaths.swift:325 — saveData returns Bool; the catch at :340 logs the error and returns false, so the cause is lost. git grep finds no StoreVolumeFreeSpace or StorageErrorClassifier reference under Services/Attachments
- esc-chatmail/Services/Attachments/AttachmentDownloader.swift:602 — the sweep loops over rows fetched by the queued-or-local_inline_ predicate (:577) with no space check; :811 fetches the whole attachment, :845 writes it, :908 sets .failed when the write failed
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:486 — schedulePendingAttachmentDownloads runs only after performSync returned, so only after an admitted, successful run (admission at :421); InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:242 does the same
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Helpers.swift:525 — context.delete(attachment) plus a warning when persistInlineAttachmentData fails (:571); createAttachment returns Void, so createNewMessage (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:176) cannot give a verdict
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Creation.swift:51 — the body write comes first and throws on failure (:53); MessagePersister.swift:657 maps out-of-space to SyncResourceAbort.insufficientStorage, the contract the inline part lacks
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/Attachments/DocumentAttachmentCard.swift:181 — a .failed row is downloaded again when its view appears, so failed rows heal on view, not through the sweep; SyncReconciliation.swift:529 skips IDs already stored, so a dropped inline row is not recreated by reconciliation

**Trigger.** A device near full. Either a sync admitted just above 200 MB free brings large attachments, or a queued backlog is still downloading when space runs out. The inline drop needs the inline write to fail while the body write before it and the store save after it both succeed.

**Impact.** Eager attachment downloads can take free space from 200 MB to near zero, after which sync is refused until the user frees space. Each row still queued in that sweep is downloaded and discarded once, then left failed until its bubble is viewed; while the disk stays full, each viewing downloads and discards it again. An inline image can go missing silently and stay missing, because recovery needs the deleted row.

**Verifier.** All cited lines match today's code. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or docs/scalability-review.md marks this as deliberate; step 6 has no built note and lazy download (step 12) is unbuilt. Bounds the auditor missed: the discard is one pass per backlog, not a loop, and views retry failed rows. On a truly full disk the inline drop is a narrow window; a failed save rolls it back. Nothing was run.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md "Suggested order" step 6 "Handle a full disk end to end" (line 1562). It is built in code for bodies and sync only (commits 981f47ee, 6e32394), and the doc has no Built note for it. `attachments-eager-permanent-download` (line 1104, step 12) is not built. The inline-row drop and saveData's Bool are new.

**Invariant risks**

- Never throw an inline-write verdict from inside a context.perform. In createNewMessage the message is already inserted (MessagePersister+Creation.swift:89); in the update path the row is already mutated (MessagePersister+Updates.swift:502). Only orchestrator save points save and nothing rolls back one message, so a .failed verdict would still commit the half-built row. Decide before inserting, as the body write does (Creation.swift:49-54).
- A write failure must not enter downloadAttachmentWithRetry's catch (AttachmentDownloader.swift:962-1001). That would download the attachment 3 more times with backoff, a second retry loop where :809 says the API client is the only retry owner. Out of space must end the sweep without touching retryAttempts or marking the row .failed.
- Applying the body contract (any other I/O error means .failed) to inline parts would freeze the cursor and spend escape-hatch strikes, though local_inline_ rows already have a recovery owner: the sweep predicate (:578) feeds them to SynthesizedInlineAttachmentRecovery. Making saveData throw churns about 27 test call sites, and the per-write backup mark (BackupExclusion rule) must stay in the one writer.
- The floor must stay inside the registered download operation, which cancelAndAwaitAllDownloads drains, and add no account-scoped state that needs a reset. It must read free space off the main actor (AttachmentDownloader is @MainActor and the volume query was never timed). It must leave at least StoreVolumeFreeSpace.lowStorageThresholdBytes free, or prefetch starves sync admission.

**Fix.** Add AttachmentPaths.writeData(_:to:) returning AttachmentWriteResult (.saved, .outOfSpace or .ioError, classified by StorageErrorClassifier.isOutOfSpace) and keep the backup mark in it. saveData becomes a Bool wrapper over it. In the downloader, inject availableStorageBytes. Before each sweep fetch, stop when available minus byteSize is below 2× lowStorageThresholdBytes; a nil reading stops the sweep. On-view downloads check byteSize plus a small floor. On .outOfSpace, remove the file, leave the row .queued, end the sweep and never retry. In the persister, stop deleting an inline row whose write failed: keep it .queued with no localURL, so local_inline_ recovery heals it. On the create path, write inline parts next to the body write, before routing and insertion, and throw MessageBodyWriteFailure.outOfSpace.

**First step.** Add AttachmentPaths.writeData returning a classified AttachmentWriteResult and make saveData its Bool wrapper, with the backup mark unchanged. Change createAttachment to keep a failed inline row .queued with no localURL, not context.delete it. This stops the permanent loss.

**Pinning test.** AttachmentDownloaderTests: with injected free space below the floor, enqueueAllPendingAttachments calls getAttachment zero times and rows stay .queued; an injected .outOfSpace write stops the sweep after one call, with no retry. MessagePersister: a failed inline write persists a queued local_inline_ row.

**Payoff.** Eager prefetch can no longer push free space below sync's 200 MB admission and stop new mail. A full disk no longer downloads and discards attachments, and inline images no longer go missing for good.

### `attachments-storage-disk#6` · medium · performance · effort S · known-open

**The daily body-file sweep still walks the whole Messages directory on the main actor, under the lock every body read and every save takes, and on the Mac it runs inside the open app**

Area: Attachments, body files and disk lifecycle. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

The daily cleanup's HTML sweep is a static member of a @MainActor class and is not nonisolated. After an off-main fetch of every Message id into one Set, it returns to the main actor and calls HTMLContentHandler.cleanupOrphanedFiles synchronously: one contentsOfDirectory of the flat Messages directory plus a per-file check and unlink, all in a single hold of the boundary's NSRecursiveLock, with no cancellation check. Body loads and every context's save notification take that lock. On the Mac the job runs as an in-process activity of the open app.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/DatabaseMaintenance/DatabaseMaintenanceService.swift:6 — `@MainActor` on the class; DatabaseMaintenanceService+Cleanup.swift:114 `static func cleanupOrphanedHTMLFiles` carries no `nonisolated` (its neighbour at :94 does), fetches all ids into a Set at :127-130 inside context.perform, then calls `htmlContentHandler.cleanupOrphanedFiles` synchronously at :138
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:658-667 — one `accountBoundary.perform` wraps `contentsOfDirectory` (:659) and the whole per-file loop with removeItem (:664); no chunking, no Task.isCancelled; FileSystemErrorHandler.swift:251 materializes the full [URL] listing
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:15 — single NSRecursiveLock; :298 loadHTML, :253 saveHTMLResult, :503/:513/:533/:552 the exists and signature reads all go through `accountBoundary.perform`
- esc-chatmail/Services/Caching/CacheCoordinator.swift:138-148 — the NSManagedObjectContextDidSave publisher (object nil in the app) calls `HTMLContentHandler.shared.captureAccountGeneration()` on the posting queue, which takes the same lock (HTMLContentHandler.swift:19-23)
- esc-chatmail/Platform/BackgroundActivityTaskRegistry.swift:43-46, 110-117, 147 — activities live only in this process; the block hops to `Task { @MainActor in }` and awaits the handler; Services/Background/BackgroundActivitySchedulePolicy.swift:20, 46-49 — earliest run is 15 minutes after scheduling plus up to 60 minutes of tolerance; App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:219-220 schedules it at every launch
