- esc-chatmail/Platform/ExternalURLOpener.swift:45 — iOS opens a URL outside the shared list whenever systemCanOpen accepts it; esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/EmailLinkSchemePolicy.swift:26 — the note records that canOpenURL accepts shortcuts:, smb:, app-settings: and the app's own OAuth redirect scheme, and that "Only the Mac enforces that"

**Trigger.** A later change of entitlement or capability: Xcode's Data Protection capability defaults to Complete, which would lock the store and bodies away from locked-device BGAppRefresh and BGProcessing runs, and no test or declaration would catch it. Separately, a user on iOS taps a crafted link in an email using a scheme an Apple app owns.

**Impact.** No user-visible failure today. The cost is drift. The file protection class is implicit while the keychain's is explicit. An unused push privilege ships in every build. The refresh token sits in two app keychain items nobody reads (same class and access group as the SDK's copy, so this is hygiene, not wider exposure). The iOS link gate stays wider than the Mac's. NSAllowsLocalNetworking is dead config, not a privilege.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited line. Corrections: (1) NSAllowsLocalNetworking does nothing at a 17.x deployment target (from Apple's ATS documentation, not measured). (2) The locked-background requirement is stated, at the keychain (TokenManager:350), and the store-load policy accounts for data protection; only the file class is undeclared. (3) docs/mac-app-plan.md:122 already notes aps-environment is unused. (4) The iOS scheme gap is a known, recorded open item, not new. The default protection class is inferred; no device was inspected.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md:122 (Phase 0, Entitlements: aps-environment recorded as unused). The iOS link width is documented only in esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/EmailLinkSchemePolicy.swift:26-33. Neither docs/scalability-review.md nor CLAUDE.md mentions any of the five parts.

**Invariant risks**

- NSPersistentStoreFileProtectionKey is API_UNAVAILABLE(macosx) (macOS SDK CoreData NSPersistentStoreCoordinator.h:166), so setting it outside #if os(iOS) breaks CI's Build (macOS). Any class stricter than completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication would lock the store and bodies away from locked-device BGAppRefresh/BGProcessing runs, and CoreDataErrorClassifier.swift:83 would keep latching them as keepStore. Xcode's Data Protection capability defaults to Complete, which is exactly such a class.
- TokenManager's writer discipline (TokenManager.swift:338-362): keychain writes and deletes stay inside cacheLock alongside the ungated epoch bump. The delete of the legacy item must be best-effort: if it throws, a keychain refusal fails persistSessionForBackgroundAccess's credentialCleanupRequired transaction (AuthSession.swift:1358) and the sign-in is rejected. .googleRefreshToken must stay in clearTokens and in hasPersistedBackgroundCredentialMaterial (AuthSession.swift:1269), or a leftover item on an upgraded device escapes orphan cleanup.
- Info.plist cleanup must keep the fetch and processing background modes and every BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers entry. That includes the retired com.esc.inboxchat.database.vacuum, because BGTaskScheduler raises on an identifier that has no handler.
- Applying the Mac allow-list wholesale on iOS stops webcal:, itms-apps: and maps: links. That is a product decision nobody has made, and it inverts ExternalURLOpenerTests.testOpen_oniOS_otherScheme_systemAccepts_reachesSystem. Any HTML write change (String.write has no protection option) must stay atomic and inside accountBoundary.perform, because DeletedRowFileReclamation reads the file's date under that lock.

**Fix.** Five small commits, behavior-neutral first. 1) Under #if os(iOS), set NSPersistentStoreFileProtectionKey to completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication (already Core Data's documented default) through an extracted, testable description configurator. Pin the entitlement file instead of threading write options through ~10 file sites, and test the configuration, not an attribute read back on the simulator. 2) Remove aps-environment and remote-notification. 3) Drop NSAllowsLocalNetworking from both plists. 4) Stop persisting the refresh token (nil in TokenInfo, no separate item) and delete the legacy item best-effort inside cacheLock. Keep the key in clearTokens and in the presence probe. 5) On iOS, refuse the app's own URL schemes before canOpenURL. Leave the wider allow-list to Kevin.

**First step.** Add a source-pinning suite asserting today's values: no default-data-protection entitlement, or only CUFUA. Then extract CoreDataStack's description setup and set NSPersistentStoreFileProtectionKey under #if os(iOS). Build iOS, then run codex-build.sh --for-testing on macOS.

**Pinning test.** A repositorySource suite that parses the plists: entitlement absent or CUFUA, iOS store option CUFUA, no aps-environment, remote-notification or NSAllowsLocalNetworking. TokenManagerTests changes from asserting the refresh token is persisted to asserting it never is and the legacy item is deleted. ExternalURLOpenerTests adds: own redirect scheme refused on iOS.

**Payoff.** Pins the protection class so a future Data Protection capability cannot break locked-device background sync; drops an unused push privilege, a dead ATS key and a redundant refresh-token copy.

### `web-content-rendering#5` · low · security · effort M · new

**Remote subresources load directly through WebKit, outside the app's SSRF and privacy boundary**

Area: WKWebView email rendering and reader. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

No app-side control governs WebKit's own subresource loads. The wrapper CSP omits img-src, font-src and default-src, the src pass checks scheme only, and no web view sets a content rule list or data store, so remote images, fonts and CSS url() images load with no private-host check. This is a recorded choice in code comments, not an oversight. The uncovered parts: the private-network rule stops at app-side fetches, and the visible-row pre-render loads the unstripped original, so trackers the preview path removes still fire.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLDisplayWrapper.swift:125 and :403 — the only CSP in the app: script-src, object-src, frame-src, style-src 'unsafe-inline', form-action, base-uri; no img-src, font-src, media-src or default-src
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentLoader+SourcePreparation.swift:89-102 — comment states 'Remote http(s) images load directly via WebKit when possible'; the preferHTML original path runs only the active-markup strip and the href/src scheme pass, skipping the tracking remover and CSS sanitizer that sanitize() applies (HTMLSanitizerService.swift:82-86)
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLSanitization/HTMLURLSanitizer.swift:5-7 and :177-179 — allowlist is by scheme (http, https, mailto, tel, cid) with no host check; comment 'Allow all other URLs including tracking pixels and newsletter images'
- esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/EmailContentSection.swift:107-142 — .task warms the full original 200 ms after a rich-HTML bubble is visible, passing a width; esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1183-1193 and :1696-1722 then build an off-screen WKWebView (pool capacity 4, :1034) and loadHTMLString with the sender-domain base URL. The section is mounted only from esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/MessageContentView.swift:55
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:19-28, esc-chatmail/Views/Components/EmailContent/BaseEmailWebView.swift:53-59, esc-chatmail/Services/Preview/EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:442-447 — configurations set the cid handler and JavaScript off; none sets websiteDataStore or a content rule list. PrivateNetworkAddressDetector is applied to link taps only (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:141-144)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1001-1002 and :1026-1031 — comment 'Every web view uses the default, persistent data store, so remote images and cookies of the mail that was read stay in it'; emptied at sign-out. esc-chatmail/Resources/Info.plist:65-68 — NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent and NSAllowsLocalNetworking true. EmailSenderBaseURLResolver.swift:14-22 — base URL https://<From domain>/, nil (about:blank) for a dotless domain

**Trigger.** A rich-HTML message row resting about 200 ms on screen in an open chat (off-screen pre-render of the original, up to 4 pooled), an HTML snapshot preview on a cache miss, or opening the reader. Nothing loads from the conversation list or during sync.

**Impact.** Each sender of a displayed rich email gets the device's IP address and a display signal, including from tracking pixels the preview path strips. A crafted email can make WebKit attempt blind GETs to loopback or private hosts; JavaScript is off, so no response is readable. Whether such a request goes out depends on WebKit's mixed-content rules and the OS Local Network prompt, which were not measured. Cookies persist only until sign-out.

**Verifier.** Opened every cited site; all are as described. Not refuted: no img-src, rule list or non-persistent store exists anywhere. Corrected: remote loading is documented as deliberate in code; "without the mail being opened" is wrong, since rows load only in an open chat; external stylesheets are blocked (link removed, style-src inline only). Private-host reachability and cookie behaviour depend on WebKit and were not run. Severity lowered: blind GETs only, no measured failure. docs/scalability-review.md does not cover it.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md Conventions, "Untrusted URLs from email content": the rule covers app-side fetches only, and no item in docs/scalability-review.md or docs/mac-app-plan.md covers WebKit subresource loads

**Invariant risks**

- Adoption parity. FullInteractiveEmailWebView.makeConfiguration (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:14-28) is shared so that a pre-rendered pool web view renders byte-identically to the live reader (FullEmailReaderWebView.swift:39-40, pool :1697). If a rule list or data store reaches only one path, or a lazy compile races the pool, the reader flashes when it adopts the pre-rendered view. FullEmailWebViewPreRenderKey (:251-271) does not key on configuration.
- Never run sanitize()'s tracking remover or CSS sanitizer, and never put a URL-rewriting proxy (a custom scheme through SSRFGuardingURLSession) on the preferHTML original path. HTMLContentLoader+SourcePreparation.swift:89-99 records that those rewrites corrupt nested-table HTML. The sender-domain base URL exists for CDNs that check the Referer (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:52-56).
- Row height after mount. Blocked or tap-to-load images in inline cards and snapshots change a card's height after it mounts, which the transcript cannot absorb (CLAUDE.md Traps). Snapshot keys hash the rendered HTML, not the configuration (EmailPreviewSnapshotCache.swift:21-35). A rule-list change therefore needs a CacheVersioning.previewSnapshotRendererVersion bump.
- Account boundary and the Mac test host. A shared nonPersistent store is account state. It must be swapped in AuthSession.clearWebViewData, after cleanupHTMLContent has drained the pool and the snapshot renderer (AuthSession.swift:414-420, 1623, 1637), and the default-store removal must stay under its soft timeout (:1013-1031). Tests must use WKContentRuleListStore(url:) in a temp directory, because the Mac host's container is real.

**Fix.** Block at WebKit's network layer; never rewrite markup. One factory compiles a versioned WKContentRuleList (injected WKContentRuleListStore) blocking loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT and ULA literals, localhost, .local and HTMLTrackingRemover's tracker domains from one shared list, and attaches it inside FullInteractiveEmailWebView.makeConfiguration (pool and reader together), BaseEmailWebView and the snapshot session; pool warms and snapshots await compilation, the synchronous reader takes it once compiled. Bump previewSnapshotRendererVersion. Next, one CSP constant for both wrapper copies: default-src 'none', img-src/font-src/media-src https: data: cid:, upgrade-insecure-requests (upgrade, not block, http). Extend CLAUDE.md's untrusted-URL rule. A nonPersistent store, dropping the visible-row WebView pre-render, and remote-image consent (reader only) are product calls.

**First step.** Add the hosted pinning test against today's code: a loopback NWListener and a wrapped page with an http://127.0.0.1 image loaded through FullInteractiveEmailWebView.makeConfiguration; confirm a connection arrives (WebKit's behavior is unmeasured), then attach the compiled rule list.

**Pinning test.** Hosted test in both plans: a 127.0.0.1 NWListener receives no connection from a page built by each factory (reader, pool, preview, snapshot) with a temp-dir rule store, while a control without the list does. Revert-check: the list's add(_:).

**Payoff.** Email markup can no longer make WebKit reach loopback or LAN literal hosts, and known tracker pixels stop firing from the unstripped original and pre-render, with no markup rewrite.

## Contacts and Person records (5)

### `contacts-person#2` · medium · performance · effort M · known-open

**Contacts is still six full-scan call sites behind five private CNContactStores; step 13 is unbuilt and contact linking added another scan**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

ContactsResolver.lookup strips the dots and +tags from a Gmail address before it runs the predicate search. Any Gmail address that is not on a card in that exact form then falls through to a full address-book enumeration that fetches thumbnail data. That enumeration runs synchronously on the actor, and a miss is never cached. Lookup is called by every received chat bubble, every rollup build (300 s TTL), sender grouping and prewarm, and these calls queue behind the background photo prefetch. Photos are negative-cached for 24 h. Three walks that fetch only email keys (self-alias, link store, filter set) and autocomplete's thumbnail pass each enumerate separately. Step 13 has not been built.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactSearchService.swift:29-41,54-58 — the predicate runs on the already-normalized address (EmailNormalizer.swift:14-21 strips dots and +tags). A Gmail miss falls through to an unpredicated enumerateContacts whose keys (15-25) include thumbnail and formatter data
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactsResolver.swift:147-173,203-211 — lookup and prewarm cache only a match, so a Gmail address on no card is enumerated again on every call
- esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/MessageBubbleLoader.swift:47-48 with esc-chatmail/ViewModels/MessageBubbleViewModel.swift:93-114 and esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/ChatMessageRowModel.swift:311-321 — the load of every received bubble calls lookup, and the loaded content is applied only after the sender result arrives
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantInfoResolver.swift:90-94 with esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantLoader.swift:31 — each rollup build looks up every participant, and rollups expire after 300 s
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ProfilePhotoResolver.swift:121-124,172-183,302-303 with ContactSearchService.swift:148-151 — photos (misses included) are cached for 24 h, so the thumbnail scan for a batch of more than 10 runs only on the uncached delta. Each remaining miss still goes through lookup
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:71-77,100-104 with ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:106-127, PersonCache.swift:271-274, ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:161-178,271-287, ConversationFilterService.swift:167-176, esc-chatmail/Models/ContactsService.swift:166-205 and docs/scalability-review.md:1626 — independent walks of email keys only (self-alias when the user's own Gmail address is on no card, the link store once per process and per change, the filter set on each change) plus autocomplete's unpredicated thumbnail pass. Step 13 has no Built entry

**Trigger.** A Gmail correspondent whose address is on no contact card, or a Gmail contact stored with other dots or a +tag before its first hit, with an address book of hundreds to thousands of cards. It fires on opening or scrolling that person's chat, on a list row rebuilding after 5 minutes or after a new message, and on any CNContactStoreDidChange.

**Impact.** For these senders, names, avatars and sender grouping resolve late. Each mounted received bubble costs one full thumbnail scan, and the scans run serially on the actor that every other lookup also uses. Nothing expires these misses, so the Contacts I/O repeats. Nothing fails, and the cost does not depend on mailbox size. The claim that a cold app refresh spends its 30 s budget on these walks is not supported. The walks on the sync path fetch email keys only: the link store walks once per process, and the self-alias walk runs only when the user's own Gmail address is unresolved. The thumbnail scans during a refresh are detached background-priority prefetches, run once per address per process.

**Verifier.** I confirmed every cited site, and step 13 has no Built entry. Corrections: autocomplete makes one unpredicated thumbnail pass per 150 ms-debounced query, not two (the first pass is name-predicated), and superseded scans are not cancelled. The filter re-walk runs once per launch and on each CNContactStoreDidChange. ProfilePhotoResolver's 24 h cache, misses included, bounds the batch path. The auditor missed the bubble path (MessageBubbleLoader), the heaviest one. I lowered severity to medium: the effect is cosmetic latency, the cost is unmeasured, and the prior review rated it degrades.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1337 contacts-resolver-full-enumeration; :1626 step 13 (no Built entry); related open items :1310 self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist (review correction :1322) and :1362 compose-autocomplete-full-scan-per-keystroke

**Invariant risks**

- Self-aliases feed participant hashing. GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:106 awaits getAliases inside the cleanup-sensitive gate. ContactsSelfAliasProvider.swift:92-114 runs predicates first and enumerates only for unresolved Gmail targets. Routing it through the index changes which cards count as self, so new mail hashes away from the stored chats (a fork). The send would also wait behind bubble lookups on the resolver actor.
- ContactLinkedAddressStore has a contract (ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:15-33,161-200). It adopts in one synchronous place, inside the gate-held cleanup of the sync run (DataCleanupService+ContactUnification.swift:49). A failed read is never an empty map. Withdrawn access drops the map. It is not an account participant. Feeding it from the async, account-fenced resolver breaks one of these. So does removing its own CNContactStore, which it keeps so CNContactStoreDidChange is delivered (:264-267).
- Account boundary: ContactsResolver is a participant (AuthSession.swift:229-243). A new miss cache and index must be cleared in invalidateAllCache and closeAccountWorkAndClear. They must be built inside beginAccountOperation, or in a stored task that close cancels and awaits. ParticipantCacheAccountBoundaryTests pins a re-ask after reopen, and updatePerson must stay generation-fenced.
- Staleness and churn. The resolver observes no CNContactStoreDidChange itself: ChatMessagesCoordinator and ParticipantsListView clear its cache, and ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator.swift:84-91 does so only on a status change. So an unfenced miss outlives a contact the user adds. Fencing hits on every change reruns the unconditional write in AvatarStorage.saveAvatar (AvatarStorage.swift:38-52). Keep the card findBestContact picks: contactIdentifier keys participant dedup and grouping (ParticipantInfoResolver.swift:57,123-128).

**Fix.** Scope it to ContactsResolver. (1) Add a lock-guarded contacts generation, bumped by the resolver's own CNContactStoreDidChange observer (injected center), an auth-status change, invalidateCache(for:) and invalidateAllCache. (2) Cache misses stamped with it, only when authorized. (3) Build lazily, inside an admitted operation, an email-keys-only index: normalized email to identifiers and labels in enumeration order. It replaces searchContactByEnumeration and the >10 batch scan; fetch name/thumbnail by identifier. Keep the predicate fast path and findBestContact's choice; clear both on close. Leave the link store, filter set and self-alias provider alone; instead apply the AliasManager validity correction and skip unchanged avatar writes. Autocomplete stays its own item.

**First step.** Give ContactsResolver an injectable contact-store seam (unifiedContacts, enumerateContacts, unifiedContact(withIdentifier:)) and NotificationCenter, defaulting to CNContactStore and .default, plus a counting fake in ContactsResolverTests; land the generation-stamped negative cache first, before the index.

**Pinning test.** ContactsResolverTests, counting fake store: repeated lookups of a Gmail address on no card enumerate once; CNContactStoreDidChange on the injected center, or close and reopen, makes the next lookup ask again; a dotted-Gmail card resolves to the old enumeration's identifier. Revert-checked.

**Payoff.** Gmail senders not in Contacts stop costing a thumbnail scan per bubble mount, rollup rebuild and prewarm; names, avatars and grouping stop queueing behind serialized scans on the resolver actor.

### `contacts-person#3` · medium · scalability · effort M · new

**Contact unification is all-or-nothing: one unbounded transaction inside the sync run under the send gate, and one anchored chat keeps the whole delta re-read every sync**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The pass runs inside the cleanup gate, in every incremental sync and before .syncCompleted. When the adopted map differs from the applied one, it rehashes and merges every conversation in scope in one uncancellable perform with one save. Each merge reads every message of both conversations and each message's labels one row at a time. While a pass is blocked, later syncs re-read the scope but rewrite nothing and merge nothing. Each process's first sync also walks the address book under the gate.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+ContactUnification.swift:49-78 — refreshIfNeeded, then the scoped repair; only .completed calls markAppliedToConversations
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:234-251 and IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:527-531 — the pass is first in the performCleanupSensitiveMutation hold, awaited before .syncCompleted; GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:54 and ChatViewModel.swift:1184 wait on the same gate
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Cleanup/DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:97-299,382,393-401 — one perform and one save (274-285); only participants are prefetched; every distinct Person.email is fetched and normalized
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationMerger.swift:252-253,265-277 and ConversationRollupSnapshot.swift:27-28 — messages?.count for each candidate, each loser message reassigned, then labels read for every message of winner and loser
- esc-chatmail/Services/Models/Conversation+Extensions.swift:40-43 and DataCleanupService+Migration.swift:180-184,232-235 — the type and hash writes are skipped when unchanged, so a blocked re-run writes and saves nothing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:161-183,271-281 — a synchronous enumerateContacts on the first call of each process and after every CNContactStoreDidChange

**Trigger.** The adopted map differs from the applied one. This happens on the upgrade to linking (once), when access is granted late or withdrawn, when contacts are imported in bulk, or when one card edit links two addresses of a heavy correspondent. The S2 store's largest chat holds 20,000 messages.

**Impact.** The sync that applies a large delta, or that merges a large chat, holds the gate for an estimated one to a few seconds (not measured). Reply bubbles and draft saves wait that long and .syncCompleted posts late. Under app refresh the pass takes part of the 30 s budget and cannot be cancelled, and a kill before the single save repeats all of it. While a pass is blocked, each sync pays only a read: a scan of the Person table and the scoped fetch, roughly tens of milliseconds (an estimate).

**Verifier.** Code is as cited. One citation was off: the messages?.count reads are at ConversationMerger.swift:252-253, not 249-250. Corrected: a blocked re-run repeats no merges and no writes (guarded setters, idempotent hashes), and a kill under app refresh at S2 is unlikely. The pass was added after the scalability review, which moved only the maintenance invocation off the sync path. Caution: CLAUDE.md requires the rehash to be atomic with adoption, so only merges and row folding can be deferred, not the per-group rehash the recommendation proposes.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md "One chat per contact" (adopt only in unifyConversationsByContactIfNeeded, under the held gate). Related, not this pass: docs/scalability-review.md participant-split-migration-walk fix (2), and rollup-full-conversation-materialization (step 11, not built)

**Invariant risks**

- The new map, and the drop when Contacts access is withdrawn, must be adopted inside the cleanup hold together with every hash rewrite (ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:15-21, DataCleanupService+ContactUnification.swift:17-24). Reading Contacts outside the hold is fine. Adopting outside it, or adopting under app refresh and leaving the rehash for later, routes mail to hashes no stored conversation has yet and splits chats.
- Batching by the adopted groups alone misses unlinking and regrouping (a1,a2 becomes a2,a3). Each batch must be a connected component of changed addresses over both maps' groups (ContactLinkedAddresses.swift:138-151), hashed with the one full adopted snapshot. Otherwise two conversations that come to share a hash end up in different batches and are never merged.
- Each merge hold must save or roll back (settleCleanupSensitiveHold, DataCleanupService.swift:351-419). Inside its own perform it must re-read the pending send records, ChatReplyDraft, PendingAction retargeting and chat-preview retry anchors, and fetch its group again by hash. A snapshot kept across a gate release can merge away a conversation that a send anchored in between.
- Gate first, then turn (ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:155-161). A merge hold must not ask for a conversation's turn in the same call as the gate. The repair must never be moved into a lease or into the maintenance boundary. markAppliedToConversations, or the mixed map, is written only after the hold that covers it has saved.

**Fix.** (1) Split refreshIfNeeded into a read that adopts nothing (authorization, then enumerateContacts, generation taken first), made before performCleanupSensitiveMutation, and an adopt kept first in the hold that re-asks authorization. (2) Group changed addresses into connected components over both maps' groups; when blocked, record a mixed applied map (adopted groups for finished components, old groups for blocked ones), so later syncs rescan only blocked components. (3) Keep every hash, type and row-fold write in the adoption hold; give each merge group its own hold that re-fetches by hash, re-reads protections and saves, with Task.isCancelled checked between, winners counted by count(for:), labels prefetched. (4) Under .appRefresh skip the whole pass.

**First step.** Add pure ContactLinkedAddresses.changedComponents(from:) (connected components over both maps' groups) and a mixed-map builder, tested in ContactLinkedAddressesTests; then have the repair report blocked conversations' addresses so unifyConversationsByContactIfNeeded records the mixed map.

**Pinning test.** ContactUnificationCleanupTests: two linked groups, one chat anchored by a pending send; the first run merges the free group and records only the anchored component pending; a second run fetches only its conversations (fetch spy). Plus a1,a2→a2,a3 regroup. Revert-check.

**Payoff.** Link changes and heavy merges stop holding the send gate in one unbounded transaction; anchored chats rescan only their component; Contacts I/O leaves the gate; app refresh skips it.

### `contacts-person#4` · medium · maintainability · effort S · new

**A Contacts lookup writes Person rows, with a precedence the sync writers contradict**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Two writers of Person.displayName follow opposite rules. A cold ContactsResolver.lookup match overwrites the name with the card's name whenever they differ, saves, and posts a change. The sync writers put back any header name that ranks better. So a nickname or first-name card flips at most once per process per contact (only where a list row's lookup is cold; chat prewarm caches without writing), and the next message carrying the header name flips it back. The Contacts name and photo are never cleared: rows still show both after access is withdrawn or the contact is deleted.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactPersistenceService.swift:25-27,41-56,67-69 — the avatar file is rewritten on every cold match before any check; displayName is overwritten whenever it differs ('Address book name always takes precedence'); a save, then invalidatePersonCacheAndPost
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/CoreDataFactories.swift:91-97 and Persistence/MessagePersister+Participants.swift:94-106 — header writers replace the stored name when isBetterDisplayName holds; the update path also collects every conversation the person is in for a display-name recompute
- esc-chatmail/Services/TextProcessing/EmailNormalizer.swift:185-188 — the ranking's own rule that a pair must never rank better in both directions 'or the stored name would flip'; the Contacts writer bypasses the ranking altogether
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactsResolver.swift:150-152,171-181,203-211 with ViewModels/ChatViewModel.swift:1672-1679 — only a cold lookup writes; prewarm (the chat's prefetch) fills the cache without writing, so list rows (ParticipantInfoResolver.swift:94) are the trigger
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ProfilePhotoResolver.swift:243-256,364-369 and AvatarStorage.swift:51-52,84-88 — the stored file is returned before Contacts is asked; avatarURL is written only when nil or empty; an absolute URL is stored; deleteAvatar has no caller, and deleteAllAvatars runs only at sign-out (AuthSession.swift:983)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator.swift:45-52,84-91 — a status change clears memory caches only; contrast ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:28-33,204-221, which drops what Contacts said when access is withdrawn

**Trigger.** After each launch, the first list-row load of a contact whose card name ranks below their header name (nicknames, first-name-only cards), then that sender's next new or refetched message; separately, withdrawing Contacts access, or deleting a contact or its photo.

**Impact.** Per affected contact per launch: one extra Person save, an avatar file rewrite, a personDisplayInfoDidChange reload of the matching rows, and the list's participations walk on main (person-change-conversation-fanout). The sync-side revert adds the same fan-out. On the update path it also adds a display-name recompute of every conversation that person is in. While access is granted the names on screen stay stable. Once it is withdrawn, rows keep the contacts' photos and, where there is no header name, the card names, until sign-out.

**Verifier.** Several points are overstated. The flip is not per message: once the header name is back, an equal name changes nothing. The sync-side revert rides on the sync's own save. CacheCoordinator.swift:267-273 invalidates PersonCache again after that save, so posting before the save only causes a redundant reload. While access is granted the display prefers the live match (PersonDisplayNameResolver.swift:95-110). There is overlap with prior items not yet built: person-change-conversation-fanout, contacts-resolver-full-enumeration (step 13) and the avatar-files item at review line 1510. The new parts are the contradictory precedence and the Contacts data still shown after access is withdrawn.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1337 contacts-resolver-full-enumeration (fix part 3, step 13 not built); :1510 avatar filenames and relative names; :897 person-change-conversation-fanout (step 5, line 1561: not built). The precedence clash and the data left after access is withdrawn are not recorded anywhere.

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: ContactsResolver and ProfilePhotoResolver must stay drained participants (AuthSession.swift:234-242) even once lookup stops writing, because their caches still hold old-account matches. Any withdrawal cleanup that writes Person rows has to run under withActiveGeneration or a non-exclusive lease, never the exclusive boundary.
- Refresh coupling: today the only personDisplayInfoDidChange after a contact edit comes from updatePerson. EditContactView and AddContactView only invalidate caches, and ChatMessagesCoordinator.handleContactStoreDidChange counts on the cold lookup writing. Deleting updatePerson without adding an explicit post leaves list rows showing the old name.
- Person.displayName is also the Hide-My-Email marker that reply addressing, identity and titles read (ReplySnapshots.swift:105-113, Message+ParticipantSetIdentity.swift:42-45). Without provenance, clearing what Contacts wrote can drop that marker or a header name and re-key conversations. Never nil it or rewrite it across the board.
- Mac tripwire: in an unsandboxed build Documents/Avatars is the user's own folder, so a new file purge at withdrawal would be destructive and sit outside clearMailDerivedCaches' SandboxTripwire guard. Gate the reads instead. Provenance attributes need ESCChatmail 7, batched with step 10, and no hasRefreshedConversationNames bump.

**Fix.** Make ContactsResolver.lookup a pure read: delete updatePerson (ContactPersistenceService.swift). Loaded titles, bubbles and sheets already rank the live contact name first, so Person.displayName stays under the header ranking alone. Keep the resolver's close/drain and AuthSession wiring. Replace the refresh its post gave: invalidateCache(for:) posts its emails, and ChatMessagesCoordinator.handleContactStoreDidChange posts once after invalidating. Show a stored avatarURL (ProfilePhotoResolver.fetchPhoto, MessageBubbleLoader.loadSenderInfo) only while a shared ContactsAccess, moved out of ContactLinkedAddressStore, is .readable; delete no files. Defer relative hashed avatar names (avatar-filename item), photos of deleted contacts (step 13's index) and any legacy-name repair (maintenance run, recoveredHeaderDisplayName, never nil).

**First step.** Delete the updatePerson call in ContactsResolver.lookup (ContactsResolver.swift:175-180) and have invalidateCache(for:) post its emails. Rewrite ParticipantCacheAccountBoundaryTests' direct-lookup test to assert the Person row is untouched and the match stays fenced by generation.

**Pinning test.** ContactsResolverTests on TestCoreDataStack: Person stored as 'Robert Smith', contactLookup returns 'Bob' with an image. Lookup leaves displayName and avatarURL alone, saves nothing, never calls saveAvatar. ProfilePhotoResolver with denied access returns nil despite a stored avatarURL. Revert-check: updatePerson.

**Payoff.** Only the header ranking writes Person.displayName. Each launch stops doing a Person save, an avatar rewrite and a row and bubble reload per contact. With access withdrawn, contact photos disappear, and card nicknames stop reaching forwarded headers.

### `contacts-person#5` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**No single owner reacts to a Contacts change: six observers, global invalidation, and the caches that hold Contacts data stay stale**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

No store-change path clears ProfilePhotoResolver's memory cache, which holds misses for 24 h. Even an open chat clears only ContactsResolver and PersonCache. So a photo added or changed (in the app's own Edit Contact sheet or in Contacts) stays missing or old on rows and the chat header until relaunch, a memory warning or 24 h. ContactsResolver's cache of matches is cleared on a store change only by a chat or Participants sheet on screen. With only the list open, the tracker's global bump rebuilds each rollup from the same cached match, so the old name comes back. The self-alias, single-flight and scan parts repeat earlier review items.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ProfilePhotoResolver.swift:121-124 — nil results are cached too; :154-157 clearCache is called only from ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator.swift:45-52, which runs only when the authorization status changed (:84-91), and from the memory warning (:73-75)
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/ChatMessagesCoordinator.swift:1934-1945 with Services/Dependencies/Dependencies.swift:289-296 — a store change in an open chat clears ContactsResolver and PersonCache, and the photo cache is left as it is
- esc-chatmail/Views/Chat/EditContactView.swift:199-215 — an in-app edit invalidates ContactsResolver and PersonCache for each address and never the photo cache; ContactPersistenceService.swift:48-51 sets avatarURL only when it is nil
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker.swift:28-34,77-83 with ParticipantRollupCache.swift:223-226 — every store change evicts every rollup; the rebuild asks ContactsResolver.lookup (ParticipantInfoResolver.swift:94), which returns the cached match (ContactsResolver.swift:150-152,171-173), and the contact's name wins (PersonDisplayNameResolver.swift:101-102)
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationFilterService.swift:56-65,167-176 — each notification walks the whole address book again, even when the filter is All
- docs/scalability-review.md:1312-1326,1337-1347,1626 — the alias recompute with no single-flight and the index rebuilt on a store change are existing items; step 13 is not built

**Trigger.** A Contacts change while the app is in the foreground. For photos: a photo added or changed, including one saved from the app's own Edit Contact sheet. For names: a rename that arrives (for example through iCloud Contacts sync) while no chat or Participants sheet is on screen.

**Impact.** A photo the user just added does not appear on list rows or in the chat header, and a changed one stays old, until relaunch, a memory warning or 24 h. Bubble avatars do update, because they read ContactsResolver directly. With only the iPhone list on screen, a renamed contact keeps the old name until relaunch or the cache drops it. Every notification still rebuilds rollups and walks the address book without delivering the change.

**Verifier.** I read every observer and every place that clears these caches. Corrected: the photo gap is wider than reported (an open chat and the in-app edit miss it too), and the stale name needs no chat on screen. The alias and scan costs are the earlier items self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist and contacts-resolver-full-enumeration. The three requestAccess sites cannot overlap in practice, since the system's permission alert is modal. The main-thread cost of authorizationStatus is unmeasured. Not checked: whether iOS empties NSCache when the app goes to the background.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1337-1360 contacts-resolver-full-enumeration and :1626 step 13 (not built) are related; :1310-1335 self-alias-contacts-requery-per-persist. The stale match and photo caches are not in that review.

**Invariant risks**

- ContactLinkedAddressStore (ContactLinkedAddressStore.swift:132-138, 152-200): a consolidated handler may only call markContactsChanged and must never call refreshIfNeeded or adopt a 'rebuilt index'. CLAUDE.md allows adoption only inside the sync cleanup, with the gate held. Adopting anywhere else forks chats.
- ParticipantRollupDependencyTracker's synchronous queue:nil observer (:28-34) is AliasManager's only validity bump (AliasManager.swift:37,113), and it works on a background launch with no UI. ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator.shared is first made when a list appears. Folding the tracker into a debounced main-actor handler, or narrowing its global bump to the changed emails, leaves self-aliases stale. Stale self-aliases fork the optimistic send's conversation.
- Order matters: clear ContactsResolver's matches first (invalidateAllCache clears and then bumps), and post postAllChanged only after every clear. A bump with no clear caches the old name again under the new fingerprint, which is today's bug. Do not treat didBecomeActive as a store change: every foreground would clear every cache and restart the full-enumeration storm.
- A new Person write (clearing avatarURL) needs beginAccountOperation plus withActiveGeneration, as updatePerson has. Clear it only when a match has no image. A failed search returns nil, so a miss is not 'no photo'. Never delete the file, because names collide on a 24-byte prefix (:1510). The skip-rewrite fix in item (3) must compare content, not whether the file exists.

**Fix.** Make ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator the one place the UI reacts to a Contacts change, and build no new index. On CNContactStoreDidChange only, not on didBecomeActive, wait about 0.5 s (injected delay), then run its existing invalidateResolutionCaches and postAllChanged even when the status is unchanged. Once that is tested, replace the store-change handlers in ChatMessagesView and ParticipantsListView with .personDisplayInfoDidChange. In updatePerson, clear avatarURL (generation-fenced) when a match has no image, because ProfilePhotoResolver reads the Person's URL first. In ConversationFilterService, run the reload and onFilterStateChange only when the filter requiresContactCache. Leave the tracker's and ContactLinkedAddressStore's observers as they are. Leave the index, the alias keying and the authorization routing to step 13.

**First step.** In ContactsAuthorizationCoordinator.startObservingStatusChanges, split the two notifications. CNContactStoreDidChange schedules a cancellable debounced task (injected delay) that awaits invalidateResolutionCaches and then calls broadcastDisplayInfoChange, whatever the status. didBecomeActive keeps calling only handlePotentialStatusChange.

**Pinning test.** ContactsAuthorizationCoordinatorTests: status unchanged, five CNContactStoreDidChange posts on an injected center give one invalidation then one broadcast, in order; didBecomeActive gives none (Revert-check: the store-change branch). ContactsResolver(contactLookup:): a hit without image clears avatarURL; a miss keeps it.

**Payoff.** A renamed contact, or a photo added, changed or removed (including one saved from the app's own Edit Contact sheet), shows on list rows and the chat header within about a second. Today it waits for a relaunch, a memory warning or 24 hours.

### `contacts-person#6` · medium · scalability · effort S · known-open

**Person rows only grow, are duplicated by design, and one changed Person still fans out to every conversation it ever joined**

Area: Contacts, Person records and identity resolution. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The core claim holds. On the view context, any Person in objectsDidChange's updated or refreshed set makes the list walk person.conversationParticipations, with no window or archived filter. Each conversation reached that way faults archivedAt and builds a full snapshot (participants and persons) before the trim drops it. This is the known-open person-change-conversation-fanout. The rest is overstated. The persister's walk runs on the sync context, off main. Duplicate Persons are a documented decision and are merged by a background pass. No "alias fingerprint" exists. A missing orphan-Person sweep is hygiene.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:116-128,235-244 — any Person in updated/refreshed passes the guard; every conversation of each such Person is returned, unfiltered
- esc-chatmail/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModel.swift:619-621 with Services/ConversationList/ConversationListStore.swift:55-65 and ConversationSnapshot.swift:63-64 — archivedAt read, then a snapshot walking participants.person, for every returned conversation
- docs/scalability-review.md:895-917,1561 — fan-out item (main-thread hot paths) and 'Not built yet: ... the Person fan-out'
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/Persistence/MessagePersister+Updates.swift:370-373 and MessagePersister+Participants.swift:100-106 — name refresh walks the relationship on the sync context, only when isBetterDisplayName accepts a new name
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationCreationSerializer.swift:87-97 and Services/Sync/DataCleanupService.swift:336-347 — duplicates accepted deliberately; mergeDuplicatePersons runs in the 6-hour store-maintenance run (EntityCleanup.swift:375-387 has no orphan-Person step)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Contacts/ParticipantLoader.swift:415-419,472 with ParticipantRollupCache.swift:178,223-226 — rollup fingerprints cover non-me participant emails only, so a bump of the user's own email (PersonCache.swift:271-275) invalidates nothing outside note-to-self

**Trigger.** A merge into the view context that carries an update or refresh of a Person registered there, for a contact who is in hundreds of conversations at S2/S3. Shown by the code: a Contacts lookup that writes a name or avatar (ContactPersistenceService) and a better header name. Not established: whether a relationship-only inverse change (a new message from that Person) also reports the Person through the merge.

**Impact.** The main thread can hitch for each such update. The cost is about one row fault per conversation of that Person, plus participant and person faults in each snapshot, including archived rows and rows past the window. It is worst just after a Contacts grant, when many Persons update in a row. The duplicate merge, orphan Persons and per-message cache invalidation are background work or hygiene, with no user-visible effect shown.

**Verifier.** I read every location cited. The list fan-out is accurate and still unbuilt. Corrections: the persister walk runs on the sync context, off main, and fires only when a name improves (review item at line 1501). Duplicate Persons are documented in the serializer and merged by the 6-hour background pass (item at line 1509); that comment's "Nothing repairs them" is out of date. There is no "alias fingerprint". The self-email bump only grows emailGenerations (item at line 1504). Orphan Persons are real but low.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md: person-change-conversation-fanout (lines 895-917); step 5 "Not built yet" (line 1561). Persister walk is item line 1501, duplicate-Person merge cost line 1509.

**Invariant risks**

- Unsaved optimistic conversations sit in the window with temporary IDs (esc-chatmailTests/ViewModels/ConversationListViewModelTests.swift:620-639). A store-only fetch misses them, so check those rows in memory or keep includesPendingChanges on the view context.
- Fetched rows must be materialized with returnsObjectsAsFaults = false (ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation.swift:186-191). A sibling delete between the fetch and the snapshot tombstones the row, and ConversationListItem.init then crashes reading its nil id (ConversationListItem.swift:16).
- A v7 uniqueness constraint on Person.email would migrate over duplicates that exist by design (ConversationCreationSerializer.swift:87-97). NSMigrationConstraintViolationError maps to .migrationRecovery (CoreDataErrorClassifier.swift:51,128-129), which deletes the store (CoreDataRecoveryHandler.swift:49-65).
- Both Person relationships cascade (ESCChatmail 6 contents:184-185). An orphan sweep must require both participation sets to be empty and must delete through the graph inside a maintenance pass (EntityCleanup.swift:406-416). Otherwise it strips conversations of their participants.

**Fix.** Build only the list half, which is the review's fix. In ConversationListViewModel+ChangeObservation, replace the conversationParticipations walk. Collect the changed Persons' objectIDs from updated/refreshed, coalesce them to one pass per main-queue turn, and run that pass as handleSiblingContextSave runs (performAndWait, MainActor.assumeIsolated, then applyConversationChanges). Read the window's IDs when the pass runs. Fetch the permanent ones with `self IN %@ AND ANY participants.person IN %@` through a helper shared with the sibling fetch (prefetch, includesPendingChanges, returnsObjectsAsFaults = false). Check temporary-ID rows in memory. Clear the pending IDs on invalidate-all. Leave the persister's off-main walk (item 1501). Drop the Person.email constraint; an orphan sweep is separate hygiene.

**First step.** Write the failing sqlite test first. Then move handleSiblingContextSave's batch fetch (prefetch of participants and participants.person, includesPendingChanges, returnsObjectsAsFaults = false) into one helper that takes an extra predicate, and route the Person pass through it.

**Pinning test.** ConversationListViewModelTests on TestCoreDataStack(storeKind: .sqlite), main-queue context. Rename a Person in 200 conversations (190 archived, 5 windowed, one unsaved optimistic). Windowed rows refresh; person.hasFault(forRelationshipNamed: "conversationParticipations") stays true. Revert-check: conversationsAffectedByPersonChanges.

**Payoff.** A Person update costs one window-bounded fetch, not a main-thread fault per conversation that Person ever joined. This removes the list hitches after a Contacts grant at S2/S3.

## Release safety and field signal (12)

### `background-energy#6` · medium · maintainability · effort S · new

**Background and cadence behavior has no field signal: telemetry is a no-op and MetricKit is absent**

Area: Background execution, sync cadence and energy. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

The app keeps no record of what the system actually does with its background work. TelemetryEventName has one case (appLaunch), and its only implementation, NoopTelemetryClient, is the production default. Nothing in the repository mentions MetricKit. Release builds also drop every log line below .warning. So in TestFlight, schedule submits, skips, BG-task expirations (which reach the run as cancellations, logged at info), clean completions and startup timing all leave no trace. Only error-level failures reach the unified log. BackgroundSyncManager's outcome switch and expiration handler store no counter or timestamp.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Observability/TelemetryClient.swift:3-5, 31-40 — one event name (appLaunch); NoopTelemetryClient.record is intentionally empty
- esc-chatmail/Services/Dependencies/Dependencies.swift:393 — telemetryClient defaults to NoopTelemetryClient.shared; the only call site is esc_chatmailApp.swift:274 (appLaunch)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-42 — the release configuration's minimumLevel is .warning, so Log.debug and Log.info are discarded in TestFlight builds
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundTaskScheduler.swift:50, 65, 134 — successful submits are logged with Log.debug only
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:233-238, 322-360 — the expiration handler only flips latches; the outcome switch returns a Bool and records nothing
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:346 — a cancelled (expired) background run is logged at info, which Release drops; only the failure at :360 is an error

**Trigger.** Every release build. It matters when tuning the 15-min refresh, 60-min processing or budget page limits, or when diagnosing stale mail, BG expiry or jetsam reports at S2/S3.

**Impact.** From inside the app there is no way to see whether refresh and processing tasks are granted, expire, or finish. Cold-launch cost and background terminations are invisible too. The scalability review's main background risks (expired slices that commit nothing, jetsam during long runs) and its own unmeasured questions (scalability-review.md:459, 1622) cannot be checked after release.

**Verifier.** I checked the whole repository with git grep: there is no MetricKit, MXMetricManager or MXDiagnostic anywhere, and no doc records a decision against telemetry. The no-op client's comment expects a real integration later. The signposts that exist (InitialSync, ChatView) only show in Instruments, and startup timing only logs when the opt-in diagnostic is turned on. BackgroundSyncStateManager holds in-memory retry state only. I could not check from code whether Xcode Organizer's aggregated battery and termination metrics cover this TestFlight app, which has about one user. The finding holds and is stronger than written, because Release drops info lines as well as debug ones.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:459 (bg-app-refresh-budget-not-honored caveat: expiry not measured) and :1622 (step 9 'Not measured or seen'); no item covers telemetry or MetricKit

**Invariant risks**

- BG completion ordering: the expiration handler (BackgroundSyncManager.swift:233-238) may only flip latches, and setTaskCompleted must follow the worker's unwind (BackgroundTaskCompletionLatch.swift:40-65). If the fix records inside the handler, or awaits an actor or disk write before latch.complete, it risks the post-expiry watchdog kill. The forced-failure Bool must stay as it is.
- Redaction and the typed allowlist (TelemetryClient.swift:37-39): IncrementalSyncAccountError.errorDescription holds both account emails (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:13-22). Records therefore take only enum cases and Log.redact(error:) domain#code (Log+Redaction.swift:104-113). They never take a localizedDescription, a message or thread ID, the account email, per-account mail counts, or raw MXDiagnostic JSON.
- Cold BG launch and DI: a background task's cold launch may never reach initializeApp, and BackgroundSyncManager.shared is built in App.init outside the @MainActor Dependencies (Dependencies.swift:409). Reaching Dependencies.shared.telemetryClient from BGTaskScheduler's queue would build the whole graph there. Inject the recorder and register the MetricKit subscriber in App.init.
- Test-host isolation and platform: App.init runs in the iOS and Mac test hosts, so the subscriber and any .standard writes are skipped when RuntimeEnvironment.isRunningUnitTests is true, and the ledger takes injected defaults (Mac-plan rule). BG and exit/launch metric code and its tests go inside #if os(iOS). Nothing writes to Core Data or the sync context (only the orchestrator's save points may save it).

**Fix.** Build a local, device-scoped ledger first; MetricKit next; a backend never required. (1) `BackgroundExecutionLedger` in Services/Observability: lock-protected, injected `UserDefaults` suite, bounded ring (~50) of typed records plus per-outcome counters. (2) Inject a synchronous `@Sendable` recorder into `BackgroundSyncManager.init` and `BackgroundTaskRegistry.runTaskOperation`; record once in the completion waiter, after the worker returns and before `latch.complete`, reading expiry from `BackgroundTaskLifecycleState`; let `performAuthoritativeSync` report its result case without changing its Bool. Count submit failures as domain#code. (3) iOS-only `MXMetricManagerSubscriber`, registered in App.init outside the test host, folding only background-exit counts and launch/hang histograms. (4) Mirror records as typed TelemetryEvents; Noop stays default.

**First step.** Add `BackgroundExecutionLedger` and a typed `BackgroundExecutionRecord` (budget, outcome case, expired, duration, launch age) in Services/Observability, inject a recorder into `BackgroundSyncManager.init`, and record once in `runBackgroundTaskOperation`'s completion waiter before `latch.complete`.

**Pinning test.** BackgroundSyncManagerTests: expiration fired during readiness yields exactly one record {expired: true, outcome: cancelled}, written before completion reports [false]. Ledger test on a UUID defaults suite: ring bounded; a record from IncrementalSyncAccountError contains no '@'. Revert-check: the waiter's recorder call.

**Payoff.** TestFlight builds would show how often refresh and processing tasks run, expire or fail, and why iOS ends the app in the background, so cadence and budget changes rest on evidence.

### `mac-platform#1` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-open

**Every merge ships a Mac build that nothing has run: CI only compiles it, and its behavior rests on one-OS measurements**

Area: macOS target architecture and platform shim layer. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

On every push to main, Xcode Cloud archives the Mac app and delivers it to the internal TestFlight Team group. Nothing waits for a Mac test run first: CI compiles the Mac app and its tests unsigned and runs none. About 56 of Mac.xctestplan's 81 suites have no platform guard and run in iOS CI. The roughly 25 whole-file `#if os(macOS)` suites, which mount AppKit views and include the mounted pins of the sidebar-identity and selection-guard fixes, plus the macOS branches of shared suites, run only when someone runs them locally. So a regression of an already fixed Mac fault can reach the internal build unchecked.

**Evidence**

- .github/workflows/ci.yml:72-76 — the Mac job 'compiles the tests and runs none', unsigned, with the Mac plan run locally and the 10x billing as the reasons
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:86-87 — the Mac archive uses distribution preparation 'TestFlight (Internal Testing Only)' and is delivered to the Team group; :94 — a merge to main ships a Mac build
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:374 — 'Until then, run the Mac test plan locally'; :391 — 'Not covered. CI runs no Mac tests.' (documented interim gap)
- esc-chatmailTests/Platform/MacConversationSidebarRowIdentityTests.swift:1 — whole-file `#if os(macOS)`, one of about 25 such Mac-plan suites; the default esc-chatmail.xctestplan skips only Performance and Scale suites, so the unguarded Mac-plan suites run in iOS CI
- esc-chatmailTests/Platform/MacSheetItemHandOverTests.swift:17-22 — HONEST SCOPE: 'no test presents a sheet'; the build-562 fault was measured only in a throwaway program, so the proposed CI gate would not have caught it
- esc-chatmail/Platform/MacSidebarListSelectionGuardView.swift:102-106 — on a system that builds lists differently, the guard finds no table and the fill covers the list's own selection: a cosmetic fallback, not an unknown failure

**Trigger.** A merge that breaks the behavior one of the ~25 macOS-only suites mounts (sidebar row identity, selection guard, menus, drop views, reply field) when the PR author did not run Mac.xctestplan locally.

**Impact.** A Mac-only regression, including the return of a fixed fault such as the ghost sidebar rows, can reach the internal TestFlight build the developer uses every day. TestFlight can reinstall an earlier build. No external users or macOS 26 users are known to receive it.

**Verifier.** The cited lines match the code. Several claims in the original finding did not hold up:
- None of the three cited faults shows that the CI gap caused anything. The 80-point sheet strip was found on 2026-11-10 in a local Debug build, the day before Xcode Cloud delivered any Mac build. No tests existed for the ghost rows or the build-562 sheet when they shipped, and the test host cannot present a sheet.
- Most of the Mac plan already runs in iOS CI.
- iOS ships through the same ungated archive.
- Delivery is internal only.
- The macOS 26 risk falls back to a cosmetic result.
That leaves documented structural debt, not a high-severity issue.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md PR F: "Three constraints on Mac tests", Signing (:374, "Until then, run the Mac test plan locally") and "Not covered. CI runs no Mac tests." (:391); decision 3 (:85-94) added Mac shipping on 2026-11-11, after that stopgap; not in docs/scalability-review.md

**Invariant risks**

- Never launch an unsandboxed Mac build. The fix must not relax verify-mac-test-host.sh:24-36 or MacUnitTestHostGuard. Ad-hoc signing must keep the entitlements ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX generates. The ad-hoc xcconfig must stay CI-only, because a local host shares the TestFlight MushMail container and keychain group.
- Only Mac.xctestplan may set ESC_CHATMAIL_MAC_TEST_PLAN (MacUnitTestHostPolicyTests.testEveryOtherTestPlan_doesNotSetTheMarker), so a new CI plan without KeychainServiceTests would break it. Skip that suite with -skip-testing instead; run-tests.sh refuses only -testPlan and -destination.
- ci.yml:75-76 keeps the 10x-billed Mac CI to one build. Fold the tests into build-macos through run-tests.sh (build-for-testing, then test-without-building) rather than adding a second Mac job, and keep the plan's 120/300 s allowances.
- Some pins were measured on macOS 27.2. One is testList_withRowsIdentifiedByObjectIDs_drawsStaleRowsAfterARowMoves, which asserts the system fault itself, and these can fail on macos-26. Scope them by OS. Never loosen MacSidebarRowID or the selection guard to get a green run. A launch smoke check must not bring back the removed UI_TEST_AUTHENTICATED hooks, which would be an auth path outside AuthSession.

**Fix.** Gate in GitHub CI before merge, because Xcode Cloud starts at the merge. Turn build-macos into one build-and-test step: DESTINATION='platform=macOS' Scripts/run-tests.sh -xcconfig <CI-only ad-hoc xcconfig> -skip-testing:esc-chatmailTests/KeychainServiceTests. The xcconfig sets identity "-", Manual style, no team and an empty CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS. That drops keychain-access-groups but keeps the sandbox entitlements, and the xcconfig probably also needs ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME=NO for the injected test bundle. Leave both sandbox checks as they are. Start with continue-on-error to get a baseline on macOS 26, scope the OS-specific failures, then make the job blocking. Add an Xcode Cloud Mac test action only once you have confirmed it withholds the TestFlight delivery. Defer the launch smoke check.

**First step.** On a draft PR, add the CI-only ad-hoc xcconfig and switch build-macos to run-tests.sh with continue-on-error. Then read the run: does verify-mac-test-host.sh pass, does the host load the test bundle on macos-26, and which suites fail?

**Pinning test.** Revert-check on the draft PR: put the bare object ID back in place of MacSidebarRowID in MacConversationSidebar. MacConversationSidebarRowIdentityTests must turn the Mac job red. Add a default-plan repositorySource test pinning ci.yml's Mac step, its xcconfig, and that only KeychainServiceTests is skipped.

**Payoff.** The 25 AppKit-mounting Mac suites, and the macOS branches of shared suites, gate every PR on macOS 26, the deployment floor nothing has run on, before Xcode Cloud ships the merge.

### `observability-errors#1` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**No crash, hang, exit or jetsam signal reaches the developer: MetricKit is absent and telemetry is a one-event no-op**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The code matches the finding. No MetricKit subscriber or crash SDK exists. `TelemetryClient` has one conformer, `NoopTelemetryClient`, whose `record` does nothing, and the app sends it one event (`appLaunch`). Release logging goes only to OSLog, at warning and above, and the startup-timing diagnostics are off. So when the app is killed in the background (jetsam, watchdog, task-assertion timeout), the app keeps nothing it could read back. The finding overstates two things. "Solely through MetricKit" ignores Xcode Organizer and the device's own analytics logs. The gap costs late detection, not a failure, so this is medium, not high.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Observability/TelemetryClient.swift:3-5 — TelemetryEventName has the single case appLaunch
- esc-chatmail/Services/Observability/TelemetryClient.swift:31-41 — NoopTelemetryClient.record is intentionally empty; the comment expects a future 'production integration' (a placeholder, not a documented decision against diagnostics)
- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:274-279 — the only telemetryClient.record call (git grep 'telemetryClient' finds no other), recording appLaunch/initialized
- esc-chatmail/Services/Dependencies/Dependencies.swift:393 — default telemetryClient is NoopTelemetryClient.shared
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-48 — Release: minimumLevel .warning, enabledDiagnostics [] (so logStartupTiming at esc_chatmailApp.swift:13-16, a Log.diagnostic(.startup) call, emits nothing); Log.swift:139-141 writes only to os_log
- esc-chatmail.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:551,559 — the only packages are GoogleSignIn-iOS and SwiftSoup; git grep -i for MetricKit/MXMetricManager/Crashlytics/Sentry/Bugsnag/PLCrashReporter finds no matches in Swift sources

**Trigger.** An iOS background exit nobody sees: a jetsam kill during a BGProcessing or cold background sync (the scalability review's S2/S3 re-list and hub-fault memory), a watchdog kill, or a background-task assertion timeout, on a device not attached to Xcode.

**Impact.** Background exits and hangs on iOS leave nothing in the app to inspect or export, and Release builds record no launch timing. A regression in background memory or time, such as the still-open hub-fault cost the scalability review measured (+49 MB, 3.8 s cold at S2), has no field confirmation inside the app. The cost is late detection, not a failure the user sees. Other routes exist outside the app, unverified here: Organizer's TestFlight crash, hang and termination reports, and the device's own analytics logs. They depend on opt-in, and the aggregate metrics need more users than this small TestFlight audience probably has. On the Mac (no BGTasks), the owner already reads the unified log and crash reports.

**Verifier.** I opened every cited location, plus Log.swift, LoggerConfiguration.swift, LogLevel.swift, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and the docs. No guard, file logger, launch sentinel or diagnostics export exists. CLAUDE.md and the docs record no decision against MetricKit or telemetry. Two changes: severity high→medium, since no failure results and no class of bugs becomes more likely (rubric: structural debt with a nameable cost); "solely through MetricKit" softened, since Organizer and the device's analytics logs also surface exits. Those outside routes come from platform knowledge, not code.

**Invariant risks**

- Unit-test host: App.init runs in every test host, and a Mac host's container is the real app's. Registering or writing there must sit inside the existing `!RuntimeEnvironment.isRunningUnitTests` block (esc_chatmailApp.swift:69), after `MacUnitTestHostGuard`, which stays first (pinned from source). Tests inject a temp directory.
- Redaction/allowlist: raw `MXDiagnosticPayload.jsonRepresentation()` carries the iOS 17 exception `composedMessage`/`arguments`, which can hold addresses or subjects. That bypasses `Log.redact` and the allowlist rule in TelemetryClient.swift:37-39. Also, `TelemetryEvent.counters` is keyed by free `String`s.
- Account/cleanup boundary: anything mail-derived on disk must join `AuthSession.clearMailDerivedCaches`, and `Documents` is the user's own folder on an unsandboxed Mac. Keep the records in Caches with no mail content, delete only the store's own prefixed files, and never write `isExcludedFromBackup` (BackupExclusion is the only writer). Never enable UIFileSharingEnabled, which would expose Documents/Messages.
- Launch/background budgets: App.init runs on cold BGTask launches. Reading past payloads, JSON work and pruning go on a utility queue, are never awaited by initializeApp, and never happen inside a sync run, a lease or the auth-transition gate. ENOSPC is logged once, never thrown or retried. `@unchecked Sendable` needs a `///` note, and warnings are errors.

**Fix.** iOS only at first (`#if os(iOS)`), since the Mac already has crash reports and the unified log. Add a platform-neutral `DiagnosticsRecordStore` that takes `Data` plus a kind and writes an allowlisted projection atomically into `Caches/Diagnostics`: metadata, exit, signal and exception type, `formatString` and the call-stack tree, without `composedMessage`/`arguments`. Cap the folder by count and bytes and prune only the store's prefixed files. Then add `MetricKitDiagnosticsRecorder`, an NSObject `MXMetricManagerSubscriber` with a static `shared`. It handles diagnostics and the daily `applicationExitMetrics` and launch histograms, and is registered in App.init inside the `!isRunningUnitTests` block, with file work on a utility queue. Log one redacted summary line per payload. A file-backed TelemetryClient with enum counter keys comes later. A TestFlight read-out needs the separate export.

**First step.** Write `DiagnosticsRecordStore` (injected directory, `record(kind:json:)`, allowlisted projection, count and byte cap, pruning only its own prefixed files) and its tests on a temp directory, before any MetricKit code. MetricKit payloads have no public initializer.

**Pinning test.** `DiagnosticsRecordStoreTests` on a temp directory: an address in a crash's exception `composedMessage` is not stored, N+5 records leave the N newest within the byte cap, a foreign file survives pruning, and `repositorySource` pins registration behind `!isRunningUnitTests` in `#if os(iOS)`.

**Payoff.** Background exits on TestFlight iPhones (jetsam, watchdog, task-assertion timeout, locked file 0xdead10cc), plus hangs and crashes, become readable. That gives field evidence for the scalability review's background-memory estimates.

### `observability-errors#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**Mailbox health has no user surface: sync status is write-only, inbound abandonment is unobserved, a store reset is unannounced**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Run-level sync failures other than revoked credentials and a full disk have no user surface. `SyncEngine` writes "Sync failed: …" and "Network unavailable" into `SyncUIState`, and no view reads it. Pull-to-refresh returns without an outcome. `.syncMessagesAbandoned` has observers only in tests. The two automatic store deletions log and say nothing to the user. The finding overstates the scope: revocation and a full disk are both surfaced, abandoned mail is retried by the drain, automatic deletion needs proven corruption or a migration error, and the prior review already flagged the unread `uiState`.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:358-363 — generic catch: `uiState.update(isSyncing: false, status: "Sync failed: \(formatSyncError(error))")`; lines 545-580 build the strings; git grep finds no reader of uiState/isSyncing/syncStatus outside SyncEngine
- esc-chatmail/Views/Main/ConversationListView.swift:8-10,58-73,170 — engine observed only for isBlockedByInsufficientStorage; the only banners are storage and abandoned pending actions; `.refreshable { await viewModel.performSync() }`, which (ConversationListViewModel.swift:157-159) returns Void
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncFailureTracker.swift:298-310 — posts .syncMessagesAbandoned with no app observer; lines 540-552 the drain retries each abandoned ID up to maxAbandonedMessageRetries (5, Constants.swift:139) with 15 min-12 h backoff before deleting it
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataErrorClassifier.swift:123-136 — automatic deletion only for migration-family errors or proven corruption; everything else keeps the store for the launch screen's Try Again / Reset Mailbox
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataRecoveryHandler.swift:49-65 — backup, Log.error, remove store; no persisted marker or notice (no grep hit for one)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/TokenManager.swift:424-428 with SignInView.swift:22-26 — revoked credentials do reach the user ("Reconnect your Google account"), and esc_chatmailApp.swift:424-426 stops the 60 s loop then

**Trigger.** A run-level failure that keeps repeating and is neither auth revocation nor out-of-space: a deterministic save or validation failure, a persistent non-auth 4xx, repeated quota or server errors, long offline stretches. Also a pull-to-refresh that fails, a message that is still unfetchable after the 3-run escape hatch and 5 drain attempts, or a launch that hits a migration error or a corrupt store.

**Impact.** An inbox that stopped syncing looks the same as one with no new mail, and pull-to-refresh gives no feedback when it fails. Losing a message for good needs failures spread over many hours, so it is rare. After an automatic reset, which is rare and only happens on corruption or a failed migration, saved reply drafts, queued archive and mark-read actions and send markers are gone with no explanation. That cost can be named, but it is not a high-severity failure at S2 under common conditions.

**Verifier.** The code is as cited. Three parts are wrong. Revocation is surfaced (requireReauthentication, then SignInView) and stops the loop. Full disk has a banner and a backoff, so "retries every 60 s whatever the outcome" is false for both. Abandonment is not loss, because the drain retries. The automatic reset is an allow-list (migration or corruption), and other load failures keep the store. priorStatus is not "new": docs/scalability-review.md:1516 lists "No view observes SyncEngine.uiState" under Hygiene. The new parts are the abandonment notice and the reset notice. Medium, not high.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1516 (Hygiene, iOS: "No view observes SyncEngine.uiState…", not built); store-load-recovery-ladder (lines 109-123) and step 1/step 6 (lines 1534, 1562): built

**Invariant risks**

- Account boundary: the failure arm writes uiState after endRun (SyncEngine.swift:358-361), but the success and full-disk arms record before endRun on purpose (338-341), because beginQuiescence resets the state once the run ends. Health must be recorded before endRun and reset in resetStorageStateForAccountTransition (AuthSession.swift:368-374, called beside resetPendingActionRetryState). Otherwise one account's 'sync failing' verdict shows in the next account.
- Re-render cost: the list and the Mac sidebar observe SyncEngine for one flag only (ConversationListView.swift:8-10, MacConversationSidebar.swift:32-33), and setBlockedByInsufficientStorage publishes only on a change (SyncEngine.swift:394-400). A published Date, age or per-run counter would re-render the whole list on every 60 s run. Publish only a coarse verdict, and only when it changes.
- Sync staging: health code must never write lastSuccessfulSyncTime or call recordSuccess/reset, because that time is history recovery's floor. A drain give-up is staged inside stageAbandonedRetryOutcome (SyncFailureTracker.swift:540-544) and may be reported only after the run's save commits, as with commit(_:) at 298-310. An unreadable ledger is never zero.
- Store-reset notice: write it only on the automatic ladder branches (CoreDataStack.swift:361-387), through injected defaults, because a Mac test host shares the real container's UserDefaults. Do not clear it in performDurableLocalCleanup. The restore right after an automatic reset runs that cleanup itself: it finds files but no Account row (AuthSession.swift:1217-1239), wipes the bodies and attachments, and moves the mailbox start to now (1657). Never weaken that isolation check.

**Fix.** Engine: keep an in-memory MailboxHealth on SyncEngine: consecutive run-level failures, failure class, last clean run. Record it in every runSyncTask arm before endRun, reset it in resetStorageStateForAccountTransition, and publish only when the pure MailboxHealthPolicy verdict changes. UI: one banner in the existing slot on ConversationListView and MacConversationSidebar. It yields to the storage and reauth banners and appears after 3 consecutive failed runs over at least 10 minutes; a failed pull-to-refresh shows it at once. Store: the ladder's automatic branches write a one-time StoreResetNotice (kind and date) through injected defaults, shown once after authentication. Then retire SyncUIState's strings. Report drain give-ups only after the save commits, or not at all.

**First step.** Add MailboxHealth and a pure MailboxHealthPolicy, with no UI yet. Record each runSyncTask outcome before endRun, moving the failure arm's write ahead of endRun, and reset the value in resetStorageStateForAccountTransition. Pin it with policy and engine tests.

**Pinning test.** MailboxHealthPolicyTests: quiet on one transient failure, the threshold, yields to storage and reauth. An engine test that resetStorageStateForAccountTransition clears a failed run's verdict (Revert-check: that reset). A ladder test that only the automatic reset writes the notice.

**Payoff.** Two silent failures become visible: an inbox that stopped syncing, and a mailbox the recovery ladder wiped and rebuilt. Today both look the same as an inbox with no new mail.

### `observability-errors#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Shipped builds keep no diagnosable record: info is dropped, background tasks log nothing, no health snapshot or log export**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

Release builds filter out `Log.debug` and `Log.info` before they reach `os_log`. That drops run outcomes, phase timings, "sync was cancelled", the offline skip and store-load retries. Warnings and errors still reach the unified log as `.default`/`.error`, and that includes every failed or full-disk background sync. What a shipped build actually lacks is the BGTask lifecycle: no line is written when a task fires, expires, completes, is blocked or skips while offline. Nothing in the app collects the stored health state or exports logs either.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-55 — release: minimumLevel .warning, enabledDiagnostics [], and it is the active config whenever DEBUG is not set
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/Log.swift:115 — `guard level >= config.minimumLevel else { return }` comes before os_log at :141; LogLevel.swift:21-22 maps warning to .default and error to .error, so those still reach the unified log
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:344-362 — a cancelled run (this is what a BGTask expiry produces) is logged only with log.info at :346; failed and full-disk runs use log.error with syncType "Background incremental" (:290); the offline skip at :513 is info
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:188-361 — handleAppRefresh, handleProcessing, runBackgroundTaskOperation and performAuthoritativeSync, including all result cases, contain no log call; the file's only logs are .debug at :112-143
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundTaskRegistry.swift:233-255 — runTaskOperation: no log on expiration, completion or reschedule; only a failed submit is logged, at error (:147)
- esc-chatmail/Platform/MacSettingsView.swift:67-94 — the Settings form shows Account, Sign Out… and Version only, with no diagnostics or export action

**Trigger.** An iOS tester reports that background refresh never runs or mail stopped arriving.
