In a Release build a task that never fired, one that fired and completed, one that fired and expired (cancelled), one that was blocked by another run, and one skipped while offline all leave no log line.

**Impact.** Background sync that expires every time leaves no trace, so remote triage of iOS background behavior means guessing or shipping a Debug build. Behaviors CLAUDE.md calls unobserved on a device (expiry, maintenance cancellation) cannot be verified from shipped builds. Runs that fail with an error can still be diagnosed today through a sysdiagnose or `log collect` on iOS and `log show` on the Mac. The claim of "no diagnosable record" is overstated.

**Verifier.** Confirmed: Release drops info-level logs, and the BGTask lifecycle is unlogged. Corrected: about 183 warning and 276 error call sites still log in Release, including failed background syncs, failed schedule submits, store-load failures and the store reset. On the Mac the device is the Mac itself, and an iOS sysdiagnose needs no Mac. `lastSuccessfulSyncTime` has test-only callers in IncrementalSyncCursorTests (seen in grep output; I did not open that file). Abandoned pending actions already show a banner (AbandonedPendingActionsModel.swift:4-8). No document records a decision on diagnostics.

**Invariant risks**

- Completion order: iOS may suspend as soon as setTaskCompleted returns (BackgroundTaskCompletionLatch.swift:41-43, BackgroundTaskRegistry.swift:218-220). A record written after onComplete, in the expiration handler or asynchronously is lost. An 'expired' flag kept apart from BackgroundTaskLifecycleState.complete (:22-28) can disagree with the result reported to iOS. Do no I/O while the unfair lock is held.
- Redaction: Release still emits warning and error lines that are not redacted. The LogRedactionTests.swift:284-364 allowlist includes raw messageId and attachmentId values, gmailMessageId, file paths and \(error)/localizedDescription. A raw OSLogStore export would package them. Lowering Release to .info would add lines nobody has audited, such as CoreDataStack.swift:258, which logs the whole storeDescription (the store path).
- Account boundary and reads: store counts must take the non-exclusive lease (SyncRunCoordinator.swift:193). They must never wait on the exclusive boundary while holding it, must never save, and must never use the sync context. A failed count reads as 'unreadable', never as 0. Ledger counts keep the state == nil disjunct.
- Tests: the Mac test host shares the real container, so journal and snapshot tests inject a UUID-named defaults suite, their own store and their own pasteboard. Code touching BGTask stays inside #if os(iOS). The journal holds no mailbox data, so it is not an account-boundary participant; list it under 'left in the preferences on purpose'.

**Fix.** Two PRs, journal first. (1) iOS `BackgroundRunJournal`: injected `UserDefaults`, lock-guarded ring of ~20 typed entries (task, budget, start, end, outcome enum, expired), no mailbox data. `performAuthoritativeSync` gets an outcome-returning core behind the existing Bool. Write at handler entry and in the completion waiter before `onComplete`, taking `expired` from `BackgroundTaskLifecycleState.complete`'s own transition; same in `BackgroundTaskRegistry.runTaskOperation`. Abnormal endings add one `Log.warning`. Show the last runs as read-only Settings.bundle rows (iOS has no in-app settings). (2) A typed, counts-only snapshot under the non-exclusive lease, copyable from Mac Settings. Keep Release at `.warning`; no raw OSLogStore export (on iOS it sees only the current process).

**First step.** Add BackgroundRunJournal (injected defaults, capped ring guarded by a lock). Have BackgroundTaskCompletionLatch.complete pass the computed (reported, didExpire) to a hook that runs before onComplete. Wire it into BackgroundSyncManager.runBackgroundTaskOperation through an outcome-returning performAuthoritativeSync core.

**Pinning test.** BackgroundSyncManagerTests: block readiness, fire expiration, then release. Inside onComplete, assert the journal (UUID defaults suite) already holds an appRefresh entry with expired=true, reported=false and outcome cancelled. Revert-check: the pre-completion hook.

**Payoff.** Shipped builds would show whether background tasks fire, expire, get blocked or fail. CLAUDE.md's unobserved claims about expiry and maintenance cancellation could then be checked from TestFlight builds.

### `observability-errors#5` · medium · performance · effort S · new

**Timing instrumentation is computed and then discarded in shipped builds; signposts cover chat open only**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: confirmed (high confidence).

Confirmed. Release uses `LoggerConfiguration.release`: minimum level `.warning` and no diagnostic areas. `Log.log` therefore drops every `Log.info` before it reaches os_log. As a result, `SyncTimingRecorder`'s phase and run timings for both sync paths, `logStartupTiming` (an opt-in `.startup` diagnostic, even in Debug) and the cleanup passes' durations are measured and then thrown away in shipped builds. `CoreDataPerformanceLogger`'s signposts are off outside DEBUG and wrap only `InitialSync`. `ChatInitialLoad` is the only interval emitted in every build. One exception the finding missed: `logSyncSummary` has no gate and writes one os_log `.info` line with the initial sync's total time. Background expiration logs nothing.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-55 — release config: minimumLevel .warning, enabledDiagnostics []; chosen whenever DEBUG is not set (DEBUG is defined only in the Debug configuration, project.pbxproj:397)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/Log.swift:92,115 — diagnostic() returns unless the area is enabled; log() returns when level < minimumLevel, so Log.info never reaches os_log in Release
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncHelpers.swift:54-68 — SyncTimingRecorder.finish and finishRun log only via Log.info
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncHelpers.swift:96-121,152-157 — subsystem "com.esc.inboxchat"; isEnabled false outside DEBUG gates both signpost calls; logSyncSummary is ungated os_log .info (called once, InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:246)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/ChatViewPerformanceSignposts.swift:9-45 — ChatInitialLoad begin/end is ungated, under the bundle ID subsystem, while LogCategory.swift:19-21 uses "com.esc.chatmail.<category>"
- esc-chatmail/Services/Background/BackgroundSyncManager.swift:233-238 — the BGTask expiration handler only expires and cancels; nothing logs that the budget ran out

**Trigger.** A TestFlight or App Store (Release) build in normal use. A launch, sync, maintenance or archive that gets slower, or a BGAppRefresh run cut off at its time limit, leaves no persisted duration and no warning line.

**Impact.** Scale and background-budget work can be checked only by query-plan structure in the simulator, which the plan itself notes (docs/scalability-review.md:1591, 1622: "nothing was timed"). A regression or an expired background run in a shipped build cannot be seen afterwards in the unified log. It degrades nothing by itself, but it means step 8's budget work cannot be verified in the field.

**Verifier.** Checked: Log.swift, LoggerConfiguration.swift, LogDiagnosticArea.swift, ScopedLogger.swift (log.info goes to Log.info), the pbxproj DEBUG condition, and every signpost, MetricKit and telemetry use (none besides those cited). Nothing in CLAUDE.md or docs records this as a deliberate decision. Correction: initial sync's total time does reach os_log at info level in Release through the ungated logSyncSummary. Info-level lines are not persisted by default, so the conclusion holds. The background expiration path logs nothing, which strengthens the claim. Maintenance passes are mostly not timed at all.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1591 and :1622 ('nothing was timed'); step 8 (line 1603) not built; no observability item in the review

**Invariant risks**

- Redaction (CLAUDE.md Logging): six `timing.finishRun(outcome: "failed error=\(error.localizedDescription)")` calls (IncrementalSyncOrchestrator.swift:166,205,575,585,591; InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:267) slip past LogRedactionTests, whose scan only reads lines containing "Log." (LogRedactionTests.swift:218). Raising the summary to warning, or Release's floor to .info, would publish that text as %{public}@, along with the raw messageId lines in OriginalEmailTelemetry (OriginalEmailSourceLoader.swift:12-14).
- Mac test-host guard: `MacUnitTestHostGuard.exitUnlessPermitted()` must stay the first statement of esc_chatmailApp.init (pinned in MacUnitTestHostPolicyTests.swift:96-118). A launch signpost or a MetricKit subscriber goes after it, and the subscriber goes in initializeApp, which does nothing under unit tests.
- Sync and boundary ordering: never persist timings into the sync context or UserDefaults.standard (IncrementalSyncCursorTests.swift:110-192 pins both). The maintenance interval must end between `maintenanceRun.task.value` and `endRun` with no new await (StoreMaintenanceCoordinator.swift:89-94). The expiration handlers must keep `lifecycleState.expire()` before `cancellationLatch.expire()`, and must take their start time before installExpirationHandler, which tests fire synchronously.
- Toolchain traps under warnings-as-errors: adding a `private var x = nil` to SyncPhaseTimer makes its memberwise init private under CI's Swift 6.2, which breaks SyncTimingRecorderTests' `SyncPhaseTimer(name:startedAt:)` in CI only. Also, MXMetricManager is API_TO_BE_DEPRECATED in the Xcode 27 SDK (replaced by MetricManager, which needs iOS/macOS 27), while CI builds with Xcode 26.

**Fix.** Keep Release's .warning floor. (1) Make SyncTimingRecorder's outcome a typed value built from counts, enum names and Log.redact(error:). (2) Add one shared OSSignposter (com.esc.inboxchat, pointsOfInterest, as ChatViewPerformanceSignposts uses) with intervals named by StaticString for the recorder's run and phases, StoreMaintenanceCoordinator's admitted operation, initializeApp and applyConversationWideMutation, begun outside the perform blocks. (3) Add a pure SyncRunDurationPolicy that logs the summary at .warning only over a budget (foreground, appRefresh, processing, maintenance, launch); SyncEngine.performIncrementalSyncForBackground judges against its own budget. (4) Warn once from both BG expiration handlers, after the latches, with the budget and elapsed time. Defer MetricKit: nothing consumes it (NoopTelemetryClient).

**First step.** Replace the six `finishRun(outcome: "failed error=\(error.localizedDescription)")` calls with a typed outcome that uses Log.redact(error:). Add a SyncTimingRecorderTests case proving a sentinel description never reaches summary(...) before raising any log level.

**Pinning test.** SyncTimingRecorderTests: a failed outcome whose NSError description holds a sentinel address is absent from summary (Revert-check: the typed outcome). SyncRunDurationPolicyTests: the threshold for each budget. BackgroundSyncManagerTests: an expiration calls the injected onExpired once, with its budget.

**Payoff.** In TestFlight builds, slow syncs, maintenance runs, launches and expired background tasks would leave a persisted, redacted warning line and Instruments intervals. That makes the step 8 budget work checkable on a device.

### `testing-ci-release#1` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**Nothing stands between a merge and TestFlight: the shipping workflow and the test workflow are unconnected**

Area: Test architecture, CI and release pipeline. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The core claim holds. Xcode Cloud's Default workflow, configured in App Store Connect, archives iOS and macOS on any push to main and sends both to TestFlight internal testing. It does not wait for GitHub CI, and main has no branch protection. So a merge whose PR CI was red, a stacked PR that never had CI, or a main run cancelled by the next merge still ships. CI also tests a Debug build on Xcode 26 / iOS 26, while the shipped build is Release from Xcode 27.2. That SDK is tested only locally, by convention.

**Evidence**

- .github/workflows/ci.yml:7-18 — CI runs only for PRs and pushes targeting main; concurrency group ci-${{ github.ref }} with cancel-in-progress: true, so a second merge cancels the first merge's run on main
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:23,29 with Scripts/run-tests.sh:5 — runs-on macos-26 with the image's default /Applications/Xcode.app; CONFIGURATION="Debug"
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:81-88 — the 'Default' workflow archives on pushes to main and apparently not on PRs; it 'lives there, not in the repo'; it delivers to TestFlight Internal Testing (Team group); it uses the latest Xcode (27.2); a newer push cancels a running build
- ~/.claude/projects/-esc-chatmail/memory/auto-merge-does-not-wait-for-ci-here.md:11 — branches/main/protection returns 404 and rulesets are empty (checked 2026-11-02); this cannot be seen from the repository
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:93,436 — build 546's commit was 'not looked up', not impossible to find; build 528's sidebar bug was found by use, but CLAUDE.md says CI runs only a source pin for that area, so a CI gate would not have caught it
- web/netlify.toml:5,14 with web/package.json:11 — Netlify deploys production on every push to main with `pnpm build` (tsc -b + vite build); web.yml's vitest and e2e do not gate it

**Trigger.** A merge to main whose PR CI is red or still running; a stacked PR (base not main) merged without having been retargeted and tested; two merges close together, which cancel the first CI run while its Xcode Cloud archive may already have finished; any change whose behavior depends on the iOS/macOS 27 SDK or on Release optimization.

**Impact.** Untested or red commits reach the internal TestFlight builds that the owner uses daily with his real mailbox. CI's green result covers neither the shipped toolchain/SDK nor the Release configuration. CI-only failures under Swift 6.2 make main red while the build still ships. No end users are reached: distribution is internal testing only, and a build can be traced through Xcode Cloud's check runs or App Store Connect.

**Verifier.** I read ci.yml, web.yml, the manifest, netlify.toml, run-tests.sh, mac-app-plan.md and the maintainer notes. Several points were corrected. Every PR that targets main does get CI. A cancelled main run is replaced by a run on a newer commit that contains the cancelled one. Builds can be traced. Build 528's bug was not something CI could catch. The only audience is TestFlight internal testers. Gating is done by the maintainer checking CI before merging, which is not enforced. This is a process gap, not one that makes serious bugs likely, so the severity is medium rather than high.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md decision 3, lines 79-94 ("Xcode Cloud builds the Mac app too": the Default workflow, its start condition and Xcode version, recorded as facts rather than as an accepted gap). docs/scalability-review.md has no CI or release item.

**Invariant risks**

- Required checks get stuck behind the path filters. ci.yml:10,13 ignores web/** and web.yml:10-19 runs only for web/ and fixtures changes, so a required job never reports and a web-only or iOS-only PR can never merge. Retargeting a stacked child fires a pull_request 'edited' event, which ci.yml:8 does not listen for.
- Never launch an unsandboxed Mac build. CI's Mac build is unsigned (ci.yml:72-76,92), so a 'run the Mac tests' gate needs a launch that MacUnitTestHostGuard and verify-mac-test-host.sh refuse. A local unsigned Release MushMail.app must be deleted after the compile check.
- Toolchain: moving CI to Xcode 27 drops the Swift 6.2 check that CLAUDE.md's Traps rely on (PRs 387 and 444). Pinning Xcode Cloud to 26 would ship an SDK 26 binary that no local or device test has used. Both CI's macos-26 runner and Xcode Cloud's 'Latest Release' need to stay as they are, or be pinned on purpose.
- Scripts/codex-build.sh:37 hard-codes -configuration Debug, so adding a second -configuration is not a reliable override. A ship-gate that force-pushes, or that runs from a workflow_dispatch on a branch, would ship an older or untested commit.

**Fix.** Ship only from a ref that green CI advances. In ci.yml, add a release-compile job: an unsigned Release build for generic iOS and macOS, through a new CONFIGURATION override in codex-build.sh. Also add a ship-gate job that needs every build and test job, runs only on push to refs/heads/main, has contents: write, and pushes with `git push origin $GITHUB_SHA:refs/heads/testflight` without --force. Git refuses an older SHA as non-fast-forward, and a cancelled run skips the push. Then Kevin, in App Store Connect, switches Default's start branch from main to testflight and pins Xcode 27.2. Keep CI on Xcode 26 and keep the path filters. Add no required checks.

**First step.** Land the ship-gate job alone while Default still starts on main. After one merge, confirm that testflight holds that merge's green SHA. Then Kevin switches Default's start branch, and the next Xcode Cloud check run must be on that SHA.

**Pinning test.** A source-pin suite using repositorySource, in the default plan. It asserts that ci.yml's ship-gate needs every build and test job, runs only on push to refs/heads/main, and pushes without --force or a + refspec. Then watch one merge whose cancelled run ships nothing.

**Payoff.** Only commits whose iOS tests and Mac build passed reach the TestFlight builds Kevin uses daily. Stacked, red and cancelled merges stop shipping, and the Release-only #else branches compile before an archive.

### `testing-ci-release#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**The app's real launch path and its Release build are never executed before they ship**

Area: Test architecture, CI and release pipeline. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

No automated gate runs the composed app. In the test host, initializeApp() returns before the real AppStartupBootstrap, CacheCoordinator start, auth restore, sync start and ContentView, so the App struct's wiring runs under no test plan. CI builds and tests Debug only. Release is first compiled by Xcode Cloud's post-merge archive, which goes straight to internal TestFlight. The parts are covered, though: real store load, per-version SQLite migrations, the reset ladder, bootstrap coalescing and retry, and AuthSession restore through the bootstrap. The first run happens on the developer's own internal-TestFlight devices, not on ordinary users' devices.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/App/esc_chatmailApp.swift:192-195 — initializeApp() returns when isRunningUnitTests; lines 51-54: the host still loads CoreDataStack.shared.persistentContainer (iOS default URL, auto-migration on per CoreDataStack.swift:160-162)
- esc-chatmailTests/Views/AppLifecyclePolicyTests.swift:6-7 — 'The App struct that carries these decisions out runs under no test plan'
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:50-56,91-92 with Scripts/run-tests.sh:5 and Scripts/codex-build.sh:37 — every CI build is -configuration Debug; xcscheme:98-99 ArchiveAction is Release
- esc-chatmailTests/CoreData/RecipientHeadersV6MigrationTests.swift:27-35 and CoreDataStackLoadFailureResetTests.swift:24-33 — a real v5 SQLite store migrated to the current model; the production load and reset ladder run against unopenable stores
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:86-87 — the Xcode Cloud archive goes out as 'TestFlight (Internal Testing Only)' to the Team group; :436 — a Debug Mac build was run by hand on the real mailbox
- esc-chatmail/Configuration/Debug.xcconfig vs Release.xcconfig — identical except the header comment; project.pbxproj:398 (-Onone, Debug) and :457 (wholemodule, Release) are the optimizer differences

**Trigger.** A change to startup ordering in esc_chatmailApp/AppStartupBootstrap, to the default closures in AuthSession.init or Dependencies.shared, to Info.plist or entitlements, or to code whose behavior changes only under -O/wholemodule. All of these merge green and first run in the auto-shipped internal TestFlight build.

**Impact.** A launch-order or wiring defect, or an optimizer-only defect, first shows up on the developer's daily-use devices running the real mailbox. On the Mac, local builds may not be launched, so TestFlight is often the first launch. A Release compile error fails the archive and ships nothing. Migration and store-reset regressions are mostly caught by the existing per-version suites.

**Verifier.** What does not hold: "never executed before ship" (developers launch Debug builds by hand), and the claim that a new model version or a store-load failure would pass unnoticed (per-version SQLite migration suites and the reset-ladder suite exist; the iOS host loads the real container). Debug and Release differ only in optimization and the DEBUG define, and the #if DEBUG blocks in launch files hold test hooks and preconditions. The shipping channel is internal TestFlight, so no ordinary user is reached. That makes it structural debt (medium), not high.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md, Testing: "There is no UI test target (the never-run esc-chatmailUITests and the app's UI_TEST_MODE / UI_TEST_AUTHENTICATED launch-argument hooks were removed)"; docs/scalability-review.md does not cover CI or launch testing

**Invariant risks**

- No test hooks in a Release build. The 'stubbed Gmail endpoint' or a seeded signed-in state would need an override compiled into the shipped binary. The Gmail base URL is a constant (Constants.swift:331), and ea41dfd5 removed UI_TEST_AUTHENTICATED, which forced isAuthenticated = true. An override would skip prepareLocalStoreForAuthenticatedAccount and give a local process (on the Mac, `open --args` or an environment variable) a way to send OAuth tokens to another host.
- Never launch a Mac build for the smoke. CI's Mac build is unsigned and therefore unsandboxed, so its cleanup deletes ~/Documents/Messages. A signed local build shares the container and keychain with the TestFlight MushMail used daily, and would migrate its store. So the Mac gets a Release compile only, and any UI test target must be iOS-only and left out of Mac.xctestplan.
- Release can only `build` the app, never `build-for-testing`: the test target needs seams that exist only in DEBUG (CoreDataStack.swift:52 init(unloadedPersistentContainerForTesting:), FreshInstallHandler.swift:32). Release.xcconfig also keeps SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS on, so the job fails on warnings that appear only in Release, which is the point of it.
- Isolate the smoke's state. FreshInstallHandler destroys any store whose UserDefaults and keychain installation IDs do not match (FreshInstallHandler.swift:94-136, 257). The iOS unit-test host has the same bundle ID and loads the default-URL store (esc_chatmailApp.swift:51-52). So the smoke needs its own erased simulator, and a seeded store needs a two-launch protocol. A later Gmail fake must use TestCoreDataStack and injected defaults: InitialSyncOrchestrator reads .standard (InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:276-311).

**Fix.** Split it into three, with no app hooks. (1) Per PR: give codex-build.sh a CONFIGURATION variable (Debug is hardcoded at :37) and add a CI job that builds the app alone (not for testing) in Release, for the iOS simulator, unsigned. Then use plutil to check the built Info.plist: the five GOOGLE_* keys must be resolved (where Debug traps, Release logs and returns "", Constants.swift:33-38), and the BGTask identifiers must be present. A Mac Release compile is Kevin's call, since macOS minutes bill at 10x. (2) An iOS-only smoke on its own erased simulator: launch that .app signed out, then check that it is still running after 20 s, left no crash report, and wrote AppInstallationID and the store. It stops at restore's no-session exit (AuthSession.swift:529-533). (3) The Gmail fake: hosted Debug, later.

**First step.** Add CONFIGURATION="${CONFIGURATION:-Debug}" to Scripts/codex-build.sh. Add a CI job that runs CONFIGURATION=Release ./Scripts/codex-build.sh CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO on the iOS simulator, then uses plutil to check the built Info.plist's GOOGLE_* values and BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers.

**Pinning test.** Scripts/launch-smoke.sh, run in CI: erase a dedicated simulator, install the Release .app and launch it. Fail on exit within 20 s, a new crash report, or no AppInstallationID or ESCChatmail.sqlite in the data container. Revert-check: blanking GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID in Release.xcconfig fails the plist check.

**Payoff.** Catches compile errors and warnings that appear only in Release before merge, not as a failed Xcode Cloud archive. Catches launch-order or plist crashes before the automatic internal TestFlight build reaches Kevin's devices.

### `testing-ci-release#3` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-open

**The Mac app ships on every merge with no automated test run, because its test host shares the real app's identity**

Area: Test architecture, CI and release pipeline. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

CI's macOS job compiles the app and its tests unsigned and runs none of them. Xcode Cloud archives every merge to main and sends it to internal TestFlight, with no test step. Mac.xctestplan, an allow-list of 81 of the 430 test classes, runs only on a developer Mac in a signed, sandboxed host, because MacUnitTestHostGuard refuses any host that is unsandboxed or was started by another plan. What blocks CI is signing: keychain-access-groups needs a provisioning profile, and an unsigned build has no sandbox. The shared container does not block it, since on a runner the container is empty. As a result, no automated test runs the Mac-only AppKit and Platform code before it ships, and its coverage depends on a local run that is sometimes skipped.

**Evidence**

- .github/workflows/ci.yml:72-75,92 — 'It compiles the tests and runs none'; the build is unsigned because keychain-access-groups needs a profile; 'the Mac test plan runs locally'; runs codex-build.sh --for-testing CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:374,391 — 'running Mac tests in CI means setting up signing there. Until then, run the Mac test plan locally'; 'Not covered. CI runs no Mac tests.'
- docs/mac-app-plan.md:86,94 — the Xcode Cloud action 'Archive - macOS' has distribution 'TestFlight (Internal Testing Only)'; 'A merge to main therefore ships a Mac build as well as an iOS one.'
- Mac.xctestplan:13-18,29-111 — sets ESC_CHATMAIL_MAC_TEST_PLAN and selects 81 test classes; esc-chatmail/Services/Security/MacUnitTestHostPolicy.swift:44-51 — the host refuses unless it is sandboxed and that marker is set
- docs/mac-imessage-ui-plan.md:435 — build 528's sidebar bug: 'Why nothing caught it' — the only repo probe identified its rows by Int and moved none, so no existing test could have caught it
- docs/scalability-review.md:1596 — 'the Mac test plan was not run' for step 7's change, though AuthSessionTests and HTMLContentAccountBoundaryTests gained tests and are in that plan

**Trigger.** A change to Mac-only code (Platform/ AppKit views, #if os(macOS) branches, the Mac UI) that is merged without the developer running DESTINATION='platform=macOS' ./Scripts/codex-test.sh locally. The merge still produces an internal TestFlight Mac build.

**Impact.** Before a Mac build reaches internal TestFlight, nothing automated executes the Mac-only behavior: CI only checks that it compiles. A regression is caught only by a local run, which is not always done, or later by the owner using the app. Shared Services logic is still covered by the iOS CI run. The local-run hazard is contained: the guard admits only the allow-list, the store is a throwaway, and the suites checked use temp directories and keychain services named by UUID. What that containment costs is coverage, not data loss.

**Verifier.** I confirmed the CI job, the plan, the bundle ID (pbxproj 272/321), the entitlements, the guard and run-tests.sh. Four corrections. First, the gap is already documented ("Not covered. CI runs no Mac tests", "Until then, run…locally"), and the documented blocker is signing, not the shared identity. Second, the build 528 example is misattributed: the docs say no test existed that could have caught it. Third, the 21-of-25 Dependencies count is accurate but irrelevant, because the guard keeps those suites out of Mac hosts. Fourth, distribution is internal TestFlight only. Together these lower the severity to medium.

**October review.** docs/mac-app-plan.md, PR F "Three constraints on Mac tests" > Signing (line 374: "Until then, run the Mac test plan locally") and "Not covered. CI runs no Mac tests." (line 391); ci.yml:72-76

**Invariant risks**

- A deny-list, or any non-allow-list plan, run before the host's container is provably separate. A CI-only bundle ID protects only CI. On a dev Mac the host shares ~/Library/Containers/com.esc.inboxchat with the TestFlight app used daily (mac-app-plan.md:96), so iOS-written suites would empty or rewrite the real mail data and caches. MailDerivedCacheCleanupTests empties them, others write UserDefaults.standard, and some reach the real Contacts. CLAUDE.md keeps these suites out of Mac.xctestplan for that reason.
- Weakening the backstops to get it running. That means CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX=NO, calling xcodebuild test or test-without-building directly instead of run-tests.sh (which skips verify-mac-test-host.sh), or setting ESC_CHATMAIL_MAC_TEST_PLAN anywhere but Mac.xctestplan (MacUnitTestHostPolicy.swift:44-51, run-tests.sh:51-56,156).
- Making the keychain tolerate the ad-hoc host. Without an access group, the data protection keychain returns -34018. Do not add a file-keychain fallback, drop kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain, or XCTSkip on -34018 (KeychainService.swift:226-239, KeychainServiceTests.swift:22-41). Each would hide the PR C bug, where the session is gone after a relaunch, in the signed local run. Skip that one test from CI's command line instead.
- Changing the project's bundle ID. Decision 2 keeps com.esc.inboxchat, and the OAuth client is keyed by bundle ID (mac-app-plan.md:65). KeychainService's default service is Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier (KeychainService.swift:102), so even a Debug-only change moves where tokens are stored. Xcode Cloud archives Release. Any project change must be [sdk=macosx*]-scoped and made in Xcode with Kevin's permission, never by hand-editing project.pbxproj.

**Fix.** Do it in two steps. Step 1, a CI lane with no project edit: add a tracked CI-only xcconfig. It signs ad hoc (CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual, CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=-, empty DEVELOPMENT_TEAM), points CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS[sdk=macosx*] at a new entitlements file with no keychain-access-groups, sets PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER=$(inherited).ci, and leaves the ENABLE_* sandbox settings alone. In the build-macos job, run DESTINATION='platform=macOS' Scripts/run-tests.sh -xcconfig <that file> -skip-testing esc-chatmailTests/KeychainServiceTests/testSave_updatesAccessibilityForDuplicateItem. That keeps verify-mac-test-host.sh and MacUnitTestHostGuard in front of the launch, and the allow-list stays. Triage macOS 26 failures as real findings, not by loosening assertions. Step 2, only after Kevin decides on a separate Debug container and the guard refuses the shipping bundle ID: consider a deny-list.

**First step.** Add the xcconfig and the entitlements file without keychain-access-groups. In a draft PR's Mac job, print -showBuildSettings for both targets and `codesign -d --entitlements` on MushMail.app. That confirms ad-hoc signing, app-sandbox, Xcode's testing exceptions and the .ci bundle ID.

**Pinning test.** The CI job itself: verify-mac-test-host.sh passes, and SandboxTripwireTests and MacUnitTestHostPolicyTests run green in the ad-hoc host. Add a default-plan repositorySource test asserting ci.yml's Mac job calls run-tests.sh with that xcconfig, never CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO or a bare test-without-building.

**Payoff.** Every PR would run the 81 Mac suites before the merge that ships a TestFlight Mac build. It is also their first run on macOS 26, the deployment minimum, where no Mac test has run.

### `testing-ci-release#4` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Concurrency and Core Data confinement are checked by no compiler mode, sanitizer or test-plan flag**

Area: Test architecture, CI and release pipeline. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

No automated run turns on Core Data's ConcurrencyDebug assertion or Thread Sanitizer. All three test plans pass no arguments, and CI's xcodebuild call adds none. Several production confinement fixes are justified only by that flag: PendingActionSnapshot is built inside perform, saveIfNeeded checks hasChanges on the context's own queue, and resetViewContextState goes through perform. The same goes for the main-queue test contexts in 53 suites. A revert of any of them passes CI. The default plan cannot be run under the flag as it stands, because TestCoreDataStack.viewContext is private-queue and test bodies touch it off-queue by design. Swift 5 with strict concurrency set to minimal is a documented ratchet and is not part of the defect.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail.xctestplan:2-9 — one configuration with empty options. Performance.xctestplan:2-9 is the same, Mac.xctestplan:11-26 sets only an env var and timeouts, and esc-chatmail.xcscheme:39-56 has only plan references, with no launch arguments or sanitizer
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:50-56 — run-tests.sh gets only a result bundle path and test timeouts. There is no ConcurrencyDebug argument, no -enableThreadSanitizer and no retry flag
- esc-chatmailTests/PendingActions/PendingActionsManagerTests.swift:444-449 — 'under -com.apple.CoreData.ConcurrencyDebug 1 this traps…' and 'without that flag the same revert passes here'
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:13-21 and esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataStack.swift:534-544 — production code moved on-queue because the off-queue form 'traps under -com.apple.CoreData.ConcurrencyDebug 1'
- esc-chatmailTests/TestSupport/TestCoreDataStack.swift:154-161 — the default test viewContext is private-queue and is touched by 'the test body's direct (lock-free) access from the cooperative thread', so a whole-plan flag would trap in test code
- CONCURRENCY.md:34-49 — SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = minimal is a documented ratchet floor, and targeted is known not to compile yet

**Trigger.** A change that moves a Core Data access off its context's queue in production code is not caught: for example, mapping PendingActionSnapshot outside perform, or reading hasChanges before performAndWait. Neither is a new @MainActor suite that hands stack.viewContext to main-actor code. Both pass CI.

**Impact.** A confinement regression shows up as an occasional crash or a silently lost change, in the app or as a crashed CI test runner, with no failing assertion that names it. This has happened before: the GmailSendServiceOptimisticFailureTests runner crash. Today the fixes are kept only by authors remembering to make a manual run under the flag.

**Verifier.** The finding's core is confirmed: no plan, scheme, script or CI step sets ConcurrencyDebug or TSan. 53 test files carry the 'no test here can reproduce' HONEST SCOPE note. What changed: the auditor's open question is settled, because the default suite is not clean under the flag by design, so only a per-suite ratchet is feasible. The minimal/Swift 5 setting and the graveyard are documented decisions and not defects. 'CI advisory' and 'an account-boundary bug can ship' are not supported by repo lines. The parallelizable key was dropped from the scheme in 6b68cf21; its effective default is unverified.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md Testing bullet on makeMainQueueViewContext ("Prove any new conversion with the ConcurrencyDebug flag before and after", a manual step only); docs/scalability-review.md:652 (manual proof for MessageActionsTests). No Suggested-order step covers CI.

**Invariant risks**

- Putting the flag on esc-chatmail.xctestplan, or adding a second configuration to it, traps every off-queue test. TestCoreDataStack.viewContext is private-queue and is touched off-queue by design (TestCoreDataStack.swift:144-161), and about 52 suites use neither main-queue helper. They would crash once per test, CI would go red and the local host would keep crashing, which Kevin asked to stop. Every configuration of a plan also runs on each invocation.
- A plan copied from Mac.xctestplan inherits ESC_CHATMAIL_MAC_TEST_PLAN, which only that plan may set. run-tests.sh must keep refusing -testPlan and -destination, so the new plan needs its own switch, refused on a Mac destination as --performance is, and its own -resultBundlePath, because an existing bundle path fails the run.
- An allowlist taken by grep, not by measurement, is unsafe. The main-queue suites were proven once, by hand (PendingActionsManagerTests.swift:24-26). The sync invariant suites (IncrementalSyncCursorTests, MessagePersisterDispositionTests, AbandonedMessageRetryTests) use neither helper. Runs expected to crash must be announced first and stopped at the first crash in each suite.
- Replacing wall-clock waits contradicts CLAUDE.md's Testing rule (a deadline-plus-poll waitUntil; FakeSyncClock only for backoff). TSan as a gate fails no test by default and would be noisy against the @unchecked Sendable debt. Pinning -parallel-testing-enabled in run-tests.sh changes every local and CI run, and codex-test.sh documents that flag as an escape hatch.

**Fix.** Add a separate iOS-only ConcurrencyDebug.xctestplan rather than a second configuration of the default plan. It passes commandLineArgumentEntries -com.apple.CoreData.ConcurrencyDebug and 1, sets an env var naming the plan, copies the Mac plan's timeouts but never ESC_CHATMAIL_MAC_TEST_PLAN, and its selectedTests lists only suites measured clean under the flag. Reference the plan in the scheme, as PR F did. Give run-tests.sh a --concurrency-debug switch that is refused on a Mac destination and with --performance, and that adds -parallel-testing-enabled NO. Add a step to CI's existing test job with its own result bundle. Ratchet by adding suites, then switch to skippedTests. Leave TSan for later, scheduled and advisory.

**First step.** Build for testing once. Run each candidate suite under the flag through a copied .xctestrun, as the recorded recipe does, starting with suites whose headers claim a clean proof. Announce expected crashes to Kevin first, stop each suite at its first crash, and record the clean set.

**Pinning test.** A canary test asserts that UserDefaults reads com.apple.CoreData.ConcurrencyDebug as 1 whenever the plan's env var is set. A repositorySource test pins the plan's argument, its missing Mac env var and its selected suites. Revert-check: reading hasChanges before performAndWait crashes the plan.

**Payoff.** Turns the manual "prove it under ConcurrencyDebug" rule into a deterministic CI gate. An off-queue Core Data access in covered code fails a named test instead of shipping as a rare crash or a lost save.

### `testing-ci-release#5` · medium · performance · effort M · known-partial

**Performance and scale have no gate before release and no signal after it**

Area: Test architecture, CI and release pipeline. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

CI runs only the default plan, which skips the three performance and scale suites, so no automated check covers the app's S2 query plans or the hub-fault bounds. One default-plan test says this itself: the `isUnread == YES` spelling passes it, and only ScaleQueryPlanTests catches the plan. The harness's own machinery is tested in CI, and CLAUDE.md asks for a manual --performance run. The measure tests have no baselines and catch only slowdowns past a 20–45 s timeout. In the app, the only telemetry client is a no-op and MetricKit is unused.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail.xctestplan:20-24 — skippedTests: PerformanceRegressionTests, ScaleHubFaultTests, ScaleQueryPlanTests; .github/workflows/ci.yml:50-56 runs Scripts/run-tests.sh with no --performance
- Scripts/run-tests.sh:64-80 — Performance plan only with --performance (refused on Mac); default plan excludes it because 'the scale harness takes about half a minute to seed its store'
- esc-chatmailTests/CoreData/MessagePredicatesSQLiteTests.swift:118-120 — HONEST SCOPE: `isUnread == YES` passes this CI test; 'What that spelling costs is the query plan, which ScaleQueryPlanTests pins'
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/PerformanceRegressionTests.swift:66,155-158 — measure(metrics:options:) and measureAsync(timeout: 30.0); no .xcbaseline is tracked; XCTestCase+Async.swift:126-139 fails only when wait(for:timeout:) expires
- esc-chatmailTests/Performance/ScaleHubFaultTests.swift:27-34 — strict XCTExpectFailure wrappers, measured on the iOS 27.0 simulator only, which come off only when the suite runs
- esc-chatmail/Services/Observability/TelemetryClient.swift:31-40 — NoopTelemetryClient, the Dependencies default; LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-48 — Release logs .warning and up with enabledDiagnostics [], so startup timing is off

**Trigger.** A PR that changes a hot predicate's spelling, an index or a relationship write so that SQLite plans a scan, for example `unreadInInbox` written as `isUnread == YES`. It passes CI, and a merge to main ships a TestFlight build through Xcode Cloud.

**Impact.** Plan and hub-fault regressions are caught only if someone runs --performance by hand, which CLAUDE.md asks for. The step-5 fixes and the strict expected-failure ratchet are therefore enforced by process, not by CI. The app itself reports nothing about launch, hangs or background memory exits. Because a mailbox starts empty at sign-in and older mail is never loaded, S2 is reached only after long use, so exposure comes slowly.

**Verifier.** The mechanism holds. Corrections: SQLiteQueryPlanRecorderTests and ScaleStoreSeederTests already run in CI, and CLAUDE.md documents a manual gate. The measure tests do catch gross slowdowns through their timeouts. 'Deterministic and cheap in CI' is unproven: the scale suites have never run on Xcode 26 / iOS 26, the recorder relies on private Core Data API, and plans made with statistics are SQLite's own choices. CI adoption therefore needs a trial run first. No doc rejects running these suites in CI or adding MetricKit. TestFlight crash and hang reports exist outside the code; I did not verify them.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:74 (root cause 9), :1498 (asked only for an opt-in SQLite suite), Suggested order step 4 :1537-1540 (built 2026-11-16, --performance only); CLAUDE.md Testing, "The scale harness ... also runs only under --performance"

**Invariant risks**

- Un-skipping the scale suites in the default plan breaks them. The recorder is process-wide (SQLiteQueryPlanRecorder.swift:28-30) and ScaleQueryPlanTests.swift:61-62 counts every ZMESSAGE plan it records, so tasks left by other tests make it flaky. Seeding also takes tens of seconds (ScaleStoreTemplate.swift:8-12), which can pass the 120 s per-test allowance (ci.yml:50-56).
- The strict XCTExpectFailure ratchet and the plan assertions that depend on statistics were measured on iOS 27.0 only (ScaleHubFaultTests.swift:28-35; SQLiteQueryPlanRecorder.swift:14-21). CI runs Xcode 26 / iOS 26. Making the step blocking right away risks red CI, and quieting it with isStrict=false or by deleting wrappers would break the rule that a wrapper comes off only in its fix's own change.
- Baselining PerformanceRegressionTests or running them in CI goes against run-tests.sh:77-79, which calls them timing-sensitive. .xcbaseline files are tied to one machine, so runner variance would make them flaky.
- MetricKit: the logging redaction rule and TelemetryClient.swift:37-39's typed allowlist forbid logging diagnostic JSON, whose exception reasons can hold mail content. Persisting payloads would create an on-disk store that clearMailDerivedCaches does not know about. The code must build for the Mac target, which CI compiles, and must register after the isRunningUnitTests return (esc_chatmailApp.swift:192-195).

**Fix.** PR 1 (CI): in ci.yml's iOS job, after the default plan and reusing its build, add a step that runs `run-tests.sh --performance -only-testing:esc-chatmailTests/ScaleQueryPlanTests -only-testing:esc-chatmailTests/ScaleHubFaultTests -parallel-testing-enabled NO`, with a 600 s allowance and its own result bundle. Keep PerformanceRegressionTests out of CI and add no baselines. Mark the step `continue-on-error: true` until it passes on iOS 26, then make it blocking. Add a nightly schedule in its own concurrency group. PR 2: an iOS-only MXMetricManager subscriber, registered after the unit-test return in initializeApp, that turns metric payloads into number-only TelemetryEvent counters. Never log diagnostic JSON.

**First step.** Add the scale step to ci.yml's test job with continue-on-error: true and push a branch. From its xcresult, read the seed time and memory, and check whether each plan assertion and strict wrapper holds on CI's iOS 26 runtime.

**Pinning test.** A source suite (repositorySource) pinning that ci.yml runs --performance with both scale suites and the default plan still skips them. Revert-check: a throwaway branch spelling unreadInInbox `isUnread == YES` must turn that CI step red.

**Payoff.** A plan or hub-fault regression fails its PR before Xcode Cloud ships the TestFlight build. CI then enforces the strict-wrapper ratchet, and real use reports launch, hang and memory-exit numbers.

### `observability-errors#4` · low · maintainability · effort S · new

**Error redaction drops the causal chain; nested Swift error enums log as case ordinals**

Area: Observability, diagnostics and error handling. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

`Log.redact(error:)` keeps only the top-level domain#code. For APIError it keeps only the case name and drops the payload. `Log.log` then appends the bridged code, which for a Swift enum with no CustomNSError conformance is its case tag. So when a Swift wrapper is what gets thrown, the cause is missing from Release logs: a failing sync save reaches SyncEngine as CoreDataError.saveFailed and is logged only as `esc_chatmail.CoreDataError#2`, and 4xx statuses inside APIError.invalidData are dropped. On store load the raw Cocoa domain#code is logged, but not its SQLite code or its NSUnderlyingErrorKey chain.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/Log+Redaction.swift:104-113 — an APIError is reduced to its case name; every other error to `\(nsError.domain)#\(nsError.code)`, with no userInfo or underlying walk
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/Log.swift:126-131 — appends ` (code: \(nsError.code))` after the redacted error, which repeats the code for an NSError and gives the enum tag for a Swift error
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:93 with esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncEngine.swift:360 — saveAsync wraps the save error in CoreDataError.saveFailed, and the run's only error line is `log.error("\(syncType) sync failed", error: error)`
- esc-chatmail/Services/CoreData/CoreDataRecoveryHandler.swift:33-41 — the raw store-load NSError is logged at error level with the branch taken (migration / corrupt / keep on disk), so the Cocoa code is kept; the SQLite code under userInfo is not
- esc-chatmail/Services/API/GmailAPIClient.swift:421,477 — a 5xx status is logged at warning before APIError.serverError is thrown, and per-attempt failures log URLErrors unwrapped (GmailAPIClient+History.swift:42 is the only producer of networkError, and it wraps a constant)
- esc-chatmail/Services/Logging/LoggerConfiguration.swift:41-48 — Release has minimumLevel .warning, so the NSDetailedErrorsKey lines (CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:33-39, Log.debug) and the sync timing outcome (SyncHelpers.swift:65-67, Log.info) are never emitted

**Trigger.** A Release or TestFlight sync whose saveAsync fails on every run for a reason other than a full disk (validation, constraint or I/O), or a store load latched as keepStore, investigated from `log show` alone.

**Impact.** The persisted line for a failed sync save names only the wrapper and its case tag, so validation, constraint and I/O failures cannot be told apart without a reproduction or a screenshot of the user's status text. A kept store shows Cocoa 256 or 134xxx without the SQLite or POSIX cause the classifier acted on. Only diagnostics are affected; the app behaves the same.

**Verifier.** The original claim was too broad. CoreDataRecoveryHandler logs the raw store-load NSError at error level, so the Cocoa code is kept. GmailAPIClient logs 5xx statuses at warning (persisted), and URLErrors are logged unwrapped as NSURLErrorDomain#code. I dropped the classification part of the claim: AppLoadingPolicy:140-155 unwraps PersistentStoreLoadError itself, errorChain follows CoreDataError, and I found no case it classifies wrongly. That a Swift enum's bridged code is its case tag is a Swift runtime default I inferred, not something I ran. Since only diagnostics are affected, I rated it low.

**Invariant risks**

- The fix must not widen StorageErrorClassifier.errorChain (StorageErrorClassifier.swift:58-80) or give the app's error enums a CustomNSError conformance that sets NSUnderlyingErrorKey. errorChain decides the store-reset allow-list (CoreDataErrorClassifier.swift:67-75) and isOutOfSpace, which routes a sync into the full-disk backoff. ConnectionErrorDetector.isPreTransmissionError walks NSUnderlyingErrorKey (RetryStrategy.swift:148), so APIError.networkError(cannotConnectToHost) would read as pre-transmission on the send path, a duplicate-send hazard. CustomNSError would also change the bridged domain and code that the classifiers compare.
- Redaction is a hard rule at the call site, because the pipeline emits %{public}@ (Log.swift:141). Log only domain, code, the NSNumber under userInfo[NSSQLiteErrorDomain] and typed numeric payloads. Never log localizedDescription, an interpolated error, or string payloads: invalidData, notFound and quotaExhausted carry Gmail's message or a 300-character body prefix (GmailAPIClient.swift:264,543,567). Also never log NSValidationValueErrorKey, NSFilePathErrorKey or failing URLs.
- Managed objects never cross contexts. The NSError that saveAsync throws carries NSValidationObjectErrorKey objects through the continuation to SyncEngine on the main actor. The redactor must never touch or stringify userInfo values, which would fire a fault off-queue and trap under ConcurrencyDebug. Read entity names only inside the context's perform, at CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:92.
- LogRedactionTests' static guard matches its allowlist exactly. Editing a fingerprinted line (CoreDataSaveOperations.swift:30,35,68,73) means updating legacyRawSensitiveLogFingerprints in the same change. New lines may not interpolate localizedDescription or an error. A plain NSError with no chain must still redact to exactly "SensitiveDomain#42" (LogRedactionTests.swift:138).

**Fix.** Change logging only: leave errorChain and the enums' bridging as they are. In Log+Redaction.swift, add a private chain walk: identity dedupe, at most 8 links, detailed errors collapsed to a count plus their distinct domain#code. It follows CoreDataError and PersistentStoreLoadError underlyingError, AuthError payloads, APIError.networkError/decodingError, and the three userInfo error keys. Print each app enum as Type.case through an exhaustive switch with no default, keeping numeric payloads only (serverError(503), retryAfter). Print an NSError as domain#code, plus sqlite=N where present. Drop the "(code:)" suffix in Log.swift. Log 4xx statuses where they are thrown. In saveAsync's catch, on the context's queue, log each failure's entity, validation key and code at error level.

**First step.** Add failing LogRedactionTests first: saveFailed wrapping Cocoa 1570 whose detailed error carries a PII validation value; Cocoa 256 carrying SQLite 13; invalidData holding an address. Then implement the walk in Log+Redaction.swift and drop Log.swift's suffix.

**Pinning test.** LogRedactionTests asserts that saveFailed prints its case, NSCocoaErrorDomain#1570 and sqlite=13, and no address, "#2" or "code:". A guard (Revert-check: no CustomNSError) asserts isPreTransmissionError(APIError.networkError(URLError(.cannotConnectToHost))) and isOutOfSpace(APIError.networkError(ENOSPC)) stay false.

**Payoff.** A sync save that keeps failing, or a kept store, shows its Core Data, SQLite or HTTP cause in Release `log show`. The app behaves the same, and no new PII is logged.

## Enforcing the invariants (10)

### `account-boundary-auth#2` · medium · maintainability · effort M · new

**The account boundary is composed by convention in closures no test runs, and its hand-copied sequences have drifted**

Area: Account boundary, auth session and credential lifecycle. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The structural point holds. About twenty participants are wired by hand into AuthSession's default closure literals, and no test runs that wiring, so dropping a participant from cleanupHTMLContent or reopenHTMLContent fails nothing. One drift is real: alias-cache invalidation sits in the four sign-out sequences, outside the shared performDurableLocalCleanup. So signing in as a different account keeps the old account's aliases until initial sync's profile fetch, and in that window the only reader that runs is a new compose's optimistic hash. The other sub-claims are dead code, deliberate choices or documented behavior, not drift.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:402-438 — cleanupHTMLContent/reopenHTMLContent fan-out written as default-argument closures; 431 and 434 call actors (HTMLContentRecoveryService, EmailPreviewSnapshotCache) with no await, which CLAUDE.md's Traps section records as compiling and still hopping
- esc-chatmailTests/Security/AuthSessionTests.swift:3311-3326 — makeAuthSession replaces every closure with a no-op; 1865-1867 HONEST SCOPE: "That the defaults call them is not run by any test"; a grep finds no test that pins the HTML fan-out's contents
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:873, 1130, 1787, 1845 — AliasManager/SendAsAliasManager.invalidate() only in the four sign-out sequences; 1237-1239 an interactive sign-in of another account runs only performDurableLocalCleanup (1609-1684), which has none; Services/Sync/AliasManager.swift:42-45 then reuses cachedAccountAliases
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:113-116 — the new profile's aliases replace the cache before any message is persisted; ViewModels/ComposeViewModel.swift:385 and Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:106 — a new compose's optimistic hash is the only reader on an empty store
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:342, 871-872 — clearConversationCaches defaults to {}, but grep finds no conversation cache type to clear: a dead hook with a misleading comment, not a leak
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:167-183 — the inspector's list is explicit on purpose, per its comment, and matches the 12 non-Account entities of ESCChatmail 6.xcdatamodel exactly

**Trigger.** The next participant added or moved without being wired into AuthSession's default closures. For the stale aliases: an authenticated session marked requiresReauthentication, SignInView ('Reconnect'), and the user picks a different Google account and sends New Message to the old account's address before initial sync's first profile fetch succeeds.

**Impact.** A missed participant fails no build and no test, and it stays open across an account switch. The stale aliases fork at most a new compose addressed to the old account's own addresses into a mis-hashed chat. Reply addressing is unreachable because the store is empty. The window normally lasts seconds and lasts longer only while the first profile fetch keeps failing.

**Verifier.** Every cited line was opened and the mechanisms confirmed. Downgraded from high. CLAUDE.md already records the duck-typed contract, the wiring rule and the await-less closures. The silent renderer refusal (EmailPreviewSnapshotRenderer.swift:331-341) is a commented degrade-not-cross choice, like reopenPreSignInAccountWork. The inspector list has not drifted, and clearConversationCaches has nothing to clear. CoreDataStack.resetStore (511-532) does not invalidate aliases. Initial sync sets aliases before it persists anything, so sync-side hashing is safe.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md, "Account-generation boundary": "A new participant must be wired into AuthSession's six injectable closures ... Otherwise it never closes" and "Participant contract (duck-typed; there is no shared protocol)". These record the hand-wiring convention as the current rule. Nothing records a decision against consolidating it. docs/scalability-review.md has no item on boundary composition or on alias invalidation.

**Invariant risks**

- The order is load-bearing and differs by direction. CacheCoordinator closes first. Reopen closes it again first, even at cold launch, and reopens it last: AuthSession.swift:404, 429 and 437, and the deliberate asymmetry in CLAUDE.md. Participant caches must drain before resetCoreDataStore (AuthSession.swift:1627-1630). HTMLContentHandler closes before deleteAllHTMLFromClosedAccount (405-407). A registry that runs in registration order loses all of this.
- The six paths differ on purpose, so one teardown()/bringUp() would flatten them. The sign-outs persist the marker and call closeAdmission before their first await (813-828); sign-in and restore take the gate first. reopenAccountWork is all-or-none, with three refusal outcomes that are not interchangeable (1514-1559). reopenPreSignInAccountWork deliberately degrades (1577-1607). The crash-resume pair takes no gate of its own.
- Ownership is a tree, not a flat list. FullEmailWebViewManager is the only close/reopen owner of FullEmailReaderAccountBoundaryRegistry (FullEmailWebViewManager.swift:1565-1575). HTMLContentLoader fans out to four participants (HTMLContentLoader.swift:712-724). Participants span actors, @MainActor classes and lock-guarded types that are captured synchronously. A lazy .shared singleton that registers itself can also join while the boundary is closed and admit work.
- Traps: in default-argument position, actor calls such as 431 and 434 compile without await. Moved into an ordinary function they need one, and a needless await fails the build. CI's Swift 6.2 rejects non-Sendable captures that 6.4 accepts, so the change has to build on both. Any runtime test of the real fan-out must never run deleteAllHTMLFromClosedAccount or resetStore on .shared, and must stay out of Mac.xctestplan, because the Mac test host runs in the real container.

**Fix.** Do not build the registry or a single teardown/bringUp. (1) Add an injectable `invalidateAccountAliases` closure (default: both alias actors' invalidate), called in performDurableLocalCleanup right after resetCoreDataStore; route the four sign-out calls through it. Give AliasManager and SendAsAliasManager a generation bumped by invalidate, so a load straddling it returns its value but never re-caches. (2) Move the HTML close/reopen bodies into named ProductionHTMLContentAccountTransition statics, beside ProductionParticipantCacheAccountTransition, keeping deleteAllHTMLFromClosedAccount a separate step. (3) Add a source-scan test: every declarer of reopenAccountWork/reopenAdmission is named by a Production* fan-out or its documented owner. Keep the inspector list explicit; pin it against the model's entities.

**First step.** Add `invalidateAccountAliases: @Sendable () async -> Void` to AuthSession.init, defaulting to both alias actors' invalidate(). Call it in performDurableLocalCleanup right after resetCoreDataStore, and add the generation check to AliasManager's getAliases, getCachedAliases and setAliases.

**Pinning test.** AuthSessionTests: a sign-in that finds another account's row calls invalidateAccountAliases after resetCoreDataStore and before publishing (Revert-check names the call). AliasManager test: invalidate while getAliases is suspended in an injected selfAliasProvider leaves hasCachedAliases false.

**Payoff.** Ends the stale-alias window after an account switch. A participant left out of the fan-out then fails a default-plan test instead of failing silently, and the six transition paths keep their order.

### `concurrency-model#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · known-partial

**The gate hierarchy is hand-rolled continuation queues: ordering by comment, no priority propagation, no cancellation, no deadline or holder diagnostics**

Area: Concurrency model and Swift 6 readiness. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

The gates are separate continuation queues whose ordering rules live only in comments, with no deadline or holder logging; no violation or leak exists today, so the permanent hang is hypothetical. The present cost is narrower: the chat-preview repair runs at .background, takes an account lease, then queues on the throwing cleanup gate, whose waiters cannot escalate the holder. A send's optimistic bubble or a sign-out can wait for one batch of at most 25 rows. The non-throwing variant does chain Task values, and several waits honor cancellation.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:95-112 — performThrowing runs the operation in the caller's task; the tail later waiters await is a Task parked on CompletionGate's continuation (17-35), so no waiter reaches the holder. Lines 155-161: gate-then-turn order is a comment ('Both fail silently, as a hang. No holder of a conversation's turn asks for the gate today')
- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:57-65 — non-throwing perform runs the operation in its own Task and the stored tail awaits task.value, so its holders (DataCleanupService.swift:201,234,375; MessageActions.swift:603) sit on a Task-value await chain; 'nothing escalates' holds only for performThrowing holders
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:225,266,281 — chat-preview pass runs at repairTaskPriority (default .background, line 79), takes the lease first, then queues on performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation. Lines 144-153: comment accepts a send waiting a whole batch at background priority, batch cut to 25, 'Unmeasured'
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:59-70,416-421 and esc-chatmail/Services/Chat/RichContentVerdictRefresher.swift:80-86 — the verdict backfill and refresher run at .utility because leased work blocks sign-out and background jobs can sit unscheduled; the chat-preview pass, also leased, stays at .background
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncRunCoordinator.swift:273-297 — beginQuiescence cancels only activeRun's task and parks on boundaryDrainWaiters until every lease is released: no deadline, no log. Lines 155-176,332-349: acquireRunWithTask's wait does end on cancellation. esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:2053-2062 — auth gate is a bare continuation FIFO
- esc-chatmail/Services/Send/GmailSendService+OptimisticUpdates.swift:54-62 — a send's optimistic creation queues on performThrowingCleanupSensitiveMutation and takes anchor turns inside it. esc-chatmail/Services/Send/OutboundConversationSendSequencer.swift:66-87 — that wait is cancellation-aware

**Trigger.** Today: the chat-preview pass has work (the mailbox-wide sweep after an update that bumps chatPreviewDerivationVersion, or the short deferred re-check after each sync while a failed send is retained) and the user taps Send or signs out while background-priority work is starved by higher-priority load. A permanent hang needs a future change that takes two gates in the wrong order or leaks a lease or turn; none exists in the code read.

**Impact.** A send's optimistic bubble, a draft save or a sign-out waits for one batch of at most 25 rows (HTML reads, derivation, save) plus the actor hops that release the gate and lease, all scheduled at background priority with nothing to escalate them. The wait is bounded, not a hang; its length on a device is unmeasured. If a later change breaks an ordering rule or leaks a lease, the affected transition or send would wait forever with no log naming the holder.

**Verifier.** Read the serializer, SyncRunCoordinator, launch repair coordinator, refresher, creation serializer and send sequencer whole, plus the auth gate and send call site. All cited code is as described. CLAUDE.md documents the uncancellable auth gate, the lease rule and the gate-then-turn rule as known traps; the code accepts the background-priority gate hold for sends. docs/scalability-review.md does not cover it. Lowered to medium: no reachable hang, bounded present cost. Device scheduling of background tasks was not observed.

**October review.** docs/scalability-review.md:1049-1071 version-bump-full-mailbox-rederivation lists "replies waiting behind a batch for the gate". Built since: 25-row batches and cancellation inside the caller's task (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:144-153, 271-278). Still left: the hold runs at background QoS, the batch is saved on main (line 347), and nothing logs who holds the gate. Not in the Suggested order's built steps.

**Invariant risks**

- Exclusion is transitive only because performThrowing's wait for earlier holders cannot be cancelled (ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:96-119). Each successor waits only for the tail ahead of it. So a waiter that leaves early on cancellation opens its CompletionGate while the earlier holder is still running, and a send and a cleanup snapshot then overlap. A cancelled waiter must keep its slot until it reaches the front, as OutboundConversationSendSequencer.swift:66-105 does. Taking several keys at once must stay one actor turn.
- The two variants handle cancellation differently on purpose. performThrowing runs the batch in the caller's task so that cancel() reaches it (ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:271-278). perform must not pass cancellation on (MessageActions, and the maintenance passes, which stop only between passes). Escalation through an awaited Task would also miss the main cost: the 25-row derivation runs in a context.perform GCD block (ChatPreviewRepair.swift:117-130, 182, 258, 323).
- The auth gate and the quiescence drain must stay uncancellable and must never go ahead when a deadline passes. signOut persists its marker and calls closeAdmission before it waits (AuthSession.swift:813-828), and signIn holds the gate and quiescence across Google's sign-in UI (666-692). Any deadline is for logging only. Going past a lease that is still held lets destructive cleanup run while old-account work is live.
- A DEBUG rank check through a TaskLocal gives false positives, because unstructured Tasks inherit task-locals. ChatViewModel's merge hold (ChatViewModel.swift:1184-1201) calls adoptUnsentReply, which calls scheduleReplyDraftSave, which calls taskManager.run, which calls saveReplyDraft on the same gate (1237, 1313-1317, 1347). That is legitimate and cannot deadlock. Trip the check only when the asking task is the holding task (withUnsafeCurrentTask), and log rather than call assertionFailure in hosted tests.

**Fix.** Keep the gates; do not replace them with one primitive. (1) Run the chat-preview pass and the missing-preview pass's gate hold at .utility, through one helper shared with richContentVerdictBackfillPriority (nil stays nil), and rewrite the init doc. (2) Pass the AccountWorkRequest into prepareAndSaveChatPreviewBatch and refuse there, and again before its save, once a transition has started (new SyncRunCoordinator.isAccountWorkRequestCurrent): isActiveRun stays true for a lease during quiescence. (3) Diagnostics only: give each serializer call site a label, record the holder's label and start time, and log one Log.warning naming holder and waiter after about 5 s. Do the same for beginQuiescence's remaining lease kinds and the auth gate's owner path. Never cancel or go ahead when a deadline passes.

**First step.** Add static accountHeldPassPriority(_ base: TaskPriority?) -> TaskPriority? (nil maps to nil, anything else to .utility) to ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator. Use it for richContentVerdictBackfillPriority and at the chat-preview taskManager.run (line 225). Rewrite the init doc (lines 59-70) to say why.

**Pinning test.** ChatPreviewRepairTests: hold the injected serializer's gate with a probe, start the repair so its lease queues, begin quiescence, then release the probe. Assert no row is derived (didDeriveRow) and quiescence returns. Add a pure test of accountHeldPassPriority, and Revert-check both.

**Payoff.** Sends, draft saves and sign-out queued behind a chat-preview batch stop waiting on background-QoS work. Sign-out stops waiting for a queued batch. A future gate hang names its holder in the log.

### `invariant-enforcement#1` · medium · reliability · effort S · new

**Account teardown is seven hand-copied sequences with closure-wired participants, and the copies have drifted**

Area: Invariant enforcement, complexity budget and change safety. Verdict: corrected (medium confidence).

AuthSession writes the close, quiesce, drain and cleanup steps out by hand in each of its six paths, and two drifts are real. First, both crash-resume paths call `GIDSignIn.sharedInstance.signOut()` directly instead of the injected `signOutGoogleSession`. Second, when sign-in resets the store (`prepareLocalStore` → `performDurableLocalCleanup`), it skips the AliasManager and SendAsAliasManager invalidation that the removal paths perform. In production both effects are narrow. The most concrete cost is in the Mac test plan: AuthSessionTests drive the resume paths, so the real SDK sign-out runs in a test host whose keychain is the installed app's.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:1774, :1838 — `GIDSignIn.sharedInstance.signOut()` called directly; :338-340 is the injected default; :850, :1109 and :1717 use `signOutGoogleSession()`
- esc-chatmailTests/Security/AuthSessionTests.swift:1536-1563 — sets the reset marker on a mock keychain and calls `restorePreviousSignIn` (reaches :1774); :3309 injects `signOutGoogleSession: {}`, which that path ignores; Mac.xctestplan:37 runs the whole AuthSessionTests suite; CLAUDE.md:40 says the Mac host's keychain is the real one
- AuthSession.swift:873-874 — sign-out invalidates both alias caches; :1609-1657 (`performDurableLocalCleanup`), reached from sign-in at :774-777, does not; AliasManager.swift:41-47 serves `cachedAccountAliases` without reloading; InitialSyncOrchestrator.swift:113-116 replaces them at the initial sync's first phase
- AuthSession.swift:342 — `clearConversationCaches` defaults to `{}`; nothing remains for it to clear (the conversation cache was removed in commit 5cde4648), so it is a vestigial hook, not drift
- esc-chatmail/App/FreshInstallHandler.swift:190-205 — awaits `GIDSignIn.disconnect` with no app-side bound; the SDK's GIDSignIn.m:1061-1071 (DerivedData checkout) uses a default URLRequest with `retryEnabled` and a 15 s `maxRetryInterval`, so the wait is long but finite; AppStartupBootstrap.swift:16-20 runs it before store load and before the restore
- esc-chatmail/Services/HTMLContent/HTMLContentHandler.swift:32-47 — a nil generation checks only the open flag; MessagePersister.swift:145-147 writes sync HTML with no token, but the sync run is drained by `beginQuiescence` before cleanup (AuthSession.swift:845-846), so no leak follows

**Trigger.** The main one is running Mac.xctestplan, whose AuthSessionTests resume tests call the real SDK sign-out, on a Mac where the TestFlight MushMail is signed in. A rarer one is in production: signing in as a different Google account from the reconnect screen, then sending to the old account's address or to your own before the first sync fetches the profile. A third is an iOS reinstall launch on a stalled network.

**Impact.** The Mac test run deletes the GTMAppAuth keychain item that the installed app shares. On its next launch, the app finds no SDK session and rejects its orphaned credentials (AuthSession.swift:519-534, 555-559), so the user must sign in again (the store is kept). In production, the stale alias set can fork one chat during a window of a few seconds. A reinstall launch can sit on the loading screen for minutes. No cross-account leak or wedge was shown.

**Verifier.** I read AuthSession.swift whole, plus FreshInstallHandler, AliasManager, SendAsAliasManager, HTMLContentResultCache, the AuthSessionTests helper, the Mac plan and the SDK sources. Several parts of the claim do not hold: the `clearConversationCaches` no-op is a leftover hook. The disconnect wait is finite, and because it runs before any account exists, it cannot clobber one. There are 42 nil-defaulted tokens, not 41; they are debt, and the sync writer is covered by quiescence. The inspector's list matches the model minus Account today. The second loader is per view model and keyed by message ID. The Mac keychain deletion is inferred from code, not run.

**October review.** CLAUDE.md, Account-generation boundary: "All orchestration lives in AuthSession" and "Participant contract (duck-typed; there is no shared protocol)". docs/scalability-review.md has no item on this.

**Invariant risks**

- Gate and close happen in opposite orders on purpose (CLAUDE.md:61). Sign-outs persist the marker and call closeAdmission before their first await (AuthSession.swift:813-828), while signIn and restore take the gate first (:666-679). One executor entry that does both the same way would either lose a queued sign-out's intent or supersede a transition it should wait for. If the executor takes the gate, calling it from the crash-resume pair (:497, :502), which takes no gate, deadlocks on a gate that is non-reentrant and whose waits cannot be cancelled.
- The reopen outcomes are not interchangeable. reopenAccountWork is all-or-none (:1514-1559). reopenPreSignInAccountWork deliberately degrades and still publishes the existing session (:1577-1607). The restore maps outcomes through AuthRestoreReopenPolicy (:636-646), and signIn's catch clears the session it replaced (:709-728). A 'reopened' token that gates publishing must keep all four, plus pendingActionAuthenticationDidRecover after every publish.
- The cleanup order matters, and the closes have different shapes. CacheCoordinator closes first, even at cold launch. HTMLContentHandler closes before its delete. The participant caches are drained before resetCoreDataStore (:1627-1634). The tripwire-throwing deletion runs before clearMailDerivedCaches (:394-397). A thrown error keeps the reset marker. A registry that iterates in arbitrary order, or a protocol that cannot throw, breaks these. Making generation tokens required changes MessagePersister's tokenless sync HTML writes and the body-materialization throw contract.
- FreshInstallHandler runs before the store loads and outside the gate (AppStartupBootstrap.swift:16-36). Routing it through an executor that resets through CoreDataStack moves it after the load. Wrapping GIDSignIn.disconnect in withSoftTimeout lets the SDK's late completion run its own signOut (GIDSignIn.m:475) over a session signed in meanwhile. That is the hazard recorded at AuthSession.swift:1104-1107.

**Fix.** Fix the drift in place; do not build the executor, registry or required tokens. (1) Replace `GIDSignIn.sharedInstance.signOut()` at AuthSession.swift:1774 and :1838 with `signOutGoogleSession()`. (2) Invalidate both alias caches in `performDurableLocalCleanup` after `resetCoreDataStore`, through a new injected `invalidateAliasCaches` closure, and give `AliasManager` an invalidation epoch checked after its awaits, so a load already in flight cannot re-cache the old account. (3) Separately (M), extract the body the four removal paths share into one gate-free private helper, keeping each entry's marker, close-before-gate order, token capture and exact sweep count. Never wrap FreshInstallHandler's `GIDSignIn.disconnect` in a soft timeout.

**First step.** Replace the two direct SDK sign-outs (AuthSession.swift:1774, :1838) with `signOutGoogleSession()`. In new tests beside AuthSessionTests.swift:1399/1429, inject a recording closure and assert it ran. Do not run Mac.xctestplan before this lands.

**Pinning test.** AuthSessionTests: both resume paths call the injected `signOutGoogleSession` (Revert-check names the two call sites). A sign-in over another account's store runs `invalidateAliasCaches` after `resetCoreDataStore`. AliasManagerTests: an invalidate during a suspended load is not overwritten.

**Payoff.** Mac test runs no longer delete the Google keychain item of the MushMail used daily, every store reset clears the old account's aliases, and the copied teardown sequences stop drifting.

### `invariant-enforcement#2` · medium · reliability · effort M · new

**Ordering rules between hand-built gates, turns and leases exist only in comments; a violation is a silent hang nobody would see**

Area: Invariant enforcement, complexity budget and change safety. Verdict: corrected (high confidence).

The gate, conversation turns, leases, the exclusive run and the auth-transition gate are all built by hand on continuations. Their ordering rules (gate before turn, a lease holder never waits for the exclusive run, no transition inside a transition) exist only in comments and CLAUDE.md. Nothing checks them: no task-local record of held locks, no assert, no timeout, no log naming the holder, and telemetry is a no-op. A lease and an exclusive run are the same `SyncRun` type. A protocol default sends the lease-safe enqueue to the overload that waits for the run, so a missing witness compiles and no test would catch it. No violation exists today.

**Evidence**

- esc-chatmail/Services/Conversation/ConversationRollupMutationSerializer.swift:155-161 — the gate-then-turn rule is a comment ('Both fail silently, as a hang. No holder of a conversation's turn asks for the gate today'); :15 and :126-141 the gate is one more string key in the turn table; :46 `perform(conversationKeys: Set<String>)` is internal, and MessageActions.swift:113, 138 and 872-875 build the URI key strings themselves
- esc-chatmail/Services/Sync/SyncRunCoordinator.swift:20-23, 193-204, 266-268 — a lease and an exclusive run are both `SyncRun`, and `isActiveRun` accepts either; 190-192 'must never wait on the exclusive boundary' is a comment; 292-296 the quiescence drain loop waits with no bound or log
- esc-chatmail/Services/PendingActions/PendingActionsManagerProtocol.swift:87-108 — the protocol extension makes the lease-safe `queueAction`/`queueConversationAction(within:)` fall back to the acquiring overloads, which call `acquireRun` (PendingActionsManager.swift:546, 620); MessageActionsTests.swift:1941-1955: the mock implements only the acquiring overloads, so no test runs the real `within:` witnesses (PendingActionsManager.swift:567-590, 641-664)
- esc-chatmail/Services/ConversationList/ConversationLaunchRepairCoordinator.swift:264-313 — a lease is taken and released by hand around a wait on the cleanup-sensitive gate; 481-484 'a leaked lease hangs every later sign-out'
- esc-chatmail/Services/Security/AuthSession.swift:2053-2062 — the transition gate parks on an uncancellable `withCheckedContinuation` with no reentrancy check; 2083-2093 its only bound is a DEBUG test helper
